pr_chain.title: Resolve custom cast property types via CastsAttributes get method
pr_chain.description:
When generating PHPDoc for Eloquent models, custom cast classes (implementing Laravel's `Illuminate\Contracts\Database\Eloquent\CastsAttributes` interface) are currently reported as the cast class itself rather than the actual type returned by the `get` method. This produces incorrect type hints for IDE autocompletion — for example, a property cast through a custom caster that returns `array` is documented as `\App\Casts\MyCaster` instead of `array`.

    We need to update the model PHPDoc generation so that when a model property uses a custom cast class, the type hint reflects the return type of that caster's `get` method. The resolution should:
    - First use the native return type declaration of the `get` method if present.
    - Fall back to the `@return` docblock annotation on the `get` method when no native return type exists.
    - If neither is available, fall back to the existing behavior (the cast class type or `mixed` as appropriate).

    Note: there is a known limitation where docblock-based return types referencing class names may not be fully namespaced (e.g. `\CastedProperty` instead of the fully-qualified class). If possible, investigate how to provide the correct namespace context to the DocBlock parser; otherwise document this limitation in tests.

    Also add test coverage for the various scenarios: native return type, docblock return type, primitive return types (with and without nullability), and casting classes that declare no return type at all.

## Environment Setup
Check `composer.json` for dependency definitions and install scripts, and `phpunit.xml.dist` for PHPUnit configuration. Tests for the `ModelsCommand` live under `tests/Console/ModelsCommand/` — look at `tests/Console/ModelsCommand/AbstractModelsCommand.php` to understand how test environment (Laravel version) and migrations are set up. A migration for the new test fixture can be added to `tests/Console/ModelsCommand/migrations/`.

## Implementation Plan
- Add a helper method (e.g. `checkForCustomLaravelCasts`) in `src/Console/ModelsCommand.php` that, given a cast type string, checks whether the class exists and implements `CastsAttributes`.
    - When the interface is implemented, reflect on the `get` method and extract its return type — first from the native return type declaration, then from the `@return` docblock tag.
    - Wire this helper into the property type resolution path (around the existing `$this->properties[$name]['type'] = ...` assignment) so resolved types feed into the PHPDoc generation.
    - Create test fixtures under `tests/Console/ModelsCommand/LaravelCustomCasts/` covering: casters with native return types, docblock return types, primitive return types (both declared and via docblock), nullable primitives, and no return type. Include a model that uses all of these casters and a migration for the table.
    - Add a test class (e.g. `tests/Console/ModelsCommand/LaravelCustomCasts/Test.php`) that skips on Laravel < 7.0 and asserts the generated PHPDoc contains the expected types for each casted property.

pr_chain.title: Include model interfaces in generated IDE helper stubs
pr_chain.description:
When generating IDE helper stubs for Eloquent models, the current output only includes the class extending `\Eloquent` but loses any interfaces the original model explicitly implements. This causes static analysis tools like Psalm to lose type information about the model's contracts (e.g., `Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable`).

    The goal is to modify the stub generation so that when a model class explicitly implements interfaces (not inherited from its parent), those interfaces are preserved in the generated stub class declaration. The output should look like:

    ```php
    class User extends \Eloquent implements \Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable {}
    ```

    Additionally, add test coverage for this behavior with a model that implements a non-parent interface, verifying the generated stub output includes the interface declaration.

## Environment Setup
Check `composer.json` for dependencies and autoloading setup. Review `phpunit.xml.dist` for test configuration and bootstrap. Look at existing test patterns in `tests/Console/ModelsCommand/` (e.g., the `AbstractModelsCommand.php` base class and existing test directories like `Generator` or `Relations`) to understand how command tests are structured.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `src/Console/ModelsCommand.php`, inside the `createPhpDocs` method, use the `ReflectionClass` on the model to get its implemented interface names. Filter this list to exclude interfaces already implemented by parent classes (to avoid redundancy).
    2. Modify the output string construction in `createPhpDocs` to conditionally append `implements \Interface1, \Interface2` to the generated class declaration when interfaces exist.
    3. Create a new test fixture model under `tests/Console/ModelsCommand/Interfaces/Models/` that implements an interface not inherited from its parent (e.g., `Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable`).
    4. Create a new test class under `tests/Console/ModelsCommand/Interfaces/` that follows the existing test patterns (extending `AbstractModelsCommand`), configures the model location, runs the `ModelsCommand`, and asserts the generated stub content includes the interface declaration.
    5. Run the full test suite to ensure existing tests still pass and the new test passes.

Please update the model discovery logic to expand any wildcard patterns before scanning for classes, and make sure it still works gracefully when a location doesn't exist.

pr_chain.title: Update carousel control icon RTL processing for better tool compatibility
pr_chain.description:
The carousel control icons (`.carousel-control-prev-icon` and `.carousel-control-next-icon`) currently use an `rtl:options` block with `autoRename` and a `stringMap` to swap the background images when processed for RTL. This approach has two limitations:

    1. It prevents tools like `postcss-rtlcss` (a PostCSS plugin that generates both `[dir=rtl]` and `[dir=ltr]` prefixed selectors) from properly processing the files.
    2. The `rtl:options` block can affect CSS scoped outside the intended block boundary.

    The goal is to refactor the RTL handling for carousel control icons in `scss/_carousel.scss` by replacing the `rtl:options` approach with inline `rtl:{value}` comments on each background-image declaration. This will:
    - Enable `postcss-rtlcss` and similar tools to process the carousel icons correctly.
    - Prevent `rtl:options` from leaking into other CSS rules.
    - Maintain the same visual behavior in the rendered RTL output.

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` for available npm scripts and the project's main configuration. The `scss/_carousel.scss` file is the only source file that needs modification, but you should also review `build/postcss.config.mjs` for the PostCSS configuration used during builds.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `scss/_carousel.scss` and locate the carousel control icon section (around line 125-145).
    2. Remove the entire `/* rtl:options: { ... } */` comment block that currently sits above the `.carousel-control-prev-icon` rule.
    3. In the `.carousel-control-prev-icon` rule, modify the `background-image` property to append an inline RTL comment: `#{"/*rtl:" + escape-svg($carousel-control-next-icon-bg) + "*/"}` — this tells RTL processors to swap in the next icon's background for RTL output.
    4. In the `.carousel-control-next-icon` rule, apply the same pattern but reference the prev icon's background: `#{"/*rtl:" + escape-svg($carousel-control-prev-icon-bg) + "*/"}`.
    5. Ensure the existing `escape-svg()` function wrapping for the base value remains intact in both rules.
    6. Do not make changes to any other carousel rules or other files in the repo.

pr_chain.title: Clean up documentation URL handling and update Hugo serve options
pr_chain.description:
As part of our ongoing effort to improve the reliability and maintainability of the documentation site, we need to consolidate how URLs and paths are constructed in the Hugo templates. Currently, several templates use `printf` to build URLs, which can produce malformed paths in certain conditions (e.g., double slashes, missing trailing slashes). We also need to update the local Hugo server command to output more useful warnings during development.

    Please replace the now-deprecated `printf`-based URL construction with Hugo's `urls.JoinPath` function across all affected templates. This function safely joins path segments, normalizes separators, and ensures consistent output. Specifically, update the following files:

    - `site/layouts/_default/examples.html`: color-modes.js script path
    - `site/layouts/partials/docs-sidebar.html`: sidebar navigation hrefs
    - `site/layouts/partials/docs-versions.html`: version switcher links
    - `site/layouts/partials/header.html`: color-modes.js script path
    - `site/layouts/partials/social.html`: social sharing image path
    - `site/layouts/shortcodes/docsref.html`: simplify the reference logic by assigning the path to a variable before calling `relref`

    Additionally, update the `docs-serve` script in `package.json` to include `--noHTTPCache`, `--renderToMemory`, and `--printPathWarnings` flags, which will improve the local development experience by surfacing template and path warnings immediately.

    Leave the `home/plugins.html` partial as-is for now — a `TODO` comment is already in place for it since its links contain `#` fragments that `urls.JoinPath` would escape.

## Environment Setup
- `package.json` — contains the npm scripts for building the docs, serving them locally, and running tests. Look at the `scripts` section, particularly `docs-serve`, `docs-build`, `docs-vnu`, and `lint`.
    - `hugo.yml` — Hugo site configuration; relevant for understanding how the docs site is structured and how URLs are used.
    - `js/tests/README.md` and `js/tests/karma.conf.js` — describe how JavaScript tests are configured (though this change is docs-only, it's good to be aware of the testing setup).
    - `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` — provides general contribution guidelines and likely mentions how to set up the project.
    - `.github/workflows/docs.yml` — shows how the docs are built and linted in CI.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `site/layouts/_default/examples.html`, replace the `printf` used to build the color-modes.js path with `urls.JoinPath "/docs" $.Site.Params.docs_version "assets/js/color-modes.js"`.
    2. In `site/layouts/partials/header.html`, make the same replacement for the color-modes.js script path.
    3. In `site/layouts/partials/docs-sidebar.html`, replace the `printf` used to build sidebar hrefs with `urls.JoinPath "/docs" $.Site.Params.docs_version $group_slug $doc_slug "/"`.
    4. In `site/layouts/partials/docs-versions.html`, replace the two `printf` calls with `urls.JoinPath`. Be careful to include the trailing slash as shown in the existing code (i.e., `urls.JoinPath $group_slug $page_slug "/"` and `urls.JoinPath $page_slug "/"`).
    5. In `site/layouts/partials/social.html`, replace `printf` paths and the `path.Join` calls with `urls.JoinPath`. Pay attention to the `img` segment — the original used `"img/"` with a trailing slash; `urls.JoinPath` handles separators, so use `"img"` without the slash.
    6. In `site/layouts/shortcodes/docsref.html`, assign `path.Join "docs" $.Site.Params.docs_version (.Get 0)` to a variable (`$pageToReference`), then call `relref . $pageToReference | relURL`. This makes the logic clearer and avoids the double `relURL` call.
    7. In `site/layouts/partials/home/plugins.html`, add a `TODO` comment (if not already present) noting that `urls.JoinPath` should be used here in the future, but the `#` in links prevents it for now.
    8. In `package.json`, update the `docs-serve` script to:
       `"docs-serve": "hugo server --port 9001 --disableFastRender --noHTTPCache --renderToMemory --printPathWarnings --printUnusedTemplates"`

pr_chain.title: Fix version picker comparisons in docs-versions.html
pr_chain.description:
In the Bootstrap documentation site, the version picker dropdown (located in `site/layouts/partials/docs-versions.html`) has a bug where it incorrectly shows links to older versions of the docs for pages that were added in newer versions. This causes 404 errors when users click those links.

    The issue is that the code compares page front matter parameters (like `.Page.Params.added`) directly using the `eq` function. When the front matter stores versions as numbers (e.g., `5.3` instead of `"5.3"`), the comparison fails because it's comparing a number with a string, resulting in false matches.

    Your task is to fix the version comparisons in this partial template so that all version values are explicitly cast to strings before comparison, and refactor the repeated checks into local variables for better readability and maintainability.

    The expected behavior:
    - For a page added in v5.3: the dropdown should show "v5.2.3", "v5.1.3", and "v5.0.2" as disabled items
    - For a page added in v5.2: the dropdown should show "v5.2.3" as a link, but "v5.1.3" and "v5.0.2" as disabled
    - For a page added in v5.1: the dropdown should show "v5.2.3" and "v5.1.3" as links, but "v5.0.2" as disabled
    - For pages not added in any of these versions (or without an `added` parameter), all older versions should be links

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` and `hugo.yml` in the repository root for build and development commands. Look for any existing documentation on how to run the site locally (possibly in `README.md` or `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`). The relevant file to modify is `site/layouts/partials/docs-versions.html`. The `dist` directory contains compiled output, but you should not need to modify it for this task.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `site/layouts/partials/docs-versions.html`.
    2. After the existing `$versions_link` logic, add three new variables:
       - `$added_in_51` which evaluates to `eq (string .Page.Params.added) "5.1"`
       - `$added_in_52` which evaluates to `eq (string .Page.Params.added) "5.2"`
       - `$added_in_53` which evaluates to `eq (string .Page.Params.added) "5.3"`
    3. Replace the three version comparison blocks in the dropdown list to use these new variables instead of the inline `eq` calls with `.Page.Params.added`.
    4. Specifically:
       - For the v5.2.3 item, use `$added_in_53` as the condition for showing the disabled item.
       - For the v5.1.3 item, use `(or $added_in_52 $added_in_53)` as the condition for showing the disabled item.
       - For the v5.0.2 item, use `(or $added_in_51 $added_in_52 $added_in_53)` as the condition for showing the disabled item.
    5. Verify the logic by reviewing the template or running the local docs build to check the rendered dropdown for various pages with different `added` values (including string and number forms in front matter).

pr_chain.title: Fix AArch64 timer overflow and wall-clock time calculation
pr_chain.description:
We need to address two related issues on AArch64:

    1. **Timer tick overflow**: The `get_timer_ticks()` function in `src/arch/aarch64/kernel/processor.rs` computes `(1000000 * get_timestamp()) / u64::from(CPU_FREQUENCY.get())`. On AArch64, `get_timestamp()` returns the raw counter value from `cntpct_el0`, which can be very large (64-bit). When multiplied by 1,000,000, this can overflow a `u64`, causing incorrect timer values and potentially breaking time-based functionality.

    2. **Incorrect wall-clock time**: The current system combines boot time and timer ticks in several places across the codebase (e.g., `src/syscalls/timer.rs`, `src/fs/mem.rs`, `src/executor/network.rs`, `src/executor/device.rs`, `src/time.rs`). On AArch64, the PL031 RTC provides wall-clock time at boot. However, the RTC value is set as the "boot time" without subtracting the current timer ticks, so `get_boot_time() + get_timer_ticks()` doesn't accurately represent the current time since boot.

    The goal is to:
    - Make time calculations overflow-safe on AArch64
    - Ensure wall-clock time (`CLOCK_REALTIME`, `gettimeofday`, file timestamps) is accurate
    - Clean up the scattered time calculations into a unified `now_micros()` API in each architecture's `systemtime` module

    Please implement a solution that:
    1. Fixes the overflow in AArch64's `get_timer_ticks()` and related deadline calculations
    2. Provides a unified `now_micros()` function in each architecture's systemtime module that returns the current time in microseconds since UNIX epoch
    3. Removes the separate `get_boot_time()` export from the architecture abstraction in `src/arch/mod.rs`
    4. Updates all call sites to use the new `now_micros()` function instead of manually adding `get_boot_time()` and `get_timer_ticks()`

## Environment Setup
Check the following files for build/test instructions:
    - `Cargo.toml` - workspace configuration and dependencies
    - `rust-toolchain.toml` - required Rust toolchain
    - `.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo configuration
    - `Makefile` (if present) - build automation
    - `xtask/` directory - contains custom build and CI tooling (check `xtask/src/ci/mod.rs` for test integration)

## Implementation Plan
1. **Fix AArch64 timer overflow**:
       - In `src/arch/aarch64/kernel/processor.rs`:
         - Update `get_timer_ticks()` to perform the multiplication in `u128` before converting back to `u64` with a `try_from` and unwrap
         - Update `__set_oneshot_timer()` to use `u128` arithmetic for the deadline calculation, similarly converting back with `try_from`
       - This prevents overflow when `get_timestamp()` returns large values

    2. **Refactor architecture time API**:
       - In `src/arch/aarch64/kernel/systemtime.rs`:
         - Remove `get_boot_time()` function
         - Add a `now_micros()` function that returns `*BOOT_TIME.get().unwrap() + super::processor::get_timer_ticks()`
         - In `init()`, when setting `BOOT_TIME`, subtract the current timer ticks: `BOOT_TIME.set(micros - current_ticks)` where `current_ticks = super::processor::get_timer_ticks()`
       - In `src/arch/x86_64/kernel/systemtime.rs`:
         - Remove `get_boot_time()` function
         - Add a `now_micros()` function that returns `*BOOT_TIME.get().unwrap() + super::processor::get_timer_ticks()`
       - In `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/systemtime.rs`:
         - Replace `get_boot_time()` (which currently returns a stub value) with a `now_micros()` that returns `super::processor::get_timer_ticks()` (since RISC-V doesn't have wall-clock support currently)

    3. **Update architecture abstraction**:
       - In `src/arch/mod.rs`, remove the `pub use ... get_boot_time` re-exports for all three architectures. The `systemtime` module is already re-exported via the architecture module (e.g., `pub use self::aarch64::*`), so `arch::kernel::systemtime::now_micros()` should be accessible.

    4. **Update all call sites**:
       - In `src/executor/device.rs`: Replace `arch::get_boot_time() + arch::processor::get_timer_ticks()` with `arch::kernel::systemtime::now_micros()` in the two `create()` methods (for both DHCP and non-DHCP cases)
       - In `src/executor/network.rs`: Replace the `now()` function's calculation with `arch::kernel::systemtime::now_micros()`
       - In `src/fs/mem.rs`: Replace all `arch::processor::get_timer_ticks() + arch::get_boot_time()` with `arch::kernel::systemtime::now_micros()`
       - In `src/syscalls/timer.rs`:
         - For `CLOCK_REALTIME` in `__sys_clock_gettime`: use `arch::kernel::systemtime::now_micros()`
         - The `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` case should only use `arch::processor::get_timer_ticks()`
         - In `__sys_clock_nanosleep`: Handle absolute time correctly by subtracting `now_micros()` for realtime or `get_timer_ticks()` for monotonic
         - In `__sys_gettimeofday`: Use `arch::kernel::systemtime::now_micros()`
       - In `src/time.rs`: Replace `arch::processor::get_timer_ticks() + arch::get_boot_time()` with `arch::kernel::systemtime::now_micros()` in `SystemTime::now()`

    5. **Verify consistent behavior across architectures**: Ensure the x86_64 and riscv64 implementations compile correctly with their respective `get_timer_ticks()` implementations.

pr_chain.title: Refactor FUSE module to improve type safety and reduce unsafe code
pr_chain.description:
The FUSE implementation in this kernel has several maintainability issues that we need to address:

    1. **Unsafe allocation pattern**: The code relies on `alloc` with manual `Layout` calculations and unsafe `assume_init()` calls on potentially uninitialized memory. This is unsound as written since `new_uninit().assume_init()` on a struct containing regular (non-`MaybeUninit`) fields is immediate undefined behavior. We need a safer approach that only uses `MaybeUninit` where appropriate and removes dependence on unstable features like `ptr_metadata` and `maybe_uninit_write_slice`.

    2. **Poor type safety**: The `send_command` interface uses generic `FuseIn`/`FuseOut` marker traits with separate `S` and `T` type parameters, which do not clearly express the relationship between a FUSE operation's input and output structures. The code should use a single associated type that ties each operation to its corresponding request/response pair.

    3. **Code duplication**: Each operation (init, lookup, open, read, write, etc.) has its own manual command creation and response parsing logic, much of which is common between operations. The per-operation boilerplate should be deduplicated and only the variable parts specified.

    4. **Naming and organization**: ABI struct definitions are scattered throughout `src/fs/fuse.rs`. These should be moved to a dedicated module (`src/fs/fuse_abi.rs`) with clear, conventional Rust naming (e.g., `InHeader` instead of `fuse_in_header`).

    The goal is to make the module safer, easier to read, and set up for future optimization where we can access the response layout without creating a skeleton `Rsp` object (though that will require separate virtqueue API changes, out of scope here).

## Environment Setup
- Check `Cargo.toml` for crate configuration, feature flags (`fuse`, `pci`), and dependencies. The FUSE code is conditionally compiled under `#[cfg(all(feature = "fuse", feature = "pci"))]`.
    - Refer to `rust-toolchain.toml` for the Rust toolchain version pinned for this repository.
    - The CI workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the `xtask` directory (`xtask/src/ci/`) contain the build and test process used by the project. `rustfmt.toml` controls formatting conventions.

## Implementation Plan
1. Create a new module `src/fs/fuse_abi.rs` and move all ABI struct definitions (`fuse_in_header`, `fuse_out_header`, `fuse_init_in`, `fuse_init_out`, etc.) and associated constants (e.g., `FUSE_ROOT_ID`, `FUSE_GETATTR_FH`) into it. Rename to conventional Rust `CamelCase` names (e.g., `InHeader`, `OutHeader`, `InitIn`, `InitOut`, `ROOT_ID`, `GETATTR_FH`).
    2. Register the new module in `src/fs/mod.rs` (behind the same `#[cfg(all(feature = "fuse", feature = "pci"))]` gate).
    3. Refactor the operation typing in `src/fs/fuse.rs`:
       - Replace `FuseIn`/`FuseOut` marker traits and the two-generic `send_command<S, T>` with a single operation trait `Op` that has associated types for the command and response payloads and a constant for the opcode.
       - Define each operation as a distinct zero-sized type (e.g., `struct Init;`, `struct Lookup;`, `struct Open;`) implementing this trait, instead of using a const-generic `Op<CODE>` pattern.
       - Update `Cmd` and `Rsp` to be parameterized by this operation type, replacing their `FuseIn`/`FuseOut` bounds with the new `Op` trait. Use `MaybeUninit` only for fields that are actually uninitialized.
    4. Simplify command creation:
       - Create generic helper functions for common command-building logic (e.g., filling the `InHeader`).
       - For each operation, implement an associated function on its type to build the command from its specific arguments. Remove the standalone `create_*` functions.
    5. Simplify response handling:
       - Return `Rsp` objects where the response fields are properly typed, with `MaybeUninit` only where needed.
       - Replace all `new_uninit().assume_init()` usages with safe initialization (either filling `MaybeUninit` fields with `MaybeUninit::uninit()` or using `Box::new_zeroed()` where appropriate).
       - Remove dependency on unstable `ptr_metadata` and `maybe_uninit_write_slice` features.
    6. Update `send_command` in `src/drivers/fs/virtio_fs.rs` to use the new `Op`-bound signature and pass `None` for the response buffer to avoid unnecessary copying since the response memory does not need to be pre-initialized (the device writes into it).
    7. Remove now-unnecessary marker traits and any dead code after the refactor.

pr_chain.title: Forward error code to host on shutdown across architectures
pr_chain.description:
Currently, when the unikernel shuts down, the error code from the `shutdown` syscall is not forwarded to the host system in most cases. The `shutdown` method in the `SyscallInterface` trait accepts an `i32` argument but the architecture-specific `shutdown` functions ignore it, always exiting with success status. You need to modify the system shutdown path so that the error code is propagated to the host via semihosting (on aarch64/riscv64) or QEMU's debug exit mechanism (on x86_64), allowing CI and external tools to detect failures.

    Additionally, improve the `virtual_to_physical` function in the x86_64 paging module to provide better error messages when translation fails, and ensure the CI QEMU runner allocates sufficient memory (at least 64 MB) for all architectures.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's `Cargo.toml` for workspace configuration and dependencies, `rust-toolchain.toml` for the required Rust version, and `xtask/Cargo.toml` for build tooling. Look at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to understand how CI is structured, and `xtask/src/main.rs` for available commands. The `xtask` crate contains the QEMU CI runner code.

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify `src/syscalls/interfaces/mod.rs`:
       - Update the `shutdown` method in the `SyscallInterface` trait to pass the `error_code` parameter to the architecture-specific `shutdown` function: `arch::processor::shutdown(error_code)`.

    2. Modify the architecture-specific `shutdown` functions:
       - In `src/arch/aarch64/kernel/processor.rs` and `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/processor.rs`:
         - Change the signature of `shutdown` to accept an `error_code: i32` parameter.
         - Add `#[allow(unused_variables)]` attribute above the function (since the parameter is unused in non-semihosting configurations).
         - Inside the `semihosting` feature branch, replace `semihosting::process::exit(0)` with `semihosting::process::exit(error_code)`.
       - In `src/arch/x86_64/kernel/processor.rs`:
         - Change the signature of `shutdown` to accept an `error_code: i32` parameter.
         - In the `PlatformInfo::Multiboot` branch, check `if error_code == 0`, call `exit_handler.exit_success()`, otherwise call `exit_handler.exit_failure()`.

    3. Update `src/syscalls/interfaces/uhyve.rs`:
       - The `shutdown` method in the `Uhyve` implementation already passes its `arg` parameter to `SysExit::new`. Since the trait signature remains compatible (`fn shutdown(&self, error_code: i32) -> !`), simply rename the parameter from `arg` to `error_code` for clarity.

    4. Improve `virtual_to_physical` in `src/arch/x86_64/mm/paging.rs`:
       - Replace the call to `translate_addr` with the `translate` method that returns a `TranslateResult`.
       - Import `TranslateResult` from `x86_64::structures::paging::mapper`.
       - Match on the `TranslateResult`:
         - For `NotMapped` or `InvalidFrameAddress`, log a warning message (using the existing `warn!` macro) and return `None`.
         - For `Mapped { frame, offset, .. }`, compute the physical address as `frame.start_address() + offset` and return it wrapped in `Some`.

    5. Update `xtask/src/ci/qemu.rs`:
       - In the `memory()` method, add `memory = memory.max(64);` after the existing logic (before the `memory` variable is returned) to enforce a minimum of 64 MB for all architectures.

pr_chain.title: Implement eventfd syscall and improve poll Unix compatibility
pr_chain.description:
Implement a Linux-like `eventfd` system call in this HermitOS kernel. The `eventfd` object contains an unsigned 64-bit counter that can be used as an event wait/notify mechanism. The syscall signature is `sys_eventfd(initval: u64, flags: i16) -> i32`, returning a new file descriptor referencing the eventfd object.

Key behaviors:
- `EFD_NONBLOCK` flag sets the descriptor in non-blocking mode
- `EFD_SEMAPHORE` flag provides semaphore-like read semantics (reads return 1 and decrement counter; otherwise reads return the full counter value and reset it to 0)
- Reads block when counter is 0; writes block when counter would overflow (at `u64::MAX`)
- The descriptor must support poll (readable when counter > 0, writable when counter < u64::MAX)

Additionally, improve Unix compatibility of the existing `poll` syscall:
- Make `poll` return the number of ready file descriptors
- Handle timeout properly (return 0 on timeout instead of error)
- Update `poll_fds` to reset `revents` field before polling

Also add a `sys_fcntl` syscall with support for `F_SETFD` (with `FD_CLOEXEC` argument, return 0) and `F_SETFL` (with `O_NONBLOCK` argument, set non-blocking mode via ioctl).

Refactor socket type handling in `sys_socket` to use a bitflag type, allowing flags like `SOCK_NONBLOCK` and `SOCK_CLOEXEC` to be combined with base types. When `SOCK_NONBLOCK` is set, immediately configure the socket as non-blocking.

Improve TCP and UDP socket poll behavior:
- For TCP sockets in `Listen` state, register wakers and return `Pending` instead of `POLLNVAL`
- For TCP sockets, handle `Established` state properly in accept logic
- Ensure all poll event checks use independent `if` statements rather than `else if` chains
- TCP sockets in closed/closing states should return appropriate events (POLLOUT/POLLIN/etc or POLLHUP) instead of POLLNVAL

Also install a serial interrupt handler for COM1 on x86_64 to echo received non-control characters.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repo files for build/test configuration:
- `Cargo.toml` - workspace dependencies and features
- `rust-toolchain.toml` - Rust toolchain specification
- `xtask/Cargo.toml` and `src/xtask/` - build and CI tooling
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - CI workflow showing build/test commands
- `tests/` directory - integration test infrastructure (including `tests/hermit_test_runner.py` and `tests/common/mod.rs`)

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create eventfd module** (`src/fd/eventfd.rs`):
     - Define `EventState` struct with counter, read_queue, and write_queue fields
     - Define `EventFd` struct with async mutex state and flags
     - Implement `new(initval: u64, flags: EventFlags)` constructor
     - Implement `ObjectInterface` trait with async_read/async_write/poll methods:
       - Read: if counter > 0, return counter value (or 1 with EFD_SEMAPHORE) and reset/decrement; otherwise register read waker and return Pending
       - Write: if counter won't overflow, increment counter and wake readers; otherwise register write waker and return Pending
       - Poll: return POLLIN if counter > 0, POLLOUT if counter < u64::MAX
     - Implement `Clone` that copies counter state

  2. **Add EventFlags bitflags** (`src/fd/mod.rs`):
     - Define `EventFlags` with EFD_SEMAPHORE (0o1), EFD_NONBLOCK (0o4000), EFD_CLOEXEC (0o40000)
     - Remove `EMPTY` constant from `PollEvent`, use `PollEvent::empty()` instead
     - Add `mod eventfd;` declaration
     - Add public `eventfd(initval: u64, flags: EventFlags) -> Result<FileDescriptor, IoError>` function

  3. **Update poll_fds function** (`src/fd/mod.rs`):
     - Change return type from `Result<(), IoError>` to `Result<u64, IoError>`
     - Use counter instead of boolean `ready` flag
     - Reset `i.revents = PollEvent::empty()` before polling
     - Only increment counter if returned event is non-empty
     - Return counter when any descriptors are ready

  4. **Update poll public function** (`src/fd/mod.rs`):
     - Change signature to `poll(fds: &mut [PollFd], timeout: Option<Duration>) -> Result<u64, IoError>`
     - Use `block_on(poll_fds(fds), timeout)` directly

  5. **Update sys_poll** (`src/syscalls/mod.rs`):
     - Convert timeout to `Option<Duration>` (None for negative timeout)
     - Return count of ready descriptors
     - On ETIME, return 0 instead of error

  6. **Add sys_eventfd and sys_fcntl** (`src/syscalls/mod.rs`):
     - Add `extern "C" fn __sys_eventfd(initval: u64, flags: i16) -> i32` that validates flags, calls `crate::fd::eventfd()`
     - Add `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn sys_eventfd` wrapper using `kernel_function!`
     - Add `extern "C" fn __sys_fcntl(fd: i32, cmd: i32, arg: i32) -> i32` supporting F_SETFD/FD_CLOEXEC and F_SETFL/O_NONBLOCK
     - Add `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn sys_fcntl` wrapper

  7. **Update poll implementations** in `src/fd/stdio.rs`, `src/fs/mem.rs`:
     - Replace `PollEvent::EMPTY` with `PollEvent::empty()`
     - Change `else if` chains to independent `if` statements

  8. **Update TCP socket** (`src/fd/socket/tcp.rs`):
     - Add `listen: AtomicBool` field to Socket struct
     - In `async_accept`, handle `Established` state as ready
     - Rewrite poll to:
       - Handle Closed/Closing/CloseWait with appropriate POLLOUT/POLLIN events or POLLHUP
       - Return POLLHUP for FinWait1/FinWait2/TimeWait
       - For Listen state, register wakers and return Pending
       - For other states, check can_send/can_recv independently
     - When fresh connection established in non-blocking mode (listen flag set), report POLLIN events

  9. **Update UDP socket** (`src/fd/socket/udp.rs`):
     - Replace EMPTY with empty()
     - Change else-if chains to independent ifs
     - Register both recv and send wakers when pending

  10. **Install serial interrupt** (`src/arch/x86_64/kernel/mod.rs`, `src/arch/x86_64/kernel/serial.rs`):
      - Add `receive()` method to SerialPort for UART variant
      - Add `serial_interrupt` handler (x86-interrupt fn) reading from COM1, printing non-control chars, calling `apic::eoi()`
      - Add `install_serial_interrupt()` setting up IDT entry at IRQ 36
      - Call from `boot_processor_init()`

  11. **Add SockType bitflags** (`src/syscalls/net.rs`):
      - Define `SockType` with SOCK_DGRAM, SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_NONBLOCK, SOCK_CLOEXEC
      - Update `__sys_socket` to take `SockType` instead of raw i32
      - Validate with `type_.intersects(SockType::SOCK_STREAM | SockType::SOCK_DGRAM)`
      - Set non-blocking via `socket.ioctl(IoCtl::NonBlocking, true)` when SOCK_NONBLOCK set
      - Update imports

  12. **Misc cleanup**:
      - Move FIONBIO constant inside `__sys_ioctl` function
      - Change `expect("FD is already used")` to `unwrap()` in accept path

pr_chain.title: Simplify PollEvent flag propagation across file descriptor implementations
pr_chain.description:
We need to refactor the `poll` method implementations across several file descriptor types to eliminate repetitive, verbose flag-propagation logic. Currently, each implementation individually checks `event.contains()` for each poll flag (POLLIN, POLLOUT, POLLRDNORM, etc.) and conditionally inserts them into a result set. This approach is verbose, error-prone, and obscures the actual logic of which events are available.

    The goal is to replace this pattern with a cleaner approach: compute an "available" set of poll events based on the state of the file descriptor, then intersect it with the requested `event` set using bitwise operations on the `PollEvent` bitflags type. This makes the code more concise, easier to review, and reduces the risk of missing a flag in one branch.

    This change should be applied to the `poll` implementations in:
    - `src/fd/eventfd.rs` (EventFd)
    - `src/fd/socket/tcp.rs` (TCP Socket)
    - `src/fd/socket/udp.rs` (UDP Socket)
    - `src/fd/stdio.rs` (GenericStdout, GenericStderr, UhyveStdout, UhyveStderr)
    - `src/fs/mem.rs` (RomFileInterface, RamFileInterface)

    For each implementation, identify which events are "available" based on the current state (e.g., `can_send()`, `can_recv()`, `pos < len`, `counter > 0`), build a single `PollEvent` value representing those available events, and then return the intersection of that with the `event` parameter. Keep the existing semantics for special cases like returning `POLLHUP` or `POLLNVAL` when no events are available.

    Please also rename the local variable from `result` to something more descriptive like `ret` or `available` where appropriate, to improve readability.

## Environment Setup
The repository is a Rust workspace. Check `Cargo.toml` at the root for workspace configuration and member dependencies. The `rust-toolchain.toml` file specifies the required Rust toolchain. For CI-specific build and test infrastructure, examine `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the `xtask` directory (particularly `xtask/src/ci/mod.rs` and related files) which orchestrate builds and testing.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Familiarize with the `PollEvent` type**: Look at `src/fd/mod.rs` to understand the `PollEvent` bitflags definition, particularly the flag constants (POLLIN, POLLOUT, POLLRDNORM, etc.) and available methods like `contains()`, `intersection()`, `insert()`, and the bitwise `&` operator.

    2. **Refactor `src/fd/eventfd.rs`**:
       - In `EventFd::poll`, replace the series of `if event.contains()` checks with a single `available` `PollEvent` that accumulates POLLOUT/POLLWRNORM/POLLWRBAND (if `counter < u64::MAX - 1`) and POLLIN/POLLRDNORM/POLLRDBAND (if `counter > 0`).
       - Compute `let ret = event & available;` after dropping the guard.
       - Use `ret` instead of `result` throughout the rest of the method.

    3. **Refactor `src/fd/socket/tcp.rs`**:
       - In `Socket::poll`, for each state branch, build an `available` set and use `let ret = event & available;`.
       - For the `Closed | Closing | CloseWait` state, the available set includes POLLOUT/POLLWRNORM/POLLWRBAND and POLLIN/POLLRDNORM/POLLRDBAND. Return `POLLHUP` if `ret` is empty.
       - For the general state branch, build `available` from `can_send()` (write flags) and `can_recv()` or the fresh-connection check (read flags). Compute `ret` and use it for the empty check and final return.

    4. **Refactor `src/fd/socket/udp.rs`**:
       - In `Socket::poll`, replace the if/else logic with a conditional expression: if `socket.is_open()` is true, build `avail` from `can_send()` and `can_recv()` and use `event & avail`; otherwise use `PollEvent::POLLNVAL`.
       - Assign to `ret` and use it for the empty check and return.

    5. **Refactor `src/fd/stdio.rs`**:
       - For each of `GenericStdout`, `GenericStderr`, `UhyveStdout`, `UhyveStderr`, replace the three `if` checks with a single `let available = PollEvent::POLLOUT | PollEvent::POLLWRNORM | PollEvent::POLLWRBAND;` and return `Ok(event & available)`.

    6. **Refactor `src/fs/mem.rs`**:
       - For `RomFileInterface::poll` and `RamFileInterface::poll`, compute an `available` set. For ROM files, only read flags (POLLIN/POLLRDNORM/POLLRDBAND) when `pos < len`. For RAM files, additionally always include write flags (POLLOUT/POLLWRNORM/POLLWRBAND).
       - Use `let ret = event & available;` and return `Ok(ret)`.

    7. **Review for consistency**: Ensure all renamed variables (`result` → `ret` or `available`) are updated in the file. Verify the logic is equivalent to the original (especially for the TCP case where `may_recv()` and `listen` swap logic is combined).

    8. **Run `cargo fmt`**: Ensure the code is formatted per `rustfmt.toml`.

    9. **Run clippy**: Verify no new warnings are introduced by checking `.github/workflows/ci.yml` or `xtask/src/clippy.rs` for how clippy is configured and run.

pr_chain.title: Refactor eventfd to use the `ready!` macro for cleaner polling logic
pr_chain.description:
In `src/fd/eventfd.rs`, the `async_read`, `async_write`, and `poll` methods use explicit `if let Poll::Ready(mut guard) = pinned.as_mut().poll(cx) { ... } else { Poll::Pending }` patterns inside `future::poll_fn` closures. This repetitive nesting makes the code harder to read and maintain.

    Refactor these methods to use the `ready!` macro (imported from `core::task`) to extract the `Poll::Ready` case. The `ready!` macro returns early with `Poll::Pending` if the poll result is not ready, allowing you to flatten the logic and reduce nesting levels. This should preserve all existing behavior exactly — no functional changes, just a readability improvement.

    Focus on:
    - `async_read`: Handle both semaphore and non-semaphore paths.
    - `async_write`: Simplify the counter-add and queue-wake logic.
    - `poll`: Flatten the waiter-registration branch.

    Ensure all existing tests and behavior remain intact.

## Environment Setup
Check `Cargo.toml` (and `Cargo.lock`) for project dependencies and workspace structure. Look at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to see how the project is built and tested. The `rust-toolchain.toml` may pin a specific Rust version. Review `xtask/` for build/test orchestration if needed.

## Implementation Plan
- Import `ready` from `core::task` alongside the existing `Poll` and `Waker` imports.
    - In `async_read`, replace the nested `if let Poll::Ready(...)` with `let mut guard = ready!(pinned.as_mut().poll(cx));` and adjust the indentation of the ready-path logic accordingly.
    - In `async_write`, apply the same `ready!` extraction to flatten the guard acquisition, then simplify the counter-check and queue-wake logic.
    - In `poll`, similarly use `ready!` to extract the guard when registering a waiter, and flatten the event-queue selection logic.
    - Compile and run the affected tests to ensure behavior is unchanged.

pr_chain.title: Add per-thread error number storage and retrieval in kernel
pr_chain.description:
Implement thread-local storage (TLS) for error numbers in the Hermit kernel. Currently, the kernel does not maintain a per-thread error number, which is needed for proper errno handling in system calls. The goal is to:

    1. Add a thread-local static variable to store the error number (errno).
    2. Provide a function to retrieve the current thread's errno value.
    3. Introduce a mechanism to automatically set the errno based on return values from kernel functions.
    4. Integrate this errno handling into the `kernel_function!` macro so that return values from kernel functions are checked and errno is updated accordingly.

    The errno storage should be per-thread (using Rust's `#[thread_local]` attribute) so that concurrent threads have independent errno values. The implementation must work on supported architectures (x86_64, aarch64) while gracefully handling unsupported configurations (riscv64 and `common-os` feature).

## Environment Setup
Check the following files in the repository root for build and test configuration:
    - `Cargo.toml` - Main crate configuration, dependencies, and feature flags
    - `rust-toolchain.toml` - Rust toolchain version specification
    - `rustfmt.toml` - Code formatting configuration
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - Continuous integration setup showing build/test commands
    - `xtask/Cargo.toml` - Build tooling configuration
    - `tests/hermit_test_runner.py` - Test runner script for integration tests
    
    The project uses Rust with nightly features (see attribute declarations in `src/lib.rs`). Dependencies are managed via Cargo.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Extend `src/errno.rs`**:
       - Add a `#[thread_local]` static variable `ERRNO` of type `core::cell::UnsafeCell<i32>` initialized to 0. This should be `pub(crate)` and gated behind `#[cfg(all(not(feature = "common-os"), not(target_arch = "riscv64")))]`.
       - Add a public `#[no_mangle]` function `sys_get_errno() -> i32` that returns the current thread's errno. For unsupported configurations (riscv64 or `common-os`), return 0.
       - Define a `pub(crate)` trait `ToErrno` with:
         - A default method `to_errno(&self) -> Option<i32>` returning `None`.
         - A method `set_errno(self) -> Self` that checks `to_errno()` and writes the errno value to `ERRNO` (or ignores it for unsupported configurations).
       - Implement `ToErrno` for:
         - `i32`: returns `-self` if `self < 0`, else 0.
         - `i64` and `isize`: returns `i32::try_from(-self).unwrap()` if `self < 0`, else 0.
         - `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `usize`, `*mut u8`, `()`, and `!`: use the default `to_errno()` (returns `None`).

    2. **Update `src/lib.rs`**:
       - Add `#![feature(never_type)]` and `#![feature(thread_local)]` to the feature attribute list.

    3. **Modify `src/macros.rs`**:
       - Update the `kernel_function!` macro (both variants) to:
         - Import `ToErrno` trait using `use $crate::errno::ToErrno;`.
         - Calls `.set_errno()` on the return value of the kernel function.
         - For arity-0 and arity-1 cases, wrap in a block `{{ ... }}` and add `#[allow(unreachable_code)]` to handle the possibly divergent `!` return type.
         - For arity-2 through arity-6 cases, wrap in `{{ ... }}` and call `.set_errno()` on the result.
       - The second macro variant (for riscv64, newlib, and `common-os`) should also apply `.set_errno()` on the direct function call result.

    4. **Verify feature gating**: Ensure all errno logic is properly gated to handle:
       - `common-os` feature: errno is not stored (returns 0).
       - `riscv64` architecture: errno is not stored (returns 0).
       - Other configurations (x86_64, aarch64 without `common-os`): errno is stored in TLS.

pr_chain.title: Remove unused close method and simplify fd cleanup
pr_chain.description:
The `ObjectInterface` trait in `src/fd/mod.rs` defines a `close` method with an empty default implementation. This method is never called in a meaningful way—it's only invoked via the `fd::close` helper function and in the `__sys_close` syscall handler, where it does nothing beyond what `remove_object` already accomplishes.

Additionally, the `fd::close` wrapper function is only used in one place: the `Drop` implementation for `File` in `src/fs/mod.rs`, where it simply removes the object from the descriptor table.

Your task is to:
1. Remove the unused `close` method from the `ObjectInterface` trait.
2. Remove the `fd::close` wrapper function entirely.
3. Update all callers to use `remove_object` directly, which already handles descriptor removal and cleanup.

The goal is to eliminate dead code and simplify the file descriptor close path without changing any runtime behavior—`remove_object` already removes the descriptor from the table, and the `close` method's empty implementation provides no additional cleanup.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's `Cargo.toml` and `xtask/Cargo.toml` for project setup and build configuration. The `.github/workflows/ci.yml` file contains CI pipeline details including build and test steps. Tests are located in the `tests/` directory with supporting code in `tests/common/mod.rs`. The `Cargo.toml` and `rust-toolchain.toml` specify the Rust toolchain and dependencies needed for building and testing.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `src/fd/mod.rs`, remove the `close` method definition from the `ObjectInterface` trait declaration (the line with the comment "close a file descriptor").
    2. In the same file, remove the entire `pub(crate) fn close(fd: FileDescriptor)` function, as it becomes unused.
    3. In `src/fs/mod.rs`, update the `Drop` implementation for `File` to call `remove_object` directly instead of `fd::close`. Import `remove_object` alongside the existing `insert_object` import from `crate::fd`.
    4. In `src/syscalls/mod.rs`, simplify the `__sys_close` function: after `remove_object(fd)`, map the result to return 0 on success instead of calling the now-removed `close` method.
    5. Verify the changes compile by running the project's build system or CI checks.

pr_chain.title: Replace deprecated SBI legacy extensions with SBI 2.0 equivalents on riscv64
pr_chain.description:
The RISC-V SBI legacy extensions (console_putchar, shutdown, set_timer, send_ipi) have been deprecated. Replace them with their SBI 2.0 counterparts on the riscv64 architecture. This migration also fixes a bug where IPI cannot be sent to hart IDs greater than 63, as the current code uses `1 << hart_id` which overflows for hart_id >= 64. The SBI 2.0 IPI extension introduces a `hart_mask_base` parameter to support arbitrary hart IDs.

    Specifically:
    - Replace `sbi::legacy::console_putchar` with `sbi_rt::console_write_byte` in `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/mod.rs`
    - Replace `sbi::legacy::shutdown()` with `sbi_rt::system_reset(sbi_rt::Shutdown, sbi_rt::NoReason)` in `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/processor.rs`
    - Replace `sbi::legacy::set_timer` with `sbi_rt::set_timer` in `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/processor.rs`
    - Replace `sbi::legacy::send_ipi(&[1 << hart_id])` with `sbi_rt::send_ipi(sbi_rt::HartMask::from_mask_base(0b1, hart_id))` in `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/processor.rs`
    - Replace `sbi::hart_state_management::hart_start` with `sbi_rt::hart_start` in `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/mod.rs`
    - Update the Cargo.toml dependency from `sbi = "0.2"` to `sbi-rt = "0.0.3"` for riscv64 target, and update Cargo.lock accordingly
    - Ensure the system still shuts down gracefully after the SRST call; since `system_reset` may return (unlike legacy shutdown which never returns), add a `loop { core::hint::spin_loop(); }` after the call to prevent continuation of execution

    The migration should be complete and consistent—all legacy SBI calls on riscv64 should be replaced.

## Environment Setup
Check `Cargo.toml` for the riscv64 target-specific dependencies section and the workspace configuration. The `Cargo.lock` file will be updated automatically when the dependency is changed. For testing, review `src/arch/riscv64/` directory and the test files under `tests/` to understand the test harness. The project uses Cargo as the build system.

## Implementation Plan
- Update `Cargo.toml`: change the riscv64 dependency from `sbi = "0.2"` to `sbi-rt = "0.0.3"` (this will also pull in `sbi-spec` as a transitive dependency)
    - Update `Cargo.lock` by running `cargo update` (or equivalent) to reflect the new dependency tree
    - In `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/mod.rs`: 
      - Replace `sbi::legacy::console_putchar(*byte)` with `sbi_rt::console_write_byte(*byte)` in the `output_message_buf` function
      - Replace `sbi::hart_state_management::hart_start(...)` with `sbi_rt::hart_start(...)` in the `finish_processor_init` function
    - In `src/arch/riscv64/kernel/processor.rs`:
      - Update `shutdown(error_code)` to call `sbi_rt::system_reset(sbi_rt::Shutdown, sbi_rt::NoReason)` and then add an infinite `spin_loop` after it (since SRST may return on error)
      - Update `set_oneshot_timer` to use `sbi_rt::set_timer` for both the set and disable cases
      - Update `wakeup_core` to use `sbi_rt::send_ipi` with `HartMask::from_mask_base(0b1, hart_id)` instead of the legacy bit-vector approach
    - Verify the code compiles for riscv64 target and check that all SBI calls are now using the `sbi_rt` crate
    - Ensure the `Cargo.lock` is updated after the dependency change and the code compiles without errors

When the kernel encounters an unsupported command-line flag, it currently panics with a hard error message. Instead, it should just log a warning with the same message (e.g., "Found argument '...' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context...") and continue processing the remaining arguments. Change the behavior so an unrecognized flag only produces a warning rather than crashing the kernel.

pr_chain.title: Add configurable async shell for interrupt statistics and system control
pr_chain.description:
We need to add a feature-gated interactive shell to the HermitOS kernel that runs as an async task on x86_64 systems. This shell should allow users to view interrupt statistics and shut down the system, with a help command to discover available functionality.

    The goal is to provide a lightweight debugging and control interface for the kernel over the serial port, making it easier to inspect runtime behavior and manage the system without requiring external tools.

    Please ensure this feature is added behind a new Cargo feature flag (e.g., "shell" or similar) so it can be enabled or disabled as needed without affecting the default kernel build.

## Environment Setup
Check the Cargo.toml file at the repository root to understand the existing feature flags and dependency structure. Also review the workspace configuration in Cargo.toml to see how the xtask crate is included, which may contain build and test related tooling.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add a new feature flag (e.g., "shell") to Cargo.toml with an associated optional dependency on the `simple-shell` crate.
    2. Add the `simple-shell` crate as an optional dependency in Cargo.toml, version 0.0.1.
    3. Create a new `src/shell.rs` module that:
       - Imports the `simple_shell` crate
       - Implements a `read()` function that reads from the COM1 serial port
       - Defines a static `Lazy` shell with commands for:
         - Showing help text (with aliases "help", "?", "h")
         - Displaying interrupt statistics (with command "interrupts" and alias "i")
         - Shutting down the system (with command "shutdown" and alias "s")
       - Exports an `init()` function that spawns the shell as an async task using the existing executor
    4. Register the `shell` module in `src/lib.rs` behind the feature flag and x86_64 architecture check, and call its `init()` function in the `initd` kernel thread after filesystem initialization.
    5. Modify `src/arch/x86_64/kernel/serial.rs` to:
       - Add a buffer (VecDeque) to the SerialPort struct for shell input
       - Change the `receive()` method to `buffer_input()` that stores received characters in the buffer
       - Add a `read()` method to retrieve characters from the buffer
       - Ensure `COM1` is made `pub(crate)` so shell code can access it
    6. Add a stub `read()` method returning `None` to `src/arch/aarch64/kernel/serial.rs` to maintain interface consistency (marked with `#[allow(dead_code)]`).
    7. Modify `src/arch/x86_64/kernel/interrupts.rs` to use `println!` instead of `info!` for printing interrupt statistics, making them visible in all output modes.
    8. Update Cargo.lock as needed when dependencies are added.

pr_chain.title: Add Cargo feature flag to enable booting kernel without std
pr_chain.description:
Introduce a new Cargo feature flag `nostd` that allows the kernel to be booted without relying on the standard library (`std`). This feature should make the kernel behave similarly to how it operates when the `common-os` feature is enabled, but specifically for environments where `std` is not available.

    The goal is to allow linking against the kernel with a plain `main` function (rather than Hermit's `runtime_entry`) and to skip the thread-local error number storage that depends on `std`. This makes the kernel usable in no_std contexts.

    The implementation should:
    1. Add a `nostd` feature flag to the Cargo.toml feature list.
    2. Update error number handling in `src/errno.rs` so that the thread-local `ERRNO` storage and the `sys_get_errno` function are only compiled when neither `nostd` nor `common-os` features are active, and so that errno values are simply ignored when either feature is enabled.
    3. Update the initialization in `src/lib.rs` so that when either `nostd` or `common-os` is enabled, the kernel calls the application's `main` function instead of `runtime_entry`.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's `Cargo.toml` file for feature definitions and dependency configuration. Review `xtask/Cargo.toml` and any workflows in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for build and test procedures. The `rust-toolchain.toml` file indicates the Rust toolchain version to use.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add a `nostd = []` entry to the `[features]` section in the root `Cargo.toml`.
    2. Modify `src/errno.rs`: gate the `ERRNO` static with `not(any(feature = "common-os", feature = "nostd"))` instead of just `not(feature = "common-os")`.
    3. In `src/errno.rs`, gate the `sys_get_errno` function with `cfg(not(feature = "nostd"))` to omit it when the feature is active.
    4. In `src/errno.rs`, update the `set_errno` method's cfg_if block to treat `nostd` the same as `common-os`, ignoring errno values.
    5. In `src/lib.rs`, update the two cfg attributes around the `runtime_entry` and `main` extern declarations in `initd` to treat `nostd` the same as `common-os`, so that the kernel calls `main` when either feature is enabled.

pr_chain.title: Fix incorrect metadata length in FUSE command and response allocations
pr_chain.description: The FUSE filesystem implementation allocates command and response buffers with an incorrect metadata length, passing a zero value instead of the actual buffer size when constructing the fat pointer. This causes the kernel to report incorrect buffer bounds for these dynamically sized allocations, potentially leading to undefined behavior or memory safety issues when the buffers are accessed. The metadata length should reflect the actual allocated size to ensure correct memory management and validation.

pr_chain.title: Fix FUSE command header length calculation to exclude struct padding
pr_chain.description: The FUSE protocol expects the length field in command headers to represent the total command size without padding, but the current implementation uses the memory layout size which includes padding bytes. Please correct the length calculation in both the command creation and capacity-based initialization paths so the header reports the true unpadded size. This ensures compatibility with FUSE servers that validate the length field.

pr_chain.title: Align Uhyve default mount path with virtiofsd
pr_chain.description: We need to change the default mount point for the Uhyve filesystem from `/host` to `/root`. The goal is to ensure consistency between Uhyve and virtiofsd, which both currently use `/root` as their mount path (as configured by xtask and runh). This will avoid confusion and make the filesystem behavior predictable across different backends.

pr_chain.title: Explicitly enforce little-endian encoding in virtqueue descriptor structures
pr_chain.description: Update the split and packed virtqueue implementations to explicitly use little-endian integer types for all descriptor and ring fields, as required by the Virtio specification. This ensures correct behavior across all platforms regardless of native endianness, even though the current target platforms happen to be little-endian already.

We need to add support for building with cargo-careful so we can catch potential undefined behavior in dev builds. Please wire it up in the build tooling and make sure CI runs dev builds with it enabled, while keeping release builds on the standard path.

Update the Action Mailer Basics guide to reflect current Rails conventions and best practices. pr_chain.title: Refresh Active Record Validations guide structure and content
pr_chain.description:
The Active Record Validations guide (`guides/source/active_record_validations.md`) needs a comprehensive structural and content refresh to better serve both new and experienced Rails developers. The current guide has several areas that could be clearer, more accurate, and better organized.

    Key goals:

    - Use more appropriate examples: Replace examples using `Person.create` in contexts where `Person.new` is more semantically correct, since `create` runs validations and persists records, which can confuse readers about the validation lifecycle.

pr_chain.title: Clarify Strict Locals documentation for partial compilation performance
pr_chain.description:
The current documentation for Strict Locals in the Action View overview guide is misleading. It presents Strict Locals as a general feature for enforcing which locals a partial accepts, without explaining the real motivation behind it. The actual purpose is to address a performance problem: when partials are rendered with different combinations of locals, Rails must compile a separate version of the partial for each combination, which wastes memory and increases compilation time.

    The guide currently says "By default, partials will accept any `locals` as keyword arguments. To define what `locals` a partial accepts, use a `locals:` magic comment." This framing makes it seem like Strict Locals is a general validation feature that should be applied to all partials as a best practice. In reality, it's a targeted tool for solving the "megamorphic partial" problem — partials that are rendered with many different local variable combinations across the application.

    We need to rewrite the Strict Locals section to:
    - Explain that partials are compiled to Ruby methods, and each unique set of locals requires a separate compilation
    - Show a concrete example demonstrating the compilation duplication problem
    - Clarify that Strict Locals is meant for solving this performance issue, and is not recommended as a default for every partial
    - Re-frame the `locals:` comment as a "signature" rather than a "magic comment" to better match the intent

    The tone should be: "Use this when you have a performance problem with partials being compiled many times. Don't just add it everywhere."

## Environment Setup
This is a documentation-only change to the Rails guides. Check `guides/README.md` for instructions on how the guides are built, and `guides/rails_guides.rb` for how the guide generation works. The relevant Rake tasks can be found in `guides/Rakefile`. Some guide generation options may be documented in `guides/.rubocop.yml` and `guides/.document`.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `guides/source/action_view_overview.md` and find the "Strict Locals" section.
    2. Remove the existing INFO box that introduces Strict Locals as a way to define accepted locals.
    3. Rewrite the opening of the Strict Locals section to explain the compilation problem:
       - State that partials compile to Ruby methods
       - Explain that each distinct combination of locals triggers recompilation
       - Show an example ERB snippet with two render calls using different locals
       - Show the resulting compiled method signatures to illustrate duplication
    4. Add a concluding note clarifying that strict locals is meant for addressing this compilation issue when it becomes a problem (e.g., many combinations or performance-sensitive paths), and that it's not recommended to apply it to all partials by default.
    5. Rename all references from "locals:` magic comment" to "locals:` signature" throughout the section.
    6. Update the example code blocks to use `html+erb` as the language identifier instead of just `erb`.
    7. Fix any spelling errors (e.g., ensure "combinations" is spelled correctly).
    8. Ensure the final paragraph about `local_assigns` and reserved keywords is updated to use "signature" nomenclature consistently.

instruction:
## Update PopupSmart integration to use a config object for script loading.

The PopupSmart component currently reads a single `popupSmartUrl` string from the public runtime config. This needs to be updated to support a configuration object, `popupSmartConfig`, that contains both a `url` and an `id` field.

    The PopupSmart component should:
    - Read `popupSmartConfig` from the public runtime config.
    - Extract the `url` and `id` from the config object.
    - Only load the PopupSmart script when both `url` and `id` are present, in addition to the existing conditions (user has a role, user is not staff).
    - When loading the script, set the `id` as a `data-id` attribute on the script element.
    - Change script loading to async with defer, instead of the current synchronous (async=false) loading.

    Additionally, the Next.js configuration file should:
    - Replace the `POPUP_SMART_URL` environment variable configuration with a `POPUP_SMART_CONFIG` environment variable that expects a JSON string.
    - Parse this JSON string to create the `popupSmartConfig` object.
    - Pass this `popupSmartConfig` object to the public runtime config instead of the old `popupSmartUrl` string.

    The goal is to support the new PopupSmart API which requires both a URL and an ID, while maintaining backward compatibility with a config object structure.

## Environment Setup
Check `apps/condo/package.json` and the root `package.json` for dependency management scripts. Review `apps/condo/next.config.js` for environment variable handling. Refer to `apps/condo/README.md` for app-specific setup details. Use the root `turbo.json` and `apps/condo/jest.config.js` to understand test execution setup.

## Implementation Plan
- Update `apps/condo/next.config.js` to parse the `POPUP_SMART_CONFIG` environment variable as JSON and expose it as `popupSmartConfig` in the public runtime config, instead of the current `POPUP_SMART_URL` string configuration.
    - Modify `apps/condo/domains/common/components/PopupSmart.tsx` to destructure `popupSmartConfig` from the public runtime config instead of `popupSmartUrl`.
    - Extract `url` and `id` from the `popupSmartConfig` object using lodash `get`.
    - Update the useEffect dependency array and condition to require both `popupSmartUrl` and `popupSmartId` for script loading.
    - When creating the script element, set the `data-id` attribute to the `popupSmartId` value.
    - Change script loading attributes from `async = false` to `async = true` and add `defer = true`.

pr_chain.title: Add ability to extend Keystone default configuration
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to allow consumers of the `prepareKeystone()` function to customize the internal Keystone configuration object (e.g., cookie settings, session parameters) without having to re-create the entire configuration or use workarounds like `extendExpressApp`. Specifically, a new optional parameter, `extendKeystoneConfig`, should be accepted by `prepareKeystone()`. When provided as a function, it will receive the default Keystone configuration object as an argument and should return a partial or full configuration object that will be merged (spread) over the default configuration when constructing the `Keystone` instance. This enables developers to override specific settings like `cookie.sameSite` and `cookie.secure` for cross-domain scenarios while preserving all other defaults (e.g., cookie secret).

  This change is minimal and focused on the `packages/keystone/KSv5v6/v5/prepareKeystone.js` file.

## Environment Setup
- Check the root `package.json` for workspace configuration and dependency management scripts.
    - Check the `packages/keystone/package.json` for package-specific scripts and dependencies.
    - The repository uses a monorepo structure with `yarn`; refer to `yarn.lock` for dependency versions.
    - Refer to `turbo.json` for task orchestration details if needed (e.g., how to run tests or linting for a specific package).
    - Test configuration can be inferred from `packages/keystone/jest.config.js`.
    - For overall setup and development context, consult `docs/develop.md` and `docs/contributing.md`.

## Implementation Plan
- Add a new optional parameter `extendKeystoneConfig` to the destructured arguments of `prepareKeystone()`.
    - Validate that if `extendKeystoneConfig` is provided, it is a function (similar to existing checks for `apps` or `extendExpressApp`). Throw an error if it is not a function.
    - After `prepareDefaultKeystoneConfig(conf)` is called to create the default `keystoneConfig`, invoke `extendKeystoneConfig(keystoneConfig)` if the parameter is a function, and store the result (e.g., in `extendedKeystoneConfig`).

pr_chain.title: Add certificate and third-party integration health checks to the Condo app
pr_chain.description:
We need to extend the health check capabilities of the Condo application to include monitoring for external service certificates and integration status. Currently, the health check system only covers Redis and PostgreSQL. The goal is to add two new types of health checks:

    1. **Certificate health checks**: Validate that X.509 certificates used for external integrations (specifically Sber ID and SBBOL) are present and not expiring within a configurable window (default 14 days). These checks should parse the certificate content from environment configuration and use Node's native crypto module to inspect validity dates.

    2. **PFX certificate health checks**: A specialized variant that handles PFX/PKCS#12 certificates (used for SBBOL), which requires decrypting the PFX content with a passphrase before validating the embedded certificate.

    3. **Integration status checks**: A generic helper that allows any third-party integration to report its health status by executing a read-only business function that returns 'success', 'warn', or 'fail'.

    These checks should be registered in the Condo app's health check configuration alongside the existing Redis and PostgreSQL checks. The implementation should be structured so that the configuration parsing (reading from environment variables) happens outside the reusable health check functions, keeping them generic and testable.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files in the repository to understand the project setup:
    - `package.json` (root and `apps/condo/package.json`) - for dependency management and script commands
    - `yarn.lock` - for lockfile details
    - `turbo.json` - for monorepo task orchestration
    - `packages/keystone/package.json` - for the keystone package dependencies
    - `apps/condo/jest.config.js` - for test configuration in the Condo app
    - `packages/keystone/jest.config.js` - for test configuration in the keystone package
    - `docs/develop.md` and `docs/contributing.md` - for general development guidelines

## Implementation Plan
1. Add new health check factory functions to `packages/keystone/healthCheck.js`:
       - `getCertificateHealthCheck`: validates a certificate string using Node's `X509Certificate` class from the `crypto` module, checking that the current date plus a configurable number of days falls within the certificate's validity window.
       - `getPfxCertificateHealthCheck`: wraps the certificate check by first decrypting a PFX buffer using `tls.createSecureContext` and extracting the certificate.
       - `getIntegrationHealthCheck`: provides a generic wrapper for any third-party integration that can report a status string.
    2. Export the new functions from `packages/keystone/healthCheck.js`.
    3. Update `apps/condo/index.js` to import the new health check functions and register instances for the Sber ID and SBBOL certificates in the existing `checks` array. The environment configuration parsing (e.g., `JSON.parse(conf['SBER_ID_CONFIG'])`) should be done in the `apps/condo/index.js` file, passing the extracted certificate data to the generic check functions.
    4. Ensure the new health check functions include proper error handling (returning `false` on failure) and log errors for observability.
    5. Add comprehensive JSDoc comments for each new function to document parameters and expected return values.

pr_chain.title: Set default maxResults query limit to 1000 for Keystone lists
pr_chain.description:
When querying Keystone list types (e.g., `allTickets`) without specifying the `first` argument, the system currently attempts to fetch all records from the database. This can lead to database statement timeouts or 502 errors when the dataset is large. The existing configuration already sets `maxTotalResults` to 1000, which limits the total number of returned objects including nested ones. However, this does not prevent the initial database query from attempting to retrieve all rows.

    Implement a default `queryLimits.maxResults` of 1000 for all Keystone lists registered through the schema registration function. This ensures that when the `first` argument is not provided or is set to a value greater than 1000, the underlying database query is capped at 1000 records, preventing timeouts and server errors.

## Environment Setup
Review the following repository files to understand the project setup, dependency installation, and testing procedures:

pr_chain.title: Implement category sorting by order field in marketplace UI components
pr_chain.description:

    Update the marketplace components to sort parent categories and subcategories using the `order` field instead of alphabetical sorting. This applies to:

    1. **Invoice form** (`apps/condo/domains/marketplace/components/Invoice/BaseInvoiceForm.tsx`): The services list groups market items by parent category. Both the groups (parent categories) and the options within each group (subcategories and market items) should be sorted by `order`.
    2. **Market item form** (`apps/condo/domains/marketplace/components/MarketItem/BaseMarketItemForm.tsx`): The category select dropdowns should fetch categories sorted by `order`.
    3. **Market item content** (`apps/condo/domains/marketplace/components/MarketItemContent.tsx`): The category filter dropdown in the table should sort parent groups and subcategory options by `order`.
    4. **GraphQL queries** (`apps/condo/domains/marketplace/gql.js`): Ensure the `order` field is fetched for categories, parent categories, subcategories, and related entities so the components have access to it.

    The `order` field is already present on the `MarketCategory` model. This change ensures consistent, admin-defined ordering across all marketplace UI elements.

## Implementation Plan

      - Use parent category ID as the group key instead of name.

pr_chain.title: Sort marketplace categories and services alphabetically within groups

    For all cases, the primary sort key should remain the existing `order` field, but the secondary sort key should be the human-readable label (category name or service name) rather than an internal ID or key. This ensures a stable, user-friendly alphabetical order while preserving any intentional ordering from the `order` field.

Ensure the "All categories" special option always stays first regardless of label.

Update the sorting logic for groups and options to use this label for secondary alphabetical sorting while retaining the primary order-based sorting.
