pr_chain.title: Fix help dialog sizing and network data division by zero
pr_chain.description:
We need to address two issues that affect usability and stability:

    1. **Dialog box sizing**: The help dialog box (opened with `?`) and the delete confirmation dialog (opened with `dd` on a process) use percentage-based constraints that can result in boxes that are too small for their content, especially when the terminal window is small (e.g. less than 100 columns wide). The help dialog text can wrap awkwardly or get cut off. Similarly, the delete dialog can render too small on certain terminal sizes. The goal is to make these dialogs size themselves appropriately based on their actual content length, so they always fit their content without being clipped or excessively wrapped. We need a temporary fix that sizes the dialogs based on the text content length, rather than a percentage of the screen. Ideally we would add scrolling to the help dialog for the long-term, but for now a fixed-size approach based on content is acceptable.

    2. **Network data division by zero**: The network data harvester in `src/app/data_harvester/network.rs` calculates the receive/transmit rates by dividing the delta of total bytes by the elapsed time since the last sample. If the elapsed time is 0.0 seconds (which can happen when the timer granularity causes two samples to occur within the same clock tick), this division produces a panic (division by zero) that crashes the application. We need to guard against this case and return 0 for the rate when elapsed time is zero.

    Additionally, while investigating the dialog sizing, there are a few minor cleanups to include:
    - The help text in `src/constants.rs` should use clearer wording for the navigation keybindings ("Change your selected widget" instead of "Move currently selected widget").
    - Reorganize the constants in `src/constants.rs` to group related items (e.g. move the config file path constants next to the default config content).
    - Remove the `#[allow(dead_code, unused_variables)]` attribute from `get_search_start_position` in `src/canvas/drawing_utils.rs` since it is now used.
    - When the search widget is opened, set the cursor direction to `RIGHT` in `src/app.rs` so the cursor is positioned at the start of the search query.
    - Add a "Bugs and Requests" section to the README to let users know where to file issues.

## Environment Setup
Check `Cargo.toml` for the project configuration, dependencies, and any workspace settings. This is a Rust project using Cargo, so build and test instructions will be in `Cargo.toml` (standard `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo run`). The `rustfmt.toml` file contains formatting rules. The project also has `README.md` with general usage info. There is no `Makefile` or `tox.ini` in the repo listing, so rely on Cargo's standard commands. Note the `.travis.yml` may contain CI-related build steps if you need a reference, but the canonical build/test workflow is via Cargo.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Dialog sizing fix** (in `src/canvas.rs`):
       - For the help dialog: Replace the percentage-based `Vertical` and `Horizontal` `Constraint`s with fixed `Length` constraints. Compute the vertical size based on the number of lines in the help text (the `GENERAL_HELP_TEXT`, `PROCESS_HELP_TEXT`, or `SEARCH_HELP_TEXT` constant, based on the current category). Use `GENERAL_HELP_TEXT.len() + 3` as the height (adding space for borders and the title bar). For the horizontal constraints, if the terminal width is less than 100 characters, use full width (0% left/right margins); otherwise keep the 20/60/20 split. pr_chain.title: Refactor widget drawing code into separate module files
pr_chain.description:
The `canvas.rs` file has grown very large as all widget drawing logic is implemented directly on the `Painter` struct within a single file. This makes the file difficult to navigate and work with, especially as new widgets are added. We need to split the widget drawing code into separate, focused modules.

The goal is to:
- Extract each widget's drawing logic from `src/canvas.rs` into its own file under `src/canvas/widgets/`
- Create a shared `widgets` module that re-exports the widget traits
- Move shared widget-related constants (headers, border styles, minimum thresholds) from `canvas.rs` into appropriate locations
- Keep all existing behavior identical — this is purely a structural/organizational refactor

This will make it easier for contributors to add new widgets and for maintainers to navigate the codebase.

## Environment Setup

Since this is a Rust project, building and testing is typically done via `cargo` commands — refer to these config files for the project setup. `rustfmt.toml` specifies code formatting rules that should be followed.

1. Create a new directory `src/canvas/widgets/` with the following module files:
       - `basic_table_arrows.rs` — for the basic table arrow navigation widget

       - `network_graph.rs` — for the network graph/labels widget

pr_chain.title: Refactor dialog rendering and improve process kill error reporting

pr_chain.title: Fix CPU table scroll clipping with hidden cores
pr_chain.description:
Fix a bug where the CPU table scroll position can exceed the number of visible (non-hidden) CPU entries, causing the scroll to potentially go off-screen. This happens when scrolling and hiding/showing CPU cores interact, since hiding a core reduces the effective list length but the scroll position isn't adjusted.

  The core issue is that the scroll position is checked against the full CPU data list length (`canvas_data.cpu_data.len()`), but when `show_disabled_data` is false, hidden cores are not rendered. This means the scroll position can point to an index beyond the visible list.

  Your task is to track the number of visible CPUs separately from the full list, and use that count when checking scroll bounds for the CPU table. Also ensure the scroll position is clamped when cores are hidden so it never exceeds the visible count.

## Environment Setup
Check the `Cargo.toml` file for the project structure and dependencies. The project uses Rust with cargo. Look at `.travis.yml` for CI setup hints. The `rustfmt.toml` file indicates formatting standards. You'll primarily work in `src/app.rs` and `src/main.rs`.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `src/app.rs`:
    - Add `use std::cmp::max;` at the top of the file.
    - Add a `num_cpus_shown: u64` field to `CpuState` struct.
    - Initialize `num_cpus_shown: 0` in the `Default` implementation for `CpuState`.

  2. In `src/main.rs`:
    - Replace the pre-fill loop for `core_show_vec` with a simple assignment: `app.cpu_state.core_show_vec = vec![true; app.canvas_data.cpu_data.len()];`.
    - Set `app.cpu_state.num_cpus_shown = app.canvas_data.cpu_data.len() as u64;` in the same block.

  3. In `src/app.rs`, in the `on_esc` method:
    - After the `cpu_state.is_showing_tray = false;` line, add logic that checks if `current_scroll_position >= num_cpus_shown`. If so, set `current_scroll_position` to `max(0, num_cpus_shown as i64 - 1) as u64` and reset `previous_scroll_position` to 0.

  4. In `src/app.rs`, in the `on_space` method:
    - After toggling a core's visibility, check if `show_disabled_data` is false. If so, increment or decrement `num_cpus_shown` based on whether the core is now hidden or shown.

  5. In `src/app.rs`, in the `change_cpu_table_position` method:
    - Compute a `cap` value: if filtering or searching, use `canvas_data.cpu_data.len()`, otherwise use `cpu_state.num_cpus_shown`.
    - Use this `cap` instead of `canvas_data.cpu_data.len()` in the bounds check.

pr_chain.title: Fix CPU legend coloring and refactor average CPU data handling
pr_chain.description:
We need to fix a bug where CPU legend entries are colored incorrectly when the average CPU row is hidden, and refactor the code to improve how average CPU data is handled. The issue occurs because:

1. When `show_average_cpu` is false, the average CPU entry ("AVG") is still included in the harvested data but excluded during conversion, causing index mismatches between the data vectors and the legend display.
2. The legend coloring logic uses incorrect indices, so the selected row highlight and per-CPU color assignment don't align with what's actually displayed.

The goal is to:
- Make the average CPU entry only be included in the harvested data when `show_average_cpu` is true
- Refactor the CPU data conversion to remove the need for offset calculations
- Fix the CPU legend rendering so colors and selection highlighting work correctly whether or not the average CPU row is shown
- Streamline the legend rendering by combining the data preparation and row generation into a single iteration

Please ensure the solution works correctly for:
- `show_average_cpu` = true (average CPU row shown with its special color)
- `show_average_cpu` = false (average CPU row hidden, per-core colors align correctly)
- The tray selection mode (where CPU cores can be toggled on/off)
- Both scrolled and non-scrolled states of the legend

## Environment Setup
Check `Cargo.toml` for project dependencies and build configuration. Tests are typically run via `cargo test` — look at the `[dev-dependencies]` section in `Cargo.toml` and any test-related configuration. The repository contains test files in the `tests/` directory (`arg_tests.rs`, `invalid_config_tests.rs`) that you can examine for test patterns. Code style should follow `rustfmt.toml` (run `cargo fmt` to check).

## Implementation Plan
1. **Modify `src/app/data_harvester/cpu.rs`**:
   - Change `get_cpu_data_list` to accept a `show_average_cpu: bool` parameter
   - Only add the "AVG" entry to the returned vector when `show_average_cpu` is true

2. **Update `src/app/data_harvester.rs`**:
   - Add a `show_average_cpu: bool` field to `DataState` (defaulting to `false`)
   - Add a setter method `set_show_average_cpu(&mut self, show_average_cpu: bool)`
   - Pass `self.show_average_cpu` to `cpu::get_cpu_data_list()` in `update_data()`

3. **Update `src/main.rs`**:
   - Pass `app.app_config_fields.show_average_cpu` to `create_event_thread()` as a new parameter
   - In `create_event_thread`, call `data_state.set_show_average_cpu(show_average_cpu)` after initialization
   - Remove the `show_avg_cpu` parameter from all `convert_cpu_data_points()` calls
   - Move the CPU pre-fill logic (initializing `core_show_vec`) to before the `convert_cpu_data_points()` call, using `app.data_collection.cpu_harvest.len()` instead of `app.canvas_data.cpu_data.len()`

4. **Refactor `src/data_conversion.rs`**:
   - Remove the `show_avg_cpu` parameter from `convert_cpu_data_points()`
   - Remove the `cpu_listing_offset` variable and the `if !show_avg_cpu && itx == 0 { continue; }` block
   - Change the `itx_offset` calculation to simply use `itx`
   - Add a `legend_value: String` field to `ConvertedCpuData`
   - Populate `legend_value` in the conversion loop: `format!("{:.0}%", cpu.0.round())`

5. **Fix `src/canvas/widgets/cpu_graph.rs`**:
   - In `draw_cpu_legend()`:
     - Replace the two-pass approach (stringified data collection then row generation) with a single `filter_map` iteration over the sliced data
     - Use `Cow<'_, str>` for the row strings to avoid unnecessary allocations
     - Compute an `offset_scroll_index` that accounts for rows skipped due to filtering (when `is_showing_tray` is false and the row is disabled/hidden)
     - When building rows:
       - For tray mode: include `[ *]`/`[ ]` toggle indicator based on `core_show_vec[itx + start_position]`
       - For normal mode: show percentage from `cpu.legend_value` if `show_disabled_data` is true OR `core_show_vec[itx]` is true
       - If a row would be empty (normal mode, row hidden/disabled), increment `offset_scroll_index` and skip it
     - Style rows correctly:
       - Selected row (when in `CpuLegend` widget position): use `currently_selected_text_style` when `itx == offset_scroll_index`
       - Average CPU row (index 0 when `show_average_cpu`): use `avg_colour_style`
       - Otherwise: use `cpu_colour_styles[itx % len]` — do NOT add `start_position` to the index

pr_chain.title: Fix process widget tab handling and search field sizing
pr_chain.description:
There are two bugs in the process table widget that need fixing:

1. **Tab handling bug**: When pressing Tab while the process table is in focus (and not in the search input), the code looks up `widget_states` using `current_widget.widget_id - 1`, but the process table itself is identified by `widget_id`. This off-by-one error means the grouping toggle and search-by-name action don't work correctly when Tab is pressed while focused on the process table. Additionally, the logic ordering is wrong: the widget state lookup should only happen if we're actually in a mode where tab handling is relevant.

2. **Search field sizing bug**: The search field prompt text ("Search by PID...", etc.) may be longer than the available width, causing layout issues. The current logic checks if `chosen_text.len() != min(num_columns / 2, chosen_text.len())` to determine "small mode", which is overly complex and doesn't work reliably. Additionally, when in grouped mode, the search prompt always says "Search by Name" but the abbreviation shown in small mode incorrectly uses "p> " when searching by PID even in grouped mode (grouped mode always searches by name, so the abbreviation should always be "n> ").

Fix both issues:
- Correct the tab handling to use the right widget ID lookup and proper ordering.
- Simplify the small-mode detection in the search field to use a fixed width threshold, and ensure the PID/Name abbreviation logic respects the grouped state.

Testing: After making changes, verify that:
- Pressing Tab while focused on the process table toggles grouping (when not in search mode), and pressing Tab while in search mode toggles between PID and name search.
- When the terminal is narrow (less than ~70 columns), the search field shows abbreviated prompts ("p> " or "n> ") and works correctly in both grouped and ungrouped modes.

## Environment Setup
Check `Cargo.toml` for project dependencies and Rust version requirements. The repository contains tests in the `tests/` directory (see `tests/arg_tests.rs`, `tests/invalid_config_tests.rs`) and uses `clippy.toml` and `rustfmt.toml` for linting/formatting. Reference `src/app.rs` for the tab handling logic and `src/canvas/widgets/process_table.rs` for the search field rendering code.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `src/app.rs`, restructure the `on_tab` method so that the widget state lookup only occurs when `is_in_search_widget` is true (using `widget_id - 1` for the search input), and separately handle the non-search case by looking up `widget_id` directly (the process table's own ID) to toggle grouping.
    2. In `src/canvas/widgets/process_table.rs`, replace the `small_mode` calculation with a simple width check (e.g., `num_columns < 70`).
    3. Update the search prompt abbreviation logic in the same file to check `is_grouped` before deciding between "p> " and "n> " – if grouped, always use "n> ".
    4. Remove the now-unused `min` import from the `std::cmp` use statement.
    5. Run the existing tests and verify the changes compile without new warnings or clippy lints.

pr_chain.title: Refactor HierarchicalWorld subdivision logic and add lock/unlock operations
pr_chain.description:
Refactor the `HierarchicalWorld` class to change how subdivision decisions are made, and add new public methods for locking and unlocking world chunks at specific coordinates.

    The current logic ties the ability to subdivide a node to whether it has reached its maximum depth (`canSubdivide()` returns false at max depth). This should be changed so that `canSubdivide()` always returns true, and instead the subdivision is prevented by checking whether the node is a leaf (i.e., it has reached max depth) at the point where subdivision would actually occur.

    Specifically:
    - Change `canSubdivide()` to always return `true`.
    - Add a private `isLeaf()` helper that returns true when the node's depth equals its max depth.
    - In the `syncRec` method, replace the check `canSubdivide()` with `!isLeaf()` to determine whether the node could potentially subdivide, then check `canSubdivide()` before actually calling `subdivide()`.
    - In `requestCreateAt`, call `subdivide()` unconditionally instead of checking `canSubdivide()` first.
    - Add two new public methods: `lockAt(x, y)` that locks the node and recursively locks any child nodes containing the specified point, and `unlockAll()` that recursively unlocks all nodes.
    - Also remove the `hxd/res/World.hx` file, which contains an unnecessary typedef alias.

    This change improves control over LOD (level of detail) management by allowing external logic to override the automatic subdivision decisions through `canSubdivide()` overrides, while respecting the maximum depth constraint through `isLeaf()`. The new `lockAt` and `unlockAll` methods provide more flexible chunk locking for editing scenarios.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's build configuration files to understand how to set up the Haxe environment and run tests: `all.hxml` for Haxe compilation entry points, `haxelib.json` for library dependencies, and `Makefile` (in `tools/mikktspace/` and repo root) for build/test automation.

## Implementation Plan
- Edit `h3d/scene/HierarchicalWorld.hx`:
      - Add a private `isLeaf()` method that returns `data.depth == data.maxDepth`.
      - Change `canSubdivide()` to simply return `true`.
      - In `subdivide()`, add an early return if `isLeaf()` is true.
      - In `syncRec`, change the subdivision check to use `!isLeaf()` instead of `canSubdivide()`, and wrap the `subdivide()` call in a `canSubdivide()` check.
      - In `requestCreateAt`, remove the `canSubdivide()` check around `subdivide()`.
      - Add `lockAt(x, y)` method that sets `locked = true` and recursively calls itself on children containing the point.
      - Add `unlockAll()` method that sets `locked = false` and recursively calls itself on all children.
    - Delete the file `hxd/res/World.hx`.
    - Verify the changes compile without errors and existing functionality (particularly subdivision behavior) still works as expected.

pr_chain.title: Add configurable subdivision multiplier to HierarchicalWorld
pr_chain.description:
The HierarchicalWorld class currently uses a fixed threshold of `data.size * 2.0` to decide when to subdivide a node based on camera distance. This hardcoded multiplier limits flexibility — different world types or scenes may need different subdivision densities (e.g., areas where finer granularity is needed at greater distances, or where coarser subdivision is acceptable when closer).

    We need to make this threshold configurable per world instance by adding a `subdivPow` field to the `WorldData` type. This field will act as a multiplier on the current node's `size` when comparing against the camera distance during the subdivision test in `syncRec`. The default behavior should remain the same (`2.0`) for backward compatibility, but users can now provide a custom value when creating a world to control how aggressively it subdivides relative to camera distance.

    The field must be propagated to child nodes during `subdivide()` so that the multiplier is consistent across the hierarchical tree.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository root for `haxelib.json` (project metadata), `all.hxml` (build configuration), and `README.md` (general setup/contribution notes). Test infrastructure is minimal — look at `samples/all.hxml` and `samples/gen.hxml` for example build targets. No dedicated test config file (e.g., tox.ini or Makefile) exists beyond `tools/mikktspace/Makefile`, which is unrelated to core library testing.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `h3d/scene/HierarchicalWorld.hx`, add a new field `subdivPow : Float` to the `WorldData` typedef (near `size` and `depth`).
    2. In `subdivide()`, when constructing each `childData`, copy the parent's `subdivPow` value into the child's `WorldData`.
    3. In `syncRec()`, replace the hardcoded `data.size * 2.0` with `data.size * data.subdivPow`.

pr_chain.title: Fix directional shadow map depth clear to ensure proper depth reset
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to resolve a bug in the directional shadow map rendering path where the depth buffer is not being properly cleared when rendering to a color target. This can cause incorrect shadow results, particularly with dynamic scenes where the shadow map content may not be fully overwritten between frames.

    Specifically, in `h3d/pass/DirShadowMap.hx`, the `processShadowMap` method currently calls `ctx.engine.clear(0xFFFFFF)` when the target texture is a color format (i.e., not a depth format). This overload of the clear method appears to only set the color value and does not reset the depth buffer. Since a depth buffer is attached to the shadow map texture, it is not being cleared, leading to stale depth data from previous frames affecting shadow calculations.

    Please ensure that when clearing the shadow map target, both the color and depth components are reset appropriately. The fix should explicitly pass a depth value (e.g., `1.0`) to the clear call, matching the behavior already used in the depth-texture branch of the same method.

## Environment Setup
Review the project configuration files to understand how to build and test the repository: `haxelib.json` (package metadata and dependencies), `all.hxml` (build targets), and `samples/` directory for example usage. The `.travis.yml` file may also provide CI build and test commands.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `h3d/pass/DirShadowMap.hx` and locate the `processShadowMap` method around line 269.
    2. Identify the branch where the target texture is not a depth format (the `else` block that calls `ctx.engine.clear(0xFFFFFF)`).
    3. Modify the clear call to also specify the depth clear value by passing a second argument of `1.0` (i.e., `ctx.engine.clear(0xFFFFFF, 1.0)`), ensuring both color and depth are reset.
    4. Verify the change aligns with the clear semantics used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., the depth-only clear in the same method).
    5. Test the shadow map behavior with a sample scene that uses directional lights to confirm shadows render correctly without stale depth artifacts.

pr_chain.title: Add low-precision float buffer upload support and format compression utility
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to enable uploading float data to vertex buffers that use low-precision formats (F16, U8, S8), and to provide a utility for computing a best-fit compressed buffer format.

    Currently, `h3d.Buffer.uploadFloats` throws an error when the buffer format has low precision, making it impossible to upload vertex data directly to compressed formats. We need to change this so that when a buffer uses low precision, the float data is automatically converted to the appropriate low-precision representation (e.g., 32-bit floats to 16-bit half-floats, unsigned bytes, or signed bytes) before being uploaded via `uploadBytes`.

    Additionally, we need to add a `getCompressed()` method to `hxd.BufferFormat` that returns a compressed version of the current format. This method should:
    - Match each input to a predefined set of common vertex attributes (position, normal, uv, color, data) and use a suggested lower precision for each (e.g., F16 for positions/uvs, S8 for normals).
    - Preserve the original precision for inputs that don't match the known set.
    - Since hardware often requires vertex buffer strides to be 4-byte (or 8-byte) aligned, the method should refine the compressed format so that the total stride fits the alignment constraints, upgrading precision if needed to fill unused space, or use the original precision if compression would exceed the stride budget.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's build and configuration files: `all.hxml`, `samples/all.hxml`, `samples/gen.hxml`, and `haxelib.json` for dependency and build setup. The `Makefile` in `tools/mikktspace/` and the `.travis.yml` may also contain build/test instructions.

## Implementation Plan
- In `h3d/Buffer.hx`:
      - Remove the early `throw "Can't upload floats on low precision buffer";` check in `uploadFloats`.
      - Add a branch that handles the `format.hasLowPrecision` case: iterate over each vertex and each input in the format, convert each float component according to the input's precision (F32: write as-is 4 bytes, F16: use `hxd.BufferFormat.float32to16`, U8: use `float32toU8`, S8: use `float32toS8`), write into an allocated `haxe.io.Bytes` buffer, and call `uploadBytes` at the end.
      - Ensure byte alignment for each input is the same as in `BufferFormat` (4-byte alignment after each input).
    - In `hxd/BufferFormat.hx`:
      - Add a `compressed` field to `BufferFormat` to cache the computed compressed format.
      - Add a private static `COMPRESSED_CONFIG` holding an array of `BufferInput` with candidate names/types and suggested low precision (e.g., `{ name: "data", type: DVec4, precision: F16 }`, `{ name: "color", type: DVec4, precision: F16 }`, etc.).
      - Implement `getCompressed()` which:
        - If cached, return it.
        - Build a new array of `BufferInput` by matching each input in the current format against `COMPRESSED_CONFIG`. If matched, use the compressed precision; otherwise keep the original precision.
        - Compute the minimum stride bytes (with 4-byte alignment) for the compressed inputs, and the maximum stride (aligned to 8 bytes).
        - If there's a gap, try to upgrade precisions of inputs (from lowest priority) to fill the gap while staying within the max stride.
        - Cache and return the new compressed `BufferFormat` created via `make()`.

Currently, the `uploadBuffers` function reallocates and re-uploads texture SRV (Shader Resource View) and sampler descriptors every frame. Implement a caching mechanism that reuses the previously allocated SRVs and sampler views when the textures, frame count, and heap state haven't changed. pr_chain.title: Fix depth state transitions, camera zoom limit, and shader DCE ordering
pr_chain.description:
Three related changes are needed in this Haxe game framework:

    1. **DX12Driver depth state handling**: In `h3d/impl/DX12Driver.hx`, the driver currently always transitions depth buffers between DEPTH_READ and DEPTH_WRITE states, even when the texture is already in the correct state. This causes unnecessary resource transitions that impact performance. Additionally, when binding depth textures as shader resources, the code unconditionally sets the state to DEPTH_READ, which can conflict with existing transitions.

    2. **Camera minimum zoom distance**: In `h3d/scene/CameraController.hx`, the default `minDistance` is 0, which allows the camera to zoom to the exact target point, causing degenerate views (zero distance, divide-by-zero in some calculations). The minimum should be increased to prevent this.

    3. **Shader dead code elimination (DCE) ordering**: In `hxsl/Dce.hx`, the `markRec` function iterates over `v.deps` (a Map), which has non-deterministic iteration order in Haxe. This can lead to non-reproducible shader output. The fix is to maintain an additional ordered list (`adeps`) alongside the map, and iterate over that for deterministic processing.

    The goal is to fix these three issues: optimize DX12 depth transitions, prevent degenerate camera zoom, and ensure deterministic shader DCE output.

## Environment Setup
Check `haxelib.json` for project metadata and dependencies. For build and test configuration, look at `all.hxml` at the repo root and `samples/all.hxml` for sample builds. The `.travis.yml` file shows CI configuration that may indicate how compilation is tested. The project uses Haxe with hxml build files rather than a Makefile or tox.ini.

## Implementation Plan
1. **DX12Driver.hx - getDepthView transition optimization**:
       - In the `getDepthView` function, before calling `transition(depthBuffer.t, readOnly ? DEPTH_READ : DEPTH_WRITE)`, check if the texture's current state already matches the target state.
       - The condition should be: `if (depthBuffer != null && (depthBuffer.t.state & (DEPTH_READ | DEPTH_WRITE) == COMMON))` — this checks if the texture is currently in the common state, meaning no DEPTH_READ or DEPTH_WRITE bit is set. Only then perform the transition.
       - This avoids redundant transitions when the texture is already properly staged.

    2. **DX12Driver.hx - shader resource binding state handling**:
       - In the shader resource view creation section (around line 1677), when determining the state for a depth texture being used as a shader resource, check the texture's current state first.
       - If the texture already has either DEPTH_READ or DEPTH_WRITE set (meaning it's not in COMMON state), preserve that existing state instead of forcing DEPTH_READ.
       - The logic: `if (t.t.state & (DEPTH_READ | DEPTH_WRITE) == COMMON) DEPTH_READ else t.t.state`
       - This prevents conflicts when a texture is already being used as a depth render target.

    3. **CameraController.hx - min zoom distance**:
       - Change the default `minDistance` from `0.` to `1`.
       - This prevents users from zooming to zero distance from the target, which would cause degenerate camera matrices and potential division-by-zero in the rendering pipeline.
       - Note: The `zoom` function already clamps to `minDistance`, so this change will be enforced automatically.

    4. **Dce.hx - deterministic dependency marking**:
       - Add a new field `adeps` (array of `VarDeps`) to the `VarDeps` class, alongside the existing `deps` Map.
       - Initialize `adeps` as an empty array in the constructor.
       - In `markRec`, change the iteration from `for (d in v.deps)` to `for (d in v.adeps)`.
       - In the `link` function, when adding a new dependency, check if it already exists in the `deps` map first:
         ```
         if (!w.deps.exists(v.id)) {
             w.deps.set(v.id, vd);
             w.adeps.push(vd);
         }
         ```
       - This ensures that each dependency is added only once, and the iteration order in `markRec` is deterministic (insertion order rather than map hash order).

pr_chain.title: Fix DX12 render target format support, HierarchicalWorld stability, and TextInput draw behavior
pr_chain.description:
We need to address several issues in the Heaps framework that are affecting DX12 render target support, HierarchicalWorld behavior, and TextInput performance:

    1. **DX12 render target format support**: The current `getRTBits` implementation in DX12Driver doesn't support newer formats like `RG11B10UF` and `RGB10A2`. Additionally, the bit packing for render target information is incorrect — the `PSIGN_RENDER_TARGETS` and `PSIGN_LAYOUT` offsets overlap, and the pipeline signature bytes are being written with 32-bit ints when they should be 8-bit values. This causes incorrect shader pipeline hashing and potential rendering artifacts. We need to fix the format encoding to properly support these formats and correct the bit layout.

    2. **HierarchicalWorld flickering and missing refresh**: The current implementation subdivides and collapses immediately based on distance checks, which causes visible popping/flickering when the camera moves. Add a delay/hysteresis system (using elapsed time accumulation) to smooth out these transitions. Also add a `refresh()` method that completely resets the subdivision state.

    3. **TextInput content change event spam**: The `drawRec` method currently calls `interactive.draw(ctx)` which can trigger `onContentChanged()` callbacks unnecessarily. We need to prevent this by temporarily bypassing the interactive's parent container during the draw, preventing domkit style updates.

    4. **CacheFileBuilder DX12 compilation**: When compiling shaders for XBoxSeries (which uses DX12), the `out.baseRegister` assignment incorrectly references `sign.fragmentRegStart` which doesn't exist in the DX12 driver's root signature structure — it should use the register start from the signature's register array.

    Please address all these issues in the relevant files. Check the existing code structure carefully — some of these changes may require restructuring related code to maintain clean integration.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository configuration files: `haxelib.json`, `all.hxml`, `samples/all.hxml`, and `samples/gen.hxml` for build dependencies and project structure. The main test/run configuration is in the `.hxml` files, and the project uses Haxe with the HashLink target. Review the existing code in the affected files (`h3d/impl/DX12Driver.hx`, `h3d/scene/HierarchicalWorld.hx`, `h2d/TextInput.hx`, `hxsl/CacheFileBuilder.hx`) to understand the current implementation.

## Implementation Plan
1. Fix DX12 render target bit packing: Update `PSIGN_LAYOUT` offset to not overlap with `PSIGN_RENDER_TARGETS`, change `getRTBits` to correctly pack format and channel info, add support for `RG11B10UF` and `RGB10A2` formats, and change pipeline signature writes from 32-bit ints to 8-bit values where appropriate.
    
    2. Add HierarchicalWorld transition smoothing: Introduce `stateAccu` and `stateCooldown` variables, accumulate elapsed time based on whether the player is close enough to subdivide, and only subdivide/collapse after the cooldown threshold is reached. Also add a `refresh()` method that resets the subdivision state.
    
    3. Fix TextInput draw behavior: Modify `drawRec` to temporarily null out the interactive's `parentContainer` during drawing to prevent domkit style updates, then restore it after the draw completes.
    
    4. Fix CacheFileBuilder DX12 compilation: Update the `out.baseRegister` assignment to use `sign.registers[1].start` instead of the non-existent `sign.fragmentRegStart` field.

pr_chain.title: Reduce allocations in Polygon.projectPoint and Segment.project methods
pr_chain.description:
The current implementations of `Polygon.projectPoint` and `Segment.project` allocate multiple new `Point` instances on every call. This is wasteful in hot code paths where these methods may be called frequently (e.g., collision detection loops). 

    The goal is to:
    1. Add an optional `out` parameter to both methods so callers can provide a reusable `Point` instance to write results into.
    2. If no `out` is provided, preserve the existing behavior of returning a new `Point` instance (for backwards compatibility).
    3. Ensure `Polygon.projectPoint` internally reuses a single `Point` instance when iterating over edges, rather than allocating one per edge.

    Additionally, the `Polygon.projectPoint` implementation currently has a subtle bug: it returns `null` if no edge is closer than the initial `minDistSq` of `1e10` (which can happen if the polygon has zero edges). We should make the behavior deterministic — always return a valid `Point` (either the provided `out` or a fallback).

## Environment Setup
Check the following files for build/test instructions:
    - `all.hxml` (Haxe compilation configuration, likely includes test targets)
    - `haxelib.json` (defines dependencies and library metadata)
    - `.travis.yml` (may reference how tests are run in CI)
    - `samples/all.hxml` and `samples/gen.hxml` (sample compilation targets)

## Implementation Plan
1. **Modify `h2d/col/Segment.hx`**:
       - Change the signature of `project` to `public inline function project( p : Point, ?out : Point ) : Point`
       - Inside the method, if `out == null`, create a new `Point()`.
       - Replace all `new Point(...)` return sites with `out.set(...)` calls followed by `return out`.
       - Update the doc comment to describe the new `out` parameter.

    2. **Modify `h2d/col/Polygon.hx`**:
       - Change the signature of `projectPoint` to `public function projectPoint(pt: h2d.col.Point, ?out : h2d.col.Point)`
       - Inside the method:
         - Create a local `closest` `Point` to track the best result during iteration.
         - Initialize `out` to `new Point()` if `null`, and also create `closest` as `new Point()`.
         - In the loop, reuse a single `Point` temporary by calling `new Segment(p1, p2).project(pt, out)` — this writes into the same `out` each iteration.
         - After finding the closest, `out.load(closest)` to copy the final result into the caller's `out`.
         - Always return `out` (never `null`).
       - Update the doc comment to describe the new `out` parameter and guarantee it's never `null`.

    3. **Verify the `Point.load` method exists**: Check `h2d/col/Point.hx` for a `load` method that copies values from another point. If not present, use manual field assignment (`out.x = closest.x; out.y = closest.y;`).

    4. **Update all existing call sites** of `project` and `projectPoint` within the repo to ensure they still work (they should, since `out` is optional).

    5. **Run the full test suite** to confirm no regressions.

pr_chain.title: Fix SpotShadowMap camera globals and DCE array swizzle bug
pr_chain.description:
We need to make two related fixes to the Heaps Haxe game framework:

1. **SpotShadowMap (h3d/pass/SpotShadowMap.hx)**: The current implementation uses an unnecessary `Border` shader object that adds overhead. We need to remove the `Border` field and all related code. Instead of drawing a border after the shadow map render, we should set the camera state (view projection matrix, camera position, and camera far plane) before rendering the shadow map so that any shaders using these globals (e.g., depth-based effects) work correctly with the light camera. Currently, these globals are only set during the merge pass in Mixed mode, but not during the main shadow map draw.

2. **DCE (hxsl/Dce.hx)**: There's a bug in dead code elimination where assignments to array elements through a swizzle (e.g., `arr.swizzle.x = value` or `vec.rgb[0] = value`) are not being tracked correctly. The pattern matching in the `check` function only handles direct array access (`TArray`) but not when the array access is wrapped in a swizzle (`TSwiz`). This causes variables written through swizzled array access to be incorrectly eliminated.

The goal is to ensure shadow maps render correctly with shaders using camera globals, reduce unnecessary rendering overhead, and fix the DCE bug to prevent incorrect shader optimization.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository configuration files to understand how to build and test:
    - `haxelib.json` - project definition and dependencies
    - `all.hxml` - main Haxe build configuration
    - `samples/all.hxml` and `samples/gen.hxml` - sample project build configs
    - `.travis.yml` - CI configuration showing test/build commands
    - `tools/mikktspace/Makefile` - build tooling reference

## Implementation Plan
1. In `h3d/pass/SpotShadowMap.hx`:

pr_chain.title: Restrict editor property editing code to JavaScript targets
pr_chain.description:
We need to constrain the `editProps()` methods in the material system and the base `AnyProps` class to only compile when building for JavaScript targets. Currently, these methods are guarded by the `#if editor` conditional compilation flag, which means they get included in builds targeting other platforms (like HashLink or native) when the `editor` flag is set. This causes compilation failures because the `js.jquery.JQuery` class (used to generate property editing UI) is only available on JavaScript targets.

    The goal is to modify the conditional compilation guards in `h3d/mat/Material.hx`, `h3d/mat/PbrMaterial.hx`, and `hxd/impl/AnyProps.hx` so that the `editProps()` override methods are only compiled when both the `editor` flag is defined **and** the target is JavaScript (`js`). This will allow non-JS targets to define the `editor` flag without pulling in the jQuery-dependent code.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repository files to understand installation and build setup:
    - `haxelib.json` — describes Haxe library dependencies and project configuration
    - `all.hxml` — likely contains Haxe compiler flags and defines used for the project
    - `README.md` — may contain general build instructions
    - `.travis.yml` — CI configuration that may show how the project is built and tested

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `hxd/impl/AnyProps.hx` and locate the `#if editor` preprocessor directive guarding the `editProps()` method (around line 24).
    2. Change the guard from `#if editor` to `#if (editor && js)` for the `editProps()` method.
    3. Open `h3d/mat/Material.hx` and locate the `#if editor` preprocessor directive guarding the `editProps()` override method (around line 286).
    4. Change the guard from `#if editor` to `#if (editor && js)` for the `editProps()` override.
    5. Open `h3d/mat/PbrMaterial.hx` and locate the `#if editor` preprocessor directive guarding the `editProps()` override method (around line 511).
    6. Change the guard from `#if editor` to `#if (editor && js)` for the `editProps()` override.
    7. Verify there are no other `#if editor` guards in these files that also need updating — only the `editProps()` methods that directly reference `js.jquery.JQuery` need this change.

instruction:
## Restore IAM user and secret for reused AWS accounts after fleet manager claim deletion

Fix the issue where an AWS account that was claimed via a fleet manager account claim (using a trusted ARN for STS role-based access) loses its IAM user and associated secret when that account claim is deleted. This leaves the account unable to be claimed again by a regular (non-fleet-manager) account claim.

    Specifically, implement the following:
    - When a fleet manager account claim is deleted, clean up the fleet manager IAM role and its secret, and restore the account's IAM user and secret so the account can be claimed normally again.
    - Add a helper method to the `Account` type that identifies an account in a "ready" and "reused" state that is missing its IAM user secret and has no claim link, is not a BYOC account, and is not an STS account. This method should be used by the account controller to trigger re-initialization of the account (which recreates the IAM user and secret).
    - Update the account controller's reconcile logic to check for this condition and re-initialize the account if it matches.
    - Replace direct usage of the `utils` package for `GetOperatorConfigMap` and `RequeueAfter` in the accountclaim controller with the `controllerutils` alias (the `pkg/utils` package) for consistency.
    - Update the UBI base image tag in both `build/Dockerfile` and `build/Dockerfile.olm-registry` from `8.9-1029` to `8.9-1108` for security and maintenance.
    - Simplify the `checkIAMSecretExists` function to use a single return statement.

    The goal is to ensure that accounts claimed via fleet manager can be seamlessly reclaimed by regular account claims after the fleet manager claim is removed.

## Environment Setup
Check `Makefile` at the repository root for common development and build targets. The project uses Go modules (`go.mod` and `api/go.mod`). Look at `api/v1alpha1/account_types.go` and the controller files under `controllers/` for the core logic. The `README.md` and `docs/2.0-Development.md` may contain additional context for local development.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Add helper method to Account type**:
       - In `api/v1alpha1/account_types.go`, add a method `IsReusedAccountMissingIAMUser()` on the `Account` struct. It should return `true` if the account is ready, `Status.Reused` is true, `Spec.IAMUserSecret` is empty, the account is not a BYOC account, does not have a claim link, and is not an STS account.

    2. **Update account controller reconcile logic**:
       - In `controllers/account/account_controller.go`, modify the condition that triggers account initialization. The current condition is `currentAcctInstance.ReadyForInitialization()`. Change it to also check for `currentAcctInstance.IsReusedAccountMissingIAMUser()`, so that accounts missing their IAM user secret can be re-initialized.

    3. **Clean up fleet manager resources on account claim deletion**:
       - In `controllers/accountclaim/accountclaim_controller.go`, within the `Reconcile` function, in the block that handles `accountClaim.DeletionTimestamp != nil`, add logic to check if the claim is a fleet manager claim (i.e., `accountClaim.Spec.FleetManagerConfig.TrustedARN != ""`). If so:
         - Delete the IAM role secret associated with the claim (using `accountClaim.Spec.AwsCredentialSecret.Name` and namespace).
         - Get the claimed account (via `accountClaim.Spec.AccountLink`). If the account is not a BYOC account, build an AWS client via role assumption and call `r.CleanUpIAMRoleAndPolicies` to remove the fleet manager role.
         - Note that the account initialization (triggered in step 2) will be responsible for recreating the IAM user and secret.

    4. **Update utility package usages**:
       - In `controllers/accountclaim/accountclaim_controller.go`, find usages of `utils.GetOperatorConfigMap` and `utils.RequeueAfter` and replace them with `controllerutils.GetOperatorConfigMap` and `controllerutils.RequeueAfter` (where `controllerutils` is the already-imported alias for `pkg/utils`).

    5. **Update UBI base image tags**:
       - In `build/Dockerfile` and `build/Dockerfile.olm-registry`, change the base image from `registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi-minimal:8.9-1029` to `registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi-minimal:8.9-1108`.

    6. **Simplify checkIAMSecretExists**:
       - In `controllers/accountclaim/accountclaim_controller.go`, refactor the `checkIAMSecretExists` function to remove the gosimple suppression comment and return `true`/`false` directly based on the error from `r.Client.Get`.

pr_chain.title: Add feature-flagged validation cleanup for failed AWS accounts without IDs
pr_chain.description:
We need to add a new validation check to the account validation controller that identifies and cleans up `Account` custom resources that are in a `Failed` state and have no associated AWS account ID. This addresses a real operational issue: many `Failed` accounts without AWS account associations are accumulating, making it appear that accounts aren't being reused when in reality those accounts are simply unusable.

The new check should:
- Only trigger for accounts in the `Failed` state that have no `AwsAccountID` in their spec.
- Skip accounts that are currently being deleted (have a `DeletionTimestamp`).
- Be controlled by a new feature flag `feature.validation_delete_account` read from the operator ConfigMap, defaulting to disabled.
- When the feature flag is enabled, delete the qualifying `Account` custom resource.
- When the feature flag is disabled, log a "dry run" message indicating what would be cleaned up, without actually deleting.
- The check should run before other validation checks but must not interrupt the normal validation flow for accounts that don't qualify for deletion.

Please also add unit tests covering the new `ValidateRemoval` function and the updated `Reconcile` behavior, and update the ConfigMap templates to include the new feature flag with a default value of `false`.

## Environment Setup
Check the `Makefile`, `go.mod`, and `api/go.mod` for build and dependency management. The `Makefile` contains the standard targets for building, testing, and running the operator. Look at `controllers/validation/account_validation_controller_test.go` for the existing test patterns to follow.

## Implementation Plan
- Add a new `AccountNotForCleanup` value to the `ValidationError` enum type in `controllers/validation/account_validation_controller.go`.
    - Create a new `ValidateRemoval(account awsv1alpha1.Account) error` function that returns an `AccountValidationError` with `AccountNotForCleanup` type when the account is not both `Failed` and lacking an `AwsAccountID`.
    - In the `Reconcile` method, add a new package-level boolean variable `accountDeletionEnabled` and read the `feature.validation_delete_account` key from the ConfigMap after the existing feature flags are parsed.
    - After the AWS client is retrieved (or the retrieval error is logged), invoke `ValidateRemoval` on the account. If it passes (returns nil), delete the account when `accountDeletionEnabled` is true, or log a dry-run message when false. Handle delete errors by returning `utils.RequeueWithError(err)`.
    - Add unit tests for `ValidateRemoval` covering the three scenarios: non-failed account, failed account with AWS ID, and failed account without AWS ID. Also add a reconcile test case for an account with a `DeletionTimestamp` that is in the `Failed` state with no AWS account ID.
    - Update `hack/olm-registry/olm-artifacts-template.yaml` and `hack/templates/aws.managed.openshift.io_v1alpha1_configmap.tmpl` to add the new `feature.validation_delete_account` flag with a default value of `"false"`.

pr_chain.title: Make ConcurrentModificationException a retryable error during account creation
pr_chain.description:
Currently, when the AWS Organizations API returns a `ConcurrentModificationException` during account creation (i.e., when AWS returns "AWS Organizations can't complete your request because it conflicts with another attempt to modify the same entity. Try again later."), the account CR is marked as `Failed`. This is incorrect since this error is transient and should be retried. As a result, new account CRs get created needlessly, inflating our failed account count.

    The goal is to treat `ConcurrentModificationException` as a retryable error, similar to other transient errors like `TooManyRequestsException` or `ServiceException`, and NOT mark the account as failed. This will prevent unnecessary account CR creation.

    Please ensure that the new error type is properly defined, mapped correctly in the CreateAccount function, and handled appropriately in the BuildAccount logic (i.e., don't set the account status to failed for this error). Also add unit tests to verify the behavior.

## Environment Setup
Look at the following repo files to understand how to install dependencies and run tests:
    - `go.mod` and `api/go.mod` for Go module dependencies
    - `Makefile` for build and test targets
    - `.golangci.yml` for linting configuration
    - `boilerplate/generated-includes.mk` and `boilerplate/_lib/container-make` for containerized build/test setup
    - `controllers/account/account_suite_test.go` for the test suite setup

## Implementation Plan
1. Add a new sentinel error `ErrAwsConcurrentModification` to `api/v1alpha1/shared_types.go` alongside the existing AWS error variables (e.g., near `ErrAwsTooManyRequests`).
    2. In `controllers/account/account_controller.go`, update the `CreateAccount` function's error handling switch statement to map `organizations.ErrCodeConcurrentModificationException` to the new `awsv1alpha1.ErrAwsConcurrentModification`.
    3. Verify that the `BuildAccount` function already handles `ErrAwsConcurrentModification` correctly (it should fall through to the default case which is non-fatal and returns the error without marking the account as failed). If not, add a case to treat it as non-fatal.
    4. Add unit tests in `controllers/account/account_controller_test.go`:
       - Test that `CreateAccount` maps `ErrCodeConcurrentModificationException` to `ErrAwsConcurrentModification`.
       - Test that `BuildAccount` does not set the account state to `AccountFailed` when `ConcurrentModificationException` occurs.

pr_chain.title: Treat missing account pool in configmap as empty service quotas
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to change how the `GetServiceQuotasFromAccountPool` function in `pkg/utils/utils.go` handles the case when the requested account pool name is not present in the operator configmap's `accountpool` data.

    Currently, this scenario returns an error (`fixtures.NotFound`), which can cause unnecessary reconcile failures and error conditions. Instead, when the specific account pool name is not found in the parsed configmap data, the function should treat it as if the pool's service quota configuration were empty and return an initialized (empty) `RegionalServiceQuotas` map with a nil error. This makes the function's behavior consistent with how it treats a pool that exists but has no service quotas configured.

    This change should be accompanied by unit tests that verify the new behavior for the "pool not found" case, while still erroring correctly for other failure modes such as the operator configmap not existing, the `accountpool` key missing from the configmap data, or the pool data being malformed. The existing error paths for those other scenarios must remain intact.

    Please also ensure the project's linting and validation checks pass.

## Environment Setup
The repository uses Go modules; please refer to `go.mod` for dependency management and `go.sum` for dependency checksums. The `Makefile` likely contains the primary build and test targets. There is also a `.golangci.yml` file for linting configuration. Test suites for this package are located in `pkg/utils/`.

## Implementation Plan
- Modify the `GetServiceQuotasFromAccountPool` function in `pkg/utils/utils.go` so that when the `accountPoolName` is not found in the `data` map, it returns an initialized (non-nil) but empty `awsv1alpha1.RegionalServiceQuotas` map and a nil error.
    - Log an informational message (not an error) at the debug or info level for this case, explaining that the account pool is not configured.
    - Add a Ginkgo test suite for the `pkg/utils` package (if not already present) to cover the new behavior for `GetServiceQuotasFromAccountPool`.
    - Write specific test cases to verify: (1) returning an empty map with no error when the pool is missing, (2) still returning an error when the configmap cannot be retrieved, (3) still returning an error when the `accountpool` key is absent, and (4) still returning an error when the pool data is malformed.
    - Ensure all existing and new unit tests pass, and verify the code conforms to the project's linting rules (e.g., via `make lint` or the configured golangci-lint).

pr_chain.title: Add conditional skip for reusable account IAM user recreation
pr_chain.description:
When a reused AWS account is claimed by a new account claim, the operator currently recreates the IAM user and secret, then continues through the full account initialization process (region initialization, etc.). For accounts that are already initialized and only need their IAM user recreated (due to being reused), this full initialization is unnecessary and causes errors or delays.

    The goal is to:
    1. Add a new helper method `IsReusedAccountWithIAMUserSecret()` to the `Account` type that returns `true` when an account is ready, has `Status.Reused == true`, has `Spec.IAMUserSecret` set, is not BYOC, has no claim link, and is not STS.
    2. After the IAM user and secret are successfully recreated during account initialization, check this condition and immediately exit the reconcile loop without calling `initializeRegions` (and without further processing) when the condition is met.
    3. Simplify the existing `IsReusedAccountMissingIAMUser()` method to use a direct boolean return expression for consistency and readability.

    This is important because when a reused account is claimed, only the IAM user needs recreation; the account itself is already initialized (regions, quotas, etc.). Skipping re-initialization avoids unnecessary AWS API calls and potential failures.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository root for `go.mod` and `go.sum` for Go module dependencies. Look at the `Makefile` in the repo root for development, build, and test targets. Refer to the `controllers/account/account_suite_test.go` and `controllers/account/account_controller_test.go` files for existing test patterns. The `api/v1alpha1/account_types_test.go` file exists for testing the API types. The `build/Dockerfile` and `build/Dockerfile.olm-registry` are provided for container builds but are not needed for local development.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open the file `api/v1alpha1/account_types.go`.
    2. Locate the `IsReusedAccountMissingIAMUser` method. Refactor its return statement to directly return the boolean expression (removing the if-else).
    3. Immediately after `IsReusedAccountMissingIAMUser`, add a new method `IsReusedAccountWithIAMUserSecret` that returns `a.IsReady() && a.Status.Reused && a.Spec.IAMUserSecret != "" && !a.IsBYOC() && !a.HasClaimLink() && !a.IsSTS()`.
    4. Open `controllers/account/account_controller.go`.
    5. Find the code block where, after the IAM user is created and saved, there's a log line `reqLogger.Info("IAM User created and saved", "user", iamUserUHC)`. Just after this log line, before the call to `r.initializeRegions(...)`, add a check: if `currentAcctInstance.IsReusedAccountWithIAMUserSecret()` is true, return `reconcile.Result{}, err` immediately (exiting the reconcile function without region initialization).
    6. Ensure no other logic is modified within the reconcile flow.

pr_chain.title: Correct misleading Makefile target comments for fleetmanager accountclaims

pr_chain.title: Use cluster region for non-BYOC AWS client during account claim finalization

This is necessary because S3 bucket cleanup operations will fail if the client is not configured for the region where the buckets reside.

pr_chain.title: Handle Service Quota Errors in Opt-In Regions with Manual Action Status
pr_chain.description:
We need to improve how the operator handles service quota increase requests in AWS opt-in regions that do not support quota increases. Currently, when the operator attempts to process a quota increase request for a region that doesn't support this operation, it fails with a `NoSuchResourceException` error and the process stops. 

    The goal is to:
    1. Detect when a `NoSuchResourceException` error occurs during quota increase processing (specifically when checking if a quota needs to be increased)
    2. Set the service quota status to a new `MANUAL_ACTION` status for that particular quota in that region
    3. Ensure that accounts with quotas in `MANUAL_ACTION` status are not considered to have open quota increase requests (so the operator doesn't keep retrying)
    4. Log the situation appropriately so operators know manual intervention is required

    This change should not break existing functionality for supported regions or other error handling paths.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files for build and test setup:
    - `Makefile` for standard build/test targets
    - `go.mod` and `go.sum` for Go module dependencies
    - `.golangci.yml` for linting configuration
    - `api/go.mod` for the api module dependencies
    - Review `docs/2.0-Development.md` for development workflow guidance

## Implementation Plan
1. Add a new constant `ServiceRequestUnknown` with value `"MANUAL_ACTION"` to the `ServiceRequestStatus` type in `api/v1alpha1/account_types.go`
    2. Update the `HasOpenQuotaIncreaseRequests()` method to exclude quotas with `ServiceRequestUnknown` status from being considered "open"
    3. In `controllers/account/service_quota.go`, modify the `HandleServiceQuotaRequests` function to check for `NoSuchResourceException` errors returned from `serviceQuotaNeedsIncrease`
    4. When that specific error is detected, set the `serviceQuotaStatus.Status` to `ServiceRequestUnknown` and return nil (no error)
    5. Update `api/v1alpha1/zz_generated.deepcopy.go` and `api/v1alpha1/zz_generated.openapi.go` to reflect the new constant if generated files need regeneration
    6. Add or update test cases in `api/v1alpha1/account_types_test.go` and `controllers/account/service_quota_test.go` to cover the new status handling

pr_chain.title: Enable opt-in region enablement for existing ready accounts
pr_chain.description: We need to extend the account validation flow so that existing, ready, non-CCS accounts can have supported opt-in regions enabled when the feature flag is turned on. Currently, opt-in region processing only applies to accounts in a creating state, so accounts already in a ready state never receive region enablement even when configured. The validation controller should detect ready accounts that have pending opt-in region requests and initiate the enablement process, while also accounting for the existing concurrency limits on region enablement requests.

pr_chain.title: Add documentation for opt-in regions and update base image references
pr_chain.description:
We need to document the AWS opt-in regions feature that was recently implemented in the operator. The feature allows both new and existing accounts to have AWS opt-in regions enabled through a feature flag and configuration in the AAO ConfigMap. The feature is hidden behind a feature flag (`feature.opt_in_regions`) and uses an `opt-in-regions` key in the ConfigMap to specify which regions to enable.

    The documentation should cover:
    - How to specify opt-in regions in the AAO ConfigMap
    - What happens when a new account has opt-in regions defined (the `OptingInRegions` state)
    - How the region status is tracked in the Account CR status
    - What `MANUAL_ACTION` status means (insufficient permissions)
    - How to enable opt-in regions for existing ready accounts via the account validation controller
    - AWS limits on concurrent region enablement (max 6 regions per account, max 9 accounts simultaneously) and how batching is used to work around these limits

    Additionally, we should update the base image references in both Dockerfiles from ubi-minimal 8.9-1161 to a newer version (8.10-896) to ensure we're using an up-to-date base image with security patches.

    Please create a new documentation file `docs/9.0-Opt-In-Regions.md` that covers the topics listed above. The documentation should include links to relevant code sections for reference. Also update the base image tags in `build/Dockerfile` and `build/Dockerfile.olm-registry`.

## Environment Setup

Documentation is organized in the `docs/` directory with a `docs/README.md` index. There's also a `mkdocs.yml` for documentation site configuration.

## Implementation Plan
1. Create a new documentation file at `docs/9.0-Opt-In-Regions.md` covering the opt-in regions feature
    2. Document how to configure opt-in regions via the AAO ConfigMap (feature flag and region list)
    3. Explain the account lifecycle states related to opt-in regions (including `OptingInRegions` state and status tracking in Account CR)
    4. Include information about existing account handling and AWS API limits with batching
    5. Add links to relevant code sections (region_enablement.go, account_validation_controller.go) in the documentation
    6. Update the base image references in both `build/Dockerfile` and `build/Dockerfile.olm-registry` from `ubi8/ubi-minimal:8.9-1161` to `ubi8/ubi-minimal:8.10-896`

pr_chain.title: Handle misconfigured role permissions during Opt-In region enablement
pr_chain.description:
When an account has misconfigured role permissions (e.g., `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` lacks the necessary permissions), the region enablement flow currently gets stuck in a retry loop. The `HandleOptInRegionRequests` function calls `RegionNeedsOptIn`, which retries on `AccessDeniedException` a limited number of times, but when the retries are exhausted, the error is logged and the function continues with `regionOptInRequired` set to its zero value (false), incorrectly marking the region as enabled or leaving it in a TODO state forever.

    The goal is to detect when the AWS API returns an `AccessDeniedException` during the initial `RegionNeedsOptIn` call and mark the region's status as `MANUAL_ACTION` instead of leaving it in `TODO`. This prevents the controller from continuously retrying to enable regions on accounts with incorrect permissions and signals that a human needs to intervene.

    Additionally, accounts with regions in `MANUAL_ACTION` status should not be counted as "open" region requests, so the `HasOpenOptInRegionRequests` method needs to exclude this new status. Finally, add a log message to `CalculateOptingInRegionAccounts` to make it easier to debug how many accounts are currently opting into regions.

## Environment Setup
Check the `Makefile` for build, test, and lint targets. The `go.mod` file at the repository root defines Go module dependencies. For API-related changes, also check `api/go.mod`. Review `boilerplate/openshift/golang-osd-operator/README.md` and `boilerplate/generated-includes.mk` for any standard project setup instructions. The `.golangci.yml` file defines linting rules.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Add a new `OptInRequestStatus` constant**: In `api/v1alpha1/account_types.go`, add a new constant `OptInRequestUnknown OptInRequestStatus = "MANUAL_ACTION"` alongside the existing `TODO`, `ENABLING`, and `ENABLED` statuses.
    
    2. **Update `HasOpenOptInRegionRequests`**: In `api/v1alpha1/account_types.go`, modify the loop in `HasOpenOptInRegionRequests` to also skip over regions whose status is `OptInRequestUnknown` (i.e., `MANUAL_ACTION`), since these do not require automated action.
    
    3. **Update `HandleOptInRegionRequests`**: In `controllers/account/region_enablement.go`, in the error handling block after the `RegionNeedsOptIn` call, check if the error message contains `"AccessDeniedException"`. If so, set `optInRegionRequest.Status` to `awsv1alpha1.OptInRequestUnknown` (the new `MANUAL_ACTION` status).
    
    4. **Add logging to `CalculateOptingInRegionAccounts`**: In `controllers/account/region_enablement.go`, change the function signature to accept a `reqLogger logr.Logger` parameter and add an `Info` log message at the end that reports the `numberOfAccountsOptingIn` value.
    
    5. **Update call sites**: Update the two callers of `CalculateOptingInRegionAccounts` — one in `controllers/account/account_controller.go` (in `handleOptInRegionEnablement`) and one in `controllers/validation/account_validation_controller.go` (in `ValidateOptInRegions`) — to pass the `reqLogger` argument.

pr_chain.title: Remove IAM secret validation logic from account controller
pr_chain.description:
We need to remove the IAM secret validation logic from the account controller. Currently, there is a block of code in the `Reconcile` function that runs when an account is ready and a feature flag is enabled, which checks if the IAM user secret is valid and attempts to heal it if not. Since this validation is no longer performed or needed, we should remove this code path entirely.

    The goal is to simplify the account reconciliation flow by removing the unused secret-probing functionality. This includes removing the `probeSecretEnabled` constant (which was always false and disabled the feature), the `ProbeSecret` method, and the `IsKubeSecretValid` and `ValidateIAMSecret` methods that were only used by `ProbeSecret`. We should also remove any now-unused imports and related test cases.

    This change reduces unnecessary code complexity and eliminates dead code paths that could confuse future maintainers. It also improves reconciliation performance by removing a conditional block that, while currently disabled, adds no value to the reconciliation logic.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repository files for build, dependency, and test instructions:
    - `go.mod` and `api/go.mod` for module dependencies.
    - `Makefile` for common build and test targets.
    - `boilerplate/generated-includes.mk` for included boilerplate targets.
    - `.golangci.yml` for linting configuration.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `controllers/account/account_controller.go`:
       - Remove the `probeSecretEnabled` constant and its explanatory comment from the const block.
       - Remove the entire `if currentAcctInstance.IsReady() && probeSecretEnabled { ... }` block from the `Reconcile` method. This block handles role assumption, IAM user UHC name construction, and calls to `ProbeSecret`.
       - After removal, verify that any imports used exclusively by the removed block (e.g., `stsclient`, `fmt` if only used there) are still needed elsewhere in the file; if not, remove them.

    2. In `controllers/account/iam.go`:
       - Remove the entire `ProbeSecret` function.
       - Remove the entire `IsKubeSecretValid` function.
       - Remove the entire `ValidateIAMSecret` function.
       - Check for and remove any imports that become unused after deleting these functions. Specifically, the `sts` package import is likely only used by `IsKubeSecretValid` and should be removed. Also verify if `types` from `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/types` is still used elsewhere; if not, remove that import.

    3. In `controllers/account/iam_test.go`:
       - Remove the `TestValidateIAMSecret` test function.
       - Remove the `TestIsKubeSecretValid` test function.
       - Remove any test helper functions or variables that were only used by these removed tests.
       - Check for and remove imports that become unused, such as `sts` and `metav1` (if only used by `TestIsKubeSecretValid` and `TestValidateIAMSecret`).

    4. After making changes, run code generation and validation tools if required by the project to ensure no generated files are out of date.

pr_chain.title: Update total account watcher to count only active AWS accounts
pr_chain.description: We need to adjust the total account watcher so that it only counts AWS accounts in the ACTIVE status when determining the current account total. This is necessary because recently cleaned-up accounts remain in a SUSPENDED state for 90 days before deletion, and counting them against the account limit incorrectly prevents creation of new accounts. The goal is to prevent the account limit from being reached prematurely and avoid the need to raise the ACCOUNT_LIMIT.

pr_chain.title: Use name_prefix for Spark IRSA policy to avoid regional conflicts
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to make the IAM policy used for Spark job execution IRSA unique across different AWS regions when deploying the same solution with the same name in different regions. Currently, the policy name is set using the `name` argument, which creates a fixed name (`${local.name}-spark-irsa`). This conflicts when deploying identical configurations in multiple regions within the same account.

    Please update the `aws_iam_policy` resource named "spark" in both `analytics/terraform/spark-eks-ipv6/spark-team.tf` and `analytics/terraform/spark-k8s-operator/spark-team.tf` to use `name_prefix` instead of `name`. This allows AWS to append a unique suffix to the policy name, preventing conflicts when deploying the same solution in different regions with the same `local.name` value.

## Environment Setup
This is a Terraform project. Check `analytics/terraform/spark-eks-ipv6/versions.tf` and `analytics/terraform/spark-k8s-operator/versions.tf` for Terraform and provider version requirements. Review the repository's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` for linting and formatting hooks, and check `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general contribution guidelines. The `README.md` files in each blueprint directory may contain deployment instructions.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `analytics/terraform/spark-eks-ipv6/spark-team.tf`
    2. Locate the `aws_iam_policy` resource named "spark" (around line 69)
    3. Change the `name` argument to `name_prefix` (keeping the same value: `"${local.name}-spark-irsa"`)
    4. Open `analytics/terraform/spark-k8s-operator/spark-team.tf`
    5. Locate the `aws_iam_policy` resource named "spark" (around line 68)
