    2. Inspect the current loop structure, noting how `meta` and `text` are accumulated across iterations and how entries get pushed to the result vector.
    3. Design a single-pass approach: iterate over stripped lines once, maintaining a `Vec<FixtureEntry>` where a newly encountered `//-` marker starts a new entry (pushing a fresh `FixtureEntry` with empty text), and any other line appends content (with a newline) to `last_mut()` of the result vector.
    4. Replace the loop implementation with the designed single-pass logic, ensuring the function still returns the result vector after processing all lines. Preserve all existing surrounding code, including documentation comments and the margin-stripping steps.
    5. Run the existing test suite (via the workspace's testing setup) to confirm no behavioral regressions and that all tests involving fixture parsing continue to pass.

We need to clean up the formatting handler so it reads more naturally and avoids importing std modules locally. Please consolidate the process-related imports at the top of the file and streamline how we configure the rustfmt command's stdin and stdout.

pr_chain.title: Clean up unnecessary parenthesization in percentage calculations
pr_chain.description: The analysis statistics reporting contains unnecessary parentheses around arithmetic expressions used to compute unknown-type percentages. These extra parentheses trigger compiler warnings and make the code harder to read. Please remove the redundant grouping so the calculations are written in the simpler, idiomatic form while preserving the exact same behavior.

When the auto-import assist is triggered for an unresolved name, the assist group label currently just says "auto import". Update it so the group label includes the actual path being imported, e.g. "Import Foo::Bar", so users can see at a glance what each action group will do.

pr_chain.title: Improve status bar label responsiveness during cargo check progress updates
pr_chain.description: Update the status display logic so the status bar label refreshes immediately when a progress report message arrives, rather than waiting for the next spinner tick. Also separate the spinner frame advancement from the label rendering to avoid coupling these concerns. This ensures the displayed package name updates promptly when cargo check reports new progress.

pr_chain.title: Extend auto-import assist to support functions in value namespace
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to make the `auto_import` assist work for functions, not just types. Currently, the `Module::find_use_path` method in `crates/ra_hir/src/code_model.rs` only looks up paths in the type namespace, so when a user tries to auto-import a function by name, no suggestions appear.

    Your task is to:
    1. Update `Module::find_use_path` to determine the correct namespace for a given `ModuleDef` (values vs types) and use that when searching for a path.
    2. Add a test case in `crates/ra_assists/src/assists/auto_import.rs` to verify that the assist can auto-import a function from a module.

    Functions, constants, and statics live in the value namespace; everything else (structs, enums, traits, etc.) lives in the type namespace. The `ItemInNs` enum from `hir_def::item_scope` already models this distinction.

## Environment Setup
Check `Cargo.toml` at the repo root for workspace structure and dependency details. Each crate has its own `Cargo.toml` (e.g., `crates/ra_hir/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ra_assists/Cargo.toml`) — look there for crate-specific dependencies and test configuration. For CI and testing setup, review `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` to see how tests are invoked in CI.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `crates/ra_hir/src/code_model.rs` and locate the `Module::find_use_path` method (around line 238).
    2. In that method, replace the hard-coded `ItemInNs::Types(item.into())` with a call to a new helper function that determines the correct namespace.
    3. Add a private helper function `determine_item_namespace(module_def: ModuleDef) -> ItemInNs` that matches on the `ModuleDef` variant:
       - For `Static`, `Const`, or `Function`, return `ItemInNs::Values(module_def.into())`.
       - For all other variants, return `ItemInNs::Types(module_def.into())`.
    4. In `crates/ra_hir/src/code_model.rs`, add `item_scope::ItemInNs` to the `pub use hir_def::{...}` line so the helper can reference it.
    5. Open `crates/ra_assists/src/assists/auto_import.rs` and add a new test to the `tests` module.
    6. The test should use `check_assist_with_imports_locator` with `auto_import` and `TestImportsLocator::new`. Create a test fixture where an unresolved function call `test_function` appears at the cursor position, and a `pub mod PubMod` contains a `pub fn test_function`. The expected output should insert `use PubMod::test_function;` above the function call.

instruction:
## Refactor resource spec export to automate omitting defaults and generating overrides

Implement a generalized mechanism for the export flow that simplifies how default values are omitted and how per-region spec overrides are generated for `ClusterSpec` (EC2) and `TitusClusterSpec` (Titus). The current implementations in `ClusterHandler` classes rely on manual, per-property `if/else` logic and numerous `copy` calls to translate clouddriver types into spec types and to strip out values that match defaults. This is error-prone and verbose.

    The goal is to introduce a reusable, reflection-based helper that:

    1. Converts a clouddriver "active server group" model object into the corresponding spec data class by matching constructor parameter names to source property names (replacing the existing hand-written `exportSpec` translation logic).
    2. Derives a spec instance containing only properties that differ from a given baseline/default object, using the existing `ResourceDiff` mechanism. Properties whose values are unchanged (or null in the working object) should be omitted.
    3. Supports an allow-list of property names to consider and a force-list of property names to always include.

    The EC2 and Titus cluster export paths should be reworked to use these helpers, eliminating the verbose conditional blocks used to construct `_defaults` and `overrides`.

    Note: `TitusServerGroupSpec.container` currently has a non-null default value. To support the spec-building mechanism where properties may be omitted, change `container` to be nullable (`Container? = null`). Update all code that reads `defaults.container` to handle the nullability (e.g., use `?: error("Container image not specified or resolved")`).

## Environment Setup
- Refer to the root files: `build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts`, `gradle.properties`, `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`, and `.travis.yml` for build and dependency setup.
    - Check `keel-core/build.gradle.kts`, `keel-plugin/build.gradle.kts`, `keel-ec2-plugin/build.gradle.kts`, and `keel-titus-plugin/build.gradle.kts` for module-specific dependencies.
    - The `.github/workflows/pr.yml` may contain CI commands for building and running tests.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create a new helper module/file**: In `keel-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/plugin/`, create a new file `ResourceSpecExportHelper.kt` with two top-level inline functions:
       - `inline fun <reified T : Any, reified S : Any> buildSpecFromDiff(base: T, working: T, allowedProperties: Set<String>? = null, forcedProperties: Set<String> = emptySet()): S?`
         - Instantiate `ResourceDiff(working, base)`.
         - If `!diff.hasChanges()`, return `null`.
         - Collect property names from `diff.children` where `isAdded || isChanged`. Filter by `allowedProperties` if provided, and union with `forcedProperties`.
         - If the resulting set is empty, return `null`.
         - Use reflection (`S::class.primaryConstructor`) to build the spec. For each constructor parameter whose name is in the filtered set, find the corresponding property on `T` via `T::class.memberProperties` and get its value from `working`.
         - If all resolved parameter values are `null`, return `null`; otherwise, call the constructor with `callBy`.
       - `inline fun <reified I : Any, reified O : Any> convert(obj: I): O`
         - Use reflection to find the primary constructor of `O`, match parameters by name against `I`'s properties, and invoke `callBy` with values from `obj`.
       - Ensure these functions handle cases where a matching property is not found (skip it).

    2. **Refactor `ResourceDiff` (in `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/diff/ResourceDiff.kt`)**:
       - Add a `children: Set<DiffNode>` property that returns the root-level child `DiffNode`s from `diff` (using `diff.visitChildren` with `visit.dontGoDeeper()`).
       - Refactor `affectedRootPropertyNames` and `affectedRootPropertyTypes` to derive from `children`.

    3. **Update `TitusClusterSpec`** (in `keel-titus-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/titus/cluster/TitusClusterSpec.kt`):
       - Change `val container: Container` to `val container: Container? = null` in `TitusServerGroupSpec`.
       - Update `resolve()` method: change `resolveContainer(defaults.container)` to `resolveContainer(defaults.container ?: error("Container image not specified or resolved"))`.
       - Review and update any other direct usages of `defaults.container` in the file if needed.

    4. **Update `TitusImageResolver`** (in `keel-titus-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/titus/cluster/TitusImageResolver.kt`):
       - Change `getContainerFromSpec` to return `resource.spec.defaults.container ?: error("Container not specified or resolved")`.

    5. **Refactor `TitusClusterHandler`** (in `keel-titus-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/titus/cluster/TitusClusterHandler.kt`):
       - Replace the manual `exportSpec` (which currently creates a `TitusServerGroupSpec` with all fields populated) with a call to the new `convert` function, converting `TitusServerGroup` to `TitusServerGroupSpec`. The existing `generateContainer` logic for the container field must still be applied, so you may need to build the `TitusServerGroupSpec` and then override `container` with the generated one, or adjust the source `TitusServerGroup` to have the resolved container before conversion.
       - Replace the manual `generateOverrides` logic: for each region, create the working spec (via `convert`), then call `buildSpecFromDiff(defaults, workingSpec)` to compute the override spec (or `null` if no changes). Set `overrides[region]` to the result if non-null.

    6. **Refactor `ClusterHandler`** (in `keel-ec2-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/ec2/resource/ClusterHandler.kt`):
       - Replace the manual construction of `_defaults = ClusterSpec.ServerGroupSpec(...)` with a call to a new `exportSpec` function on the `ServerGroup`/`ActiveServerGroup` model that uses the `convert` helper to map the clouddriver fields to `ClusterSpec.ServerGroupSpec`. Handle the special cases that were previously in `exportSpec` methods (e.g., `LaunchConfiguration.exportSpec`, `Health.exportSpec`). Note: There may be no direct property-name match between clouddriver `ActiveServerGroup` and `ClusterSpec.ServerGroupSpec` (e.g., `launchConfiguration`, `health`, `scaling`, etc. differ). You may need to restructure this: build a "working" `ClusterSpec.ServerGroupSpec` from the base server group's sub-objects using `convert` on nested types (e.g., `LaunchConfiguration` to `LaunchConfigurationSpec`), apply the existing default-omission logic within those conversion functions, then use something like `buildSpecFromDiff` with a baseline "dummy" spec (e.g., `ClusterSpec.ServerGroupSpec()`) to omit default values. Since `ClusterSpec.ServerGroupSpec` differs from `TitusServerGroupSpec`, you may need to handle defaults manually or adjust the baseline. Ensure the overall goal of omitting defaults and generating overrides is achieved.
       - Replace the manual `generateOverrides` with a loop using `buildSpecFromDiff` against `defaults`.
       - Remove the now-unused `healthDiff` variable and any other dead code.

    7. **Fix YAML serialization** (in `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/serialization/ObjectMappers.kt`):
       - Modify `configuredYamlMapper()` to disable `YAMLGenerator.Feature.USE_NATIVE_TYPE_ID` (add `com.fasterxml.jackson.dataformat.yaml.YAMLGenerator.Feature.USE_NATIVE_TYPE_ID` import). This prevents the YAML mapper from emitting type information that was causing issues when serializing specs.

    8. **Update tests** (in `keel-titus-plugin/src/test/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/titus/resource/TitusClusterHandlerTests.kt`):
       - Adjust references to `spec.defaults.container.repository()` to use `spec.defaults.container!!.repository()`.
       - Add a new test asserting that default-valued fields (e.g., `constraints`, `entryPoint`, etc.) are null in `spec.defaults` after export.
       - Add assertions in the "export with overrides" context that the override spec omits default fields (e.g., `override.constraints` is null, `override.migrationPolicy` is null, etc.).

    9. **Review all imports and remove unused ones** across modified files.

    10. **Run formatting and ensure compilation**.

pr_chain.title: Return HTTP 404 when delivery config is not found
pr_chain.description:
When a client requests a delivery config that does not exist (e.g., GET `/delivery-configs/non-existent-config`), the `DeliveryConfigController` currently propagates an unhandled exception, causing Spinnaker to return a 500 Internal Server Error. The expected behavior for a missing resource is to return a 404 Not Found response.

    The `keel.persistence` package defines a `NoSuchDeliveryConfigException` that is thrown by the repository when a delivery config cannot be found. Your task is to handle this exception in the controller and map it to an HTTP 404 response, consistent with how `InvalidConstraintException` is already handled.

    Note: There is an existing `@ExceptionHandler(InvalidConstraintException::class)` method named `onNotFound` that also returns 404. You should rename this method to something more specific (e.g., `onConstraintNotFound`) to avoid ambiguity, and add a new handler for `NoSuchDeliveryConfigException`.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files for build and test configuration:
    - `build.gradle.kts` (root build script, defines module structure and dependencies)
    - `keel-web/keel-web.gradle.kts` (module-specific build config for the web service)
    - `gradle.properties` (gradle settings)
    - `.travis.yml` or `.github/workflows/pr.yml` (CI configuration showing how tests are typically run)
    - `README.md` for project overview

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `keel-web/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/rest/DeliveryConfigController.kt`.
    2. Add an import for `com.netflix.spinnaker.keel.persistence.NoSuchDeliveryConfigException`.
    3. Rename the existing `onNotFound` exception handler method to `onConstraintNotFound` (keeping its annotation and behavior for `InvalidConstraintException`).
    4. Add a new `@ExceptionHandler(NoSuchDeliveryConfigException::class)` method annotated with `@ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)` that logs the exception message at info level (mirroring the pattern of the existing handler).
    5. Verify the change compiles and the existing tests in the `keel-web` module still pass.

pr_chain.title: Align actuationInProgress method signature with generic ResourceHandler type
pr_chain.description:
Modify the `actuationInProgress` method in the `ResourceHandler` interface to use the generic type parameter `S` (the resource spec type) instead of an unconstrained generic type `T`. This change should be propagated to all implementations of this method across the various handler classes.

    Currently, the `ResourceHandler` abstract class defines `actuationInProgress` with a generic method type parameter (`<T : ResourceSpec>`), which does not align with the class-level generic type parameter `S`. This inconsistency requires implementors to perform unchecked casts when accessing the specific spec type.

    Update the method signature to use the class-level type parameter: `open suspend fun actuationInProgress(resource: Resource<S>): Boolean = false`.

    Then, update all override implementations to use their specific resource spec type:
    - `ImageHandler` should accept `Resource<ImageSpec>`
    - `ApplicationLoadBalancerHandler` should accept `Resource<ApplicationLoadBalancerSpec>`
    - `ClassicLoadBalancerHandler` should accept `Resource<ClassicLoadBalancerSpec>`
    - `ClusterHandler` should accept `Resource<ClusterSpec>`
    - `SecurityGroupHandler` should accept `Resource<SecurityGroupSpec>`
    - `TitusClusterHandler` should accept `Resource<TitusClusterSpec>`

    Remove the unnecessary unchecked casts in each implementation since the resource parameter will now be properly typed. Additionally, add a type-coercing extension function in `ResourceActuator` to handle calls with a wildcard-spec `Resource<*>`.

## Environment Setup
Check the `build.gradle.kts` file for build configuration, and look at `keel-plugin/keel-plugin.gradle.kts` and other module-level `.gradle.kts` files for module-specific dependencies. The `keel-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/plugin/ResourceHandler.kt` file contains the abstract class that needs modification. Tests are located in `keel-actuator/src/test/kotlin/` directory—the Gradle build files should contain test configuration.

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify the `actuationInProgress` method signature in `ResourceHandler.kt` to accept `Resource<S>` instead of the generic `<T : ResourceSpec> Resource<T>`.
    2. Update the method documentation to reference the resource parameter directly rather than an id/type description.
    3. In each handler implementation file (ImageHandler, ApplicationLoadBalancerHandler, ClassicLoadBalancerHandler, ClusterHandler, SecurityGroupHandler, TitusClusterHandler), change the override signature to use the specific spec type (e.g., `Resource<ImageSpec>`).
    4. Remove unnecessary type casts (e.g., `resource.spec as ImageSpec`) from the method bodies since the spec will now be properly typed.
    5. Add a private type-coercing extension function in `ResourceActuator.kt` (`actuationInProgress`) to handle calls on wildcard-spec resources, following the existing pattern for `desired`, `current`, `create`, and `update` methods.

pr_chain.title: Prevent deployment approval of artifacts with invalid statuses.
pr_chain.description: We need to ensure that versions of an artifact with an invalid status are never considered for deployment approval. The goal is to filter artifact versions based on the artifact's status information when querying for versions and when determining the latest approved version for an environment. This will prevent canary clusters or manual judgement requests from being initiated for artifacts that should not be allowed in a given environment due to their status.

We need to add some debug logging around image resolution to help troubleshoot why certain images are being selected or rejected. Also, there's a serialization issue where the versioning strategy for Debian artifacts is leaking into API responses — it should be write-only. Finally, we can clean up a stale TODO comment in the resource event code.

When a cluster references an artifact by reference instead of directly by artifact, the currently deployed image approver doesn't recognize it as an artifact-backed cluster, so the artifact version never gets marked as successfully deployed. We need the approver to also handle reference-based image providers by resolving the artifact from the delivery config, and move the ArtifactVersionDeployed event into the core events package since it's now used more broadly.

pr_chain.title: Add depends-on constraint support for Titus Docker image deployment tracking
pr_chain.description:
We need to add support for tracking currently deployed Docker image versions in Titus clusters so that the depends-on constraint can work for Titus resources, just as it does for EC2 clusters with deb artifacts.

    Currently, when a Titus cluster references an artifact via a `ReferenceProvider`, keel does not know which version of the referenced Docker image is actually deployed in the cluster. This means the depends-on constraint cannot evaluate whether a newer artifact version is safe to promote to downstream environments, because the "currently deployed" state is never recorded.

    The goal is to:
    1. Detect the currently deployed Docker image version when reading the current state of Titus clusters.
    2. Emit an `ArtifactVersionDeployed` event when the running image is identified so that the existing approval logic can mark that version as successfully deployed.
    3. Add a `CurrentlyDeployedDockerImageApprover` for Titus that mirrors the existing `CurrentlyDeployedImageApprover` for EC2 — it should resolve reference-based image providers against the delivery config and mark the deployed version as successfully deployed if it was already approved.

    Additionally, we can clean up the EC2 path by extracting the artifact-matching logic into a shared helper on `DeliveryConfig` so both EC2 and Titus use the same lookup with the correct artifact type.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files to understand how to install dependencies and run tests:
    - `build.gradle.kts` — build configuration and dependency management
    - `settings.gradle.kts` — module setup
    - `gradle.properties` — Gradle configuration
    - `gradlew` / `gradlew.bat` — Gradle wrapper for running builds/tests
    - `.github/workflows/pr.yml` — CI configuration showing test steps
    - `.travis.yml` — alternative CI config with install/test scripts
    - `gradle/installViaTravis.sh` — install script used in CI

## Implementation Plan
1. Add a shared `matchingArtifact` extension function on `DeliveryConfig` in `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/DeliveryConfig.kt` that looks up an artifact by reference and type, throwing `NoMatchingArtifactException` when not found.
    2. Update `keel-ec2-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/ec2/image/CurrentlyDeployedImageApprover.kt` to use the new shared helper instead of doing the lookup inline.
    3. Update `keel-titus-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/titus/cluster/TitusClusterHandler.kt`:
       - In the `getServerGroups` method, after retrieving active server groups, check if all returned server groups share the same container digest (i.e., a single version is deployed everywhere).
       - If so, look up the Docker image via `cloudDriverService.findDockerImages` to resolve the tag for that digest.
       - If found, publish an `ArtifactVersionDeployed` event with the resource ID, artifact version (tag), and provider `"titus"`.
    4. Create a new `CurrentlyDeployedDockerImageApprover` class in `keel-titus-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/titus/image/CurrentlyDeployedDockerImageApprover.kt`:
       - Listen for `ArtifactVersionDeployed` events.
       - For resources with a `TitusClusterSpec`, check if the default container is a `ReferenceProvider`.
       - Look up the matching Docker artifact in the delivery config using the new shared helper.
       - If the version is already approved for the environment, and not yet marked as successfully deployed, mark it as successfully deployed.
    5. Update existing tests in `keel-titus-plugin/src/test/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/titus/resource/TitusClusterHandlerTests.kt` to mock `findDockerImages` and verify the `ArtifactVersionDeployed` event is published when a consistent digest is found.
    6. Add new test coverage in `keel-titus-plugin/src/test/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/titus/image/CurrentlyDeployedDockerImageApproverTests.kt` for the new approver.

pr_chain.title: Enable environment-level locations inheritance for submitted resources
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to allow a `SubmittedEnvironment` to optionally declare a `locations` property. When a resource within that environment does not specify its own `locations`, the environment-level value should be automatically applied to the resource during JSON deserialization of the submitted delivery config. This avoids making the `locations` property nullable on resource specs and removes the need to look up the environment later to resolve locations. The environment-level locations should only be applied to resources within that environment and should not leak into the broader deserialization context. The `SubmittedEnvironment` model should retain the optional `locations` property even though the persisted `Environment` model does not need it — the value is applied to resources at parse time and then discarded.

## Environment Setup
Refer to the `README.md`, `build.gradle.kts`, and `gradle.properties` for project-level build and dependency setup. The `keel-core/keel-core.gradle.kts` file describes the module-specific build configuration. The `gradlew` script is the Gradle wrapper, and the `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties` pins the Gradle version.

## Implementation Plan
1.  In `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/DeliveryConfig.kt`:
        *   Add a `@JsonDeserialize` annotation to the `SubmittedEnvironment` data class, referencing a new custom deserializer class (e.g., `SubmittedEnvironmentDeserializer`).
        *   Add an optional `locations` property of type `SubnetAwareLocations?` with a default value of `null` to the `SubmittedEnvironment` constructor.
    2.  In `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/Locatable.kt`:
        *   Annotate the `locations` property in the `Locatable` interface with `@get:JacksonInject("locations")` so that Jackson can inject a value from the deserialization context if present in the JSON is absent.
    3.  Create a new file `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/serialization/DeserializationContexts.kt`:
        *   Add an internal extension property `DeserializationContext.mapper` that returns the `ObjectMapper` from the parser's codec.
        *   Add an internal inline function `DeserializationContext.instantiationException` to wrap instantiation errors.
    4.  Create a new file `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/serialization/SubmittedEnvironmentDeserializer.kt`:
        *   Implement `StdNodeBasedDeserializer<SubmittedEnvironment>`.
        *   In the `convert` method, parse the `name`, `constraints`, `notifications`, and optional `locations` from the JSON root node using the context's `ObjectMapper`.
        *   Create a copy of the `ObjectMapper`, and set its `injectableValues` to include a map with key `"locations"` and the parsed (possibly null) environment-level locations.
        *   Use this copied mapper to deserialize the `resources` set, which will cause the `@JacksonInject` on the `Locatable.locations` property to be populated with the environment-level value when the resource JSON does not contain its own `locations`.
        *   Construct the `SubmittedEnvironment` instance with the parsed values.
        *   Ensure errors during parsing or construction are wrapped in an appropriate `JsonMappingException`.
    5.  Refactor `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/serialization/SubmittedResourceDeserializer.kt`:
        *   Remove the now-duplicated `private val DeserializationContext.mapper` and `private inline fun <reified T> DeserializationContext.instantiationException` since they are now provided by the new `DeserializationContexts.kt` file in the same package.
    6.  Add a new test file `keel-core/src/test/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/serialization/SubmittedEnvironmentDeserializerTests.kt` covering:
        *   Successful deserialization when `locations` is present on a resource spec (the resource-specific value should be used).
        *   Successful deserialization when `locations` is omitted from the resource spec (the environment-level value should be inherited).
        *   Validation of the inheritance behavior ensuring the resource's `locations` matches the environment's.

pr_chain.title: Implement flexible region staggering for multi-region EC2 cluster deployments
pr_chain.description:
Add support for staggered deployments of multi-region EC2 clusters. When a cluster's deployment strategy specifies a stagger list with per-region time windows (`hours`) and/or pause durations (`pauseTime`), orchestration tasks for each region must be submitted sequentially, with each subsequent region waiting for the prior region's deployment to complete, respecting the configured time windows.

    Regions not listed in the stagger configuration should deploy in parallel only after all staggered regions have completed. In-place changes (e.g., capacity or scaling policy updates) should continue to be applied immediately without staggering. Also, validate that `hours` values in stagger entries contain a single range (e.g., "9-17") rather than comma-separated values or multiple ranges.

pr_chain.title: Support top-level service account in delivery config diffs
pr_chain.description: We need to ensure that the ad hoc diff calculation correctly incorporates a service account defined at the delivery config level when computing resource diffs. Currently, resources within environments only receive service account metadata if it's defined per-resource, causing diffs to fail or behave incorrectly when the account is set at the delivery config root. The goal is to propagate the delivery config's top-level service account into each resource's metadata before performing diff calculations.

pr_chain.title: Return deleted delivery config from delete endpoint for client confirmation
pr_chain.description: We need the DELETE endpoint for delivery configs to return the deleted configuration in its response body. Currently the endpoint returns no content, but since we already fetch the delivery config before deletion, it would be helpful to return it so callers have confirmation of what was removed. Update the endpoint to return the DeliveryConfig object rather than void.

pr_chain.title: Relocate Jackson serialization tests to the API-Jackson module
pr_chain.description: Move the ConstraintTests and DeliveryArtifactTests from the core module to the API-Jackson module, where they more logically belong alongside the Jackson serialization code they test. Ensure the API-Jackson module has the necessary test dependencies to support these relocated tests, including access to the configured object mapper.

pr_chain.title: Publish deployment events for all image tags matching a digest
pr_chain.description:
We need to fix an issue in the Titus cluster handler where deployment events are not being published for all applicable image tags. Currently, when checking if a deployed server group's image digest matches a known image, the code only looks for the first matching image and publishes an event for that single tag. This is problematic because container registries can have multiple tags pointing to the same digest (e.g., `latest`, version tags, or commit-based tags).

    The consequence is that clusters using a tag that isn't the first match returned won't be marked as "deployed." This breaks the promotion flow, as downstream stages rely on these deployment events to know when an artifact version has been successfully deployed.

    The fix should ensure that for each image tag associated with the deployed digest, we publish a separate `ArtifactVersionDeployed` event. This way, regardless of which tag users reference in their delivery configuration, the event is emitted and the cluster is correctly marked as deployed.

## Environment Setup
Review the repository's build configuration files to understand how to install dependencies and run tests:
    - `build.gradle.kts` (root build file with module configuration)
    - `keel-titus-plugin/keel-titus-plugin.gradle.kts` (module-specific build config)
    - `settings.gradle.kts` (module list)
    - `.github/workflows/pr.yml` and `.travis.yml` (CI configuration showing test invocation)
    - `gradle.properties` (Gradle properties)

## Implementation Plan
- Locate the `getServerGroups` method in `keel-titus-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/titus/cluster/TitusClusterHandler.kt`.
    - Modify the code that fetches Docker images to filter all images matching the deployed container digest instead of using `find` to get only the first match.
    - Replace the single event publication with a loop that iterates over all matching images and publishes an `ArtifactVersionDeployed` event for each tag.
    - Add an inline comment explaining why we publish an event for every matching tag (e.g., handling cases like `latest` where multiple tags share the same digest).
    - Verify the logic handles the case where no images match (no events published) and where multiple images match (multiple events published).

pr_chain.title: Fix duplicate resource error message to show correct environment mapping
pr_chain.description:
When a delivery config contains resources with duplicate IDs across environments, the validation logic in `ResourcePersister` should produce an error message that clearly identifies which environments contain the duplicated resources. Currently, the logic that filters environments to only those containing duplicates is broken — it uses `filter` which returns a new list, but the result is discarded, so the subsequent `isNotEmpty()` check always sees the full unfiltered list. This means the error message incorrectly includes environments that don't actually contain any duplicate resources.

    The goal is to fix the environment filtering logic so the error message accurately reports only the environments (and their resource IDs) that contain duplicates. This will make the `DuplicateResourceIdException` message useful for debugging configuration issues.

    Please update the filtering logic in the `validate` method of `ResourcePersister.kt` to correctly modify the mutable list in place, so that only environments with duplicate resources remain in the map used to build the error message.

## Environment Setup
Check `build.gradle.kts` and `keel-core/keel-core.gradle.kts` for build configuration and dependency management. The `.travis.yml` file contains CI build and test setup. Review `README.md` files for any additional setup instructions. The Gradle wrapper (`gradlew`/`gradlew.bat`) is present for building and testing.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/actuation/ResourcePersister.kt`.
    2. Locate the `validate` method and find the block that filters `envToResources`.
    3. Change the `filterValues` lambda parameter type from `List<String>` to `MutableList<String>`.
    4. Replace the `rs.filter { it in duplicates }` call with `rs.removeIf { it !in duplicates }` — this mutates the list in place, removing all resource IDs that are not in the duplicates list.
    5. After the `removeIf` call, the subsequent `rs.isNotEmpty()` check will correctly evaluate whether any resources remain in that environment's list (meaning the environment contains duplicates).
    6. The resulting `envsAndDuplicateResources` map will only contain environments that actually have duplicate resources, producing an accurate error message.

pr_chain.title: Improve OpenAPI rendering for nullable properties and descriptions
pr_chain.description:
The API documentation generated by springdoc-openapi for Keel's REST endpoints is missing important details that consumers need:

    1. **Nullable/optional properties**: The generated schemas don't consistently reflect which Kotlin properties are nullable or optional. Properties with default values or marked as nullable in the Kotlin types should appear as non-required and explicitly `nullable: true` in the OpenAPI output. Currently, only non-nullable properties without defaults are correctly marked as required, but nullable properties are not being explicitly marked, and the `nullable` attribute isn't being set on individual property schemas.

    2. **Property/class descriptions**: Several key models (e.g., `SubmittedResource`, `SubmittedEnvironment`) lack human-readable descriptions in the generated API docs. We want to add descriptions to classes and properties to make the API more self-documenting.

    3. **Polymorphic types**: The `DeliveryArtifact` type is used in several places but its subtypes (`DebianArtifact`, `DockerArtifact`) aren't registered in the API docs, so the schema just shows a generic `DeliveryArtifact` reference without indicating the possible subtypes.

    4. **Java time types**: Properties using Java time types like `Instant`, `Duration`, `LocalDate` etc. aren't being rendered as strings with the appropriate `format` (e.g., `date-time`, `date`, `duration`). The current customizer tries to modify the schema in place, but this doesn't work reliably — the return value is ignored by the framework.

    5. **Compatibility with springdoc-openapi 1.2.32**: Upgrading the springdoc-openapi dependency to 1.2.32 changes some behavior around `$ref` handling. Properties that are references to other schemas can't have extra attributes like `description` directly on the `$ref` schema — they need to be wrapped in `allOf`. The existing customizers need to be updated to handle this.

    The goal is to make the generated OpenAPI spec at `/v3/api-docs` accurate and useful: correct `nullable` flags on properties, clear `required` lists, descriptive text on important models and properties, proper subtype registration for polymorphic types, and correct rendering of Java time types.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's `build.gradle.kts` and `settings.gradle.kts` for the overall build configuration. The `keel-web/keel-web.gradle.kts` file contains the dependencies for the web module where the OpenAPI generation happens. The `gradle.properties` file may contain property versions. There's also a `Makefile` and `.travis.yml` that can provide hints on standard build/test commands.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Define custom annotations** in `keel-api/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/docs/`:
       - Create a `Description` annotation that can target classes and properties, with a `value` parameter for the description text.
       - Create an `Optional` annotation for properties that should be marked as optional in the API docs, even if they look required based on their Kotlin type or constructor parameters.

    2. **Refactor the schema customizer infrastructure** in `keel-web/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/apidocs/`:
       - Create an `AbstractSchemaCustomizer` base class that extends `BaseModelConverter` and provides a hook to customize a schema whether it's being resolved directly or as a reference. It should look up the referenced schema in the context's defined models when `isResolveAsRef` is true.
       - Refactor `KotlinOptionalPropertyConverter` to extend `AbstractSchemaCustomizer`. In its `customize` method, it should:
         - Determine required/optional properties by inspecting the Kotlin constructor parameters (using `JsonCreator` or primary constructor).
         - For each property schema, set `nullable` based on whether the Kotlin type is marked nullable.
         - Mark required properties in the schema's `required` list and ensure optional properties are removed from that list.
       - Create `ApiAnnotationModelConverter` that also extends `AbstractSchemaCustomizer`. It should:
         - Read `@Description` annotations from classes and properties and apply them to the schema. If a property schema is a `$ref`, wrap it in `allOf` with a schema containing the description.
         - Read `@Optional` annotations and mark the property as optional (removing from required list).
         - Ensure proper ordering: `KotlinOptionalPropertyConverter` should run first (highest precedence) and `ApiAnnotationModelConverter` last (lowest precedence).

    3. **Fix Java time property rendering**:
       - Update `JavaTimePropertyCustomizer` to return a new `StringSchema` with the appropriate `format` instead of trying to modify the existing schema in place, since the return value is what matters.

    4. **Register polymorphic subtypes**:
       - Update `SubtypesModelConverter` to use the `rawClass` extension instead of checking for `TypeBase` directly.
       - Add `DeliveryArtifactModelConverter` that extends `SubtypesModelConverter<DeliveryArtifact>` and registers `DebianArtifact` and `DockerArtifact` as subtypes.

    5. **Add the `rawClass` extension** in `_apidocs.kt`:
       - Replace the existing `baseType` extension with `rawClass` that correctly extracts the raw class from `TypeBase`, `ParameterizedType`, or a plain `Class`.

    6. **Annotate models with descriptions**:
       - Add `@Description` annotations to `SubmittedResource`, `SubmittedResource` properties, and `SubmittedEnvironment.locations`.
       - Add `@Optional` to `ClusterSpec.locations` since it's optional in practice even though it's non-nullable in the type.
       - Add a `@SwaggerRequestBody` description to the `upsert` method in `DeliveryConfigController`.

    7. **Add helper functions** for marking required/optional in `_apidocs.kt`:
       - `markRequired(property)` and `markOptional(property)` functions on `Schema`.

    8. **Rename the test file** from `ApiTests.kt` to `ApiDocTests.kt` and update/add tests to verify the new behavior.

pr_chain.title: Ensure resource deletion also removes associated diff fingerprint records
pr_chain.description: Fix resource deletion to also clean up diff fingerprint records associated with the resource. Currently, deleting a resource or deleting all resources for an application leaves orphaned diff fingerprint data in the database. The deletion logic must be updated so both individual resource deletion and application-wide deletion remove the corresponding diff fingerprint entries.

pr_chain.title: Enforce unique artifact references in delivery config validation
pr_chain.description:
We need to strengthen validation of delivery configurations to ensure that all artifacts within a single config have unique references. Currently, when a user submits a delivery config where two different artifacts share the same reference value (e.g., two Docker images both using reference "my-artifact"), the config is accepted and persisted, which can lead to ambiguous artifact resolution downstream.

    The goal is to add a validation check that rejects any delivery config containing duplicate artifact references. When this validation fails, the API should return a 400 Bad Request with a clear error message identifying which artifacts share duplicate references, similar to how we already handle duplicate resource IDs.

    Additionally, the existing exception hierarchy should be cleaned up so that `ValidationException` is properly abstracted and shared by both `DuplicateResourceIdException` and the new `DuplicateArtifactReferenceException`. The exception handler in keel-web should also be updated to catch all `ValidationException` subtypes uniformly, ensuring both duplicate resource ID and duplicate artifact reference failures return the appropriate HTTP status code.

    Please also add test coverage in the combined repository tests that verifies:
    - A delivery config with duplicate artifact references throws the appropriate exception
    - No partial data is persisted when validation fails

## Environment Setup
Check `build.gradle.kts` for the Gradle build configuration, the various module `.gradle.kts` files for module-specific dependencies, and `keel-core-test/README.md` for information about shared test infrastructure. The project uses Gradle with Kotlin DSL.

## Implementation Plan
1. Create a new `DuplicateArtifactReferenceException` class in the `keel-core` module that extends `ValidationException`, with a message that clearly identifies the duplicate references and the artifacts involved.
    2. Extract `ValidationException` into its own file in `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/exceptions/` so it can be shared across exception types.
    3. Add a validation check in `CombinedRepository.validate()` that collects all artifact references from the delivery config, detects any duplicates, and throws `DuplicateArtifactReferenceException` when found.
    4. Update the `ExceptionHandler` in `keel-web` to handle `ValidationException` (or its subtypes) rather than solely `DuplicateResourceIdException`, ensuring both validation failures return 400 Bad Request.
    5. Add test cases in `CombinedRepositoryTests` covering duplicate artifact references, verifying the exception type and that no resources/artifacts are persisted on failure.

pr_chain.title: Add Orca task details to resource task outcome events
pr_chain.description:
We need to enrich `ResourceTaskFailed` and `ResourceTaskSucceeded` events with the associated Orca task metadata (task id and task name). This is required so Deck can parse and display this information in the resource history view.

    The goal is to include the Orca task details in these two event types so consumers can correlate a resource event with the specific Orca task that caused it. Since a single resource operation corresponds to exactly one Orca task at the point these events are emitted, the task data should be stored as a single-element list to keep the schema consistent with other event types that already carry task lists (e.g., `ResourceActuationLaunched`).

    Please note that the `Task` data class already exists in `keel-core` (in `com.netflix.spinnaker.keel.api.actuation`) and is used by related event types — you should reuse it rather than creating a new model.

## Environment Setup
This is a Gradle-based Kotlin project. Consult the following files to understand how to set up dependencies and run tests:
    - `build.gradle.kts` (root build configuration, includes dependency management)
    - `settings.gradle.kts` (module structure and included projects)
    - `keel-orca/keel-orca.gradle.kts` (module-specific dependencies, especially for the orca module)
    - `gradle.properties` (project-wide Gradle configuration)
    - `.github/workflows/pr.yml` or `.travis.yml` (CI configuration showing the standard build and test workflow)

## Implementation Plan
1. **Update `ResourceEvent.kt`** in `keel-core/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/events/`:
       - Add a `val tasks: List<Task>` property to the `ResourceTaskFailed` data class (the `Task` type is already imported from `com.netflix.spinnaker.keel.api.actuation`).
       - Add a `val tasks: List<Task>` property to the `ResourceTaskSucceeded` data class.
       - Update the secondary constructors of both classes to accept a `tasks: List<Task>` parameter and pass it to the primary constructor.
       - Ensure the new parameter position matches the pattern used in the existing diff (insert before `timestamp`).

    2. **Update `OrcaTaskMonitorAgent.kt`** in `keel-orca/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/orca/`:
       - Import the `Task` class from `com.netflix.spinnaker.keel.api.actuation`.
       - When publishing a `ResourceTaskSucceeded` event, construct it with `listOf(Task(taskDetails.id, taskDetails.name))`.
       - When publishing a `ResourceTaskFailed` event, construct it with `listOf(Task(taskDetails.id, taskDetails.name))` as well.
       - Note that `taskDetails` here refers to the `ExecutionDetailResponse` object from Orca — it already exposes `id` and `name` properties.

    3. **Update `OrcaTaskMonitorAgentTests.kt`** in `keel-orca/src/test/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/orca/`:
       - Import `com.netflix.spinnaker.keel.api.actuation.Task`.
       - Create a `Task` fixture instance with appropriate id and name values.
       - Update all existing instantiations of `ResourceTaskFailed` and `ResourceTaskSucceeded` to include the new `tasks` parameter (passing a list containing the task fixture).
       - Add test assertions to verify that the published events contain the expected task id/name when the event is reconstructed from history.

pr_chain.title: Tolerate missing task references when deserializing resource event records
pr_chain.description: We need to ensure that existing persisted resource event records of type `ResourceTaskSucceeded` and `ResourceTaskFailed` can still be deserialized correctly even when they don't contain task reference data. Older records may lack this field, and currently deserialization fails for them. The task is to make the `tasks` field optional/nullable so these legacy events can be read without errors.

pr_chain.title: Fix export API to resolve resource kinds with versioned formats
pr_chain.description:
The export API in `ExportController` currently constructs a `ResourceKind` by parsing a resource type string and then looks up a `ResourceHandler` for that exact kind. However, resource kinds in Spinnaker now include an API version component (e.g., `test/whatever@v1`), and the current logic does not account for this. In particular:

    - The `typeToKind` mapping and the `parseKind` call do not handle version suffixes like `@v1`.
    - When the version is omitted from a request, the controller should default to the handler that supports the latest version for the given group and type, rather than failing to find a match.

    The goal is to make the export API backwards-compatible with the old resource kind format (where no version was specified) while also supporting the new versioned format. This means:

    1. The controller should be able to parse a kind from a cloud provider and a type, optionally including a version suffix (e.g., `cluster@v1`).
    2. If no version is provided, it should determine the latest supported version by examining the available `ResourceHandler`s for that group and type.
    3. The lookup logic in `ResourceHandler.kt` should be extended to support finding handlers by group and unqualified kind, in addition to the existing exact-match lookup.

    Please ensure the existing tests are updated to reflect the new versioned resource kind format (e.g., `test/whatever@v1`) and add coverage for the new parsing/defaulting behavior.

## Environment Setup
This is a Kotlin/Gradle project. The build configuration is in `build.gradle.kts` at the repository root, and module-specific dependencies are in each module's `*.gradle.kts` file (e.g., `keel-web/keel-web.gradle.kts`). Test configuration and runner setup can be inferred from the Gradle files and the existing test source layouts in modules like `keel-web/src/test/`. Check `gradle.properties` and the `gradle/` directory for project-wide settings and CI scripts (e.g., `gradle/buildViaTravis.sh` or `.travis.yml`).

## Implementation Plan
1. **Modify `ResourceHandler.kt`** (`keel-api/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/plugins/ResourceHandler.kt`):
       - Add a new `supporting(group: String, unqualifiedKind: String)` function that returns a `List<ResourceHandler<*, *>>` of all handlers matching the given group and kind (i.e., without version). Throw `UnsupportedKind` if the list is empty.
       - Update the existing `supporting(kind: ResourceKind)` function to use the new overload internally if appropriate, and adjust the `UnsupportedKind` exception class to accept a `String` (with a secondary constructor taking `ResourceKind`).

    2. **Update test utilities** (`keel-test/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/test/Resources.kt`):
       - Replace the `TEST_API` constant with `TEST_API_V1 = ApiVersion("test", "1")` and add `TEST_API_V2 = ApiVersion("test", "2")`.
       - Update `DummyResourceHandler` to `DummyResourceHandlerV1` (using `TEST_API_V1`) and add `DummyResourceHandlerV2` (using `TEST_API_V2`).

    3. **Modify `ExportController.kt`** (`keel-web/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/rest/ExportController.kt`):
       - Add a `parseKind(cloudProvider: String, type: String)` function that:
         - Lowercases the type.
         - Extracts an optional version suffix (e.g., `@v1`) from the type string.
         - Applies the existing `typeToKind` mapping to the base type.
         - Determines the API group from `cloudProviderOverrides` (or falls back to the raw `cloudProvider`).
         - If no version was specified, uses the new `handlers.supporting(group, normalizedType)` function to find all candidate handlers and selects the one with the highest version using a proper version comparator (e.g., `DefaultArtifactVersion` from Maven). If no version can be determined, throws an error.
         - Returns a `ResourceKind` built from `group`, `normalizedType`, and the resolved version.
       - Update the `get()` method to use the new `parseKind` and pass the resulting `kind` to the export logic.

    4. **Adjust `ResourceKind` handling**:
       - Review `keel-api/src/main/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/api/ResourceKind.kt` (not in the diff but referenced) to understand the `parseKind` companion function and ensure the new code produces a valid `ResourceKind` string format (`group/kind@vN`).

    5. **Update downstream tests and fixtures** that reference `TEST_API` or `DummyResourceHandler` to use the new v1 constants/classes (e.g., in `CombinedRepositoryTests.kt`, `DummyResourceTypeIdentifier.kt`, `DeliveryConfigTransactionTests.kt`, `DummyResourceConfiguration.kt`, `ExceptionHandlerTests.kt`, and `DeliveryConfigControllerTests.kt`).

    6. **Add new tests** in `keel-web/src/test/kotlin/com/netflix/spinnaker/keel/rest/ExportControllerTests.kt`:
       - Test that `parseKind("test", "whatever")` returns a kind with the latest version (`v2`).
       - Test that `parseKind("test", "whatever@v1")` returns a kind with the specified version (`v1`).

    7. **Add Maven artifact dependency** to `keel-web/keel-web.gradle.kts` for `org.apache.maven:maven-artifact:3.6.3` to use `DefaultArtifactVersion` for version comparison.

instruction:
## Add a reusable buffered queue with deduplication for storage backends

The project needs a reusable buffered queue component that storage implementations can use to batch calls to their `Add` methods. This queue should:
    - Accept entries to be added and return a function that provides the assigned log index (or an error) once the entry is sequenced.
    - Automatically flush entries when either the queue reaches a configured maximum size or the oldest entry reaches a configured maximum age.
    - Flush entries in FIFO order.
    - Silently de-duplicate identical entries added between flushes, returning the same assigned index (or error) to all duplicate callers. Deduplication is best-effort and only applies to entries currently in-flight in the queue.
    - The flush function receives a context and a slice of entries and returns the index of the first entry in the batch. The queue will assign sequential indices to the rest of the batch.
    - Be designed as a mix-in, allowing storage implementations to embed it.

## Environment Setup
Check the `go.mod` file for module dependencies and the Go version. Refer to the `.github/workflows/go_test.yml` and `.github/workflows/golangci-lint.yml` for the CI pipeline. The repository root also contains a `Makefile` (if present) that may define standard commands. Use standard Go tooling (`go mod tidy`, `go test`, `go vet`) as per the repository conventions.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Add the queue file**: Create `storage/queue.go`.
    2. **Define the `Queue` struct**: It should hold a buffer (using the `github.com/globocom/go-buffer` library), a `FlushFunc`, and an in-flight map for deduplication, protected by a mutex.
    3. **Define supporting types**:
       - `type IndexFunc func() (idx uint64, err error)` - a function that returns the assigned index for a queued entry.
       - `type FlushFunc func(ctx context.Context, entries [][]byte) (index uint64, err error)` - a function that flushes a batch of entries.
    4. **Implement `NewQueue`**: A constructor that takes `maxAge time.Duration`, `maxSize uint`, and a `FlushFunc`. It initializes the buffer with the specified size and flush interval, and the flush handler to the queue's internal `doFlush` method.
    5. **Implement `Add`**:
       - Accept a `context.Context` and a `[]byte` entry.
       - Use a helper `squashDupes` to check if the entry is already in-flight. If it is, return the existing `IndexFunc` without adding it again. If not, create a new in-flight entry and push it to the buffer.
       - Return an `IndexFunc` that, when called, will block until the entry's index is assigned (via the flush) and return it.
    6. **Implement the in-flight entry struct**:
       - It should contain the original entry bytes, a channel to communicate the assigned index/error, and methods to assign the index and to provide the `IndexFunc`.
    7. **Implement `doFlush`**:
       - Called by the buffer's flusher.
       - Take the slice of entries (which are the in-flight entry structs).
       - Call the provided `FlushFunc` with the underlying byte slices.
       - For each entry in the batch, assign the sequential index (starting from the returned index) or the returned error.
       - Clean up the in-flight map for flushed entries to allow future deduplication.
    8. **Handle errors**: If `buf.Push` returns an error (e.g., queue is closed), immediately assign that error to the entry's channel.
    9. **Update `go.mod`**: Add the `github.com/globocom/go-buffer` dependency and ensure `go.sum` is updated via `go mod tidy`.

pr_chain.description: Add tile reading support to the MySQL storage implementation. This means adding a ReadTile method to fetch stored subtrees by level and index, creating the corresponding Subtree table in the schema, and exposing a GET endpoint in the example MySQL server that handles both full and partial tile requests. The endpoint should parse the level/index/width from the URL path, return 404 when the tile doesn't exist, and only set a long-lived Cache-Control header when the returned tile is complete (matches the requested width).

pr_chain.title: Refactor GCP storage to use Tessera API formats for tiles and entries
pr_chain.description:
The GCP storage implementation currently handles tiles and entry bundles using raw byte slices and manual serialization logic. It manually flattens and splits tile data into fixed-size hash arrays, and uses a custom `tileSuffix` function for partial tiles. The goal is to refactor this implementation to use the standardized Tessera API types (`api.HashTile` and `api.EntryBundle`) which provide `MarshalText`/`UnmarshalText` methods for consistent serialization.

    Specifically, you need to:
    1. Modify the `setTile` method to accept an `*api.HashTile` instead of `[][]byte`, and use its `MarshalText` method to serialize the tile data before storing it.
    2. Modify the `getTile` method to return an `*api.HashTile` instead of `[][]byte`, using `UnmarshalText` to deserialize the stored data.
    3. Add a new `getEntryBundle` method that retrieves and deserializes an `*api.EntryBundle` from the object store using `layout.EntriesPath`.
    4. Update the error handling to wrap `os.ErrNotExist` with the object name for better context.
    5. Remove the now-unnecessary `tileSuffix` function and related imports (`crypto/sha256`, `slices`).
    6. Update the tests to use the new API types and add a roundtrip test for entry bundles.

## Environment Setup
Check `go.mod` for module dependencies. Review the existing test patterns in `storage/gcp/gcp_test.go` and the API type definitions in the `api/` directory (e.g., `api/state.go` or related files) to understand the available data structures and serialization methods. The repo uses standard Go tooling; you can run tests with `go test ./storage/gcp/`.

## Implementation Plan
1. Examine the `api.HashTile` and `api.EntryBundle` types in the `api` package to understand their structure and available `MarshalText`/`UnmarshalText` methods.
    2. Modify `storage/gcp/gcp.go` to import the `api` package and update the signatures of `setTile` and `getTile` to use `*api.HashTile` instead of `[][]byte`.
    3. Update the implementation of `setTile` to call `tile.MarshalText()` for serialization, and `getTile` to call `UnmarshalText` on a new `api.HashTile` instance.
    4. Add a new `getEntryBundle` method that reads an object using `layout.EntriesPath` and deserializes it into an `*api.EntryBundle`.
    5. Wrap `os.ErrNotExist` errors with the object name for better debugging, and remove the `tileSuffix` function and unused imports (`crypto/sha256`, `slices`).
    6. Update `storage/gcp/gcp_test.go`: change `makeTile` to return `*api.HashTile`, add a `makeBundle` helper, add a `TestBundleRoundtrip` test, and remove the now-obsolete `TestTileSuffix` test.

We need to add the ability to consume previously sequenced entries from the GCP sequencer. Please extend the sequencer interface to include a consumeEntries method that retrieves batches of sequenced entries, calls a provided callback with them, and marks them as consumed once the callback succeeds. Also add a background loop in Storage that periodically calls consumeEntries. Update the interface docs and add a round-trip test covering assign then consume behavior.

pr_chain.title: Add storage options for checkpoint signing and batch configuration
pr_chain.description: Implement configurable storage options that allow callers to specify a checkpoint signer and batching parameters. Add a checkpoint signing function that formats and signs standard tlog checkpoints using a provided note signer, and integrate these options into the GCP storage implementation so checkpoints are written during integration when a signer is configured.

pr_chain.title: Reduce integration latency by skipping reads of non-existent future tiles
pr_chain.description: We need to optimize the tile integration process by avoiding unnecessary storage reads for tiles that are beyond the current tree size boundaries. During integration runs, the visitor pattern can request tiles that likely don't exist yet since they represent positions beyond the current tree extent, and fetching these serially adds significant latency to the overall process. We should detect when a tile implies a larger tree size than what we're integrating at and skip the read attempt, since such tiles very probably don't exist and skipping them would reduce integration time by roughly 25%.

pr_chain.title: Add GCS read proxy to example GCP personality
pr_chain.description:
We need to make it easy for load testing tools (like the hammer) to read log contents from the example GCP personality. Currently the example server only handles writes (`POST /add`), so external tools can't read back the tiles and checkpoints that are stored in GCS. 

    The goal is to add a simple HTTP read proxy to `cmd/example-gcp/main.go` that forwards `GET` requests for checkpoints and tile paths to GCS storage. This is only a temporary debugging/testing convenience, so it should be clearly marked as such.

    Specifically:
    - Add a new public method `Get` on the GCP storage type (`storage/gcp/gcp.go`) that retrieves an object from GCS by path.
    - In the example server (`cmd/example-gcp/main.go`), register HTTP handlers that call this `Get` method for `GET /checkpoint` and `GET /tile/` routes, returning the raw bytes with a 200 status on success.
    - On error, return a 400 status with the error message in the response body.

## Environment Setup
Check `go.mod` for module name and Go version. The repository is a standard Go module with a `Makefile` absent, but you can look at `.github/workflows/go_test.yml` for how tests are run in CI and `.github/workflows/golangci-lint.yml` for linting. The storage tests are in `storage/gcp/gcp_test.go`.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `storage/gcp/gcp.go`. After the `Add` method, add a new public method:
       - `Get(ctx context.Context, path string) ([]byte, error)` — this should call `s.objStore.getObject(ctx, path)` and return the data and error. This method is intended for proxy/debug use only, so add a comment noting that.
    2. Open `cmd/example-gcp/main.go`. Add `"strings"` to the import block.
    3. In `main()`, after the existing `POST /add` handler, define a closure `serveGCS` that:
       - Uses `strings.TrimLeft(r.URL.Path, "/")` to get the resource path (relative to the bucket root).
       - Calls `storage.Get(r.Context(), resource)`.
       - On error: logs with `klog.V(1).Infof` and writes a 400 status with a message like `fmt.Sprintf("Get: %v", err)`.
       - On success: writes the bytes to the response writer.
    4. Register two routes with `http.HandleFunc`:
       - `"GET /checkpoint"` → `serveGCS`
       - `"GET /tile/"` → `serveGCS`
    5. Add a `// TODO: remove this proxy` comment above the `serveGCS` definition to mark it as temporary.

pr_chain.title: Add support for CT Static API entry formatting and sequencing
pr_chain.description:
We need to enable Tessera to support building a [CT Static API](https://c2sp.org/ct-static-api) log personality. There are two key differences from the current tlog-tiles approach that need accommodation:

    1. **Entry bundle formatting differs**: The current `EntryBundle` marshaling uses a big-endian uint16 length-prefix scheme as specified by [tlog-tiles](https://c2sp.org/tlog-tiles). The CT Static API specification instead uses raw, self-describing entry data with no length prefix. We need to support both formats without breaking existing non-CT functionality.

    2. **Entries must know their own index at marshaling time**: For CT, the SCT returned to the submitter contains the entry's sequence number in the log. To maintain RFC6962 compatibility, this index must be embedded in the Merkle leaf itself. This means the leaf data and Merkle leaf hash may not be known until after sequencing has assigned an index.

    The goal is to:
    - Make it hard or impossible to build new transparency log ecosystems that attempt to use these CT-specific patterns outside of the CT ecosystem.
    - Contain changes as close as possible to the personality layer rather than spreading CT-specific logic throughout the core.
    - Ensure non-CT logs don't pay a performance cost because this support exists.
    - Contain changes to the sequencing side, leaving integration concerned only with managing Merkle tree specifics.

    Key architectural changes needed:
    - `Entry` needs an internal function that knows how to serialize itself into bundle format, with the index as a parameter, since the CT-specific format depends on the assigned index.
    - The storage queue's `FlushFunc` must be responsible for calling each entry's bundle marshaling function during sequencing, before integration into the tree.
    - The integration layer (`TreeBuilder.Integrate`) should work with pre-sequenced entries containing both the bundle-formatted data and the leaf hash, rather than raw `Entry` objects.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files in the repository root for build, dependency, and test configuration:
    - `go.mod` — module dependencies
    - `.github/workflows/go_test.yml` — CI test workflow configuration
    - `.github/workflows/golangci-lint.yml` — linting workflow configuration
    - `CONTRIBUTING.md` — contribution guidelines
  
    The `testdata/` directory contains pre-generated log data used by some tests.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Modify `Entry` struct** (`entry.go`):
       - Add a `marshalForBundle func(index uint64) []byte` field to `Entry`.
       - Change `NewEntry` to return `*Entry` instead of `Entry`.
       - Remove the `MarshalBinary`/`UnmarshalBinary` methods and their gob dependency, replacing with a new `MarshalBundleData(index uint64) []byte` method that sets the entry's index and delegates to the internal marshaling function.
       - For default (non-CT) entries, the internal marshaling function should produce the tlog-tiles format: big-endian uint16 length prefix followed by data bytes.
       - Remove the old `IndexFunc`/`MarshalBinary` references.

    2. **Create CT-only support package** (`ctonly/ct.go`):
       - Add a new package `ctonly` containing a CT-specific `Entry` type with fields for timestamp, precertificate status, certificate data, etc.
       - Implement `LeafData(idx uint64) []byte` that produces the CT log entry format per RFC6962, including the index embedded in the `CtExtensions` field.
       - Implement `MerkleLeafHash(leafIndex uint64) []byte` that produces the RFC6962 Merkle leaf hash including the timestamped entry structure with the index extension.

    3. **Add CT-only top-level support** (`ct_only.go`):
       - Define a minimal `Storage` interface with an `Add(ctx, *Entry) (uint64, error)` method.
       - Add `NewCertificateTransparencySequencedWriter(s Storage) func(ctx, *ctonly.Entry) (uint64, error)` that converts CT entries to internal `Entry` objects with the appropriate `marshalForBundle` function which computes the leaf data and hash at sequencing time using the assigned index.
       - Include prominent comments warning that this MUST ONLY be used for CT logs, not as a basis for other transparency applications.

    4. **Update storage queue** (`storage/queue.go`):
       - Change `FlushFunc` signature to `func(ctx context.Context, entries []*tessera.Entry) error` — the storage implementation must call each entry's `MarshalBundleData` with the assigned index before attempting integration.
       - Remove the old `IndexFunc` type, replacing with a `Future` type `func() (idx uint64, err error)`.
       - Update `Add` to work with `*Entry` pointers and return `Future` instead of `IndexFunc`.
       - Refactor the internal `entry` type to a `queueItem` type that holds the `*Entry` and a channel-based future for the assigned index.
       - Update deduplication logic to use the entry's identity.

    5. **Update integration layer** (`storage/integrate.go`):
       - Add a `SequencedEntry` type with `BundleData []byte` and `LeafHash []byte` fields.
       - Change `TreeBuilder.Integrate` to accept `[]SequencedEntry` instead of `[]tessera.Entry`, using `LeafHash` directly for tree construction.

    6. **Update GCP storage** (`storage/gcp/gcp.go`):
       - Change `Add` to accept `*tessera.Entry` and call the queue's `Add` method.
       - Change `assignEntries` to set the index on each entry via `MarshalBundleData` and not return the first index — instead, apply the index directly to each `*Entry`.
       - Change `integrate` and `updateEntryBundles` to work with `[]storage.SequencedEntry`, using the pre-marshalled `BundleData` for bundle construction.
       - Update `getEntryBundle`/`setEntryBundle` to work with raw `[]byte` instead of `*api.EntryBundle` objects.

    7. **Remove obsolete `EntryBundle.MarshalText`** (`api/state.go`):
       - Change `MarshalText` to return an error, as bundle marshaling is now handled per-entry via `Entry.MarshalBundleData`.
  </think></description>

We need to make the queue flushing synchronous again. Since sequence numbers are assigned serially without gaps, there's no real benefit to running multiple flushes in parallel, and the current approach complicates things. Please restructure the queue so that flushes are handled one at a time, and make sure the entry channel gets closed appropriately.

pr_chain.title: Remove redundant origin flag and derive it from signer
pr_chain.description: Remove the command-line origin flag that allows users to specify a log origin string for checkpoint verification. Instead, derive the origin from the signer's name and use that single value consistently for both writing and reading checkpoints. This simplifies configuration and ensures the origin always matches the signing key.

pr_chain.title: Add GCP deployment instructions and env-var configuration support
pr_chain.description:
We need to improve the deployment experience for the GCP example in the `deployment/` directory. Currently, the GCP-specific deployment steps (like `gcloud` authentication) are documented in the top-level `deployment/README.md`, and the `terragrunt.hcl` for the `example-gcp` environment has hardcoded values for the GCP project ID, region, and base name.

  The goal is to:
  1. Move GCP-specific deployment instructions from the top-level `deployment/README.md` into a dedicated README in `deployment/live/example-gcp/`.
  2. Update the top-level README to simply point users to the appropriate `live` subdirectory for deployment details.
  3. Modify `deployment/live/example-gcp/terragrunt.hcl` so that the project ID, region, and base name can be customized via environment variables, with sensible defaults matching the current hardcoded values.

  This makes it easier for users to deploy the example without having to edit configuration files in the repo, while keeping the example runnable out-of-the-box.

## Environment Setup
This is a Go project, but the changes are purely in deployment configuration files. Check the repo root for `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `go.mod` for general project context. For deployment-related instructions, look at `deployment/README.md` and `deployment/live/example-gcp/terragrunt.hcl`. The repo also has a `go_test.yml` workflow in `.github/workflows/` that shows how tests are run in CI, but this task does not require running Go tests.

## Implementation Plan
1. Create a new file `deployment/live/example-gcp/README.md` with the following content:
     - A "Deployment" section header.
     - Instructions to authenticate via `gcloud` with `gcloud auth application-default login`.
     - Instructions to set the GCP project ID via `export GOOGLE_PROJECT={VALUE}`.
     - Optional instructions to customize the GCP region (defaulting to "us-central1") via `export GOOGLE_REGION={VALUE}` and the bucket name prefix (defaulting to "example-gcp") via `export TESSERA_BASE_NAME={VALUE}`.
     - Instructions to run `terragrunt apply` from the `live` directory.

  2. Update `deployment/README.md`:
     - Remove the GCP-specific `gcloud` authentication step and the deployment instructions that are now in the environment-specific README.
     - Replace the "Deploying" section with a short note pointing users to see the individual `live` subdirectories for environment-specific deployment instructions.

  3. Modify `deployment/live/example-gcp/terragrunt.hcl`:
     - Change the `locals` block to use `get_env()` with defaults:
       ```hcl
       project_id = get_env("GOOGLE_PROJECT", "trillian-tessera")
       location   = get_env("GOOGLE_REGION", "us-central1")
       base_name  = get_env("TESSERA_BASE_NAME", "example-gcp")
       ```
     - Keep the rest of the file (terraform source, inputs, remote_state) unchanged.

  4. Review the final files to ensure consistency between the documentation and the actual behavior of the terragrunt configuration.

pr_chain.title: Support configurable batching options in GCP storage
pr_chain.description:
The GCP storage implementation currently hardcodes queue parameters when creating its internal queue, ignoring any batching options that callers may have configured via the `tessera.WithBatching` option. Additionally, the `ResolveStorageOptions` function in `log.go` does not provide sensible defaults for batch-related fields when no options are supplied, which means the GCP storage would fail at runtime if the batching option is never set but the hardcoded values are removed.

    The goal is to make the GCP storage honor the batching configuration supplied through the existing `tessera.WithBatching` option when creating its internal write queue, and to ensure that `ResolveStorageOptions` provides reasonable default values so that the GCP storage works correctly both with and without explicit batching configuration.

    Additionally, update the `cmd/example-gcp/main.go` example to demonstrate using the `WithBatching` option when constructing the GCP storage, so that users have a reference for how to configure this behavior.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's Go module configuration in `go.mod` and `go.sum` for dependency management. The `Makefile` or CI workflow files (`.github/workflows/go_test.yml`, `.github/workflows/golangci-lint.yml`) may also provide hints on how tests are run and linting is configured.

## Implementation Plan
- In `log.go`, introduce a constant for the default batch max size (e.g., a value that effectively disables batching, such as 1) and set it as the default in `ResolveStorageOptions` when no `defaults` argument is provided.
    - In `storage/gcp/gcp.go`, replace the hardcoded values (`time.Second` and `256`) used when creating the write queue with the values from the resolved `StorageOptions` (`opt.BatchMaxAge` and `opt.BatchMaxSize`).
    - Remove the now-unnecessary `// TODO` comment in `storage/gcp/gcp.go` since the queue options are now configurable.
    - In `cmd/example-gcp/main.go`, add the `tessera.WithBatching(1024, time.Second)` option to the `gcp.New` call and add the necessary `time` import.

pr_chain.title: Correct storage error detection to avoid false panic when flush fails
pr_chain.description: We need to fix an incorrect assertion in the queue flushing logic that causes a panic when a storage error occurs before an entry's index is assigned. The current check assumes any missing index on an entry after a flush indicates a storage implementation bug, but it also triggers on unrelated earlier errors. Please move this validation so it only runs when the flush succeeded without errors, ensuring the panic indicates a genuine storage protocol violation rather than a legitimate error path.

pr_chain.title: Add a load-testing hammer tool for Tessera logs
pr_chain.description:
We need to add a new command-line tool, `hammer`, that generates read (and optionally write) traffic against a tlog-tiles-compatible log server in order to test its performance envelope and allow benchmarking. The tool should also perform basic conformance checking by verifying inclusion and consistency proofs.

    The tool should:
    - Support specifying one or more log URLs via a `--log_url` flag (repeatable).
    - Support reads: both random leaf reads and full-log downloads, with configurable rates (`--max_read_ops`, `--num_readers_random`, `--num_readers_full`).
    - Support writes: POST new leaves to the log's `/add` endpoint, with configurable rate and worker count (`--max_write_ops`, `--num_writers`). Writes are optional; if not enabled, the tool only reads.
    - Use the existing `client` package's `LogStateTracker` to track the log's state and verify consistency on updates.
    - Provide a terminal UI (via `tview`) to show status and allow interactive adjustment of traffic, controllable via a `--show_ui` flag (default on, but recommended off for headless CI runs).
    - Be interruptible via `<Ctrl-C>`.

    Additionally, the existing `client.GetLeaf` function is inefficient because it fetches an entire entry bundle and then throws away all but one leaf. We should replace it with a new function `GetEntryBundle` that returns the whole bundle, and update the hammer to use this new API.

    Finally, add a `hammer/README.md` documenting the tool's purpose, usage, and UI.

## Environment Setup
