pr_chain.title: Migrate when clauses in keybindings during data science settings migration
pr_chain.description:
The VS Code Jupyter extension includes a migration service (`MigrateDataScienceSettingsService`) that migrates legacy `python.datascience.*` settings and keybindings to their new `jupyter.*` equivalents. Currently, when migrating custom user keybindings, the service rewrites the `command` property but does not handle the `when` clause of a keybinding. If a user has a keybinding that includes a `when` clause referencing legacy `python.datascience.*` context keys, that clause will be left unchanged, leaving the keybinding referencing non-existent contexts. The goal is to update the keybinding migration logic so that when a `python.datascience.*` command is migrated to its `jupyter.*` equivalent, any `python.datascience.*` references in the keybinding's `when` clause are also rewritten to `jupyter.*`. Additionally, the migration currently runs settings and keybindings migration as a single operation guarded by one persistent state flag. We need to split this into two separate migration steps, each with its own persistent state flag, so that if one migration has already been performed, the other can still run (e.g. if a user had migrated settings before this keybinding fix was shipped). Look at the existing implementation in `src/client/activation/migrateDataScienceSettingsService.ts` and its unit tests in `src/test/activation/migrateDataScienceSettingsService.unit.test.ts` to understand the current behavior, then extend it. ## Environment Setup Check the repository's `package.json` for the `npm` scripts (test and build commands), and the `tsconfig.json` / `tsconfig.extension.json` for TypeScript configuration. The Python dependency files (`requirements.txt`, `pythonFiles/pyproject.toml`) are also present if Python-based testing is relevant, but the primary test setup is likely via npm scripts. Refer to `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general contribution guidelines. ## Implementation Plan
  • In `MigrateDataScienceSettingsService.activate`, introduce a second persistent state key (e.g. `'MigratedDataScienceKeybindingsService'`) to track keybinding migration separately from the settings migration. Read both flags, and conditionally run `updateSettings` and a new `updateKeybindings` method based on each respective flag.
  • Extract the existing keybinding file-fixing logic (currently inside `updateSettings`) into a dedicated method (e.g. `updateKeybindings`) that handles the custom keybindings file only. The `updateSettings` method should only handle settings files.
  • In the keybinding file fixer, when detecting a `command` containing `python.datascience.` (case-insensitive) and it's safe to migrate, after rewriting the command, also inspect the `when` property. If `when` is a string, replace all occurrences of `python.datascience.` (case-insensitive) with `jupyter.`.
  • Update the existing unit tests in `src/test/activation/migrateDataScienceSettingsService.unit.test.ts` to include keybindings with `when` clauses referencing `python.datascience.*`, and assert that the migrated keybindings have the `when` clause rewritten to `jupyter.*`. Also add a test scenario confirming that settings and keybindings migrations are independent (i.e. keybindings migration can run even if the settings migration flag is already set to `true`).
  • Run the existing unit test suite for the migrated service to ensure all tests pass.

pr_chain.title: Remove global state check when removing editor associations for disabled notebooks
pr_chain.description:
The extension currently uses extension global state flags to track whether it dynamically added editor associations for the Jupyter notebook view types (`jupyter.notebook.ipynb` for custom editors and `jupyter-notebook` for native notebooks). When the custom editor or native notebook feature is disabled, the extension only removes these dynamically-added associations if the corresponding global state flag indicates the extension previously added them.

    This causes an issue: if the association exists in the user's settings but the flag is missing (e.g., due to state corruption or a previous extension version behavior), the extension fails to remove its association when the feature is disabled. This leaves the extension's editor association orphaned in user settings, potentially causing files to open in an editor the extension no longer supports.

    Implement the following changes:
    1. Remove the dependency on `IExtensionContext` from both `CustomEditorService` and `NotebookIntegration` since the global state flags are no longer used for this purpose.
    2. Remove the `EditorAssociationUpdatedKey` constant from both `src/client/common/application/customEditorService.ts` and `src/client/datascience/notebook/integration.ts`.
    3. Always remove the editor association when the feature is disabled, regardless of whether a global state flag indicates the extension previously added it. The removal should still only happen if the association is actually present in the user's settings.
    4. In `disableNotebooks()` in `src/client/datascience/notebook/integration.ts`, remove the early return that checks the global state flag; simply call `enableDisableEditorAssociation(false)` unconditionally (for non-stable channels).
    5. Add a news entry file under `news/2 Fixes/` (e.g., `3988.md`) describing this fix.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's `package.json` for dependency installation instructions, `CONTRIBUTING.md` for development workflow, and `build/` directory for test configuration files (e.g., `build/.mocha.unittests.ts.json`, `build/.mocha.unittests.js.json`, `build/.mocha.functional.json`). Also review `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.extension.json` for TypeScript build configuration.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `src/client/common/application/customEditorService.ts`, remove the `IExtensionContext` import, the `EditorAssociationUpdatedKey` constant, the constructor parameter for `IExtensionContext`, and all usages of `this.extensionContext` within `enableCustomEditors()`. Simplify the revert logic to always filter out the `ViewType` from `editorAssociations` when `useCustomEditorApi` is false, without checking global state.
    2. In `src/client/datascience/notebook/integration.ts`, similarly remove the `IExtensionContext` import, the `EditorAssociationUpdatedKey` constant, the constructor parameter for `IExtensionContext`, and all usages of `this.extensionContext` in `enableDisableEditorAssociation()` and `disableNotebooks()`. Remove the early return based on global state in `disableNotebooks()`.
    3. Update the `enableDisableEditorAssociation()` method in `integration.ts` to remove the association unconditionally when `enable` is false, only filtering if the association is present in the settings array.
    4. Create a new news entry file `news/2 Fixes/3988.md` with a brief description stating that editor associations are now always removed when the native/custom editor feature is disabled, even if the extension doesn't remember adding them.
    5. Validate the changes by running the existing unit tests and TypeScript compilation to ensure no regressions.

pr_chain.title: Fix TensorBoard inline display URL handling for native notebooks
pr_chain.description:
When users execute `%tensorboard --logdir <log directory>` in a native notebook cell, TensorBoard returns an HTML IFrame as display output. The TensorBoard application hardcodes the IFrame source URL to use `window.location`, which in the VS Code extension context resolves to an internal `vscode-webview://` scheme that doesn't work properly. This causes the TensorBoard interface to fail to display inline in native notebooks.

    Currently, the fix for rewriting the TensorBoard IFrame URL from `window.location` to `http://localhost` is only applied in the webview notebook code path (in `jupyterNotebook.ts`). Native notebooks do not get this URL rewriting, causing TensorBoard inline display to fail.

    Implement a shared utility that rewrites TensorBoard display data HTML output to replace the `window.location` reference with `http://localhost`, and ensure this utility is applied in both the webview notebook and native notebook execution paths.

## Environment Setup
Check package.json for project configuration and scripts. The repository contains multiple configuration files for different parts of the project: pyproject.toml (Python files), tsconfig.extension.json and tsconfig.datascience-ui.json (TypeScript configuration), and test configuration files in build/ directory (e.g., build/.mocha.unittests.json, build/.mocha.functional.json). Review CONTRIBUTING.md and CODING_STANDARDS.md for development guidelines. The package.json file should contain dependency management and build/test scripts.

## Implementation Plan
1. Create a new exported function `handleTensorBoardDisplayDataOutput` in `src/client/datascience/notebook/helpers/executionHelpers.ts` that contains the TensorBoard HTML rewriting logic (currently duplicated in `jupyterNotebook.ts`).
    2. Modify the `handleDisplayData` method in `src/client/datascience/jupyter/jupyterNotebook.ts` to import and use the shared utility function instead of the local private method.
    3. Modify the `handleDisplayData` method in `src/client/datascience/jupyter/kernels/cellExecution.ts` to import and apply the shared utility function to the display data output.
    4. Add appropriate unit tests for the new shared utility function covering various HTML output scenarios.
    5. Verify the fix works for both webview notebooks and native notebooks by testing TensorBoard inline display in both contexts.

pr_chain.title: Make extension activation wait for dependencies and fix migration bugs
pr_chain.description:
We need to fix several issues with the Jupyter extension activation process to prevent deadlocks and ensure proper initialization:

1. **Wait for activation to complete**: Currently, the `activate()` function in `src/client/extension.ts` returns immediately without waiting for all activation work to finish. This causes race conditions where the extension API is returned before all services are ready. The goal is to await the `ready` promise before returning the API.

2. **Fix Jupyter interpreter migration deadlock**: The `MigrateJupyterInterpreterStateService.activate()` method in `src/client/datascience/jupyter/interpreter/jupyterInterpreterStateStore.ts` delays the Python extension activation because it waits for Python's API during our activation. This creates a circular dependency. Move this migration to run in the background so it doesn't block our activation.

3. **Use boolean flag instead of service injection**: In `src/client/datascience/notebook/integration.ts`, we currently inject `IExperimentService` and call `inExperiment()` to check if the native notebook feature should be enabled. Replace this with a simpler boolean flag injected via `UseVSCodeNotebookEditorApi` constant to avoid loading unnecessary services during activation.

4. **Fix async directory check**: In `src/client/migration/migrateDigestStorage.ts`, the `localDirectoryExists()` calls are not being awaited. Add `await` keywords to these calls so the directory checks complete before proceeding with file copies.

5. **Improve test setup**: 
   - In `src/test/index.ts`, rename the `activatePythonExtensionScript()` function to `activateExtensionScript()` and add clearer logging.
   - In `src/test/standardTest.ts`, add a setting to always trust notebooks when running smoke tests, and type the settings object as `Record<string, string | boolean>`.

This change is part of improving the extension's activation reliability and preventing race conditions.

## Environment Setup
Check these repo files for build and test setup:
    - `package.json` - main npm scripts and dependencies
    - `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.extension.json` - TypeScript compilation settings
    - `gulpfile.js` - build tasks
    - `build/.mocha.unittests.json`, `build/.mocha.functional.json` - Mocha test configurations
    - `CONTRIBUTING.md` - development workflow instructions

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify `src/client/extension.ts`:
       - Add `await ready;` before `return api;` in the `activate()` function

    2. Modify `src/client/datascience/jupyter/interpreter/jupyterInterpreterStateStore.ts`:
       - Rename the body of `activate()` to a new private method `activateBackground()`
       - Make `activate()` call `this.activateBackground().catch(noop)` to run migration in background
       - Keep the existing migration logic in `activateBackground()`

    3. Modify `src/client/datascience/notebook/integration.ts`:
       - Remove imports for `Experiments` and `IExperimentService`
       - Add import for `UseVSCodeNotebookEditorApi` from `../../common/constants`
       - Change constructor to inject `UseVSCodeNotebookEditorApi` as a boolean parameter
       - Replace `await this.experimentService.inExperiment(Experiments.NativeNotebook)` calls with `this.useNativeNb`

    4. Modify `src/client/migration/migrateDigestStorage.ts`:
       - Add `await` to both `this.fs.localDirectoryExists()` calls in `migrateKey()` and `migrateDir()`

    5. Modify `src/test/index.ts`:
       - Rename `activatePythonExtensionScript()` to `activateExtensionScript()`
       - Add console.log statement before calling it

    6. Modify `src/test/standardTest.ts`:
       - Add `isRunningSmokeTests` and `isRunningVSCodeTests` constants
       - Update `requiresPythonExtensionToBeInstalled()` to use these constants
       - Type `defaultSettings` as `Record<string, string | boolean>`
       - Add `'jupyter.alwaysTrustNotebooks': true` to settings when running smoke tests

pr_chain.title: Fix environment variable merging to include all process variables
pr_chain.description:
The environment variables provider is generating incomplete environment variable sets. When starting raw kernels, the resulting environment is missing many variables from the current process environment, causing paths to be completely wrong and kernel startup to fail.

    The issue appears to be in `_getEnvironmentVariables` in `src/client/common/variables/environmentVariablesProvider.ts`. The current implementation starts with custom environment variables (from `.env` files) and then attempts to merge in variables from `process.env`. This approach can result in the final environment missing process variables that weren't already present in the custom set.

    Additionally, path-related variables (like `PATH` and `PYTHONPATH`) are only appended if they exist in `process.env` or the custom variables, but the merging order can cause them to be lost or overwritten incorrectly.

    The goal is to ensure that `getEnvironmentVariables()` returns a complete environment — one that includes all variables from the current process, with any custom variables (from `.env` files) properly layered on top.

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` for dependency management and available scripts. Review `pyproject.toml` in the `pythonFiles` directory for Python-side dependencies. The `news/requirements.txt` file contains Python dependencies for tooling. Test configuration files can be found under `build/` (e.g., `build/.mocha.unittests.ts.json`, `build/.mocha.functional.json`) and root-level configs like `tsconfig.json` and `tslint.json`.

## Implementation Plan
- Review the `_getEnvironmentVariables` method in `src/client/common/variables/environmentVariablesProvider.ts` to understand the current merging logic.
    - Change the approach so the base merged environment starts as a copy of `process.env`, ensuring all process variables are preserved.
    - Merge custom environment variables (from `.env` files) on top of the process environment, so custom values override process values when both exist.
    - Ensure path-related variables like `PATH` and `PYTHONPATH` are handled correctly — the process values should be preserved, and custom path values should be appended rather than replacing the existing path.
    - Keep the method private unless there's a clear need for external callers; review whether making it public again is necessary for any tests or callers.
    - Verify the fix by running unit tests related to environment variables and, if possible, testing raw kernel startup to ensure the environment is complete and paths resolve correctly.

pr_chain.title: Refactor variable fetching to load helper scripts from local files for remote environments
pr_chain.description:
When the Jupyter extension connects to a remote Jupyter server (e.g., inside a Docker container or on another machine), the kernel executing code may not have the extension's helper Python scripts available in its `sys.path`. Currently, the variable explorer relies on importing these helper modules (`vscodeGetDataFrameInfo`, `vscodeGetDataFrameRows`, `vscodeGetVariableInfo`, and `vscodeDataFrameHelpers`) via `sys.path` manipulation and `import` statements. This fails when the remote environment doesn't have the extension's `pythonFiles` directory mounted or accessible.

    The goal is to refactor the variable fetching mechanism so that instead of relying on `import` statements, the extension reads the contents of the helper Python files from the local filesystem and executes them directly in the notebook/debug session. This ensures the helper functions are always available in the kernel, regardless of whether the remote machine has the extension files.

    Refactor the existing Python helper scripts and TypeScript integration to:
    1. Consolidate the DataFrame helper functions (`_VSCODE_convertToDataFrame`, `_VSCODE_getRowCount`, `_VSCODE_getDataFrameInfo`, `_VSCODE_getDataFrameRows`) into a single `vscodeDataFrame.py` file.
    2. Move the `vscodeGetVariableInfo.py` file to a separate `getVariableInfo` directory (since it's used for variable info, not DataFrame operations).
    3. Update the TypeScript constants in `src/client/datascience/constants.ts` to define paths to these script files and the function names they export.
    4. Update `kernelVariables.ts` to read the script file contents from the local filesystem (using `IFileSystem`) and execute them in the notebook rather than using `import` statements.
    5. Update `debuggerVariables.ts` to handle importing the DataFrame and variable-info scripts separately, tracking them with separate sets.

## Environment Setup
- `pythonFiles/pyproject.toml`: Contains Python project configuration including linting (black, flake8) and formatting settings for the Python helper files.
    - `package.json`: Contains the main project configuration and scripts for building, linting, and testing the TypeScript code.
    - `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.extension.json`: TypeScript compilation configuration files.
    - `CONTRIBUTING.md`: General contribution guidelines and development setup instructions.
    - `.github/workflows/pr.yml` and other workflow files: CI configuration that may show how tests are run.
    - `build/.mocha.unittests.ts.json` and `build/.mocha.unittests.js.json`: Mocha configuration files for running unit tests.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Refactor Python helper files**:
       - Create `pythonFiles/vscode_datascience_helpers/dataframes/vscodeDataFrame.py` by combining the contents of `vscodeDataFrameHelpers.py`, `vscodeGetDataFrameInfo.py`, and `vscodeGetDataFrameRows.py`. Include all functions (`_VSCODE_convertToDataFrame`, `_VSCODE_getRowCount`, `_VSCODE_getDataFrameInfo`, `_VSCODE_getDataFrameRows`) in this single file.
       - Move `pythonFiles/vscode_datascience_helpers/dataframes/vscodeGetVariableInfo.py` to `pythonFiles/vscode_datascience_helpers/getVariableInfo/vscodeGetVariableInfo.py`.
       - Remove the old files: `pythonFiles/vscode_datascience_helpers/dataframes/vscodeDataFrameHelpers.py`, `pythonFiles/vscode_datascience_helpers/dataframes/vscodeGetDataFrameInfo.py`, `pythonFiles/vscode_datascience_helpers/dataframes/vscodeGetDataFrameRows.py`.
       - Ensure `vscodeGetVariableInfo.py` no longer imports pandas or the DataFrame helpers (it shouldn't need them).

    2. **Update TypeScript constants** in `src/client/datascience/constants.ts`:
       - In `DataFrameLoading` namespace:
         - Keep `SysPath` but add `ScriptPath` pointing to `pythonFiles/vscode_datascience_helpers/dataframes/vscodeDataFrame.py`.
         - Replace `DataFrameInfoImportName`, `DataFrameInfoImport`, `DataFrameInfoFunc`, `DataFrameRowImportName`, `DataFrameRowImport`, `DataFrameRowFunc` with:
           - `DataFrameInfoFunc = '_VSCODE_getDataFrameInfo'`
           - `DataFrameRowFunc = '_VSCODE_getDataFrameRows'`
           - Add debugger-specific constants: `DataFrameImportName = '_VSCODE_DataFrameImport'`, `DataFrameImport = 'import vscodeDataFrame as ${DataFrameImportName}'` (with a placeholder for the name), `DataFrameInfoImportFunc`, `DataFrameRowImportFunc`.
       - Create new `GetVariableInfo` namespace:
         - Add `SysPath` pointing to `pythonFiles/vscode_datascience_helpers/getVariableInfo`.
         - Add `GetVariableInfoSysImport` for the sys.path append.
         - Add `ScriptPath` pointing to `vscodeGetVariableInfo.py`.
         - Add `VariableInfoFunc = '_VSCODE_getVariableInfo'`.
         - Add debugger-specific constants: `VariableInfoImportName`, `VariableInfoImport`, `VariableInfoImportFunc`.
       - Remove `VariableInfoImport` and `VariableInfoFunc` from `DataFrameLoading` namespace.

    3. **Update `src/client/datascience/jupyter/kernelVariables.ts`**:
       - Inject `IFileSystem` into the constructor.
       - Add a new private `importedGetVariableInfoScripts` map.
       - In `importDataFrameScripts`, instead of building and executing a combined import string, call a new private method `runScriptFile(notebook, DataFrameLoading.ScriptPath, token)` to read and execute the `vscodeDataFrame.py` file contents in the notebook.
       - Add a new private method `importGetVariableInfoScripts(notebook, token)` that similarly calls `runScriptFile` for `GetVariableInfo.ScriptPath`.
       - Add a private `runScriptFile(notebook, scriptFile, token)` method that:
         - Checks if the file exists locally using `fs.localFileExists(scriptFile)`.
         - If it exists, reads the file contents using `fs.readFile(Uri.parse(scriptFile))` and executes it silently via `notebook.execute(fileContents, Identifiers.EmptyFileName, 0, uuid(), token, true)`.
         - If not, logs an error with `traceError`.
       - Update `getFullVariable` and `getDataFrameInfo`/`getDataFrameRows` to call `importGetVariableInfoScripts` or `importDataFrameScripts` as appropriate.
       - Update the function call strings to use the new function names (`GetVariableInfo.VariableInfoFunc`, `DataFrameLoading.DataFrameInfoFunc`, `DataFrameLoading.DataFrameRowFunc`).

    4. **Update `src/client/datascience/jupyter/debuggerVariables.ts`**:
       - Replace the single `importedIntoKernel` set with two sets: `importedDataFrameScriptsIntoKernel` and `importedGetVariableInfoScriptsIntoKernel`.
       - Update `resetImport` and the termination handler to clear both sets.
       - Replace `importDataFrameScripts` with two methods:
         - `importDataFrameScripts`: evaluates the sys.path append and the DataFrame import statement (using `DataFrameLoading.DataFrameSysImport` and `DataFrameLoading.DataFrameImport`), then adds to `importedDataFrameScriptsIntoKernel`.
         - `importGetVariableInfoScripts`: evaluates the GetVariableInfo sys.path append and import statement (using `GetVariableInfo.GetVariableInfoSysImport` and `GetVariableInfo.VariableInfoImport`), then adds to `importedGetVariableInfoScriptsIntoKernel`.
       - Update `getFullVariable` to call `importGetVariableInfoScripts` and use `GetVariableInfo.VariableInfoImportFunc`.
       - Update `getDataFrameInfo`/`getDataFrameRows` to call `importDataFrameScripts` and use `DataFrameLoading.DataFrameInfoImportFunc`/`DataFrameLoading.DataFrameRowImportFunc`.

    5. **Add news entry**:
       - Create `news/2 Fixes/4006.md` with content explaining the fix (e.g., "Fix variable fetching on remote machines that don't have our scripts files on them.").

## Use Terraform dev override for provider version in tests

We need to update the test infrastructure so that unit and integration tests use Terraform's dev override mechanism to ensure tests run against the exact provider version specified in `go.mod`, rather than whatever version is downloaded by default. This is necessary because `go install` without a version spec uses versions from `go.mod`, which may conflict with dependency versions in `terraform-provider-google-beta` (tpgb) — causing version mismatch errors during test runs.

The goal is to:
1. Add a script that sets up a Terraform dev override configuration, installs the tpgb provider version from `go.mod`, and creates a `tf-dev-override.tfrc` file pointing Terraform to use the locally-built provider binary.
2. Update the Makefile so `make test` and `make test-integration` invoke this configuration script and run tests with `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE` pointing to the generated `.tfrc` file.
3. Simplify the CI integration test configuration to stop manually copying an old Terraform binary and instead rely on the base image's Terraform (which must be a version compatible with dev overrides).
4. Remove the Dockerfile and `install-terraform.sh` that pinned Terraform to a specific old version, and update `run-docker` to use the `go-plus` base image directly.
5. Update contributor documentation to reflect the new testing workflow.

The `config-tf-dev-override.sh` script should:
- Use `go list -json -m` to locate the `terraform-provider-google-beta` module.
- If the module has a `Dir` field (i.e., a `replace` directive is in effect), `cd` into that directory and run `go install`.
- Otherwise, run `go install github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google-beta@VERSION` using the version from `go.mod`.
- Generate a `tf-dev-override.tfrc` file (if it doesn't already exist) with a `provider_installation` block containing the `dev_overrides` and `direct` settings, using `$GOPATH/bin` as the local provider binary path.

The `.gitignore` should be updated to exclude the generated `tf-dev-override.tfrc` file.

## Environment Setup
Review the repository's `Makefile` for test/build targets, `go.mod` for module dependencies, `.ci/cloudbuild-tests-integration.yaml` for CI configuration, and `docs/contributing/index.md` for testing documentation. Check `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general contribution guidelines. The `config-tf-dev-override.sh` script (to be created) will need `jq` and `go` available in the environment.

## Implementation Plan
1. Create a new shell script `config-tf-dev-override.sh` that:
     - Uses `go list -json -m github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google-beta` to get module info.
     - Extracts the replace directory (if any) and version using `jq`.
     - Installs the tpgb provider binary (via `go install` inside the replace dir, or with `go install ...@VERSION`).
     - Generates `tf-dev-override.tfrc` (only if not already present) with the required provider installation config.
  2. Update the `Makefile`:
     - Remove the `TERRAFORM_VERSION` variable.
     - Update `test` and `test-integration` targets to invoke the new script and set `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE` to the generated file path.
     - Remove the `build-docker` target.
     - Update `run-docker` to use `gcr.io/graphite-docker-images/go-plus` directly as the image.
  3. Update `.ci/cloudbuild-tests-integration.yaml` to remove the manual Terraform binary copy step and the `TERRAFORM_VERSION` env var.
  4. Delete `Dockerfile` and `install-terraform.sh` (no longer needed).
  5. Update `docs/contributing/index.md` to describe the new testing workflow (dev override setup, running tests inside Docker container).
  6. Add `tf-dev-override.tfrc` to `.gitignore`.

pr_chain.title: Update google-beta dependency for compute instance template tags
pr_chain.description:
The conversion library depends on `github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google-beta` to understand Terraform configuration schemas and convert them into Google Cloud asset inventory format.  A newer pseudo-version of this dependency includes support for the `resource_manager_tags` field on `google_compute_instance_template` and `google_compute_region_instance_template` resources (both at the instance level and within each `disk` block).

    Your task is to update the dependency version in `go.mod` and the corresponding checksums in `go.sum` so that this library can leverage the newly added schema support.  This is a dependency-only change; no Go source code modifications are required.

    Specifically:
    1. Update the `github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google-beta` module version in `go.mod`.
    2. Regenerate the `go.sum` file to reflect the new module checksums.
    3. Verify the module graph is correct by running the project's unit tests.

## Environment Setup
This is a Go module.  The primary configuration file is `go.mod` which lists all dependencies.  The `go.sum` file contains the expected cryptographic checksums.  The `Makefile` may contain helpful targets for building and testing the project.  The repository also contains a `Dockerfile` and CI configuration under `.ci/` which could be useful for understanding the test environment, but `go mod` commands are the standard Go toolchain approach here.

## Implementation Plan
- Identify the current pseudo-version of `github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google-beta` in `go.mod`.
    - Update that version to the newer pseudo-version `v1.20.1-0.20240102184606-125d06845415`.
    - Run the Go module tidy command to update the `go.sum` file with the new checksums for this module and its transitive dependencies, if any.
    - Ensure the build and test suites still pass, using the standard Go test command.

pr_chain.title: Revert dependency update causing flaky downstream tests

The current version, `v1.20.1-0.20240104190250-de72f5fcff2a`, is causing intermittent failures in downstream CI runs. ## Implementation Plan

    - Revert `go.mod` to pin the dependency to the previous stable version (`v1.20.1-0.20240104214532-b7517d5a9ee2`).

pr_chain.title: Update Go module dependencies to fix Datapipeline scheduler service account bug
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to update the project's Go module dependencies to incorporate a fix from the upstream `terraform-provider-google-beta` and `declarative-resource-client-library` modules. This fix addresses an issue with the `scheduler_service_account_email` field in the `google_data_pipeline_pipeline` resource, which was causing a permadiff and resource recreation when the field was not explicitly specified. pr_chain.title: Update Terraform provider dependency to fix BigQuery table permadiff
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to eliminate a perpetual diff (permadiff) that occurs with `google_bigquery_table` resources when the Google Cloud API returns an empty `encryptionConfiguration` object (`{}`) for a table that was created without that field configured.

    When this empty object is encountered, the current dependency version of the `terraform-provider-google-beta` library causes the Terraform state to record `encryption_configuration` as a single-element list containing an entry with empty `kms_key_name` and `kms_key_version` values. This leads to a subsequent `terraform plan` showing a non-empty diff (`- encryption_configuration {} # forces replacement`) for a resource that was not actually changed.

    The fix is to update the `github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google-beta` module to a newer version that handles this case by setting the `encryption_configuration` field to an empty list (`[]`) in the state when the API returns an empty object. This prevents the spurious diff and the potential for unintended resource replacement.

    Please ensure the change is minimal and only updates the dependency version in `go.mod` and `go.sum` to the version that contains the upstream fix.

pr_chain.title: Align delay and slope compensation in PID longitudinal controller
pr_chain.description:
The `pid_longitudinal_controller` currently performs delay compensation by estimating the drive distance of the vehicle after `delay_compensation_time` and looking at a future `TrajectoryPoint`, but slope compensation is applied using the pitch of the **current** trajectory point. On hilly roads, this mismatch in reference time can cause conflicts: the feed-forward term is computed for the future point while the slope compensation reflects the current position, producing undesired acceleration commands.

    Your goal is to align both compensations so they reference the same point in time/space. Specifically:

    1. Refactor the control pipeline so that delay compensation and slope compensation both operate on a point projected ahead on the trajectory by the estimated running distance during the delay.
    2. Support multiple slope sources:
       - `raw_pitch`: use the vehicle's measured pitch (current behavior when enabled).
       - `trajectory_pitch`: use the pitch from the trajectory at the delay-compensated future point.
       - `trajectory_adaptive`: use `raw_pitch` while the vehicle is stopped (or below a velocity threshold), and `trajectory_pitch` while moving above that threshold.
    3. Replace the existing boolean parameter `use_trajectory_for_pitch_calculation` with a `slope_source` string parameter and a `adaptive_trajectory_velocity_th` threshold parameter.
    4. Extend interpolation/utilities to work in 3D (including z) so that pitch can be derived from trajectory elevation, and add a helper to find a trajectory pose a given arc distance ahead of an index.
    5. Update the unit tests to cover the new return types, the 3D pitch calculation, and the new utility function.

    Use the future trajectory point for both the feed-forward target and the pitch value used in slope compensation so the two compensations are consistent.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repo files for build/install/test instructions:

    - `control/pid_longitudinal_controller/CMakeLists.txt` — contains build configuration and test registration for this package.
    - `setup.cfg` / `setup.py` at the repo root — may indicate how the workspace is assembled.
    - `common/autoware_testing/CMakeLists.txt` and `common/autoware_testing/setup.py` — related to test infrastructure.

    The package is a ROS 2 C++ package; typical workflow involves `colcon build` and `colcon test`, but confirm from the listed files.

## Implementation Plan
- Add a helper function `findTrajectoryPoseAfterDistance(src_idx, distance, trajectory)` in `longitudinal_controller_utils` that returns the interpolated pose at a given arc length along the trajectory from a source index.
    - Change `lerpTrajectoryPoint` to return a `std::pair<TrajectoryPoint, size_t>` (interpolated point + segment index) and interpolate the z coordinate as well.
    - Update `getPitchByTraj` to accept a `start_idx` (renamed from `closest_idx`) and use 3D distance when locating the point one wheelbase ahead.
    - In `PidLongitudinalController`, add a `StateAfterDelay` struct (vel, acc, running_distance) and a `SlopeSource` enum (`RAW_PITCH`, `TRAJECTORY_PITCH`, `TRAJECTORY_ADAPTIVE`).
    - Refactor `getControlData` to: interpolate and insert the current pose into a local trajectory copy, compute the predicted state after delay using `predictedStateAfterDelay`, and project to the future trajectory pose using the running distance; set `target_idx` to that projected index.
    - Update `calcCtrlCmd` and `calcFilteredAcc` to use the projected trajectory point (via `control_data`) for both feed-forward and slope compensation; remove the `current_pose` argument from `calcCtrlCmd`.
    - Replace `m_use_traj_for_pitch` parameter with `slope_source` (string) and `adaptive_trajectory_velocity_th` (double) in the constructor and parameter callback.
    - Update the unit tests in `test_longitudinal_controller_utils.cpp` for the new return type of `lerpTrajectoryPoint`, the 3D behavior of `getPitchByTraj`, and add coverage for `findTrajectoryPoseAfterDistance`.

pr_chain.title: Restructure NDT scan matcher diagnostics into modular status messages
pr_chain.description:
The current `ndt_scan_matcher` publishes a single aggregated diagnostics message on the `/diagnostics` topic. This monolithic message combines all internal state into one `DiagnosticStatus`, making it difficult to reason about the health of individual subsystems (scan matching, map update, service handling, etc.).

    We need to refactor the diagnostics output to distribute the state into six separate, focused `DiagnosticStatus` messages, each with its own keys and documented transition conditions for WARN/ERROR levels:

    1. `scan_matching_status` — covers the main NDT scan matching pipeline.
    2. `initial_pose_subscriber_status` — covers the `ekf_pose_with_covariance` subscriber.
    3. `regularization_pose_subscriber_status` — covers the regularization pose subscriber (only active when regularization is enabled).
    4. `trigger_node_service_status` — covers the `trigger_node_srv` service.
    5. `ndt_align_service_status` — covers the `ndt_align_srv` service and associated map update.
    6. `map_update_status` — covers the periodic dynamic map update timer callback.

    The diagnostics should be generated by a dedicated `DiagnosticsModule` class that wraps the creation and publishing of a single `DiagnosticStatus` message. Each module instance should be owned by the relevant subsystem (e.g., map update module publishes `map_update_status`, core node publishes the others).

    The key conditions that should produce WARN or ERROR are specified in the README. For example, the map update module should raise an ERROR when the vehicle moves beyond the loaded map radius (`distance_last_update_position_to_current_position + lidar_radius > map_radius`), and a WARN when the node is not activated or no update position is available.

    Additionally, any invalid parameter configuration that previously produced a throttled warning (e.g., mismatched covariance estimation offset model sizes) should now throw at node construction to fail fast.

## Environment Setup
The main build configuration for this node is in `localization/ndt_scan_matcher/CMakeLists.txt`. It uses `ament_auto_add_executable` and `ament_auto_add_gtest`; check the `BUILD_TESTING` section for how tests are wired up. The package uses `find_package(autoware_cmake)` and `autoware_package()`, so standard Autoware build tooling applies. No separate `pyproject.toml` or `tox.ini` is present for this package.

## Implementation Plan
1.  **Create `DiagnosticsModule` class**:
        - New files: `include/ndt_scan_matcher/diagnostics_module.hpp` and `src/diagnostics_module.cpp`.
        - Constructor takes `rclcpp::Node*` and a diagnostic name string; sets up a publisher on `/diagnostics` and initializes the status message name as `<node_name>: <diagnostic_name>`.
        - Implement members:
          - `clear()` — reset the status message (keys, level, message).
          - `addKeyValue(key, value)` — append/update a key-value pair; templated overloads for numeric, `std::string`, and `bool` types.
          - `updateLevelAndMessage(level, message)` — accumulate WARN/ERROR messages and raise the status level if needed.
          - `publish()` — publish the current status.
    2.  **Wire into `NDTScanMatcher` core**:
        - In `include/ndt_scan_matcher/ndt_scan_matcher_core.hpp`, add `#include "ndt_scan_matcher/diagnostics_module.hpp"` and declare `std::unique_ptr<DiagnosticsModule>` members for:
          - `diagnostics_scan_points_`
          - `diagnostics_initial_pose_`
          - `diagnostics_map_update_`
          - `diagnostics_ndt_align_`
          - `diagnostics_trigger_node_`
        - In `src/ndt_scan_matcher_core.cpp`:
          - Remove the old `publish_diagnostic()` method and the `state_ptr_` map member.
          - Initialize the modules in the constructor (after `param_` is available).
          - Refactor callback bodies (`callback_sensor_points`, `callback_initial_pose`, `service_trigger_node`, `service_ndt_align`) to populate and publish the corresponding diagnostics module.
          - For `callback_timer()`, delegate map update logic to `MapUpdateModule` and have it use the passed-in `diagnostics_ptr`.
    3.  **Refactor `MapUpdateModule`**:
        - In `include/ndt_scan_matcher/map_update_module.hpp`, modify public/private API:
          - `callback_timer(is_activated, position, diagnostics_ptr)` — the new entry point from the core node's timer; checks activation, position availability, and calls `should_update_map` / `update_map`.
          - `should_update_map(position, diagnostics_ptr)` — update to take diagnostics pointer and record `distance_last_update_position_to_current_position`; raise ERROR when dynamic map loading lags.
          - `update_map(position, diagnostics_ptr)` — accept diagnostics pointer; record `is_need_rebuild`, `is_updated_map`, and other relevant fields.
          - `update_ndt(position, ndt, diagnostics_ptr)` — accept diagnostics pointer; record map-to-add/remove sizes and execution time.
        - Move the diagnostics-related logic from the core node into these methods.
    4.  **Update `HyperParameters` error handling**:
        - In `include/ndt_scan_matcher/hyper_parameters.hpp`, if the covariance estimation offset model sizes mismatch, replace the `RCLCPP_WARN` with a `throw std::runtime_error` to fail node startup.
    5.  **Document the new diagnostics**:
        - Append a `## Diagnostics` section to `localization/ndt_scan_matcher/README.md` describing each of the six status messages, their keys, and the exact conditions for WARN/ERROR transitions. Add images as referenced in the media folder.
    6.  **Update build files**:
        - In `localization/ndt_scan_matcher/CMakeLists.txt`, add `src/diagnostics_module.cpp` to both the executable and the gtest source lists. Note that the node-main file (`ndt_scan_matcher_node.cpp`) is intentionally commented out from the gtest build — keep that as is.

We need to rebrand the localization accuracy diagnostics to use the term "localization_error_ellipse" instead of "localization_accuracy" across the relevant config files and diagnostic messages. This includes updating the key names in the diagnostics output, the fault injection mapping, and the system error monitor's configuration to reference the new naming. Please make sure all references are consistent so the diagnostics aggregation and monitoring continue to work correctly with the updated terminology.

pr_chain.title: Add synchronized multi-LiDAR occupancy grid map fusion support
pr_chain.description:
We need to enable running the probabilistic occupancy grid map (OGM) with multiple LiDAR frames. Currently, the OGM pipeline supports only a single LiDAR frame. The goal is to add a synchronized fusion node that combines OGM outputs from multiple LiDAR sensors into a single fused map.

    The implementation should include:
    - A new launch file for the multi-LiDAR OGM method that creates individual OGM nodes for each LiDAR and a fusion node to combine their outputs.
    - A configuration file with parameters for each OGM creation and the fusion process (e.g., sensor topics, reliabilities, fusion method).
    - Updates to the existing pointcloud-based OGM node to allow `scan_origin_frame` to be empty, in which case it should use the input pointcloud's frame_id.
    - Updates to the fusion node to publish pipeline latency debug information.
    - Wiring the new method into the existing `probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map.launch.xml`.

    The new method should be selectable via the `occupancy_grid_map_method` launch argument with the value `multi_lidar_pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map`.

## Environment Setup
Check the `perception/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map/CMakeLists.txt` to understand how this package is built and which dependencies are needed. For launcher-related changes, look at `launch/tier4_perception_launch/CMakeLists.txt`. The repository uses colcon for building; refer to the top-level `setup.cfg` for general project configuration. Test configurations may be found in `perception/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map/` (e.g., `test/` directory).

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create a new launch file** `perception/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map/launch/multi_lidar_pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map.launch.py` that:
       - Loads a configuration file (YAML) containing shared parameters, per-LiDAR OGM creation parameters, and fusion parameters.
       - Validates that the lists of raw pointcloud topics, fusion input OGM topics, and reliabilities have the same length.
       - Instantiates a `pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map_node` per LiDAR, each subscribing to its corresponding raw pointcloud topic and publishing its own OGM.
       - Instantiates the `synchronized_grid_map_fusion_node` that subscribes to all per-LiDAR OGM topics and publishes the fused map.
       - Passes the appropriate parameters to each node (e.g., `map_frame`, `base_link_frame`, `gridmap_origin_frame`, map dimensions, etc.).
       - Supports `use_intra_process` and `use_multithread` launch arguments.

    2. **Create a sample configuration file** `perception/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map/config/multi_lidar_pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map.param.yaml` containing:
       - Shared parameters (map frame, base link frame, grid map origin frame, resolution, map dimensions).
       - OGM creation parameters (height filter, single-frame mode, grid map type).
       - Fusion parameters (raw pointcloud topics, fusion input OGM topics, reliabilities, fusion method).
       - Comments explaining each parameter group.

    3. **Update `pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map_node.cpp`** to make `scan_origin_frame` optional (default empty string). When empty, use the frame_id from the input raw pointcloud message before the TF lookup.

    4. **Update `synchronized_grid_map_fusion_node.cpp`** to compute and publish a `debug/pipeline_latency_ms` value similar to the existing `debug/cyclic_time_ms` and `debug/processing_time_ms` outputs. This should be based on the difference between the latest subscribed map's timestamp and the current node time.

    5. **Update `launch/tier4_perception_launch/launch/occupancy_grid_map/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map.launch.xml`** to pass the `input/obstacle_pointcloud` argument to the new multi-LiDAR launch file.

    6. **Add launch tests** for the new multi-LiDAR launch file to verify it starts correctly with the sample configuration.

pr_chain.title: Add a LiDAR-based marker localizer node and integrate it into localization launch files.
pr_chain.description:
Implement a new ROS 2 node, `LidarMarkerLocalizer`, that estimates the vehicle's pose by detecting reflective markers (e.g., "reflector") in LiDAR pointcloud data and matching them against landmarks defined in a Lanelet2 map. The node should subscribe to the pointcloud, EKF pose, and map data, and publish the estimated pose with covariance. Also, integrate this node into the existing localization launch system so it can be selected as a pose source in `pose_twist_estimator.launch.xml` and `localization.launch.xml`.

    The goal is to provide an alternative pose estimation method based on fixed marker detection, useful in environments like tunnels where GNSS is unavailable.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repository files for build/install/test instructions:
    - `localization/autoware_landmark_based_localizer/autoware_lidar_marker_localizer/CMakeLists.txt` and `package.xml` for package configuration and dependencies
    - `launch/tier4_localization_launch/package.xml` for launch package dependencies
    - Root `setup.cfg` for general Python setup (if applicable)
    These files indicate the build system (ament_cmake) and required dependencies.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create the package structure** under `localization/autoware_landmark_based_localizer/autoware_lidar_marker_localizer/`:
       - Create `CMakeLists.txt` to build a shared library and register a ROS 2 component node.
       - Create `package.xml` declaring dependencies (`rclcpp`, `pcl_ros`, `autoware_landmark_manager`, `localization_util`, etc.).
       - Create `src/lidar_marker_localizer.hpp` and `src/lidar_marker_localizer.cpp` for the `LidarMarkerLocalizer` class.
    2. **Implement the node logic**:
       - Subscribe to `~/input/pointcloud` (best-effort QoS), `~/input/ekf_pose`, and `~/input/lanelet2_map`.
       - Use `SmartPoseBuffer` to interpolate EKF pose with the pointcloud timestamp.
       - Load landmarks from the map using `autoware::landmark_manager::LandmarkManager`.
       - On each pointcloud:
         - Transform the pointcloud to the map frame using the interpolated pose.
         - Detect potential markers by analyzing high-intensity point patterns (using a pattern matching algorithm on a 2D grid, as described in the config `intensity_pattern`).
         - Validate detected markers against the nearest map landmark (distance check).
         - Compute the pose correction from the detected marker positions.
         - Publish the corrected pose on `~/output/pose_with_covariance` and debug topics (`~/debug/marker_detected`, `~/debug/marker_mapped`, `~/debug/marker_pointcloud`, `~/debug/pose_with_covariance`).
       - Implement a service `~/service/trigger_node_srv` (SetBool) to activate/deactivate the node.
       - Implement a diagnostics module for health reporting.
       - Add parameters for detection thresholds, marker dimensions, and logging (as seen in `config/lidar_marker_localizer.param.yaml`).
    3. **Add launch file** `launch/lidar_marker_localizer.launch.xml` within the new package to launch the node with configurable topic remapping.
    4. **Add default parameter file** `config/lidar_marker_localizer.param.yaml` with sensible defaults for the detection algorithm.
    5. **Add schema** `schema/lidar_marker_localizer.schema.json` documenting all parameters.
    6. **Add README** `README.md` describing the node's input/output, parameters, and design.
    7. **Integrate into tier4_localization_launch**:
       - In `localization.launch.xml`, add argument placeholders for the new parameter files.
       - In `pose_twist_estimator.launch.xml`, add `lidar-marker` to the `available_args` list, add a `use_lidar_marker_pose` flag, and include the new launch file when that flag is true, namespace the group with `pose_estimator`.
       - Create `launch/pose_twist_estimator/lidar_marker_localizer.launch.xml` (in `tier4_localization_launch`) to chain pointcloud preprocessing (crop box, ring filter) and the marker localizer node.
       - Add `autoware_lidar_marker_localizer` as an `<exec_depend>` in `launch/tier4_localization_launch/package.xml`.

pr_chain.title: Consider opposite adjacent lanes for wrong-way vehicles in blind spot module
pr_chain.description:
We need to enhance the blind spot detection module to also consider vehicles traveling in the wrong direction on the lane adjacent to the opposite side of the ego vehicle's turn. Currently, the blind spot module only generates detection and conflict areas on the adjacent lane in the direction of the turn (e.g., the lane to the left when turning left). However, there are scenarios where a wrong-way vehicle could be approaching from the opposite adjacent lane (e.g., the lane across the intersection on the opposite side of the road). To improve safety, we should extend the blind spot polygon generation to include these opposite adjacent lanes.

    The goal is to:
    1. Add a new parameter `opposite_adjacent_extend_width` to control the width of the extended detection/conflict areas on the opposite adjacent lane.
    2. Extend the `generateBlindSpotPolygons` function to identify the opposite adjacent lane (relative to the ego vehicle's turn direction) and generate additional detection and conflict areas for it.
    3. Include these new areas in the obstacle detection logic so that objects in both the standard and opposite adjacent blind spot areas are considered.
    4. Update the debug visualization to clearly show the new opposite-side areas.

    This change should be scoped to the `behavior_velocity_blind_spot_module` package only. No changes to other modules or interfaces are required.

## Environment Setup
First, review the repository structure and build configuration. The relevant package is `planning/behavior_velocity_blind_spot_module`. The package build is managed via CMake — check `planning/behavior_velocity_blind_spot_module/CMakeLists.txt`. Global build and test configuration is in the root `setup.cfg`. Also check if there is a `Makefile` or `tox.ini` at the repo root for general build/test workflows.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Add the new parameter** in `config/blind_spot.param.yaml`:
       - Add `opposite_adjacent_extend_width: 1.5 # [m]` after the existing `adjacent_extend_width`.

    2. **Declare and read the parameter** in `src/manager.cpp`:
       - In the `BlindSpotModuleManager` constructor, add a line to read `opposite_adjacent_extend_width` from the parameter server and store it in `planner_param_`.

    3. **Update the planner parameter struct** in `src/scene.hpp`:
       - Add the member `double opposite_adjacent_extend_width;` to the `PlannerParam` struct.

    4. **Extend the polygon generation** in `src/scene.cpp`:
       - In the `generateBlindSpotPolygons` function, after generating the existing adjacent lanelet (via `adjacentLeft`/`adjacentRight` depending on turn direction), also identify the *opposite* adjacent lane. This is the lanelet that is adjacent to the lanelet on the opposite side of the intersection relative to the ego turn. Use `routing_graph_ptr->adjacentLeft`/`adjacentRight` on the appropriate lanelet (the one across the intersection). Add a helper function `generateExtendedOppositeAdjacentLanelet` (mirroring `generateExtendedAdjacentLanelet`) that uses `opposite_adjacent_extend_width`.
       - Generate and append polygons for the opposite adjacent lanelet (both conflict and detection areas) to the `BlindSpotPolygons` struct.

    5. **Update the obstacle check logic** in `checkObstacleInBlindSpot`:
       - When evaluating objects, also check them against the `opposite_conflict_areas` and `opposite_detection_areas` from the returned `BlindSpotPolygons`. An object is considered an obstacle if it is in the detection area *and* has a predicted path in the conflict area — for *either* the standard areas or the opposite areas.

    6. **Update the debug visualization** in `src/debug.cpp`:
       - Add marker arrays for `opposite_conflict_areas` and `opposite_detection_areas` (e.g., using different colors to distinguish them from the standard areas).
       - Rename the existing debug data members for clarity (e.g., `conflict_areas`/`detection_areas` instead of `conflict_areas_for_blind_spot`/`detection_areas_for_blind_spot`).

    7. **Update the stop line generation** in `src/scene.cpp`:
       - The `generateStopLine` function currently returns a single index. It should now return a pair of indices — one for the default stop line and one for a "critical" stop line (likely further into the intersection to handle the opposite-side threat). Adjust the caller to select the appropriate stop line based on vehicle position relative to the default stop line.

    8. **Clean up code**:
       - Remove commented-out code (e.g., `base2front_idx_dist`).
       - Ensure all includes (e.g., `<utility>` for `std::pair`) are added to `src/scene.hpp`.

pr_chain.title: Rework pose_initializer parameters to use new node configuration layout
pr_chain.description:
We need to align the `pose_initializer` package with the new ROS Node configuration layout defined in the Autoware discussions (see https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3371). This layout standardizes how node parameters are declared and validated across the Autoware ecosystem.

    Currently, the `pose_initializer` package declares its `ekf_enabled`, `gnss_enabled`, `yabloc_enabled`, `ndt_enabled`, and `stop_check_enabled` parameters directly in the launch file via individual `<param>` tags, while the remaining parameters (covariance matrices, timeouts) come from a YAML config file. This split is inconsistent with the new configuration layout.

    The goal is to:
    1. Consolidate all parameters into the YAML config file, using substitution variables for the enabled flags.
    2. Introduce a JSON schema that documents and validates the parameter structure for the `pose_initializer` node.
    3. Update the launch file to load all parameters from the single config file, using substitution support.
    4. Update the README to include the schema documentation.

    This change will make parameter file creation more reliable and faster by providing a clear, validated schema for integrators.

## Environment Setup
Check the `localization/pose_initializer/CMakeLists.txt` file for build configuration. The repository follows standard Autoware/ROS 2 conventions — refer to the top-level `setup.cfg` for repository-wide setup. For testing, review any existing test configuration; however, this is primarily a configuration refactoring task. Build validation can be performed against the `localization/pose_initializer` package.

## Implementation Plan
1. Create `localization/pose_initializer/schema/pose_initializer.schema.json` with a JSON Schema (draft-07) that defines all node parameters under `ros__parameters` (e.g., `gnss_pose_timeout`, `stop_check_duration`, enabled flags as strings, and covariance matrices as arrays). Mark all parameters as required and disallow additional properties.
    2. Update `localization/pose_initializer/config/pose_initializer.param.yaml` to add the enabled flag entries using substitution syntax (e.g., `ekf_enabled: $(var ekf_enabled)`), keeping the rest of the parameter content unchanged.
    3. Modify `localization/pose_initializer/launch/pose_initializer.launch.xml` to remove the individual `<param name="...">` tags for the enabled flags, leaving only `<param from="$(var config_file)" allow_substs="true"/>` so all parameters are loaded from the single config file with substitutions resolved.
    4. Add the schema include directive to `localization/pose_initializer/README.md` (i.e., `{{ json_to_markdown("localization/pose_initializer/schema/pose_initializer.schema.json") }}`) so the parameter documentation is generated from the schema.
    5. Build the package locally to verify the changes compile and the launch file loads correctly with the new parameter handling.

pr_chain.title: Fix delayed obstacle_stop_planner reaction when predicted objects are used
pr_chain.description: When use_predicted_objects is enabled, the obstacle_stop_planner can react too slowly to obstacles due to a logical error in how the nearest collision point is calculated and validated. The nearest collision point is currently determined early and then checked against trajectory footprints in a later step, which can yield inconsistent results. The collision point should be determined at the point where trajectory footprints are evaluated so that the resulting stop decision and timing are accurate. Please refactor the collision search flow accordingly.

pr_chain.title: Improve scan_ground_filter performance by reducing trig and avoiding PCL conversion
pr_chain.description:
The `ScanGroundFilterComponent` in the `ground_segmentation` package is a performance bottleneck in the perception pipeline. Profiling shows that tail latency for this node is significantly higher than necessary, with a large portion of the processing time spent on:

    - **Trigonometric functions**: `std::atan2`, `std::atan`, and `std::tan` are called per-point in hot loops (e.g., `convertPointcloudGridScan`, `classifyPointCloud`, `classifyPointCloudGridScan`).
    - **Unnecessary point cloud conversions**: The current `filter()` implementation converts the input `sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2` message into a `pcl::PointCloud<pcl::PointXYZ>` before processing, and then converts the result back to a `PointCloud2` message at the end. This involves memory allocation and data copying for every point.

    The goal is to make this filter substantially faster (targeting ~1.7x tail latency improvement) **without changing the logical output**. This means the filter must produce identical results (same ground/non-ground classification) as the current implementation.

    The work should focus on:
    1.  Minimizing the use of expensive trigonometric functions in the per-point processing loops. Where possible, precompute constants (e.g., slope ratios, inverse angles) and replace direct trig calls with algebraic equivalents.
    2.  Processing the input point cloud directly from the `sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2` data buffer, accessing `x`, `y`, `z` (and `intensity` if needed) via field offsets, rather than deserializing into a `pCL` cloud.
    3.  Refactoring the point data structure to only hold the necessary information for the algorithm, reducing memory footprint and copying.
    4.  Integrating with the `pointcloud_preprocessor` framework's fast-path callback mechanism.

    The performance improvement should be verified, and the unit tests in `perception/ground_segmentation/test/` must be updated and pass to ensure the logic is unchanged.

## Environment Setup
Consult the following configuration files in the repository to understand the build and test setup:

    - `perception/ground_segmentation/CMakeLists.txt` - Contains build configuration for the `ground_segmentation` package, including test definitions.
    - `sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/CMakeLists.txt` - Contains build configuration for the `pointcloud_preprocessor` package.
    - The root `setup.cfg` and `setup.py` files may provide additional project-level setup information.

## Implementation Plan
1.  **Refactor point data structure**: Replace the `PointRef` struct with a more compact `PointData` struct that stores only essential fields (e.g., `radius`, `grid_id`, `point_state`, `orig_index`) instead of storing a pointer to a PCL point.
    2.  **Modify `convertPointcloud*` functions**: Change the signature of `convertPointcloud` and `convertPointcloudGridScan` to accept the `PointCloud2ConstPtr` directly. Access point coordinates via the `data` buffer and precomputed field offsets (`x_offset_`, `y_offset_`, `z_offset_`). Precompute `1.0f / radial_divider_angle_rad_`, `1.0f / grid_size_rad_`, and other reciprocals outside the loop to replace divisions. Replace the per-point `std::atan2` for grid ID calculation with an algebraic formula using `std::tan` precomputed as `tan_grid_size_rad_`.
    3.  **Optimize classification logic**: In `classifyPointCloud` and `classifyPointCloudGridScan`, replace direct calls to `std::atan` and `std::atan2` for slope calculations with comparisons against precomputed `tan` values (e.g., `global_slope_max_ratio_ = std::tan(global_slope_max_angle_rad_)`). Avoid any per-point trigonometeric calls. Also, simplify the `PointsCentroid::addPoint` calls to avoid unnecessary `getGridId()` etc.
    4.  **Add `faster_filter` method**: Implement the `faster_filter` method in `ScanGroundFilterComponent` and update the `filter` method to call it, or delegate the main logic entirely to `faster_filter`. This method will process the `PointCloud2` directly without PCL conversion and use the optimized `convertPointcloud`/`classifyPointCloud` functions. Ensure the `pointcloud_preprocessor::Filter` base class registers `ScanGroundFilter` in its `supported_nodes` set so the fast callback is used.
    5.  **Update unit tests**: Modify `perception/ground_segmentation/test/test_scan_ground_filter.cpp` to call the new `faster_filter` method instead of the old `filter` method to test the optimized code path. Ensure the test still constructs the node with the correct parameters and validates the output's ground/non-ground split.

pr_chain.title: Consolidate duplicate path/orientation conversion utilities into common packages
pr_chain.description:
The codebase currently has duplicate definitions of utility functions that convert between
    Autoware planning message types and interpolate orientations. These functions are defined
    independently in multiple planning packages, creating an unclear dependency structure. The goal
    is to consolidate these shared functionalities into the common `motion_utils` and

    Specifically:

    2. Move `convertPathToTrajectoryPoints()` and `convertTrajectoryPointsToPath()` into the same `conversion.hpp` as template functions `convertToTrajectoryPoints()` and `convertToPathWithLaneId()`.
    3. Move `lerpOrientation()` into the `interpolation` package's `spherical_linear_interpolation.hpp/.cpp` files, placing it in the `interpolation` namespace.
    4. Update all existing callers to reference the new canonical locations and remove the duplicate definitions from their local headers/sources.

instruction:
## Keep keyboard visible when vertically zooming the mapping zone

The mapping zone in the Shortcircuit XT UI currently hides the keyboard when you zoom vertically. The `MappingZonesAndKeyboard` component contains both the zone mapping area and the piano keyboard, and when the `Zoomable` viewport resizes its viewed component, the keyboard scrolls out of view.

    Your task is to restructure the mapping pane so the keyboard remains visible at all times, even when the vertical zoom level changes. The zones area should be independently zoomable while the keyboard stays fixed at the bottom.

    Specifically, you need to:
    1. Split `MappingZonesAndKeyboard` into two separate components: one for the zones display (which will be zoomed) and one for the keyboard (which will stay fixed).
    2. Move keyboard-only state and mouse handling into the new `Keyboard` component.
    3. Make the `MappingDisplay` a `juce::ComponentListener` so it can forward zoom and scroll events to both viewports (zones and keyboard).
    4. Guard against recursive `componentMovedOrResized` callbacks when the viewport resizes its viewed component.
    5. Force the visibility of scrollbars in the `Zoomable` viewport to prevent the viewed component from being resized when scrollbars are hidden.

## Environment Setup
Check `CMakeLists.txt` in the repository root and in `src-ui/CMakeLists.txt` for build configuration. Look at `README.md` for any build instructions. The file to modify is `src-ui/components/multi/MappingPane.cpp`.

## Implementation Plan
1. Split `MappingZonesAndKeyboard` into `Keyboard` and `MappingZones` structs. Move the piano rendering, MIDI note handling (mouseDown/Up/Drag for heldNote), and the `rectangleForKey` helper into `Keyboard`. Keep zone painting, zone rectangle calculations, and zone mouse interactions in `MappingZones`.
    2. Update `MappingDisplay` to hold both components as members, each wrapped in its own `Zoomable` viewport. Set up the keyboard viewport to only zoom horizontally, and the zones viewport to zoom both horizontally and vertically.
    3. Make `MappingDisplay` inherit from `juce::ComponentListener`. In `componentMovedOrResized`, synchronize the horizontal scroll position between the two viewports and forward zoom changes between them as needed.
    4. Add a guard flag (e.g. `bool isUpdatingComponents`) to prevent infinite recursion when the viewport resizing triggers the listener again.
    5. In the `Zoomable` constructor, call `setAutoHide(false)` on both scrollbars so they always occupy space and never cause the viewed component to be resized.
