pr_chain.title: Delay import uniqueness checking until outer package lookup completes
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to fix a false ambiguity error for conflicting imports when an outer package-level definition trumps them.

    Currently, in `findRefRecur` within `Typer.scala`, when a named or wildcard import is found, the `checkNewOrShadowed` check is applied immediately *before* recursing into the outer context. This means if two imports in the same scope conflict, an ambiguous-import error is raised even if an outer package-level definition (e.g., an `object` in the enclosing package) would shadow both imports and resolve the ambiguity.

    The fix is to postpone the uniqueness check until after the outer context has been fully explored. If the recursion into the outer context yields a different (outer) result, that result wins and no ambiguity error is raised. Only if the final result is the same as the import found earlier should `checkNewOrShadowed` be invoked to validate the import's uniqueness.

    Please ensure the change is minimal and contained to the `findRefRecur` logic for named and wildcard imports in `Typer.scala`. Add a positive test case that exercises the scenario from issue #7876.

## Environment Setup
- `build.sbt` — the main build definition; contains dependency and project configuration.
    - `project/Build.scala` — additional project/build configuration.
    - `project/build.properties` — specifies the sbt version.
    - `README.md` — may contain general build/test instructions.
    - `CONTRIBUTING.md` — may contain contribution and testing guidelines.
    - `bin/dotc` / `bin/dotd` / `bin/dotr` — launcher scripts for the compiler and tools; may indicate how the compiler is invoked.
    - Look for test-oriented configuration in `build.sbt` or `project/*.scala` to understand how the test suites (e.g., `tests/pos`) are run.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/typer/Typer.scala` and locate the `findRefRecur` method (around line 173). Review the current logic for named and wildcard imports in the `else` branch (the "find import" section).
    2. Add a new private helper method, `recurAndCheckNewOrShadowed`, as a local method inside `findRefRecur` (near the other local definitions like `checkNewOrShadowed`). This method should:
       - Accept the `previous` type, its `prevPrec` precedence, and the `prevCtx` context.
       - Recurse into the outer context using `findRefRecur(previous, prevPrec, prevCtx)` with the given context.
       - If the result of the recursion is the same object as `previous` (i.e., the outer context did not resolve to a different binding), then call `checkNewOrShadowed(found, prevPrec)` to perform the uniqueness/shadowing check.
       - Otherwise return the found (outer) result without invoking the check.
    3. Replace the two existing calls:
       - `findRefRecur(checkNewOrShadowed(namedImp, NamedImport), NamedImport, ctx)(outer)` → `recurAndCheckNewOrShadowed(namedImp, NamedImport, ctx)(given outer)`
       - `findRefRecur(checkNewOrShadowed(wildImp, WildImport), WildImport, ctx)(outer)` → `recurAndCheckNewOrShadowed(wildImp, WildImport, ctx)(given outer)`
       Ensure the `given` syntax matches the surrounding code style (the base code uses `(implicit ctx: Context)` in some places and `(given Context)` in others — follow the existing pattern in the file).
    4. Add a comment above the new helper explaining why the order is important (i.e., an outer package-level definition might trump two conflicting inner imports, so no error should be issued in that case).
    5. Create a new test file `tests/pos/i7876.scala` that reproduces the issue: define two top-level objects, import both with wildcard imports, and then reference a name that exists in both — but also define a package-level definition that shadows both. The file should compile without errors.

pr_chain.title: Reduce eager type forcing for closures with known callee types
pr_chain.description:
When typing a function literal (closure) whose expected type is not yet fully defined (e.g., a type variable), the compiler currently attempts to force/instantiate that expected type eagerly — before checking whether the closure body itself reveals the parameter types. This eager forcing can cause spurious errors or prevent valid inference in cases where the closure body is an application of a known function (e.g., `x => f(x)` or `f(_)`), because the callee's type already provides the parameter types. 

    The goal is to make the forcing of expected types for closures **lazier**: if the closure body's callee type is known and can provide the parameter types, we should not force the expected type upfront. Instead, we should only force the expected type when the callee type is not available (i.e., when the closure does not match the shape `(x1, ..., xN) => f(... x1, ..., xN ...)` or the callee type is `NoType`). This improves inference robustness — for example, code like `List(Predef.identity[Int](_))` should compile without needing an explicit type annotation on the closure when the expected type is later constrained to `List[Int => Int]`.

    Specifically, the change should:
    - Reorder the logic in `typedFunctionValue` so that the `calleeType` detection (which inspects the body shape and types the callee if needed) happens *before* any attempt to force the expected type variable via `isFullyDefined`.
    - Make `calleeType` a `lazy val` so it is only computed when actually needed (e.g., during parameter type inference).
    - Only call `isFullyDefined` on the expected type variable when the callee type does **not** exist (i.e., when no body-derived type info is available).
    - Keep the rest of the inference logic unchanged — decompose the prototype function after the above checks.

    This is a minimal, focused fix; no broader refactoring of the typer is requested.

## Environment Setup
The repository is the Dotty compiler (Scala 3). To build and run tests, check the following files:
    - `build.sbt` (main build definition; includes the `dotty-compiler` and `test` projects)
    - `project/Build.scala` (project configuration and test tasks)
    - `project/Dependencies.scala` (dependency declarations)
    - `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/typer/Typer.scala` (file containing the code to modify)
    - Tests are added under `tests/pos/` (positive compilation tests). Run the compiler tests via the `test` task defined in `build.sbt` (e.g., `sbt "testOnly *pos"` — but refer to the actual commands in the build files).

## Implementation Plan
1. In `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/typer/Typer.scala`, locate the `typedFunctionValue` method.
    2. Move the `val (protoFormals, resultTpt) = decomposeProtoFunction(pt, params.length)` line to **after** the current `pt match` block (which tries to force the expected type).
    3. Change `def calleeType: Type` to `lazy val calleeType: Type` (it is currently a `def` that may be called multiple times; making it lazy ensures it is computed at most once and only when actually referenced).
    4. In the `pt match` block for `TypeVar`, add a guard condition: only call `isFullyDefined(pt, ForceDegree.noBottom)` when `!calleeType.exists`. This ensures that if the callee type is available, we skip forcing the expected type variable.
    5. Add a positive test in `tests/pos/i7893.scala` (or extend an existing test) that exercises the case where a closure is an application of a known function with an explicit type argument, and the expected type is later constrained — e.g., `List(Predef.identity[Int](_))` assigned to `List[Int => Int]`.
    6. Run the compiler test suite (e.g., via `sbt` with the appropriate test task) to verify no regressions and that the new test passes.

pr_chain.title: Reduce eager type inference for lambda parameters in expected type
pr_chain.description:
We need to address two related issues in the typer's handling of function literals with unknown parameter types:

    1. **Issue #7879**: The compiler currently accepts a pattern match like `val head1 +: _ = List(1).view` without reporting an error, even though the resulting type of `head1` is ill-defined. This should be a negative test case — the code should be rejected with a type error. The current behavior is too permissive because the typer eagerly instantiates the expected type `TypeVar` before checking whether the function body can be used to infer parameter types.

    2. **Issue #7893**: Conversely, cases like `List(Predef.identity[Int](_))` should typecheck correctly, where the expected type is a `TypeVar` but the function body contains a call to a polymorphic method that can determine the parameter type. The current eager forcing of the `TypeVar` in `typedFunctionValue` interferes with this.

    The goal is to reorder the logic in `typedFunctionValue` so that we first attempt to determine the function's callee type (the type of the function being applied in the body) before forcing the expected type `TypeVar`. Only if the callee type cannot be determined should we fall back to forcing the `TypeVar`. This makes type inference less eager and more precise, fixing both issues. For #7879, this means the pattern match will correctly fail to compile because the type of `head1` cannot be inferred from the expected type alone.

    Please ensure:
    - The existing positive test `tests/pos/i7893.scala` (newly added) passes.
    - A new negative test `tests/neg/i7879.scala` (newly added) is added that expects an error for the pattern match example.

## Environment Setup
Check `build.sbt` at the repository root for build configuration and how to run the compiler and tests. The test suite is organized under the `tests/` directory; negative tests go in `tests/neg/` and positive tests in `tests/pos/`. The project uses `sbt` as the build tool — refer to `project/Build.scala` and `project/Dependencies.scala` for test framework setup.

## Implementation Plan
- Modify `typedFunctionValue` in `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/typer/Typer.scala` to reorder the logic:
      - Define `calleeType` as a `lazy val` so it's only computed when needed.
      - Move the `pt match { case pt: TypeVar ... }` block to *after* the `calleeType` definition but *before* calling `decomposeProtoFunction`.
      - In the `TypeVar` case, only force `pt` if `!calleeType.exists` (i.e., the callee type is not available).
    - Add the positive test `tests/pos/i7893.scala` that exercises `List(Predef.identity[Int](_))` and `List(Predef.identity[Int])` assigned to `List[Int => Int]`.
    - Add the negative test `tests/neg/i7879.scala` that attempts `val head1 +: _ = List(1).view` and expects a type error (mark with `// error` in the source).
    - Run the relevant test suites (pos and neg) to ensure the changes compile and pass.

pr_chain.title: Refine type variable instantiation before implicit search
pr_chain.description:
Improve the criterion for when type variables are instantiated before an implicit search. Currently, type variables that are completely unconstrained (no lower or upper bound other than Nothing/Any) get instantiated unnecessarily, which can lead to incorrect implicit resolution. Instead, leave such completely unconstrained type variables uninstantiated and rely on the implicit search itself to resolve them.

    Specifically, adjust the `IsFullyDefinedAccumulator` to:
    - Keep the existing behavior for type variables constrained from below or above (minimize if constrained from below, maximize if constrained from above).
    - When a new `minimizeSelected` mode is enabled, for unconstrained type variables: minimize if it has a lower bound different from Nothing, otherwise maximize if it has an upper bound different from Any, otherwise leave it uninstantiated.
    - When `minimizeSelected` is not enabled, maintain the existing fallback behavior (maximize if it appears only contravariantly or if forceDegree is `noBottom` and it has no lower bound, otherwise minimize).

    This change should make implicit searches more robust by not pre-instantiating type variables that could be resolved more precisely by the search itself.

## Environment Setup
Check `build.sbt` for general build configuration and how to run the compiler/tests. Also check `project/Build.scala` and `project/Dependencies.scala` for build details. For test running, look at `project/scripts/cmdTests` and `project/scripts/cmdTestsCommon.inc.sh` which likely contain test invocation logic.

## Implementation Plan
- Modify the `IsFullyDefinedAccumulator` class in `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/typer/Inferencing.scala` to accept a `minimizeSelected` flag (defaulting to `false`).
    - Update the accumulator's logic to handle the new `minimizeSelected` mode: when a type variable is unconstrained, check for lower/upper bounds and only instantiate if such bounds exist, otherwise leave it uninstantiated.
    - Update `instantiateSelected` in `Inferencing.scala` to pass `minimizeSelected = true` when creating the accumulator.
    - In `TypeOps.scala`, rename the `instantiate` method to `instantiateToSubType` for clarity and remove the now-unused `minimizeAll` parameter from the `ForceDegree.Value` construction.
    - Add a positive test case in `tests/pos/i7877.scala` that compiles successfully with this change, demonstrating that unconstrained type variables are not prematurely instantiated.

pr_chain.title: Prevent user subclasses of quoted.Expr and quoted.Type
pr_chain.description:
The `scala.quoted.Expr` and `scala.quoted.Type` types are currently open traits. Users can (accidentally or intentionally) create their own subclasses or instances of these types by extending the traits, instantiating them directly, or providing them as given instances. This is problematic because the compiler's implementation of quote and splice relies on these types being backed by specific internal representations (`TastyTreeExpr` and `TreeType`). When user-defined subclasses are used, the behavior is undefined and can lead to incorrect compilation or runtime errors.

    The goal is to make `scala.quoted.Expr` and `scala.quoted.Type` non-extensible by users. We need to ensure that only the compiler-internal implementation can create instances of these types. Since these types are not sealed (and should not be, as the compiler needs to extend them from a different package), the approach is to:
    - Make `scala.quoted.Expr` and `scala.quoted.Type` classes with `private[scala]` constructors, so users cannot extend or instantiate them directly.
    - Add internal base classes in `scala.internal.quoted` that the compiler's implementation extends, and have the public types extend those internal classes.
    - Update the compiler's internal classes (`TastyTreeExpr` and `TreeType`) to extend the internal base classes instead of the public traits directly.

    This will prevent users from creating invalid `Expr` and `Type` instances, while still allowing the compiler to work with its internal implementations.

    Refer to issue #7919 for the original bug report.

## Environment Setup
This is a Scala project using sbt. Check the `build.sbt` file and `project/` directory (especially `project/Build.scala` and `project/plugins.sbt`) for build configuration and dependency setup. The project's README (`README.md`) and `CONTRIBUTING.md` may also contain relevant build and test instructions.

## Implementation Plan
- Modify `library/src/scala/quoted/Expr.scala`: change `trait Expr[+T]` to `class Expr[+T] private[scala]`. Remove the restriction note from the doc comment, as it will no longer be a trait.
    - Modify `library/src/scala/quoted/Type.scala`: change `trait Type[T <: AnyKind]` to `class Type[T <: AnyKind] private[scala]`. Remove the restriction note from the doc comment.
    - Add new class definitions in `library/src/scala/internal/quoted/Expr.scala`:
      - Add a non-final `class Expr[+T] extends scala.quoted.Expr[T]` with a doc comment noting the restriction that only the compiler implementation may extend it.
    - Add new class definitions in `library/src/scala/internal/quoted/Type.scala`:
      - Add a non-final `class Type[T <: AnyKind] extends scala.quoted.Type[T]` with a similar doc comment.
    - Update `library/src/scala/internal/quoted/Expr.scala` and `library/src/scala/internal/quoted/Type.scala` to change the signatures of the `unapply` methods to accept `scala.quoted.Expr[_]` and `scala.quoted.Type[_]` respectively (instead of the internal types).
    - Update `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/tastyreflect/TastyTreeExpr.scala`: change `extends scala.quoted.Expr[Any]` to `extends scala.internal.quoted.Expr[Any]`.
    - Update `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/tastyreflect/TreeType.scala`: change `extends scala.quoted.Type[Any]` to `extends scala.internal.quoted.Type[Any]`.
    - Update `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/core/quoted/PickledQuotes.scala` to remove the now-unnecessary import of `scala.internal.quoted._` (if needed).
    - Add a negative test file `tests/neg/i7919.scala` with examples of invalid user code that should now fail to compile (e.g., extending `Expr`, instantiating `Expr`, providing a given `Expr` or `Type`, extending `Type`, etc.).

We need to add negative tests for `erasedValue` to make sure it cannot be used as a value in contexts where it shouldn't be. Specifically, add test cases that verify `erasedValue` fails to compile when passed to a method that expects a regular (non-erased) parameter, and that it also works when the parameter is marked as `erased`. Please add these as new test files in the appropriate test directories.

pr_chain.title: Fix sbt test discovery to exclude traits from eligible tests
pr_chain.description:
When the Dotty compiler extracts API information for sbt, it incorrectly marks traits as abstract-like, which causes sbt's test discovery to consider traits as potentially instantiable test classes. This happens because the `apiModifiers` method in `ExtractAPI.scala` checks for the `Abstract` and `Deferred` flags but does not check for the `Trait` flag. Since traits do not have the `Abstract` flag set, they slip through and become candidates for test discovery.

    Fix the `apiModifiers` method in `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/sbt/ExtractAPI.scala` so that:
    1. Traits are correctly identified as abstract (the `Trait` flag implies the entity is not concrete).
    2. The check order is optimized to short-circuit flag checks where possible, improving efficiency.

    Add regression tests that verify both abstract classes and traits are excluded from sbt test discovery.

## Environment Setup
Check `build.sbt` and `project/Build.scala` at the repository root for how the project is structured and how to build the compiler. For running the sbt scripted tests, look at the `sbt-dotty/` directory and any related configuration in `build.sbt` or `project/Build.scala`. The `sbt-dotty/sbt-test/discovery/test-discovery/` directory contains the scripted test framework setup.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/sbt/ExtractAPI.scala` and locate the `apiModifiers` method (around line 583).
    2. Modify the computation of the `abs` variable:
       - Keep the existing `absOver` check as the short-circuit first condition.
       - Use the `isOneOf` method to check if the symbol has any of the `Trait`, `Abstract`, or `Deferred` flags.
    3. Move the `absOver` check to the front of the `over` computation to short-circuit when possible:
       - Change `val over = sym.is(Override) || absOver` to `val over = absOver || sym.is(Override)`.
    4. Create two new test files in `sbt-dotty/sbt-test/discovery/test-discovery/src/test/scala/`:
       - `AbstractClassTest.scala`: an abstract class with a `@Test` annotated method.
       - `TraitTest.scala`: a trait with a `@Test` annotated method.
    5. Ensure both test files include the standard JUnit imports (`org.junit.Test` and `org.junit.Assert`) and have a comment indicating test discovery should not pick them up.

pr_chain.title: Fix Scala.js trait initializer call naming in Mixin phase
pr_chain.description:
When compiling for Scala.js, super calls to Scala 2.x trait constructors (which are named `$init$` rather than `<init>`) are currently not being rewritten correctly in the `Mixin` transformation phase. The issue is that the `transformSym` method in `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/transform/Mixin.scala` only renames trait constructors for Dotty (non-Scala2x) traits. However, Scala.js expects Scala 2.x trait initializer methods to also be renamed to the trait constructor name (`nme.TRAIT_CONSTRUCTOR`), since Scala.js does not rewrite these super calls into static method calls.

    The task is to modify the `transformSym` method so that when compiling for Scala.js, constructors of Scala 2.x traits are also renamed to `nme.TRAIT_CONSTRUCTOR` (i.e., `$init$`). This needs to be done conditionally — only when the `scalajs` compiler setting is enabled — since the JVM backend should continue to handle Scala 2.x trait initializers differently.

    Additionally, the diff includes updates to `project/Build.scala` to re-enable previously-excluded Scala.js test suite files (specifically in the `javalib/util/concurrent` directory and removing some exclusions in `javalib/util` and `scalalib`). These changes broaden the test suite coverage once the naming fix is in place.

## Environment Setup
Check `build.sbt` and `project/Build.scala` for build configuration and dependency management. The `project/scripts/sbt` script may provide a wrapper for running sbt commands. Refer to `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general project contribution and build guidance.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/transform/Mixin.scala` and locate the `transformSym` method.
    2. Modify the condition that currently reads:
       ```scala
       else if (sym.isConstructor && sym.owner.is(Trait, butNot = Scala2x))
       ```
    3. Update it so that the constructor renaming also applies to Scala 2.x traits when Scala.js is enabled. The condition should become something like:
       ```scala
       else if (sym.isConstructor && (sym.owner.is(Trait, butNot = Scala2x) || (sym.owner.isAllOf(Trait | Scala2x) && ctx.settings.scalajs.value)))
       ```
    4. Keep the rest of the else-if chain structure intact — do not nest additional if/else blocks inside the existing branches. Integrate the new condition cleanly into the existing chain.
    5. In `project/Build.scala`, locate the `managedSources in Test` configuration block (around line 999).
    6. Update the file filter for the `javalib/util/concurrent` directory to include all `*.scala` files instead of excluding several test files:
       Change from:
       ```scala
       ** (("*.scala": FileFilter) -- "ConcurrentHashMapTest.scala" -- "ConcurrentLinkedQueueTest.scala" -- "ConcurrentMapTest.scala" -- "ConcurrentSkipListSetTest.scala" -- "CopyOnWriteArrayListTest.scala")
       ```
       to:
       ```scala
       ** "*.scala"
       ```
    7. In the `javalib/util` directory filter (using the `*` operator), remove the exclusions for `AbstractCollectionTest.scala`, `CollectionTest.scala`, `ListTest.scala`, `MapTest.scala`, `NavigableSetTest.scala`, and `SetTest.scala`. Keep the other exclusions intact.
    8. In the `scalalib` directory filter, remove the `-- "RangesTest.scala"` exclusion.

pr_chain.title: Prevent type variables from being bounded by ExprTypes during constraint solving
pr_chain.description:
We need to fix a type inference issue in the Scala 3 compiler where type variables can incorrectly be bounded by ExprTypes (by-name types). The goal is to ensure that type parameters are never instantiated to ExprTypes, as ExprTypes are not value types and cannot be written in source code.

## Problem Case

Consider the following code:

```scala
object O {
  def f(i: => Int): Int = 1
  def m[A](a: A => Int) = 2
  def n = m(f)
}
```

When compiling `m(f)`, the compiler is trying to unify the type of `f` (which after eta-expansion becomes `(=> Int) => Int`) with the expected type `A => Int`. During this unification, the type variable `A` is incorrectly being bounded by the ExprType `=> Int`. This leads to a confusing error message showing `Found: => Int => Int` instead of reporting that eta-expansion is not possible for this case.

## Expected Behavior

The compiler should recognize that a type variable cannot be instantiated to an ExprType and should report a proper error indicating that eta-expansion is not possible for methods with by-name parameters in this context.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files in the repository root for build and test setup:
    - `build.sbt` - main build configuration
    - `project/Build.scala` - build definitions
    - `project/build.properties` - sbt version
    - `CONTRIBUTING.md` - contribution guidelines
    - `.jvmopts` - JVM options for the build

## Implementation Plan
The fix involves two files:

    1. **`compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/core/ConstraintHandling.scala`** (around line 508):
       - In the `prune` method, add a new case to handle `ExprType` bounds
       - When the bound being pruned is an `ExprType`, return `NoType` (indicating that this bound is not valid for a type variable)
       - This prevents the type variable from being instantiated to an ExprType during constraint solving
       - Add a comment explaining why this is necessary (referencing the EtaExpansion comment)

    2. **`compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/typer/EtaExpansion.scala`** (around line 198):
       - Add a documentation comment to the `etaExpand` method explaining:
         - Why we allow eta-expanding methods with by-name parameters to types like `(=> T) => T` (even though such types can't be written in source)
         - The historical context (the rule was initially stricter but was relaxed)
         - A reference to the `ConstraintHandling` fix that handles the consequences of this
     
    3. **`tests/neg/i7969.scala`** (new test file):
       - Create a new negative test file with the test case shown above
       - Mark the line with `// error: cannot eta expand` comment

    4. Documentation updates:
       - Update the test file to match the repo's test conventions (check other tests in `tests/neg/` for format)

pr_chain.title: Update authorization docs for instance-based bound action restrictions
pr_chain.description:
We need to update the Node.js security documentation in `guides/security/authorization.md` to reflect the new capability introduced in CAP 8.3: instance-based authorization for bound actions and functions.

Specifically, we need to:

1. **Update the "Supported Combinations with CDS Resources" table** (around line 341): The current table indicates that `where` conditions are not supported for actions/functions. The new behavior is:
   - For **bound actions and functions** that are bound against a **single instance** (not a collection), Node.js now supports instance-based authorization at the **entity level**. This means `where` clauses can contain references to the model (e.g., `where: CreatedBy = $user`).
   - For bound actions and functions bound against a **collection**, Node.js supports only simple static expressions (without model references) at the entity level (e.g., `where: $user.level = 2`).

2. **Update the footnotes** associated with that table to clearly explain these two distinct cases for actions/functions. The current footnote (numbered 1) needs to be renumbered and expanded.

3. **Update the "Instance-Based Authorization" section** (around line 495): The note about static expressions for all events (including actions and functions) needs to be corrected. Static expressions without model references are supported for all events, but instance-based expressions with model references are now only supported for bound actions/functions on single instances.

The goal is to make the documentation accurate and clear about what's possible with Node.js in version 8.3 and later, so developers understand the distinction between:
- Static expressions (no model reference), e.g., `$user.level = 2` — supported for all actions/functions
- Instance-based expressions (with model reference), e.g., `CreatedBy = $user` — supported for bound actions/functions on single instances only

Please ensure the terminology is consistent with the rest of the document and that footnote numbering is correct.

## Environment Setup
This is a documentation repository for the CAP documentation site. Check the following files to understand how to work with the repo:
- `package.json` — for project scripts and dependencies (VitePress-based documentation site)
- `.vitepress/config.ts` — for site configuration

- `package-lock.json` — for exact dependency versions
- `.nvmrc` — for the required Node.js version
- `.github/workflows/` — for CI/CD pipeline definitions that show how linting and validation are performed

## Implementation Plan
1. Read the current `guides/security/authorization.md` file, focusing on the "Supported Combinations with CDS Resources" table and the "Instance-Based Authorization" section.
  2. Update the table's action/function row to indicate support for `where` clauses with appropriate footnote markers.
  3. Rewrite the footnote text to clearly explain the two scenarios: (a) bound actions on single instances support model references, (b) unbound actions and collection-bound actions support only static expressions.
  4. Update the note in the "Instance-Based Authorization" section to reflect that static expressions apply to all events, while instance-based expressions apply only to bound actions on single instances.
  5. Verify footnote numbering is sequential and correct throughout the document, and ensure markdown linting passes.

pr_chain.title: Fix stale keyboard shortcut commands across page navigation
pr_chain.description:
The keyboard shortcuts dialog in the documentation site currently caches its command list in a reactive array that is populated once when the component mounts. Because the commands are derived from page-specific elements (like the "Edit on GitHub" link, "Next/Previous page" pagers, and theme configuration for secondary files), the list becomes stale when navigating between pages. This causes shortcuts to point to elements that no longer exist on the current page, leading to broken behavior (e.g., clicking a shortcut that triggers a non-existent element, or shortcuts that appear enabled but do nothing).

    The goal is to ensure that the shortcut commands are recomputed each time the page changes, so the list always reflects the current page's actual DOM elements and configuration. The implementation should keep the existing user-facing behavior and keyboard interactions intact while making the command list reactive to page navigation.

## Environment Setup
Check the `package.json` at the repository root for the site's dependencies and general setup. Review `.vitepress/config.ts` for VitePress configuration details. The component to modify is `.vitepress/theme/components/ShortcutsList.vue`. Look at the `CONTRIBUTING.md` and any relevant scripts in `package.json` for guidance on how the project is structured and how to work with the VitePress theme components.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `.vitepress/theme/components/ShortcutsList.vue` and examine the current command definition.
    2. Convert the `commands` array from a plain reactive array into a computed property that returns a fresh array of commands. This ensures the list is recomputed when any of its reactive dependencies change (such as `theme`, `page`, or `site` data from VitePress's `useData()`).
    3. Remove the `reactive` import from Vue if it's no longer used elsewhere in the component; keep `computed`, `ref`, and other necessary imports.
    4. Since `commands` is now a computed property, update all references that previously used the plain array to access `commands.value` instead. This includes the `activeCommands` computed property and the `onKeyDown` event handler that looks up a command by key.
    5. In the `activeCommands` computed, adjust the mapping logic to avoid mutating the command objects directly (since they are now part of a fresh computed array each time). The current code assigns `keyStrings` to each command; this should still work but be aware that the mapping now operates on newly created command objects.
    6. Ensure that any side effects or event listeners are properly handled — the recomputation should not break the existing keyboard event handling or dialog visibility logic.

pr_chain.title: Reset routing stats on route errors and support reset-able stats
pr_chain.description:
## Task
We need to fix an issue where the routing state of the application can become inconsistent when a route calculation or profile request fails. Specifically:

1. **Stale stats**: When a route request fails (e.g., the elevation service errors out), the `stats` property of the routing state remains set to the previous route's statistics, even though the `route` property is correctly reset to `null`. This leaves the UI in an inconsistent state, showing stats for a route that no longer exists.

2. **Atomic updates**: The routing store currently updates `route` and `stats` in two separate actions. This means there is a brief window where one property is set while the other is stale. We need a way to update both properties atomically.

3. **Reset-able stats**: The `setRouteStats` action currently always spreads its payload, which means it cannot be called with `null` to reset the stats. Make `setRouteStats` accept `null` (and return `null` in that case).

## Goal
The goal is to ensure that whenever a route is recalculated or a request fails, both the `route` and `stats` properties are reset or updated together, and that the stats can be cleared when no valid route exists.

Additionally, the `OlElevationProfileHandler` should only respond to interactions when a supported tool (e.g., DRAW or MEASURE) is active, to avoid unnecessary updates to the elevation profile when unrelated interactions are added/removed.

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` for available scripts (e.g., `test`, `lint`) and dependencies. The test setup is defined in `karma.conf.js`, `karma.conf.single.js`, and `webpack.test.config.js`. The CI workflow is configured in `.github/workflows/node.js.yml`. The `README.md` may also contain general project setup instructions.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Update `setRouteStats` action**: In `src/store/routing/routing.action.js`, modify the `setRouteStats` action so that it can accept `null`. The payload should be `{ ...routeStats }` only when `routeStats` is truthy; otherwise, the payload should be `null`.

    2. **Add a new combined action**: Add a new action `setRouteAndStats` in `src/store/routing/routing.action.js`. This action should accept two arguments `(route, routeStats)` and dispatch a new action type `ROUTING_ROUTE_AND_STATS_CHANGED` with a payload of `{ route: route ? { ...route } : null, stats: routeStats ? { ...routeStats } : null }`.

    3. **Update the reducer**: In `src/store/routing/routing.reducer.js`, add a new action type `ROUTING_ROUTE_AND_STATS_CHANGED` and handle it in the reducer. This case should update both `route` and `stats` properties atomically, spreading the payload values only if they are truthy.

    4. **Update the routing handler**: In `src/modules/olMap/handler/routing/OlRoutingHandler.js`, replace the separate calls to `setRoute` and `setRouteStats` in the `_updateStore` method with a single call to the new `setRouteAndStats` action. Also, introduce a private helper `_resetStore()` that calls `setRouteAndStats(null, null)`. Use this helper:
       - At the beginning of `_requestRouteFromCoordinates` (before clearing features) to reset the store immediately when a new route calculation starts.
       - In the catch block of `_updateStore` (previously `setRoute(null)`) to also reset the stats.
       - Remove the separate `setRoute(null)` call when only one coordinate is present, and rely on the initial `_resetStore()` call.

    5. **Update the elevation profile handler**: In `src/modules/olMap/handler/elevationProfile/OlElevationProfileHandler.js`, add a private field `#callUpdateListener` and observe the `state.tools.current` value from the store. Set this flag based on whether the current tool is in a new static `SUPPORTED_TOOL_IDS` getter (returning a list containing `Tools.DRAW` and `Tools.MEASURE`). Only add/remove listeners for `Select` and `Modify` interactions when this flag is `true`. This prevents the handler from interfering with interactions when an unsupported tool is active.

    6. **Update JSDoc**: Ensure that the new `setRouteStats` and `setRouteAndStats` actions have updated JSDoc comments indicating that `null` is an accepted value for the stats parameter.

pr_chain.title: Prevent non-unique feature IDs for routing intermediate features
pr_chain.description:
The routing intermediate features (icons added to the map for waypoints between start and destination) currently receive their feature ID based solely on their index within the list of interaction features, in the format `routing_{index}`. This can lead to non-unique feature IDs when routing features are added or removed, or when the index is reused after a feature is deleted.

    Having non-unique IDs on OpenLayers features can cause problems with map interactions, style lookups, and other operations that rely on feature identity. The goal is to ensure every routing intermediate feature gets a globally unique ID regardless of its index.

    Please make the following changes:
    - When creating an intermediate interaction feature, generate its ID using a unique identifier utility so that the `routing_` prefix is combined with a unique value (e.g. `routing_<uniqueId>`), rather than the feature index.
    - Update the corresponding test expectations to no longer assume the ID is based on the index, but instead verify the ID has the correct `routing_` prefix and is unique.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's package.json for dependency management and available scripts. The test configuration is split across karma.conf.js, karma.conf.gha.js, karma.conf.single.js, and webpack.test.config.js — review these to understand how the test suite is set up. Also check the .github/workflows/node.js.yml workflow file to see the CI test pipeline.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `src/modules/olMap/handler/routing/OlRoutingHandler.js` and locate the `_addIntermediateInteractionFeature` method (around line 356).
    2. Import a unique ID generator from the utility module. The repository has `src/utils/numberUtils.js` which likely contains a `createUniqueId` function — verify its presence and export.
    3. Modify the line that sets the feature ID:
       - Change from: `iconFeature.setId(`\${StyleTypes.ROUTING}_\${index}`);`
       - To: `iconFeature.setId(`\${StyleTypes.ROUTING}_\${createUniqueId()}`);`
    4. Ensure the imported utility is used correctly with the existing import style in the file.
    5. Open `test/modules/olMap/handler/routing/OlRoutingHandler.test.js` and locate the test case `'adds a correctly configured feature'` inside the `_addIntermediateInteractionFeature` describe block (around line 1105).
    6. Update the assertion for the feature ID:
       - Change from: `expect(feature.getId()).toBe('routing_42');`
       - To: `expect(feature.getId().startsWith(\`\${StyleTypes.ROUTING}_\`)).toBeTrue();`
       - Also add a check to verify the IDs are unique if multiple intermediate features are created (e.g. call the method twice and assert the two IDs differ).
    7. Add the necessary import for `StyleTypes` in the test file (already partially present in the diff).

pr_chain.title: Refine keyboard focus indicators to use focus-visible pseudo-class
pr_chain.description:
We need to improve our keyboard accessibility by ensuring focus indicators only appear for keyboard navigation, not mouse clicks. Currently, our interactive elements (buttons, form inputs, selects, sliders, and icons) show focus styles on every focus event, including mouse clicks. This creates visual noise where clicking an element triggers the focus highlight unnecessarily.

    The goal is to replace all `:focus` selectors with `:focus-visible` in our stylesheets to only apply focus styles when the element is focused via keyboard navigation (e.g., using the Tab key). This will preserve the visual feedback for keyboard users while preventing focus rings from appearing when using a mouse.

    The key files to modify are:
    - `src/modules/baElement.css` - contains focus styles for form elements (selects, inputs, ranges)
    - `src/modules/commons/components/button/button.css` - contains focus styles for primary, secondary, and loading buttons
    - `src/modules/commons/components/icon/Icon.js` - contains inline focus styles for icon anchors

    Please ensure all focus-related styles use `:focus-visible` instead of `:focus`. This includes:
    - Direct focus selectors (e.g., `select:focus`)
    - Adjacent sibling selectors (e.g., `input:focus ~ .control-label`)
    - Auto-fill states (e.g., `input:-webkit-autofill:focus`)
    - Generated inline styles in the Icon component

    Note that we already have a global `*:focus-visible` rule in `baElement.css` that provides a base box-shadow, but individual component-specific styles need to be updated to maintain consistent behavior.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repository files to understand the project setup and testing infrastructure:
    - `package.json` - lists dependencies and scripts
    - `package-lock.json` - locks dependency versions
    - `.eslintrc.js` - linting configuration
    - `.stylelintrc` - style linting configuration

pr_chain.title: Normalize KML icon URLs between legacy and current backend formats
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to ensure that KML vector layers display their icons correctly regardless of whether the icon URLs originate from the legacy BayernAtlas backend (`https://geoportal.bayern.de/ba-backend`) or the current backend. Currently, all KML icon URLs are passed through a proxifying function, which can break icons served directly from our own backend or map legacy icon URL patterns incorrectly.

    We need to:
    1. Create a new icon URL handling function for KML layers that distinguishes between:
       - URLs from the legacy backend with the `/icons/` path pattern, which should be remapped to the equivalent current backend URL format
       - URLs from the current backend, which should be used without proxying
       - All other URLs, which should continue to be proxified as before
    2. Update the KML format configuration to use this new function instead of the current generic one
    3. Add a utility method to `UrlService` that extracts path parameters from a URL, enabling the icon URL logic to inspect and reconstruct URL paths
    4. Add comprehensive tests covering all URL handling scenarios

    The legacy icon URL pattern is `https://geoportal.bayern.de/ba-backend/icons/{color}/{name}`, which should be transformed to `{BACKEND_URL}icons/{color}/{name}.png`. The current backend URL pattern (e.g., `https://{current-backend}/icons/...`) should remain untouched.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repository files for setup and test instructions:
    - `package.json` — for dependency management and script definitions
    - `.nvmrc` — for the required Node.js version
    - `karma.conf.js`, `karma.conf.single.js`, `karma.conf.gha.js` — for test runner configuration
    - `webpack.test.config.js` — for test-specific build configuration
    - `.eslintrc.js`, `.prettierrc.json` — for code style and linting rules
    - `.github/workflows/node.js.yml` — for the CI pipeline configuration

## Implementation Plan
1. Add a `pathParams(url)` method to `UrlService` that extracts path segments from a URL using the built-in `URL` API, filtering out empty segments and returning an array
    2. Create a new `bvvIconUrlFunction` in `VectorLayerService` that takes a URL and applies the URL routing logic:
       - Check if the URL starts with the legacy backend origin/path; if so, inspect its path params to determine if it matches the legacy icon pattern
       - For legacy icon URLs matching the pattern, construct the new URL using the configured `BACKEND_URL` and append the icon color and name with a `.png` extension
       - For URLs from the current backend (matching `BACKEND_URL` prefix), return the URL unchanged
       - For all other URLs, pass through the existing proxify logic
    3. Replace the `iconUrlFunction` usage in the KML format creation with the new `bvvIconUrlFunction`
    4. Update tests in `VectorLayerService.test.js` to cover all branches of the new icon URL function, including mocking `ConfigService` and testing legacy mapping, unchanged current-backend URLs, and proxification of external URLs
    5. Add tests in `UrlService.test.js` for the new `pathParams` method covering various URL formats and edge cases

pr_chain.title: Add configurable response interceptor support to HttpService fetch and convenience methods
pr_chain.description:
Extend the `HttpService` class to support an optional, per-call response interceptor. This allows callers to inspect, transform, or retry the Fetch API response before it is returned to the caller. The interceptor receives the original response, a repeatable fetch function, and the resource URL.

    The change should:
    - Add an `interceptors` parameter to `fetch`, `get`, `head`, and other convenience methods as appropriate.
    - Make the underlying fetch call repeatable by extracting it into an inner function that can be invoked by the interceptor.
    - Update JSDoc to document the new interceptor types and parameters.
    - Ensure `NetworkStateSyncHttpService` continues to work correctly by passing all arguments to the parent `fetch`.
    - Improve related JSDoc annotations in `LayerService.js` and `baaImageLoadFunction.provider.js` for the image load function provider typedef.

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` for dependency scripts and `karma.conf.js`, `karma.conf.gha.js`, `karma.conf.single.js`, and `webpack.test.config.js` for test runner configuration. The `.eslintrc.js` and `.prettierrc.json` define code style requirements. The `.github/workflows/node.js.yml` shows CI steps.

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify `src/services/HttpService.js`:
       - Add a `responseInterceptor` typedef and `HttpServiceInterceptors` object typedef in JSDoc.
       - In `fetch`, extract the fetch/abort logic into an internal `doFetch` async function that performs the actual `window.fetch` call with timeout and signal handling.
       - Add a fourth parameter `interceptors = {}` to `fetch`. After `doFetch()` resolves, if `interceptors.response` is a function, call it with `(response, doFetch, resource)` and return its result; otherwise return the response.
       - Add an `interceptors = {}` parameter to `get`, `delete`, `post`, and `head` convenience methods, and pass it through to `this.fetch`.
    2. Update `NetworkStateSyncHttpService.fetch` in the same file to accept and forward the new `interceptors` parameter to `super.fetch`, so network state tracking remains correct when an interceptor is used.
    3. Update JSDoc in `src/modules/olMap/services/LayerService.js` to define and reference the `baaImageLoadFunctionProvider` typedef properly.
    4. Update JSDoc in `src/modules/olMap/utils/baaImageLoadFunction.provider.js` to reference the new typedef.

pr_chain.title: Add global error handling to catch and notify about runtime errors
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to introduce a global error handling mechanism for the application. This should catch runtime errors and unhandled promise rejections, and display user-friendly notifications to inform them about issues that occurred. The primary use case is to inform the user when a GeoResource is unavailable (e.g., due to network issues, authentication problems, or server errors).

    We need to:
    1.  Define error classes that can be caught globally, specifically a base runtime error class and a specialized error for unavailable GeoResources.
    2.  Create a plugin that listens for global errors and unhandled promise rejections, and dispatches notifications to the user based on the error type.
    3.  Register this plugin in the dependency injection container and ensure it's instantiated during application startup.
    4.  Add appropriate translations for the user-facing error messages.
    5.  Adjust webpack configuration to allow the application to catch runtime errors instead of the dev server overlay.
    6.  Adjust Karma configuration to prevent browser disconnects during the test run, which can happen when global errors are being intercepted.

    Please ensure that the solution is focused and does not involve broader refactoring of the error handling or notification system.

## Environment Setup
To install dependencies and run tests, please refer to the instructions in the `README.md` file. The `package.json` file contains the project dependencies and available scripts. For test configuration and commands, look at `karma.conf.js`, `karma.conf.single.js`, and `karma.conf.gha.js`. The `webpack.config.js` file contains the development server configuration.

## Implementation Plan
1.  Create a new file `src/domain/errors.js` that exports two classes:
        - `BaRuntimeError`: extends `Error`, accepts a message and an options object (for `cause`).
        - `UnavailableGeoResourceError`: extends `BaRuntimeError`, accepts a message, `geoResourceId`, optional `httpStatus`, and options.
    2.  Create a new file `src/plugins/GlobalErrorPlugin.js` that exports a class `GlobalErrorPlugin` extending `BaPlugin`. The `register()` method should:
        - Inject the `TranslationService`.
        - Define a `handleError` function that checks if the error is an `UnavailableGeoResourceError` and dispatches a WARN notification accordingly (using `emitNotification` and `LevelTypes.WARN`). Otherwise, it should dispatch a generic error notification (using `global_generic_exception` and `LevelTypes.ERROR`).
        - Add a `window` event listener for 'error' and 'unhandledrejection' events, calling `handleError` with the error/reason from the event.
    3.  In `src/injection/config.js`, import and register the new `GlobalErrorPlugin` as a singleton.
    4.  In `src/services/StoreService.js`, retrieve the `GlobalErrorPlugin` from the injector and call its `register(store)` method in the plugin registration phase.
    5.  In `src/i18n/global.provider.js`, add the `global_generic_exception` translation key for both 'en' and 'de' locales.
    6.  In `webpack.config.js`, configure the `devServer.client.overlay.runtimeErrors` to `true` (or remove the option to default to `true`), ensuring the app doesn't conflict with the dev server's error overlay.
    7.  In `karma.conf.gha.js`, increase the `browserDisconnectTimeout` to a higher value (e.g., 90000) to accommodate the new global error handling.

instruction:
## Add LazyClassKey annotation for lazy class-keyed map injection

Implement a new `@LazyClassKey` annotation that allows Dagger to inject maps keyed by Class objects without eagerly loading the Class when the map value isn't needed. This annotation should be used on `@MapKey`-annotated methods to indicate that the map key should be represented as a lazy reference, deferring class loading until the value is actually accessed.

    The implementation requires changes to the generated code infrastructure:
    1. Support for generating anonymous `Lazy` implementations in code blocks
    2. Addition of `MapBuilder` type reference
    3. Refactoring `MapRequestRepresentation` to separate the underlying map expression generation from the dependency expression
    4. Allow `MapFactoryCreationExpression` to work with `Object` as a generic type parameter instead of requiring specific value types

    This change is part of optimizing Dagger's generated code to avoid unnecessary class loading in scenarios where maps with Class keys are injected but not all values are accessed.

## Environment Setup
Check the following configuration files for build and test setup:
    - `BUILD` - Bazel build configuration
    - `WORKSPACE` - Bazel workspace configuration
    - `.bazelrc` - Bazel settings
    - `build_defs.bzl` - Build definitions
    - `test_defs.bzl` - Test definitions
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - CI workflow configuration

## Implementation Plan
1. Add `anonymousLazy` static method to `CodeBlocks.java` that generates an anonymous `Lazy` implementation with a `get()` method containing the provided body code.
    2. Add `MAP_BUILDER` and `STRING` constant references to `TypeNames.java`.
    3. Refactor `MapRequestRepresentation.getDependencyExpression()` to extract the map construction logic into a private `getUnderlyingMapExpression()` method.
    4. Modify `MapFactoryCreationExpression` to use `TypeName.OBJECT` as fallback value type when the map type doesn't match standard provider/producer types, enabling more flexible type parameterization.
    5. Ensure all existing map request representations continue to work correctly with the refactored code structure.

pr_chain.title: Add compile-time error for final onCreate/onDestroy in base Activity classes
pr_chain.description:
When a user annotates an Activity with `@AndroidEntryPoint` and specifies a base class (e.g., `@AndroidEntryPoint(BaseActivity.class)`), Hilt generates a subclass that overrides `onCreate` and `onDestroy` methods. These overridden methods are essential for Hilt's SavedStateHandle injection and cleanup functionality.

    However, if the user marks `onCreate` or `onDestroy` as `final` in the base Activity class, Hilt's generated subclass cannot override these methods, which leads to runtime failures or silent breakage of Hilt's state management. Currently, no warning or error is produced at compile time.

    **Goal:** Add a compile-time error message when the nearest override method for `onCreate` or `onDestroy` (found via `requireNearestOverrideMethod`) is marked as `final`. The error should be reported on the offending method element.

    **Implementation location:** This validation should be added in `ActivityGenerator.java`, specifically in the `onCreateComponentActivity()` and `onDestroyComponentActivity()` methods, right after fetching the `nearestOverrideMethod`.

## Environment Setup

pr_chain.title: Add KSP Processor for Dagger Android Proguard Processor
pr_chain.description:
We need to add KSP (Kotlin Symbol Processing) support for the Dagger Android Proguard Processor. Currently, `ProguardProcessor.java` uses the standard Java annotation processing API (`AbstractProcessor`). The goal is to refactor this to use the XProcessing abstraction layer (Room Compiler Processing), which supports both Java (Javac) and Kotlin (KSP) processing environments.

    Specifically:
    1. Refactor the existing `ProguardProcessor.java` to extend `JavacBasicAnnotationProcessor` (from `androidx.room.compiler.processing.javac`).
    2. Create a new `KspProguardProcessor.java` that extends `KspBasicAnnotationProcessor` (from `androidx.room.compiler.processing.ksp`).
    3. Extract the actual proguard rule generation logic into a shared `ProguardProcessingStep.java` that extends the existing `BaseProcessingStep` class.
    4. Make `BaseProcessingStep` public and extract it into its own Bazel target so it can be shared between the proguard processor and the existing Android processor.
    5. Update the Bazel `BUILD` files to reflect these new dependencies and source files.

    The functionality must remain identical - generating proguard rules for Dagger Android projects:
    - `resources/META-INF/com.android.tools/proguard/dagger-android.pro`
    - `resources/META-INF/com.android.tools/r8/dagger-android.pro`
    - `resources/META-INF/proguard/dagger-android.pro`

## Environment Setup
Check the `WORKSPACE` file at the repository root to understand the Bazel workspace setup and external dependencies. The `java/dagger/android/internal/proguard/BUILD` and `java/dagger/android/processor/BUILD` files contain the Bazel build targets you'll need to modify. Refer to `build_defs.bzl` for build configuration macros. For testing, examine the `JAVA` test targets in existing `BUILD` files under `javatests/`.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create `ProguardProcessingStep.java`** in `java/dagger/android/internal/proguard/`:
       - Create a class that extends `dagger.android.processor.BaseProcessingStep`
       - Add a static `ClassName` constant for `dagger.android.internal.GenerateAndroidInjectionProguardRules`
       - Override `annotationClassNames()` to return the annotation
       - Override `process(XElement, ImmutableSet)` to write the proguard rules using `XProcessingEnv.getFiler()`
       - Reuse the existing rule strings (`errorProneRule`, `androidInjectionKeysRule`) and write files to `com.android.tools/proguard`, `com.android.tools/r8`, and `proguard` paths

    2. **Refactor `ProguardProcessor.java`**:
       - Change class to extend `JavacBasicAnnotationProcessor` instead of `AbstractProcessor`
       - Add a field for `XProcessingEnv`
       - Override `initialize(XProcessingEnv)` to store the env
       - Override `processingSteps()` to return `ImmutableList.of(new ProguardProcessingStep(env))`
       - Keep `@AutoService(Processor.class)` and `getSupportedSourceVersion()`

    3. **Create `KspProguardProcessor.java`** in `java/dagger/android/internal/proguard/`:
       - Create a class that extends `KspBasicAnnotationProcessor`
       - Similar structure to `ProguardProcessor` but with `KspBasicAnnotationProcessor`
       - Add `@AutoService(SymbolProcessorProvider.class)` inner `Provider` class
       - Constructor takes `SymbolProcessorEnvironment`
       - Override `initialize(XProcessingEnv)` and `processingSteps()`

    4. **Modify `BaseProcessingStep.java`** in `java/dagger/android/processor/`:
       - Change class from package-private to `public`
       - No other changes needed as it's already compatible

    5. **Update `java/dagger/android/processor/BUILD`**:
       - Add a new `java_library` target `base_processing_step` for `BaseProcessingStep.java`
       - Update `processor` target to exclude `BaseProcessingStep.java` and depend on `:base_processing_step`
       - Add dependencies for the new `base_processing_step` target and update `artifact_target_libs`

    6. **Update `java/dagger/android/internal/proguard/BUILD`**:
       - Add `KspProguardProcessor.java` and `ProguardProcessingStep.java` to `srcs`
       - Add dependencies: `//java/dagger/android/processor:base_processing_step`, `//java/dagger/internal/codegen/xprocessing`, `//third_party/java/guava/collect`, `//third_party/java/javapoet`, `@maven//:com_google_devtools_ksp_symbol_processing_api`

pr_chain.title: Enhance Dagger missing binding diagnostics for consistency and detail
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to improve the quality and consistency of Dagger's error messages, specifically for missing binding validation errors. Currently, error messages for missing bindings vary depending on whether a full or pruned binding graph is being validated, which leads to inconsistent formatting and information. The solution should:

    1. Always include detailed dependency trace information and component paths in missing binding error messages, regardless of the graph type being validated.
    2. Make `ElementFormatter` more flexible by allowing method parameter types to be elided when formatting executables, which will help reduce noise in error messages for large parameter lists.
    3. Simplify the missing binding reporting logic by removing redundant graph-handling branches and always using a consistent message generation approach.

    The improvement should result in error messages that consistently show the full dependency path, component information, and additional request/entry point details, making it easier for developers to diagnose and fix missing binding issues.

## Environment Setup
This is a Bazel-based project. Key configuration files to examine:
    - `WORKSPACE` - defines external dependencies
    - `BUILD` files in `java/dagger/internal/codegen/` and `javatests/dagger/internal/codegen/` - define build targets and test rules
    - `.bazelrc` - Bazel configuration
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - CI configuration that shows how tests are run
    - `build_defs.bzl` and `test_defs.bzl` - custom Bazel build macros

## Implementation Plan
1. **Modify `ElementFormatter.java`**:
       - Add a new overloaded static method `elementToString(XElement element, boolean elideMethodParameterTypes)` that accepts a boolean parameter to control whether executable parameter types are elided.
       - Update the existing `elementToString(XElement element)` method to delegate to the new overload with `elideMethodParameterTypes` set to `false` for backward compatibility.
       - In the new method, when `elideMethodParameterTypes` is `true` and the element is an executable, format parameters as `(…)` if there are any, or `()` if none exist, instead of listing all parameter types.
       - Update class and method Javadoc to reflect the new behavior.

    2. **Modify `DiagnosticMessageGenerator.java`**:
       - In `getMessageInternal()`, remove the conditional logic that checks `graph.isFullBindingGraph()`. Always print the dependency trace and component paths, regardless of graph type.
       - Update the requests-to-print filter to always exclude entry points and traced requests, removing the `graph.isFullBindingGraph()` check.
       - Simplify the "requested at" message to always use "also" instead of conditionally choosing between " " and " also ".
       - Always print additional entry points when there are more than one, removing the `graph.isFullBindingGraph()` condition.

    3. **Modify `MissingBindingValidator.java`**:
       - In `reportMissingBinding()`, simplify the method signature to remove the `prunedGraph` parameter and always pass `fullGraph` to the diagnostic message generator.
       - When no alternative components are found, always use `diagnosticMessageGeneratorFactory.create(fullGraph).getMessage(missingBinding)` for the missing binding usage section, removing the conditional logic that uses a pruned graph.
       - Remove the now-unused `prunedGraph` parameter from the `revisitFullGraph()` method call.
       - Clean up unused imports that were previously used for the removed branches.

    4. **Update tests in `MissingBindingValidationTest.java`**:
       - Update existing test assertions to expect component path prefixes (e.g., `[TestClass.AComponent]`) in dependency trace lines.
       - Update tests to match the new, consistent formatting of error messages.
       - Add component path information to expected error messages in tests that verify dependency traces and entry point listings.

pr_chain.title: Add @SkipTestInjection annotation to skip Hilt test class injection
pr_chain.description:
We need to add a new annotation `@SkipTestInjection` to the Hilt Android testing library. This annotation will allow users to disable the automatic test class injection performed by Hilt. This is useful for custom test infrastructure that wants to inject the test class from a different Hilt component.

The annotation should be usable either directly on the test class or on another annotation that is applied to the test class (meta-annotation). When present, Hilt should:
1. Not generate a `TestInjector` for the test class (the `_GeneratedInjector` class).
2. Generate a `TestComponentData` whose `injectTest` method throws an `IllegalStateException` with a message indicating that test injection is disabled.

The goal is to make Hilt's test injection optional, giving users flexibility when building custom test setups.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files for build and test instructions:
- `BUILD` files in the repository root and in `java/` and `javatests/` directories (Bazel targets)
- `WORKSPACE` for repository and external dependency configuration
- `.bazelrc` for Bazel settings
- `test_defs.bzl` and `build_defs.bzl` for shared build definitions
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general contribution guidelines

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create the `SkipTestInjection` annotation class**:
   - Create a new Java file at `java/dagger/hilt/android/testing/SkipTestInjection.java` in the package `dagger.hilt.android.testing`.
   - The annotation should have:
     - `@Retention(CLASS)` 
     - `@Target({ElementType.TYPE})`
     - A Javadoc explaining its purpose (skipping test injection in Hilt Android Test, useful for custom test infrastructure).

2. **Update BUILD file for the annotation**:
   - In `java/dagger/hilt/android/testing/BUILD`, add a new `android_library` target named `skip_test_injection` with:
     - `testonly = 1`
     - `srcs = ["SkipTestInjection.java"]`
     - `deps = [":package_info"]`

3. **Add class name constant**:
   - In `java/dagger/hilt/processor/internal/ClassNames.java`, add a new constant:
     - `public static final ClassName SKIP_TEST_INJECTION = get("dagger.hilt.android.testing", "SkipTestInjection");`

4. **Add method to `TestRootMetadata`**:
   - In `java/dagger/hilt/processor/internal/root/TestRootMetadata.java`, add a new method `skipTestInjectionAnnotation()` that:
     - Checks if the test element has the `@SkipTestInjection` annotation directly. If so, returns it as an `Optional<XAnnotation>`.
     - Otherwise, checks if the test element has any annotations that are themselves annotated with `@SkipTestInjection` (i.e., meta-annotations). If so, returns the first such annotation.
     - Returns `Optional.empty()` if neither case applies.
   - May need to import `Optional` and `Set`.

5. **Update `RootProcessingStep`**:
   - In `java/dagger/hilt/processor/internal/root/RootProcessingStep.java`, modify the `processEach` method:
     - When processing a test root, create `TestRootMetadata` once and check if `skipTestInjectionAnnotation()` is present.
     - Only generate a `TestInjectorGenerator` if the annotation is NOT present (i.e., test injection is NOT skipped).

6. **Update `TestComponentDataGenerator`**:
   - In `java/dagger/hilt/processor/internal/root/TestComponentDataGenerator.java`, modify the `callInjectTest` method:
     - Add a helper method to get an `Optional<XAnnotation>` for the skip test injection annotation.
     - If the annotation is present, return a `CodeBlock` that throws `new IllegalStateException("Cannot inject test when using @" + annotationName)`.
     - Otherwise, keep the existing behavior.

7. **Add test targets to `javatests/dagger/hilt/android/testing/BUILD`**:
   - Add two new `android_local_test` targets:
     - `SkipTestInjectionTest` with `srcs = ["SkipTestInjectionTest.java"]` and appropriate deps including `//java/dagger/hilt/android/testing:skip_test_injection`
     - `SkipTestInjectionAnnotationTest` with `srcs = ["SkipTestInjectionAnnotationTest.java"]` and similar deps.

8. **Create test files**:
   - Create `javatests/dagger/hilt/android/testing/SkipTestInjectionTest.java`:
     - A test class annotated with `@HiltAndroidTest` and `@SkipTestInjection`.
     - Include an `@Inject` field that is NOT provided (to verify compilation succeeds with the annotation).
     - Include a `HiltAndroidRule` and a test method that verifies calling `rule.inject()` throws `IllegalStateException` with message "Cannot inject test when using @SkipTestInjection".
   - Create `javatests/dagger/hilt/android/testing/SkipTestInjectionAnnotationTest.java`:
     - Similar to above but instead of using `@SkipTestInjection` directly on the test class, define a custom annotation that is annotated with `@SkipTestInjection`, and apply that custom annotation to the test class.
     - Verify the error message contains the custom annotation name (e.g., "@TestAnnotation").

The Hilt Android InjectionTest has a test method specifically for KitKat (API 19) that verifies a fourth constructor isn't available on that SDK version. Since we no longer need to support that behavior, please remove that KitKat-specific test case along with its now-unused `assertThrows` import.

We need to reduce the number of times we resolve parameter types in an extreme case. Specifically, in the toStableString method for executables, when running under KSP and an executable has more than 10 parameters, resolving all those types is expensive. For that case, just show the first 10 parameter types followed by ", ..." instead of resolving every single one.

    - In `tools/BUILD`, update the `deps` of the `maven_bzl` and `maven_info_bzl` `bzl_library` targets to include `@rules_java//java:rules`.

    This is a mechanical change; no logic or behavior changes should be introduced. The repository should continue to build and pass all tests after this change.

## Environment Setup

    - `WORKSPACE` — declares external dependencies and repository rules.
    - `.bazelrc` — Bazel configuration flags.
    - `BUILD` and `**/BUILD` files — define build targets.

## Implementation Plan
