pr_chain.title: Fix Hilt generated code for package-private base class constructors
pr_chain.description:
Hilt's annotation processor generates a base class (e.g., `Hilt_TestActivity`) for each `@AndroidEntryPoint`-annotated class. This generated class must copy the constructors of the user's base class (the class passed to `@AndroidEntryPoint`, or the superclass of the annotated class) so that the generated class can be properly instantiated.

    Currently, the constructor copying logic only filters out **private** constructors, but does not account for **package-private** constructors. If a base class has a package-private constructor (i.e., declared without any access modifier) and that base class is in a different package from the `@AndroidEntryPoint`-annotated class, the generated code will reference the package-private constructor and fail to compile, because the generated class is in the same package as the annotated class, not the base class.

    We need to fix the constructor copying logic so that package-private constructors are only copied when they are in the same package as the generated class (i.e., the package of the `@AndroidEntryPoint`-annotated class). Additionally, the service generator currently has its own ad-hoc constructor copying logic that ignores visibility entirely; it should be unified to use the same shared helper as the other generators.

    Please ensure the fix covers all Android entry point generator types: Activity, Fragment, View, Service, and BroadcastReceiver.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's `BUILD` files for build and test configuration. The test infrastructure uses Bazel (`WORKSPACE`, `BUILD` files, and `.bazelrc`). New tests should be added under `javatests/dagger/hilt/android/`, following the pattern of existing `android_local_test` targets.

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify the `copyConstructors` method in `Generators.java` to accept a reference to the subclass (i.e., the `@AndroidEntryPoint`-annotated element) and use it to determine constructor visibility.
    2. Add a helper method (e.g., `isConstructorVisibleToSubclass`) that checks: (a) private constructors are never copied, and (b) package-private constructors are only copied if the base class is in the same package as the subclass reference.
    3. Update all generator classes (`ActivityGenerator`, `BroadcastReceiverGenerator`, `FragmentGenerator`, `ViewGenerator`) to pass the subclass reference when calling `copyConstructors`. For `ViewGenerator`, replace its private visibility-checking method with the shared helper.
    4. Refactor `ServiceGenerator` to use the shared `Generators.copyConstructors` method with the subclass reference, instead of its own private constructor-copying logic.
    5. Add a regression test that defines base classes (Activity, Fragment, View, Service, IntentService, BroadcastReceiver) with package-private constructors in a different package from the `@AndroidEntryPoint`-annotated classes, and verify compilation succeeds.

instruction:
## Fix ATTACH property parsing to correctly handle binary values

The ICalendar grammar currently misinterprets ATTACH properties that use binary-encoded values (via BASE64 encoding with VALUE=BINARY) as URLs. The goal is to update the attach rule so it properly distinguishes between URI and binary value types, ensuring that binary attachments containing base64-encoded content are parsed correctly. This also requires the grammar to handle the case where binary content may be split across multiple lines with folding whitespace.

pr_chain.title: Extend MySQL parser to support SELECT statements with unions and subqueries
pr_chain.description: We need to update the MySQL grammar so that a query specification ending with a trailing UNION clause is valid, enabling support for SELECT statements that combine union operations with derived tables/subqueries inside stored procedures. The goal is to resolve parsing failures for such statements while keeping the grammar action-free and consistent with existing union handling. Please also add a relevant example to verify the new behavior.

pr_chain.title: Add inline routine support to Trino grammar
pr_chain.description:
We need to update the Trino SQL grammar (`sql/trino/TrinoLexer.g4` and `sql/trino/TrinoParser.g4`) to support inline routines — a feature recently added to Trino. An inline routine is a function defined inline within a `WITH` clause, e.g.:
    
    ```sql
    WITH
      FUNCTION abc(x integer)
        RETURNS integer
        RETURN x * 2
    SELECT abc(21);
    ```

    The goal is to add the necessary tokens and grammar rules to parse:

    1. Inline routine definitions in `WITH` clauses (the main new feature)
    2. `CREATE FUNCTION` / `DROP FUNCTION` statements (with `OR REPLACE` support for CREATE)
    3. New reserved keywords and identifiers associated with these features (e.g., `BEGIN`, `CALLED`, `DECLARE`, `DEFINE`, `DETERMINISTIC`, `DO`, `ELSEIF`, `FUNCTION`, `IMMEDIATE`, `ITERATE`, `JSON_TABLE`, `LANGUAGE`, `LEAVE`, `LOOP`, `CATALOG`, etc.)
    4. `CREATE CATALOG` / `DROP CATALOG` statements that are part of this Trino version sync

    Additionally, we need to add an example file (`sql/trino/examples/inline_routine.sql`) demonstrating the inline routine syntax.

    Note: In the parser grammar, you must avoid using `base` as an identifier/rule name since it's a reserved word in C# and will cause build failures for that target. Use `base_` instead.

    Also, the grammar files should be formatted according to the existing style (using antlr-format comments at the top of files).

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's root `pom.xml` and the `sql/trino` directory (which should contain its own `pom.xml` or build config) for how to build and test the grammar. Also look for any `Makefile`, `README.md`, or CI configuration files at the repo root that indicate how to validate ANTLR grammars.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Update TrinoLexer.g4**: Add new token definitions for all new keywords mentioned in the description (e.g., `BEGIN_`, `CALLED_`, `CATALOG_`, `DECLARE_`, `DEFINE_`, `DETERMINISTIC_`, `DO_`, `ELSEIF_`, `FUNCTION_`, `IMMEDIATE_`, `ITERATE_`, `JSON_TABLE_`, `LANGUAGE_`, `LEAVE_`, `LOOP_`, etc.). Keep tokens alphabetically sorted, maintain the existing formatting style, and ensure all new tokens follow the `_` suffix convention.
    
    2. **Update TrinoParser.g4**:
       a. Add a new `standaloneFunctionSpecification` entry to the `statements` rule to allow parsing standalone function definitions (for testing).
       b. Modify the `statement` rule to:
          - Add `CREATE CATALOG` and `DROP CATALOG` alternatives
          - Add `CREATE (OR REPLACE)? functionSpecification` and `DROP FUNCTION (IF EXISTS)? functionDeclaration` alternatives
          - Replace all usages of `query` with `rootQuery` in statement-level contexts (e.g., `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT`, `INSERT INTO`, `CREATE VIEW`, etc.)
       c. Add new grammar rules for `rootQuery` (which will encompass the `WITH ... FUNCTION` syntax), `functionSpecification`, `functionDeclaration`, and related rules for function body statements, parameters, return types, etc.
       d. Ensure the `with` rule allows inline function definitions (e.g., `WITH FUNCTION name(params) RETURNS type RETURN expression`).
       e. Update the `nonReserved` rule to include all newly added tokens so they can be used as identifiers when not in keyword context.
       f. Rename any rule/alternative using `base` to `base_` (e.g., in `querySpecification` or `queryPrimary` if applicable).
    
    3. **Add example file**: Create `sql/trino/examples/inline_routine.sql` with the simple inline routine example provided.
    
    4. **Format**: After making changes, ensure the grammar files are formatted with the antlr-format tool according to the comments at the top of each file (e.g., column limit, alignment settings).

We need a new ANTLR4 grammar for RISC-V 64-bit assembly (the G extension, covering the I, M, A, F, D, and C instruction sets, but not compiler pseudo-instructions). Please set it up so it fits the repository conventions: add a desc.xml declaring supported targets and ANTLR version, a pom.xml that registers it under the asm parent module, and include a couple of example .S files to validate parsing. Make sure the grammar has no useless parentheses and that all tokens referenced in parser rules are on the default channel.

pr_chain.title: Allow qualified foreign key names in DROP FOREIGN KEY clause
pr_chain.description: The MariaDB grammar should accept fully qualified foreign key references (e.g., `schema.table`) in the `DROP FOREIGN KEY` clause of `ALTER TABLE` statements. Currently, only unqualified identifiers are supported, which causes valid MariaDB statements to fail parsing. Please update the grammar to allow an optional dotted identifier suffix after the foreign key name and add a test example.

pr_chain.title: Fix VB6 grammar corner cases for empty Do-Loop and inline ElseIf
pr_chain.description:
The Visual Basic 6 grammar in `vb6/VisualBasic6Parser.g4` has two corner cases that prevent valid VB6 code from parsing correctly:

    1. **Empty `Do...Loop While/Until` statements**: A `Do` loop with no body statements (e.g., `Do` followed by `Loop Until condition`) currently fails to parse. The grammar requires at least one block between the `DO` and `LOOP` keywords when the loop has a trailing `While`/`Until` condition.

    2. **Inline `ElseIf` statements**: An `ElseIf` statement where the block begins on the same line as the `Then` keyword (separated only by whitespace, not a newline) currently fails to parse. The grammar requires at least one newline after `Then` before the block.

    Update the grammar rules in `vb6/VisualBasic6Parser.g4` to allow these valid constructs. Also add a test example file under `vb6/examples/` demonstrating both scenarios to verify the fix.

## Environment Setup
Check `vb6/pom.xml` (or the top-level `pom.xml` for the project build setup) for instructions on how to build and test the grammar. Review `README.md` files in the root or `vb6/` directory if present for testing guidance.

## Implementation Plan
- Locate the `doLoopStmt` rule in `vb6/VisualBasic6Parser.g4` and modify the third alternative (the `DO ... LOOP While/Until` case) to make the `(block NEWLINE+)` group optional.
    - Locate the `ifElseIfBlockStmt` rule and change `NEWLINE+` after `THEN` to `(WS | NEWLINE)+` so blocks can follow the `Then` keyword with either whitespace or newlines.
    - Create a new example file `vb6/examples/test1.bas` containing:
      - A subroutine with `ElseIf` statements where the block starts on the same line as `Then`.
      - A subroutine with an empty `Do...Loop Until` loop (no body statements).
    - Run the grammar tests/validation to ensure existing examples still parse and the new example parses without errors.
    - Review for any other rules that might be affected by the changes (e.g., `ifThenElseStmt` uses `ifElseIfBlockStmt`) and confirm no regressions.

pr_chain.title: Rewrite JSX element parsing to fix regex and keyword tokenization issues
pr_chain.description:
The current JSX parsing in the JavaScript/JSX grammar has several issues: 1. **Regular expressions incorrectly match JSX elements**: Code like `return (
);` gets parsed incorrectly because the lexer's `RegularExpressionLiteral` rule matches the `
` sequences instead of treating them as JSX elements. 2. **JavaScript keywords leak into JSX text content**: In JSX children, text like `from` in `
from
` gets tokenized as the `From` keyword rather than as HTML character data. The root cause is the lexer architecture: the existing `TAG` mode is never actually entered (the `TagOpen` rule in `mode TAG` references `LessThan`, but no lexer rule in the default mode pushes into `TAG`), and the JSX handling in the parser relies on token types like `TagName`, `AttributeValue`, and `htmlChardata` that are produced by lexer modes that are never activated correctly. The goal is to rewrite the JSX lexing/parsing approach to use explicit lexer modes for JSX opening elements, closing elements, and children, and to make the parser aware of these new token types. The parser should only treat a `<` as a JSX element start when it's syntactically valid to do so (e.g., after `return`, assignment, `(`, `{`, `,`, `:`, `?`, `=>`, etc.). ## Environment Setup Check the repository's root-level configuration files to understand how to build and test grammars. Look at `_scripts/templates/` for language-specific templates (e.g., `_scripts/templates/JavaScript/package.json`), and the `javascript/jsx/pom.xml` for the Maven build configuration specific to the JSX grammar. The grammar files are in `javascript/jsx/` (specifically `JavaScriptLexer.g4`, `JavaScriptParser.g4`, and `Java/JavaScriptLexerBase.java`). ## Implementation Plan 1. **Add a new lexer rule for JSX element start**: In `javascript/jsx/JavaScriptLexer.g4`, add a lexer rule `JsxElementBegin` that matches `<` but only when a new Java helper method `IsJsxPossible()` returns `true`. This rule should `pushMode(JSX_OPENING_ELEMENT)`. 2. **Implement `IsJsxPossible()` in `JavaScriptLexerBase.java`**: This method should inspect the `lastToken` field (already tracked in `nextToken()`) and return `true` only when the last token is one that can precede a JSX element (e.g., `Assign`, `Colon`, `Comma`, `Default`, `QuestionMark`, `Return`, `OpenBrace`, `OpenParen`, `Yield`, `ARROW`, and the new JSX brace tokens). 3. **Replace the old `TAG` and `ATTVALUE` modes with new JSX-specific modes**: - `mode JSX_OPENING_ELEMENT`: Handles tokens for the opening tag, including `JsxOpeningElementBegin` (nested `<`, pushes another `JSX_OPENING_ELEMENT`), `JsxOpeningElementEnd` (pops to `JSX_CHILDREN`), `JsxOpeningElementSlashEnd` (pops to default), `JsxAssign`, `JsxOpeningElementOpenBrace` (pushes to default for expressions), `JsxOpeningElementId` (element/attribute names), `JsxAttributeValue`, whitespace/comments to hidden channel. - `mode JSX_CHILDREN`: Handles content between tags, including `HtmlChardata` (any char except `<` and `{`), `JsxChildrenOpeningElementBegin` (pushes `JSX_OPENING_ELEMENT`), `JsxChildrenClosingElementSlashBegin` (pops to `JSX_CLOSING_ELEMENT`), and `JsxChildrenOpenBrace` (pushes to default for expressions). - `mode JSX_CLOSING_ELEMENT`: Handles the closing tag, including `JsxClosingElementEnd` (pops to default), `JsxClosingElementId`, and hidden whitespace/comments. 4. **Update the parser to use the new token types**: In `javascript/jsx/JavaScriptParser.g4`: - Replace references to `'{'` and `'}'` in rules like `block`, `moduleItems`, `caseBlock`, `functionDeclaration`, `classTail`, `classElement`, `methodDefinition`, `objectLiteral` with the explicit token names `OpenBrace`, `CloseBrace` (since the lexer now produces these tokens from the JSX modes too). - Replace `'='` in `variableDeclaration` and `classElement` with `Assign` token. - Update the `returnStatement` rule to use `jsxElements` instead of `htmlElements`. - Rename the parser rules (`htmlElements`, `htmlElement`, `htmlContent`, etc.) to `jsxElements`, `jsxElement`, `jsxChildren`, etc., and update their token references to the new lexer tokens (e.g., `JsxOpeningElementId`, `JsxOpeningElementEnd`, `JsxClosingElementId`, `JsxClosingElementEnd`, `JsxAttributeValue`). - Add `JsxOpeningElementOpenBrace` and `JsxChildrenOpenBrace` as tokens that open an expression context (potentially in parser rules like `objectExpressionSequence`). 5. **Add example test cases**: Create `javascript/jsx/examples/TestCases.jsx` with the examples from the issue (nested divs, keywords in text, attribute values with `>`, expression children, comments).

pr_chain.title: Fix semver lexer to allow digit '0' in version numbers
pr_chain.description:
The SemanticVersionLexer currently rejects valid semantic versions that contain the digit '0' inside numeric identifiers (e.g., `10.1.1`, `1.102.1`, `2.10.103`, `102.203.102930`). The `NUMBER` rule only allows a single `0` or a sequence of positive digits `[1-9]+`, which incorrectly prevents numeric components from including zeros after the first digit.

    The goal is to update the lexer so that numeric version components allow digits `0-9` after a leading positive digit (or a standalone `0`), aligning with the Semantic Versioning (SemVer) specification. Additionally, add example test files demonstrating that versions containing the digit '0' are now correctly tokenized.

## Environment Setup
Check the `semver/pom.xml` file for project build configuration, and the `semver/examples/` directory for existing example files. Refer to the `_scripts/templates/` directory and the `README`/`CONTRIBUTING` files (if present) for how tests are typically run in this repository.

## Implementation Plan
- Modify the `NUMBER` rule in `semver/SemanticVersionLexer.g4` to allow a leading positive digit followed by any number of digits (`[0-9]*`), while still allowing a standalone `0`.
    - Add a `DIGIT` fragment for `[0-9]` (or reuse an existing pattern) to keep the lexer clean.
    - Add example files under `semver/examples/` covering:
      - Simple versions with zeros (e.g., `2.10.103`).
      - Edge cases with zeros in pre-release and build metadata (e.g., `1.20.303----RC-SNAPSHOT.120.90.10--.102+7088`).
      - Larger version numbers with zeros (e.g., `102.203.102930-dev`).
    - Run the existing example validation (via the project's test harness) to confirm the lexer now accepts these inputs without errors.

pr_chain.title: Remove VB.NET class-based sample from VB6 grammar examples

pr_chain.title: Update TypeScript grammar with JavaScript improvements and TypeScript-specific fixes
pr_chain.description:
Enhance the TypeScript ANTLR grammar (both lexer and parser) located in `javascript/typescript/` to bring it up to date with improvements already made to the JavaScript grammar, and add a few TypeScript-specific enhancements.

    The goal is to make the TypeScript grammar more complete and accurate by:

    1. **Lexer improvements:**
       - Add support for the power operator (`**`), the power assignment operator (`**=`), the nullish coalescing operator (`??`), the nullish coalescing assignment operator (`??=`), and the optional chaining operator (`?.`).
       - Add support for the hashtag (`#`) character.
       - Remove the `get` and `set` tokens, making them regular identifiers as in the JavaScript grammar.
       - Remove direct lexer rules for `>>` and `>>>` and handle these in the parser (to allow nested generic types like `Map<string, Map<string, string>>`).
       - Improve numeric literal support: allow underscores in decimal, hexadecimal, octal, and binary literals; add support for BigInt literals (e.g., `123n`, `0xFFn`).
       - Expand Unicode escape sequence support to include the `\u{...}` form.
       - Add the `await` keyword.

    2. **Parser improvements:**
       - Improve `import` statement support to handle various forms (default imports, namespace imports, named imports, side-effect-only imports).
       - Improve `export` statement support to handle more declaration forms and re-exports.
       - Add support for import/export with string literal names.
       - Improve statement ordering and add `for await` loop support.
       - Add support for class expressions.
       - Add support for `get` and `set` methods without them being reserved keywords.
       - Add `null` type as a valid predefined type.
       - Fix nested generic type support of arbitrary depth (e.g., `Promise<Map<string, Set<string>>>`).
       - Add support for typed catch clauses, e.g., `catch (error: MyError) { ... }`.

    Ensure all existing example files in `javascript/typescript/examples/` parse correctly, and add new example files to cover the new syntax if needed.

## Environment Setup
Check the `pom.xml` file in the `javascript/typescript/` directory for build and test configuration for this grammar module. Also check the root-level `pom.xml` for the overall build structure. The repository uses Maven; review these files to understand how to build and test the grammar.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Modify the TypeScript lexer** (`TypeScriptLexer.g4`):
       - Add lexer rules for `Power` (`**`), `NullCoalesce` (`??`), `Hashtag` (`#`), `PowerAssign` (`**=`), and `NullishCoalescingAssign` (`??=`) tokens.
       - Add a lexer rule for `QuestionMarkDot` (`?.`).
       - Remove lexer rules for `Get` and `Set` tokens.
       - Comment out or remove the `RightShiftArithmetic` and `RightShiftLogical` lexer rules.
       - Update `DecimalLiteral`, `HexIntegerLiteral`, `OctalIntegerLiteral2`, and `BinaryIntegerLiteral` rules to allow underscore separators.
       - Add lexer rules for `BigHexIntegerLiteral`, `BigOctalIntegerLiteral`, `BigBinaryIntegerLiteral`, and `BigDecimalIntegerLiteral`.
       - Expand `UnicodeEscapeSequence` to support `\u{...}` form.
       - Add the `Await` keyword token.

    2. **Update the TypeScript parser** (`TypeScriptParser.g4`):
       - Replace the `nestedTypeGeneric` and related rules with a single recursive `typeGeneric` rule to support nested generics of any depth.
       - Add `NullLiteral` to the `predefinedType` rule.
       - Remove `Get` and `Set` from the `keyword` rule.
       - Update the `importStatement` rule to use new `importFromBlock` rule supporting the various import forms.
       - Add new rules for `importFromBlock`, `importDefault`, `importNamespace`, `importModuleItems`, and related rules.
       - Update the `exportStatement` rule to support the new export forms (as shown in the `Export.js` example).
       - Reorder and adjust `statement` rule alternatives to include `functionDeclaration`, `variableStatement`, and `expressionStatement` in correct positions.
       - Add support for optional chaining (`?.`) in member expressions.
       - Add support for class expressions in the `singleExpression` rule.
       - Add support for `for await` loops in the `forStatement` rule.
       - Add support for typed `catch` clauses in the `catch` rule.
       - Update `assignmentOperator` rule to include `**=` and `??=`.
       - Update `bitShiftExpression` rule to handle `>>` and `>>>` tokens (since they are no longer single lexer tokens).

    3. **Update or add new example files** in `javascript/typescript/examples/`:
       - Modify `Function.ts` to include an example with nested generic types.
       - Modify `NonNullAssertOp.js` to include an example with optional chaining (`?.`).
       - Modify `Type.ts` to include examples with type aliases and the `null` type.
       - Add new example files: `Export.js` (from JavaScript examples), `Import.js` (from JavaScript examples), `JavaScriptClass.js` (from JavaScript examples), and `Loop.ts` (with `for await` examples).

    4. **Verify the changes**:
       - Build and test the TypeScript grammar using the Maven setup defined in the `pom.xml` files.
       - Ensure all existing example files in `javascript/typescript/examples/` parse successfully.
       - Ensure all new example files added in step 3 parse successfully.

pr_chain.title: Upgrade TypeScript grammar to support v2.7 syntax
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to extend the TypeScript grammar (and related JavaScript/JSX grammars) so they can parse code written against TypeScript up to version 2.7. This includes adding support for language features introduced in TypeScript releases from 0.9 through 2.7.

    Specifically, we need to add parsing support for:
    - Named function expressions in object literals (e.g., `field: function myFunction(arg1) { return arg1; }`)
    - The `yield*` operator in JavaScript, TypeScript, and JSX
    - Type assertions (casting) in `for` statements
    - Export type aliases (with optional trailing semicolon)
    - Leading `|` or `&` in union/intersection type aliases
    - Trailing commas in tuples and function parameter lists
    - Namespace declarations
    - Boolean, number, and string literal types
    - Non-null assertion operator (existing, but should continue to work)
    - `undefined` and `never` types
    - `keyof` and indexed access types
    - `object` type
    - Generic parameter defaults
    - `unique symbol` type

    The implementation should modify the ANTLR grammar files for JavaScript, JSX, and TypeScript (lexer and parser files) and add example files demonstrating the new syntax. All grammars should remain free of actions (pure grammars without embedded code).

## Environment Setup
The repository contains per-grammar `pom.xml` files (e.g., `javascript/typescript/pom.xml`, `javascript/javascript/pom.xml`, `javascript/jsx/pom.xml`) which should be referenced for build and test instructions. There are also template configuration files under `_scripts/templates/` (e.g., `_scripts/templates/TypeScript/package.json`, `_scripts/templates/TypeScript/tsconfig.json`, `_scripts/templates/JavaScript/package.json`) that may be relevant for how the JavaScript/TypeScript projects are set up. Check these files to determine how dependencies should be installed and how tests are run for this repository.

## Implementation Plan
1. Update the JavaScript lexer and parser grammars to add the `yield*` operator as a distinct token and update the `yieldStatement` rule to accept it.
    2. Apply similar lexer/parser changes to the JSX variants of the JavaScript grammars.
    3. Update the TypeScript lexer to add new keyword tokens: `Never`, `Undefined`, `Object`, `KeyOf`, `Unique`, `Of`, and `YieldStar`.
    4. Update the TypeScript parser grammar to support all the new language constructs listed in the description, including modifying `type_`, `primaryType`, `predefinedType`, `tupleElementTypes`, `parameterList`, `typeParameter`, and `typeAliasDeclaration` rules.
    5. Add or modify example files under the `javascript/typescript/examples/`, `javascript/javascript/examples/` directories to demonstrate each new syntax feature.
    6. Ensure all modified grammars remain valid ANTLR grammars and that example files parse correctly without errors.
Update the CI workflow to use .NET 8 instead of .NET 7 wherever the dotnet version is specified.

pr_chain.title: Add Python3 target support and grammar transformation script for PL/SQL
pr_chain.description: Enable Python3 as a supported target for the PL/SQL grammar by updating the target configuration and adding a script that transforms the grammar for Python3 compatibility. The script should replace Java-style member access syntax with Python-style syntax in grammar files. This ensures the grammar can be correctly generated and tested with the Python3 ANTLR runtime.

pr_chain.title: Improve computed argument and keyword parameter support in JavaScript/TypeScript grammars
pr_chain.description:
The JavaScript and TypeScript ANTLR grammars currently fail to parse several valid ES6+ syntax patterns. Specifically:

1. **Computed arguments in arrow functions** — Arrow functions don't accept computed/destructured parameters. For example, `([reference]: any) => x` fails to parse.
2. **Computed arguments in methods** — Object literal methods with computed names like `[reference](a){}` fail to parse.
3. **Computed arguments in setters** — Object literal setters with destructured parameters like `set a([reference]=123){}` fail to parse.
4. **Keywords as parameter names** — Keywords (e.g., `this`) cannot be used as function parameter names, but this is valid JavaScript/TypeScript.
5. **Generator function declarations** — Declarations like `function* name()` fail because the `*` isn't allowed in a plain `functionDeclaration` rule.

Update both `JavaScriptParser.g4` and `TypeScriptParser.g4` to support these patterns, and add example coverage in the existing test/example files.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repo files for build/test setup:

    - `javascript/javascript/pom.xml` — Maven config for the JavaScript grammar module
    - `javascript/typescript/pom.xml` — Maven config for the TypeScript grammar module
    - `javascript/typescript/examples/` — Existing example files to extend
    - `javascript/javascript/examples/` — Existing example files that may also need updates

## Implementation Plan
1. **JavaScript grammar (`javascript/javascript/JavaScriptParser.g4`)**:
       - Update the `assignable` rule to also accept `keyword` as an alternative
       - Update the `arrowFunctionParameters` rule to use `propertyName` instead of just `identifier`

    2. **TypeScript grammar (`javascript/typescript/TypeScriptParser.g4`)**:
       - Update `functionDeclaration` to allow an optional `*` after `Function_`

pr_chain.title: Add Java package support to Maven build for grammar subprojects
pr_chain.description:
The current Maven build generates ANTLR lexer and parser classes into the unnamed (default) Java package. This prevents building reusable JARs because the generated classes cannot be properly imported and used by consuming applications.

    Your task is to introduce a mechanism that allows grammar subprojects to place their generated classes into a named Java package, while keeping the existing build process working. The solution should be implemented in the root POM so that grammar subprojects can opt in by making minimal changes to their own POM and base classes.

    Specifically, for this task, you need to:
    1. Add Maven properties to the root POM that define a package name, package path, and package line for generated code.
    2. Configure the root POM with plugins that:
       - Copy Java base classes (e.g., lexer/parser base classes) into a package directory under `target/generated-sources/`, with filtering to substitute the package declaration.
       - Add that copied directory as a source directory so Maven compiles the base classes.
    3. Update the PL/SQL grammar subproject (`sql/plsql`) to:
       - Pass the `-package` argument to the ANTLR Maven plugin so generated lexer/parser classes are placed in the package.
       - Configure the antlr4test plugin to use the package name for test execution.
       - Remove the hardcoded `sourceDirectory` configuration that bypasses the new mechanism.
    4. Update the PL/SQL Java base classes (`PlSqlLexerBase.java` and `PlSqlParserBase.java`) to include a package declaration placeholder that gets substituted during the build.

## Environment Setup
Check the root `pom.xml` for Maven configuration, dependency management, and plugin setup. Also review `sql/plsql/pom.xml` to understand the subproject build configuration. The `sql/plsql/Java/` directory contains the Java base classes that need modification. Use the existing Maven build system — no separate dependency installation is required beyond what Maven pulls automatically.

## Implementation Plan
1. In the root `pom.xml`, add properties under `<properties>`:
       - `packageName` = `org.antlr.grammars.${project.artifactId}`
       - `packagePath` = `org/antlr/grammars/${project.artifactId}`
       - `packageLine` = `package ${packageName};`
    
    2. In the root `pom.xml` `<build>` section, add the `maven-resources-plugin` with an execution that:
       - Copies files from `${basedir}/Java` (the base-class source directory) to `target/generated-sources/copy/${packagePath}`
       - Enables filtering with the custom delimiter `///{*}` so that `///{packageLine}` gets replaced with the actual package declaration
    
    3. Add the `build-helper-maven-plugin` with an execution that adds the copied directory (`target/generated-sources/copy/${packagePath}`) as a source directory, so Maven compiles the base classes along with the generated parser/lexer.
    
    4. In `sql/plsql/pom.xml`:
       - Remove the `<sourceDirectory>Java</sourceDirectory>` element
       - Add `<arguments><argument>-package</argument><argument>${packageName}</argument></arguments>` to the ANTLR plugin configuration
       - Change both `antlr4test-maven-plugin` configurations' `<packageName>` from empty to `${packageName}`
    
    5. In `sql/plsql/Java/PlSqlLexerBase.java` and `sql/plsql/Java/PlSqlParserBase.java`, add `///{packageLine}` as the first line, which will be substituted during the build.
    
    6. Verify the build works by running Maven on the `sql/plsql` module and checking that generated classes are compiled into the package directory.

pr_chain.title: Improve remote address fetching and documentation for VLESS subscription generator
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to enhance the Worker's ability to fetch remote address lists and improve the project documentation. Specifically:
    
    1. **Refactor `getAddressesapi` function**: The current implementation fetches each address API URL sequentially, which is slow and inefficient. Replace it with a concurrent fetching approach using `Promise.allSettled` to fetch all URLs in parallel. Additionally, the current parser extracts addresses individually with a regex; instead, concatenate all fetched text content and pass it through the existing `ADD()` function for cleaning and parsing.
    
    2. **Fix whitespace parsing in `ADD()` function**: The existing regex that replaces whitespace characters (tabs, spaces, quotes, newlines) with commas does not handle pipe characters (`|`). This can cause parsing issues with certain address formats. Update the regex to also handle pipe characters as separators.
    
    3. **Add a fake nginx response page**: Create a new function `nginx()` that returns a static HTML page mimicking a default nginx welcome page. This helps mask the service when it's accessed directly by bots or scanners.
    
    4. **Block known bot User-Agents**: The existing code returns "Hello World!" for User-Agents containing 'telegram', 'twitter', or 'miaoko'. This behavior appears to already exist but may need to be verified and commented clearly. If not present, add this filtering logic to prevent bots from consuming subscription resources.
    
    5. **Update documentation**: Rewrite the README to provide clearer deployment instructions for both Cloudflare Pages and Workers, including step-by-step guidance for setting up custom domains, environment variables, and addressing common pitfalls. Update variable documentation tables and add links to video tutorials.
    
    6. **Update sample address data**: Refresh the `addressesapi.txt` file with newer, tested endpoint addresses to improve performance and reliability of the default subscription.
    
    7. **Add wrangler configuration**: Create a `wrangler.toml` file to support local development and deployment workflows, specifying the Pages build output directory and compatibility date.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's configuration files for setting up the development environment:
    - `wrangler.toml` — configuration for Cloudflare Workers/Pages development and deployment
    - `package.json` (if present) — for JavaScript dependencies and scripts
    - `README.md` — may contain setup instructions
    - `.gitignore` — to understand which files are excluded from version control
    
    Note: The repository primarily uses plain JavaScript with no external dependencies (the worker runs directly on Cloudflare Workers runtime). Local testing may require the Cloudflare Workers CLI (`wrangler`).

## Implementation Plan
1. **Refactor `getAddressesapi` function** in `_worker.js`:
       - Replace the sequential `for...of` loop with `Promise.allSettled()` that maps all API URLs to fetch promises
       - Add appropriate request headers including a custom `User-Agent` header
       - Concatenate all successfully fetched text content with newline separators
       - Pass the combined content through the `ADD()` function to parse addresses
       - Remove the old regex-based line-by-line parsing (keep it commented or remove entirely)
    
    2. **Update `ADD()` function** in `_worker.js`:
       - Modify the regex from `/[	 "'\r\n]+/g` to `/[	|"'\r\n]+/g` to include pipe character `|` as a separator

       - Ensure this check happens before any subscription content generation
       - The filter already exists in the codebase; verify it's working correctly and add a comment explaining its purpose
    
    5. **Update `README.md`**:

pr_chain.title: Improve Ledger error handling and user feedback in dapp
pr_chain.description:
We're seeing poor user experience when Ledger users interact with the dapp. When a Ledger device isn't unlocked, the Ethereum app isn't open, or contract data isn't enabled, the user encounters raw, cryptic error messages or no feedback at all. We need to add better error handling to convert these technical errors into actionable, friendly messages.

The goal is to:
1. **In the login flow**: Recognize common Ledger connection errors and display helpful instructions. Also, add a warning message when the user clicks "Connect" with Ledger that reminds them to have their device ready, and disable the button while a connection attempt is in progress.
2. **In the buy/sell flow (minting and approve actions)**: Detect Ledger-specific errors (like contract data not enabled or device not detected) and show a modal with a friendly, actionable message instead of just logging to the console.

Please ensure the changes are scoped to the existing error handling in these components:
- `dapp/src/components/LoginWidget.js`
- `dapp/src/components/buySell/ApproveCurrencyRow.js`
- `dapp/src/components/buySell/ApproveModal.js`
- `dapp/src/components/buySell/BuySellWidget.js`
- `dapp/src/components/buySell/ErrorModal.js` (new file that may be created)

The error messages should be user-friendly and use `fbt` for internationalization where appropriate, following the patterns already in the codebase.

## Environment Setup
Check `dapp/package.json` for the list of dependencies and available npm scripts. The `dapp/README.md` may also contain setup instructions. The `dapp/.eslintrc.js` might be relevant for linting configuration. The GitHub Actions workflow in `.github/workflows/node.js.yml` may show how the CI runs, which could give hints on how to run tests locally.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Update `LoginWidget.js`**: 
       - Add a `warning` state and a `warningShowTimeout` state to track when to show a Ledger-specific warning message.
       - Extend the `errorMessageMap` function to check for `'Failed to sign with Ledger device: U2F DEVICE_INELIGIBLE'` and `'MULTIPLE_OPEN_CONNECTIONS_DISALLOWED'` strings in the error message, returning actionable hints.
       - When the Ledger connector button is clicked, set a timeout (e.g., 4 seconds) to display a warning if no connection happens. Configure this only for the Ledger option. Also, disable the connector buttons while a connection is activating.
       - Change the `activate()` call to use `false` as the third parameter (do not throw) and rely on the error callback to set the error state, as documented in the web3-react v6 docs. Also clear the warning and its timeout when the connection resolves.
       - Display the warning message in the widget's JSX.

    2. **Create `ErrorModal.js`**: A new reusable modal component that takes `error`, `errorMap`, and `onClose` properties. It should:
       - Look up the error in the provided `errorMap` and display the mapped friendly message, falling back to `error.message`.
       - Show the connector icon from the `AccountStore`.
       - Include appropriate styling via `<style jsx>` and be dismissible by clicking the background (but not the modal body).

    3. **Update `BuySellWidget.js`**:
       - Import the new `ErrorModal` component.
       - Add a state variable `buyErrorToDisplay` to store an error that should be shown in the modal.
       - Define an `errorMap` array with entries for Ledger-specific errors (e.g., `err.name === 'EthAppPleaseEnableContractData'` and `err.message.includes('Failed to sign with Ledger device: U2F DEVICE_INELIGIBL')`), each with a friendly `fbt` message.
       - Create an `onMintingError` function that checks the error against the `errorMap` and sets `buyErrorToDisplay` if there's a match.
       - Call `onMintingError(e)` in the catch block of `onMintOusd`.
       - Pass `onMintingError` to the `ApproveModal` and render the `ErrorModal` conditionally when `buyErrorToDisplay` is set.

    4. **Update `ApproveModal.js`**: Accept a new `onMintingError` prop and pass it down to each `ApproveCurrencyRow`.

    5. **Update `ApproveCurrencyRow.js`**: Accept an `onMintingError` prop and call it in the catch block of the approve action, right before `storeTransactionError`.

pr_chain.title: Adjust mint gas limits for multi-coin transactions
pr_chain.description:
The dapp currently estimates gas for mint transactions using a simple base limit plus a per-coin increase. This estimation is causing mint transactions to run out of gas in some scenarios. We need to update the gas estimation logic to use more accurate per-coin gas increments.

    Specifically:
    - Replace the current base mint gas limit with a new named constant for single-coin mints (base value: 200,000 gas)
    - Remove the current linear per-coin increase model in favor of explicit gas additions for 2-coin and 3-coin mint scenarios:
      - 2-coin mints should add 225,000 gas to the base limit
      - 3-coin mints should add 255,000 gas to the base limit
    - Update the mint gas calculation in the BuySellWidget component to use the new constants based on how many stablecoins are being used for the mint

    Please ensure the gas estimation logic in `dapp/src/components/buySell/BuySellWidget.js` correctly handles the three cases (1, 2, or 3 coins) and that the constants in `dapp/src/constants/Contract.js` are updated accordingly.

## Environment Setup
The dapp package has its own `package.json` with dependencies and scripts. There's also a `dapp/README.md` that may contain setup instructions. Check the root `README.md` for any monorepo-specific instructions. The CI workflow in `.github/workflows/node.js.yml` shows how the project is built and tested.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `dapp/src/constants/Contract.js`, rename `MINT_SIMPLE_GAS_LIMIT` to `MINT_BASE_GAS_LIMIT` with the same value (200000).
    2. In the same file, replace `MINT_PER_COIN_GAS_INCREASE` with two new constants:
       - `MINT_2_COIN_ADDITION_GAS_LIMIT` set to 225000
       - `MINT_3_COIN_ADDITION_GAS_LIMIT` set to 255000
    3. In `dapp/src/components/buySell/BuySellWidget.js`, update the fallback gas limit assignment to use `MINT_BASE_GAS_LIMIT` instead of `MINT_SIMPLE_GAS_LIMIT`.
    4. Replace the current `if (mintAddresses.length > 1)` block with explicit checks:
       - If `mintAddresses.length === 2`, add `MINT_2_COIN_ADDITION_GAS_LIMIT` to the gas limit
       - If `mintAddresses.length === 3`, add `MINT_3_COIN_ADDITION_GAS_LIMIT` to the gas limit
    5. Verify all references to the old constant names are updated throughout the dapp codebase.

pr_chain.title: Detect failed transactions and fix Etherscan link display
pr_chain.description:
The dapp's transaction monitoring needs to properly identify failed transactions, particularly those that run out of gas. Currently, when a transaction is mined but fails (e.g., out of gas), it is still displayed as successful in the transaction history side panel. We need to:

1. Detect failed transactions by examining the transaction receipt's `status` field. After the Byzantium fork (block 4,370,000), transaction receipts include a `status` parameter where `0` indicates failure and `1` indicates success. Transactions that fail should be marked with an `isError` flag so the UI can display them as failed.

2. Fix the Etherscan link display in the transaction side panel. When transactions are pending (not yet mined), they may have placeholder hashes for deduplication purposes that are not valid Ethereum transaction hashes. The Etherscan link should only be shown when the transaction hash is actually valid (starts with `0x`).

## Environment Setup
The dapp code is in the `dapp/` directory. Check `dapp/package.json` for dependency management and available scripts for development and testing. The `dapp/yarn.lock` file indicates that Yarn is used for package management. The project also has GitHub Actions configured in `.github/workflows/node.js.yml` which may show CI test and build steps.

## Implementation Plan
- In `dapp/src/components/TransactionListener.js`, when updating a transaction after it's mined, inspect the transaction receipt data from the RPC provider. Check if the receipt has a `status` property that is a number equal to `0`, and if so, set an `isError` flag on the transaction object.
    - In `dapp/src/components/sidePanel/SidePanelTransactionMessage.js`, add logic to determine if a transaction hash is valid by checking if it starts with `0x`. Use this to conditionally render the Etherscan link in the transaction message.
    - Ensure that the `false` render condition in the transaction message component is maintained (it was already present as a placeholder and should not be removed).
    - Verify that existing logic in the message component that checks `transaction.isError` continues to work correctly for displaying failure states (red X icons, failure text).
    - Test the changes by confirming that failed transactions show the failure UI state and that the Etherscan icon only appears for transactions with real hashes.

pr_chain.title: Add conditional decimal formatting for transaction amounts
pr_chain.description:
The dapp currently shows transaction amounts in the expanded side panel with zero decimal places via `formatCurrency(value, 0)`. This makes small amounts (under $100) appear as "$0" rather than showing meaningful values like "$0.50" or "$42.75". 

    Implement a new utility function `formatCurrencyConditional` in `dapp/src/utils/math.js` that accepts a `threshold` value, and uses a different number of decimal places depending on whether the amount is above or below that threshold. For amounts under the threshold, display 2 decimal places; for amounts at or above the threshold, display 0 decimal places.

    Then update the transaction details display in `dapp/src/components/sidePanel/SidePanelTransactionMessage.js` to use this new function for all OUSD, USDT, DAI, and USDC amount displays in the expanded transaction area (both the "left" and "right" expand-box sections, for both mint and redeem transactions). Replace all existing `formatCurrency(transaction.data.<coin>, 0)` calls with `formatCurrencyConditional(transaction.data.<coin>, 100, 2, 0)`.

    The helper should handle edge cases like empty strings or non-numeric values by returning "0.00". It should floor (not round) the value.

Also review `.github/workflows/node.js.yml` for CI configuration that shows how tests are run in this repository.

## Implementation Plan
- Add a new exported function `formatCurrencyConditional(value, threshold, decimalsBeforeThreshold, decimalsAfterThreshold)` to `dapp/src/utils/math.js`.
    - Implement the function to check if the value is empty or NaN (return "0.00" in those cases), compare the parsed value against the threshold, and delegate to the existing `formatCurrencyMinMaxDecimals` helper with the appropriate min/max decimals and `floorInsteadOfRound: true`.

pr_chain.title: Reduce Alchemy API calls in dapp by optimizing polling intervals
pr_chain.description:
We're seeing an excessive number of calls to the Alchemy API from the dapp, which is both costly and could potentially hit rate limits. The current implementation polls for data too frequently and in cases where it's not even necessary.

    The goal is to reduce the number of API calls by:
    1. Increasing the polling intervals for account balances and exchange rates so we're not querying the network more often than needed.
    2. Not fetching exchange rates when the wallet is not connected — if there's no user action, this data isn't needed until a connection is made.
    3. Not fetching exchange rates when the user is not actively using the dapp (e.g., the tab is in the background or the user is idle).

    Please make these optimizations in `dapp/src/utils/contracts.js` and `dapp/src/components/AccountListener.js`. The balance polling interval should be moderately increased, while the exchange rate interval should be increased more substantially. This is a focused change — don't refactor any surrounding logic.

## Environment Setup
Check `dapp/package.json` for the dapp's dependencies and scripts. The dapp also has a `dapp/README.md` that likely contains setup instructions. For test/CI configuration, see `.github/workflows/node.js.yml`. Note this is primarily a frontend change in the `dapp/` directory.

## Implementation Plan
- In `dapp/src/components/AccountListener.js`, increase the `setInterval` delay for the balance polling from 5000ms to 7000ms.
    - In `dapp/src/utils/contracts.js`, track whether a wallet is connected (i.e., when `account` and `library` are provided).
    - In `dapp/src/utils/contracts.js`, only start the periodic exchange rate fetch interval when the wallet is connected. Wrap the existing `setInterval` call in a conditional.
    - Increase the interval delay for exchange rate fetching from 5000ms to 20000ms for when the wallet is connected.
    - In `dapp/src/utils/contracts.js`, add a guard inside the periodic fetch logic that checks the `active` status from `AccountStore` — if the user is not 'active', skip the fetch and return early.

pr_chain.title: Add governance proposal script tooling and refactor shared utilities
pr_chain.description:
We need to improve our governance workflow tooling. Currently, the only way to interact with the Governor contract is through deployment scripts in `contracts/scripts/deploy/` which mix proposal creation with execution. We need standalone, reusable scripts for the two separate phases of the governance lifecycle:

    1. **Proposing**: Submitting a proposal to the Governor contract (anyone can do this).
    2. **Executing**: Executing a queued proposal after the timelock expires (anyone can do this).

    Additionally, the helper functions `governorArgs()` and `proposeArgs()` that build the argument arrays for the Governor's `propose()` method are currently defined in `contracts/test/helpers.js` — a test-only file. Since these utilities are needed by the new scripts (and already imported by existing deploy scripts), they should be moved to a shared location under `contracts/utils/` so both tests and scripts can import them without coupling to the test harness.

    The goal is to make it easy for anyone to construct and submit a governance proposal from the command line, inspect proposal state, and execute proposals once they're ready — without requiring modification of deployment scripts or test helper files.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repo files to understand how to set up dependencies and run tests:
    - `contracts/package.json` — lists dependencies and scripts for the contracts package
    - `contracts/README.md` — may contain setup and usage instructions
    - `contracts/buidler.config.js` — network configuration and contract setup for the Büidler environment
    - `contracts/yarn.lock` — lockfile indicating package manager usage

## Implementation Plan
1. Create `contracts/utils/governor.js` containing the `governorArgs()` (renamed to `_governorArgs()` as a private helper) and `proposeArgs()` functions, moved from `contracts/test/helpers.js` with minimal changes (keep the same behavior and export `proposeArgs`).
    
    2. Update `contracts/test/helpers.js` to remove the `governorArgs` and `proposeArgs` functions and their exports, since they now live in the shared utility file.

    3. Update imports in existing files that currently reference `proposeArgs` from `../../test/helpers.js`:
       - `contracts/scripts/deploy/switchToNewGovernor.js`
       - `contracts/scripts/deploy/upgradeToCoreAdmin.js`
       - `contracts/test/governor.js`
       - Change these to import from `../../utils/governor` or `../utils/governor` as appropriate.

    4. Create a new directory `contracts/scripts/governor/` with:
       - `README.md` — document the governance proposal lifecycle (propose → queue → execute) and how to use the scripts.
       - `propose.js` — a script that accepts command-line arguments to select an action (at minimum, a "harvest" proposal calling `harvest()` on the VaultAdmin), constructs the proposal args using `proposeArgs()` from the new utility, and sends the `propose()` transaction to the Governor contract. Support a `--doIt=true` flag to actually broadcast the transaction (default is dry-run mode).
       - `execute.js` — a script that accepts a `--proposalId` argument, fetches and displays the proposal state and actions via `proposalCount()`, `state()`, and `getActions()`, and if `--doIt=true` is set, sends the `execute()` transaction to the Governor contract.

    5. Both scripts should follow the existing pattern in other deploy scripts: use `getNamedAccounts()` for the deployer, respect `BUIDLER_NETWORK` for network selection, use `getTxOpts()` from `../../utils/tx` for gas settings, and wait for 3 block confirmations on mainnet/rinkeby (0 otherwise).

pr_chain.title: Persist OUSD balance animation state across page refreshes
pr_chain.description:
The OUSD balance in the header animates upward based on the current APY to show estimated yield accrual. Currently, this animation restarts from the base balance on every page refresh, losing all visual progress. The goal is to make the animation "survive" refreshes by persisting the animated balance and using it to continue the simulation from where it left off.

    Implement the following behavior in `dapp/src/components/buySell/BalanceHeader.js`:
    - Modify `normalOusdAnimation` to accept a `fromOusdBalance` parameter instead of always starting from the current `ousdBalance`.
    - While the animation runs, periodically (every 5 seconds) store the current animated balance, the real OUSD balance, and the timestamp to `localStorage` under a key like `animatedBalance`.
    - On initial load, check `localStorage` for previously stored animation data. If the stored real balance matches the current real balance (meaning no mint/redeem/transfer/rebase occurred), compute a simulated starting balance by extrapolating the stored animated balance forward based on the APY and elapsed time since the last stored timestamp. Then start the animation from that simulated value.
    - If the stored balance doesn't match the current balance, or no stored data exists, start the animation normally from the current real balance.

## Environment Setup
Check `dapp/package.json` for dependency scripts and `dapp/README.md` for any dapp-specific setup instructions. The repo uses Yarn workspaces, so `dapp/yarn.lock` and the root `package.json` may also contain relevant configuration.

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify `normalOusdAnimation(fromOusdBalance)` to use the passed parameter as the animation start value, and update the `to` calculation to use it as well.
    2. Inside the `callbackValue` function, add logic to store `{animatedOusdBalance, ousdBalance, time}` to `localStorage` every 5 seconds, using a module-level variable to track the last storage time.
    3. In the `useEffect` where `ousdBalance` is loaded, add a branch that reads `localStorage.getItem('animatedBalance')` before starting the default animation.
    4. If stored data exists and `animationData.ousdBalance === ousdBalance`, calculate the simulated balance as `storedAnimatedBalance + (storedAnimatedBalance * apy / 31536000) * timeElapsedSeconds`, and call `normalOusdAnimation(simulatedBalance)`. Otherwise, call `normalOusdAnimation(ousdBalance)`.
    5. Keep the existing mint/rebounce animation logic unchanged; only the fallback path needs the new persistence logic.
    6. Test by refreshing the page mid-animation and verifying the balance continues from approximately where it left off.

pr_chain.title: Replace hardcoded gas limits with estimateGas and buffers
pr_chain.description:
The dapp currently uses hardcoded gas limits for mint and redeem transactions, which are selected based on manually checking thresholds against the vault's `autoAllocateThreshold` and `rebaseThreshold`. This approach is fragile: it requires keeping the gas limit constants in sync with actual contract behavior, and if the oracles move enough between the threshold check and the transaction being mined, the transaction can run out of gas.

    We need to move to a simpler, more robust approach: use `estimateGas` on the vault contract to get a gas estimate for the exact transaction we're about to send, then pad that estimate with a buffer. This removes the need for the threshold checks and the `gasLimits` constant entirely.

    For mint transactions (`mint` and `mintMultiple`), pad the estimate by the greater of `20000` gas or 10%. For redeem transactions (`redeem` and `redeemAll`), pad by 25% since we're less concerned about gas conservation when burning tokens.

    Note: There is a known edge case where `redeemAll` can still fail if a rebase pushes the balance over the threshold between estimation and execution, but this is acceptable for now.

## Environment Setup
Check `dapp/package.json` for dependency management and any available scripts. The `dapp/README.md` may contain additional setup or run instructions. Look at `dapp/next.config.js` for build configuration.

## Implementation Plan

## Add DynamoDB token storage adapter example to documentation

Implement a new documentation example demonstrating how to create a custom token storage adapter for the Globus SDK. The example must show how to build a storage backend using AWS DynamoDB that implements the `StorageAdapter` interface. This serves as a reference for users who need to write custom token storage backends for key-value stores or other non-standard storage systems.

    The example should:
    - Demonstrate a `DynamoDBStorageAdapter` class that extends `globus_sdk.tokenstorage.StorageAdapter`
    - Show how to store and retrieve token data using DynamoDB as the backend
    - Include a working example script that uses the adapter with a NativeAppAuthClient for authentication
    - Add documentation explaining the design choices (particularly why enumeration of tokens is not supported with key-value stores)
    - Register the new example in the examples documentation toctree

    The example should illustrate the key token storage operations: storing OAuthTokenResponse data, retrieving token data by resource server, and integrating with the Globus SDK's token storage interface. The implementation must handle null refresh tokens gracefully (when access-token-only flows are used) and should demonstrate proper namespacing to support multi-user scenarios.

## Environment Setup

       - Define a class that extends `globus_sdk.tokenstorage.StorageAdapter`
       - Implement `_compute_key(resource_server)` to generate storage keys with proper namespacing
       - Implement `store(token_response)` to persist token data to DynamoDB, handling null refresh tokens

pr_chain.title: Add GCS endpoint get and update operations to GCSClient
pr_chain.description:
Add two new methods to the `GCSClient` class for managing GCS endpoints, along with a new `EndpointDocument` data class for constructing endpoint update payloads:

    1. `get_endpoint()` — fetch the details of the endpoint the client is configured to talk to via `GET /endpoint`, returning an `UnpackingGCSResponse` that unpacks the "endpoint" key from the response data.
    2. `update_endpoint()` — update a GCS endpoint via `PATCH /endpoint`, accepting either a dict or an `EndpointDocument` as the payload, with an optional `include` parameter (`["endpoint"]`, `"endpoint"`, or None) that gets joined via `utils.commajoin` into the `include` query parameter.

    The `EndpointDocument` class should extend `utils.PayloadWrapper` and model the mutable fields of an Endpoint#1.2.0 document. Fields should use `MISSING` as the default sentinel (not `None`) to distinguish between "not provided" and "explicitly null". Fields should include: `contact_email`, `contact_info`, `department`, `description`, `display_name`, `info_link`, `network_use`, `organization`, `subscription_id`, `keywords`, `allow_udt`, `public`, `gridftp_control_channel_port`, `max_concurrency`, `max_parallelism`, `preferred_concurrency`, and `preferred_parallelism`.

    Also update `PayloadWrapper` in `utils.py` to support nullable fields — specifically, add handling so that `MISSING` values are omitted from the payload, while `None` values are explicitly set (allowing nulls to be sent to the API).

    Export `EndpointDocument` from the package: add it to `_LAZY_IMPORT_TABLE` in `src/globus_sdk/_generate_init.py`, update `src/globus_sdk/__init__.py` accordingly, and export it from `src/globus_sdk/services/gcs/__init__.py` and `src/globus_sdk/services/gcs/data/__init__.py`.

## Environment Setup
Check `pyproject.toml` for project configuration and dependency management, `tox.ini` for test environment setup, and `Makefile` for common development tasks. The `requirements/` directory contains pinned dependency sets for different Python versions and test configurations. Look at `tests/README` and `docs/testing/getting_started.rst` for guidance on how to run the test suite.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create the `EndpointDocument` class**:
       - Create a new file `src/globus_sdk/services/gcs/data/endpoint.py`
       - Define `class EndpointDocument(utils.PayloadWrapper)` with `DATATYPE_BASE = "endpoint"`
       - Set `DATATYPE_VERSION_IMPLICATIONS` to map `gridftp_control_channel_port` to version `(1, 1, 0)`
       - In `__init__`, accept keyword arguments for all mutable endpoint fields with `MISSING` as the default
       - Use `self._set_value()` with appropriate callbacks for each field type (string, bool, int, list)

    2. **Update `PayloadWrapper` for nullable support**:
       - In `src/globus_sdk/utils.py`, modify `_set_value` (and the `_set_opt*` helpers) so that:
         - `MISSING` values are skipped (not set)
         - `None` values are explicitly set (as null)
         - Other values are set with the optional callback applied
       - Add docstrings to clarify the "omittable vs nullable" distinction

    3. **Add the client methods**:
       - In `src/globus_sdk/services/gcs/client.py`, import `EndpointDocument` from `.data`
       - Add a `get_endpoint()` method that calls `self.get("/endpoint")` and wraps the result in `UnpackingGCSResponse(..., "endpoint")`
       - Add an `update_endpoint()` method that:
         - Accepts `endpoint_data` (dict or `EndpointDocument`) and optional `include` keyword
         - If `include` is provided, sets `query_params["include"] = utils.commajoin(include)`
         - Calls `self.patch("/endpoint", data=endpoint_data, query_params=query_params)`
         - Wraps the response in `UnpackingGCSResponse(..., "endpoint")`

    4. **Export the new type**:
       - In `src/globus_sdk/services/gcs/data/__init__.py`, import and add `EndpointDocument` to `__all__`
       - In `src/globus_sdk/services/gcs/__init__.py`, import `EndpointDocument` and add to `__all__`
       - In `src/globus_sdk/_generate_init.py`, add `"EndpointDocument"` to the `services.gcs` lazy import table
       - Regenerate `src/globus_sdk/__init__.py` by running the `_generate_init.py` script

    5. **Add test fixture data**:
       - Create `src/globus_sdk/_testing/data/globus_connect_server/get_endpoint.py` with a `ResponseSet` containing a `RegisteredResponse` for the GET /endpoint path
       - Create `src/globus_sdk/_testing/data/globus_connect_server/update_endpoint.py` with `ResponseSet` containing default and `include_endpoint` cases for PATCH /endpoint
       - Each response should include realistic `endpoint#1.2.0` data

    6. **Add functional tests**:
       - Create `tests/functional/services/gcs/test_endpoints.py` with tests for:
         - `get_endpoint()` returning the expected endpoint data
         - `update_endpoint()` with an `EndpointDocument`
         - `update_endpoint()` with `include=["endpoint"]` returning the endpoint in the response

    7. **Add a changelog fragment**:
       - Create `changelog.d/` fragment documenting the new operations

pr_chain.title: Refactor paginator contract validation to use declarative class attributes
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to improve how paginator contracts are tested by making the required method keyword arguments explicit on each paginator class itself, rather than maintaining an imperative mapping in the test suite.

    Currently, the test `tests/unit/test_paginator_signature_matching.py` contains an explicit mapping from each paginator type to the set of method keyword arguments it requires (e.g., `HasNextPaginator` and `LimitOffsetTotalPaginator` require `("limit", "offset")`). This mapping must be kept in sync with the actual paginator implementations.

    We need to add a class attribute `_REQUIRES_METHOD_KWARGS` to the paginator classes in `src/globus_sdk/paging/` that declares which keyword arguments the paginated method must support. The test should then read this attribute directly from the paginator class attached to each paginated method, eliminating the need for the explicit mapping.

    Additionally, please improve the test's client discovery logic to automatically find all client classes exported from the `globus_sdk` package's namespace. This removes the need to maintain a hardcoded list of client classes.

## Environment Setup
Please review the repository config files to determine how to install dependencies and run tests. Key files to consult:
    - `pyproject.toml` — project metadata and build configuration
    - `tox.ini` — test automation configuration
    - `Makefile` — developer convenience commands
    - `requirements/*.txt` files — per-version dependency lists (e.g., `requirements/py3.12/test.txt`)

## Implementation Plan
1. Add `_REQUIRES_METHOD_KWARGS: tuple[str, ...] = ()` as a class attribute to the base `Paginator` class in `src/globus_sdk/paging/base.py`.
    2. Override `_REQUIRES_METHOD_KWARGS` in each concrete paginator subclass:
       - `LastKeyPaginator`: `("last_key",)`
       - `_LimitOffsetBasedPaginator` (and its subclasses `HasNextPaginator` and `LimitOffsetTotalPaginator`): `("limit", "offset")`
       - `MarkerPaginator` (and `NullableMarkerPaginator`): `("marker",)`
       - `NextTokenPaginator`: `("next_token",)`
    3. Update the test in `tests/unit/test_paginator_signature_matching.py` to read `_REQUIRES_METHOD_KWARGS` from the paginator class instead of using the imperative if/elif mapping.
    4. Refactor the test's client discovery logic to dynamically find client classes by iterating over `dir(globus_sdk)` and checking for subclasses of `globus_sdk.BaseClient`, rather than using a hardcoded tuple.
    5. Run the test suite to verify all paginated methods still satisfy their paginator's required keyword arguments.

pr_chain.title: Fix incorrect AuthClient.create_policy signature and deprecate positional arguments
pr_chain.description:
The `create_policy` method on `AuthClient` currently declares `high_assurance` and `authentication_assurance_timeout` as required positional parameters in its signature. However, these parameters are actually optional in the Auth API — they only need to be sent when `high_assurance` is True. The current signature is incorrect and forces callers to provide values that aren't always necessary.

    Additionally, the current signature allows positional usage for all parameters, but this makes it difficult to maintain backwards compatibility and evolve the API. We want to move to a keyword-only argument interface for this method, while still supporting legacy positional-argument callers during the transition.

    The goal is to:
    1. Fix the method signature so that only genuinely required parameters (`project_id`, `display_name`, `description`) are mandatory, and make `high_assurance` and `authentication_assurance_timeout` optional keyword arguments.
    2. Mark all parameters as keyword-only in the signature to establish the correct modern interface.
    3. Provide a compatibility shim that accepts legacy positional-argument calls, maps them to the keyword-only signature, and emits a `RemovedInV4Warning` to guide users toward the new interface.
    4. Ensure the compatibility layer raises appropriate `TypeError`s when too many positional arguments are passed or when a value is supplied both positionally and by keyword.
    5. Update test fixtures and add functional tests covering both the new keyword-only path and the legacy positional-argument compatibility path.
    6. Add a mypy ignore test file that documents the type-checking behavior for both supported and deprecated call patterns.

    Please also add a changelog entry documenting this behavioral change.

## Environment Setup
Check `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, and `tox.ini` for dependency management and test configuration. The `Makefile` may contain common development tasks. Requirements files are in the `requirements/` directory (e.g., `requirements/py3.11/test.txt`). Review `tests/README` and `CONTRIBUTING.adoc` for testing conventions and contribution guidelines.

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify `AuthClient.create_policy` signature: make `project_id`, `display_name`, and `description` required (without defaults or keyword-only markers), make `high_assurance` and `authentication_assurance_timeout` optional with `utils.MISSING` defaults, and add a `*` marker to make all parameters keyword-only.
    2. Create a decorator (e.g., `_create_policy_compat`) that wraps the method to handle legacy positional-argument calls — mapping positional values to keyword arguments, emitting `RemovedInV4Warning` when positionals are used, and raising `TypeError` for too many positionals or duplicate argument values.
    3. Update the docstring to clarify that required parameters may not be declared as required in the signature due to backwards compatibility, and note this behavior will change in a future major release.
    4. Update the testing fixtures in `src/globus_sdk/_testing/data/auth/create_policy.py` to remove `high_assurance` and `authentication_assurance_timeout` from default request args, only including them when explicitly provided. Adjust the `register_response` helper to support custom match criteria.
    5. Add functional tests covering: the standard keyword-only call path, legacy positional usage (expecting warning), too-many-positionals (expecting `TypeError`), and duplicate-argument errors. Add a mypy ignore test file documenting supported and deprecated call signatures.
    6. Add a changelog entry under `changelog.d/` describing the signature correction and deprecation of positional arguments.

pr_chain.title: Add session_required_mfa support to auth error info and authorize URL
pr_chain.description:
We need to bring the SDK's auth interfaces closer to parity with the Globus Auth specification by adding support for the `session_required_mfa` parameter in two places:

    1. **`AuthorizationParameterInfo` error info object**: The server can include `session_required_mfa` (a boolean indicating whether MFA is required for a session) in the `authorization_parameters` of error responses. The SDK currently parses other session-related fields (`session_message`, `session_required_identities`, `session_required_single_domain`, `session_required_policies`) but not this one. We need to parse and expose this field so users can detect MFA requirements from errors. Also, the existing `session_required_policies` attribute is documented in the class docstring but the `session_required_mfa` attribute is not documented at all.

    2. **`AuthLoginClient.oauth2_get_authorize_url` method**: The authorize URL endpoint accepts a `session_required_mfa` query parameter. The method should accept this parameter and pass it through to the query string so users can proactively require MFA when constructing authorize URLs. This should follow the same pattern as the other `session_required_*` parameters.

    The goal is to support both reactive detection (via error parsing) and proactive enforcement (via authorize URL) of MFA session requirements.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository configuration files for setup and test instructions:
    - `pyproject.toml` — project metadata and build configuration
    - `Makefile` — likely contains development task shortcuts
    - `tox.ini` — test environment configuration
    - `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — pre-commit hooks for code quality
    - `CONTRIBUTING.adoc` — contributor guidelines

## Implementation Plan
1. **Modify `src/globus_sdk/exc/err_info.py`**:
       - Add a `session_required_mfa` attribute to `AuthorizationParameterInfo.__init__`, parsed from the `authorization_parameters` dict.
       - Add a `_parse_session_required_mfa(data)` method that:
         - Returns the value if it's a `bool`
         - Calls `self._warn_type("session_required_mfa", "bool", value)` if present but not a bool
         - Returns `None` if absent
       - Update the class docstring to document `session_required_mfa` (and include the existing-but-undocumented `session_required_policies`).

    2. **Modify `src/globus_sdk/services/auth/client/base_login_client.py`**:
       - Add a `session_required_mfa: bool | None = None` keyword-only parameter to `oauth2_get_authorize_url`.
       - Add a docstring entry for the new parameter.
       - In the query_params construction logic, add the parameter to `query_params` when it is not `None`, exactly like the other `session_required_*` parameters.

    3. **Add a changelog entry**:
       - Create a new file in `changelog.d/` following the naming convention (e.g., `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_username_missing_session_params.rst`).
       - Use the template format (see `changelog.d/new_fragment.rst.j2` and existing entries).

    4. **Update tests**:
       - In `tests/functional/services/auth/test_auth_client_flow.py`:
         - Add `mfa_options = (True, False)` 
         - Expand the parametrization matrix to include MFA alongside domain, identity, policy, and prompt options
         - Update the parametrize decorator and test function signature
         - Update the expected/asserted query parameter logic to check for `session_required_mfa`
       - In `tests/unit/errors/test_common_functionality.py`:
         - Update existing tests to assert `session_required_mfa=None` in the string representation
         - Add new parametrized tests for `session_required_mfa` values (`True` and `False`), plus a malformed-type test

pr_chain.title: Convert TransferClient deprecation warnings to Sphinx admonition blocks
pr_chain.description:
In `src/globus_sdk/services/transfer/client.py`, several methods in the `TransferClient` class contain deprecation notices formatted as plain text trailing lines in their docstrings (e.g., "DEPRECATION WARNING: this helper is deprecated..."). These notices are not rendered as visually distinct warnings in the generated Sphinx documentation.

    Refactor these deprecation notices into proper Sphinx `.. warning::` admonition blocks. Each admonition block should appear **before** the list of method parameters in the docstring, rather than after them. This improves the visual hierarchy and readability of the rendered documentation.

    The following methods in `src/globus_sdk/services/transfer/client.py` are affected:
    - `create_endpoint`
    - `endpoint_autoactivate`
    - `endpoint_deactivate`
    - `endpoint_activate`
    - `endpoint_get_activation_requirements`
    - `add_endpoint_server`
    - `update_endpoint_server`
    - `delete_endpoint_server`

    For each of these methods, move the deprecation text from its current position (typically at the end of the docstring, after `:param` entries) to a `.. warning::` admonition block positioned at the start of the docstring, before any `:param` lines. The admonition block should be formatted with a blank line after the `.. warning::` directive, followed by the indented deprecation text, and then a blank line before the `:param` entries begin.

    Example transformation:

    Before:
    ```
    """
    :param data: An endpoint document with fields for the new endpoint

    DEPRECATION WARNING: this helper is deprecated with the end of Globus Connect
    Server v4 support and may no longer function with the Transfer API.
    """
    ```

    After:
    ```
    """
    .. warning::

        This method is deprecated with the end of Globus Connect Server v4
        support and may no longer function with the Transfer API.

    :param data: An endpoint document with fields for the new endpoint
    """
    ```

    Note: The deprecation text should be rephrased from "this helper is deprecated" to "This method is deprecated" for consistency with standard Sphinx documentation conventions.

    Do not modify any code logic or method behavior—only docstrings are to be altered.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repository config files for dependency installation and testing instructions:
    - `pyproject.toml`
    - `setup.py`
    - `tox.ini`
    - `Makefile`
    - `requirements/` directory (contains version-specific requirement files like `requirements/py3.12/test.txt`)

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `src/globus_sdk/services/transfer/client.py` and locate the `create_endpoint` method docstring.
    2. Extract the deprecation text ("DEPRECATION WARNING: this helper is deprecated with the end of Globus Connect Server v4 support and may no longer function with the Transfer API.") from its current position at the end of the docstring.
    3. Replace the removed text with a `.. warning::` admonition block at the beginning of the docstring, before the `:param` entries. Use the format:
       ```
       .. warning::

           This method is deprecated with the end of Globus Connect Server v4
           support and may no longer function with the Transfer API.

       ```
       Ensure there is a blank line after the admonition block and before the first `:param` line.
    4. Repeat steps 2-3 for the following methods: `endpoint_autoactivate`, `endpoint_deactivate`, `endpoint_activate`, `endpoint_get_activation_requirements`, `add_endpoint_server`, `update_endpoint_server`, and `delete_endpoint_server`.
    5. Verify that no other deprecation notices remain in plain-text format in the affected methods.
    6. Review the changes to ensure the admonition blocks are correctly indented (4 spaces for the text within the admonition) and that the docstrings remain otherwise unchanged.

Update the docstring for the operation_symlink helper so the warning about collections not supporting it is formatted as a proper Sphinx warning directive instead of plain text. This ensures the warning renders correctly in the generated documentation.

The scope construction example in the docs shows output that doesn't match the demoed inputs. Fix the example so the printed results are accurate — for instance, `str(foo)` should show the nested dependency correctly, and the optional dependency case should include its printed output alongside the repr. Make sure the example demonstrates all three methods consistently.
