pr_chain.title: Add a real-time chat application using Node.js and Socket.io
pr_chain.description:
Create a new folder `Chat-App/` containing a real-time chat application built with Node.js, Express, and Socket.io. The app should allow multiple clients to connect simultaneously, exchange messages in real-time, see a live count of connected users, and receive typing indicators when another user is composing a message.

    The application consists of:
    - A backend server (`app.js`) that serves static files from a `public/` directory and manages Socket.io connections.
    - A frontend (`public/index.html`, `public/main.js`, `public/style.css`) that renders the chat UI, handles user input, plays sound effects for received/sent messages, and communicates with the server via Socket.io.
    - A `package.json` defining the project dependencies and start scripts.
    - Two sound effect files: `iphone_text_message.mp3` (already placed in both `Chat-App/` and `Chat-App/public/`) and `iphone_send_sms.mp3` (only in `Chat-App/public/`).

    The chat functionality should include:
    - Sending and receiving text messages between all connected clients.
    - Displaying the username (defaulting to "anonymous") and timestamp for each message.
    - Broadcasting "typing..." feedback to all clients when a user focuses or types in the message input.
    - Displaying the total number of connected clients.
    - Playing a notification sound when a new message is received.

## Environment Setup
Check the `Chat-App/package.json` file for the project's dependencies and defined scripts (`start` runs `node app.js`, `dev` runs `nodemon app.js`). Also check the `Chat-App/package-lock.json` for the exact dependency tree. Other project folders like `Corona-tracker/package.json`, `Counter_App/package.json`, or `Live Clock/package.json` contain similar JSON structure but are unrelated to this task. Note: the repository root has a `README.md` that may contain general contribution guidelines.

## Implementation Plan
1. Create the `Chat-App/` directory structure with subfolders: `public/` and place the provided sound effects (`iphone_text_message.mp3`, `iphone_send_sms.mp3`) in `Chat-App/` and/or `Chat-App/public/` as specified.
    2. Create `Chat-App/package.json` with:
       - Name: `chatapp`, version `1.0.0`.
       - Scripts: `"start": "node app.js"` and `"dev": "nodemon app.js"`.
       - Dependencies: `express` (^4.18.2) and `socket.io` (^4.7.1).
       - DevDependencies: `nodemon` (^3.0.1).
    3. Create the backend `Chat-App/app.js`:
       - Import `express`, `path`, and `socket.io`.
       - Create an Express app, listen on port 3000 (or `process.env.PORT`).
       - Serve static files from the `public/` folder using `express.static()`.
       - Initialize Socket.io with the HTTP server.
       - Maintain a `Set` of connected socket IDs.
       - On connection: add the socket ID to the set, broadcast the total client count via `"clients-total"` event.
       - On disconnect: remove the socket ID and broadcast the updated count.
       - On `"message"` event from a client: broadcast the received data to all other sockets (not the sender) using `"chat-message"`.
       - On `"feedback"` event from a client: broadcast the typing feedback to all other sockets using `"feedback"`.
    4. Create the frontend `Chat-App/public/index.html`:
       - Include a title `"Chit Chat🚀"`, a name input field, a message container (`<ul>`), a message form with input and send button, and a total-clients display.
       - Load the Socket.io client script from `/socket.io/socket.io.js`.
       - Include the Moment.js library from the CDN for time formatting.
       - Link to `style.css` and include `main.js` at the end of the body.
    5. Create the frontend `Chat-App/public/main.js`:
       - Connect to Socket.io (`const socket = io();`).
       - Grab DOM elements: client total, message container, name input, message form, message input.
       - Initialize audio tones: `iphone_text_message.mp3` for received messages (play it on `"chat-message"` event).
       - On form submit, prevent default and call `sendMessage()` if the input is not empty.
       - `sendMessage()`: build data object with name, message, and current date/time; emit `"message"` on socket; call `addMessage(true, data)` to render the outgoing message locally; clear the input.
       - On `"clients-total"` event, update the total-clients display text.
       - On `"chat-message"` event, play the received-message sound and call `addMessage(false, data)`.
       - `addMessage(isOwnMsg, data)`: first call `clearFeedbackmsg()` to remove any existing typing indicator; append an `<li>` with class `message-right` (for own) or `message-left` (for others), containing the message text and a span with the name and formatted time using Moment.js (`moment(data.dateTime).fromNow()`); then call `scrolltoBottom()`.
       - `scrolltoBottom()`: scroll the message container to its scrollHeight.
       - Add `focus`, `keypress`, and `blur` event listeners on the message input to emit `"feedback"` events with the appropriate feedback text (e.g., `✍🏻${name} is typing a message` or empty string on blur).
       - On `"feedback"` event, call `clearFeedbackmsg()` and append a feedback `<li>` element with class `message-feedback`.
       - `clearFeedbackmsg()`: remove all existing `li.message-feedback` elements from the message container.
    6. Create `Chat-App/public/style.css` with the chat UI styles: use the provided Google Fonts import, set the body to use a background image (e.g., `https://coolbackgrounds.io/images/backgrounds/index/compute-ea4c57a4.png`), and style the main container, name bar, message bubbles (left/right), message form, input, send button, and client-total text.
    7. Optionally add a `Chat-App/README.md` documenting the project, its usage, setup, and stack (though it's not strictly required for functionality).

pr_chain.title: Fix default config not applied when using custom query cache
pr_chain.description:
When using a custom query cache created via `makeQueryCache({ defaultConfig })` and providing it through `ReactQueryCacheProvider`, the default config (e.g., `staleTime`) is not being applied to queries created with `useQuery`. This happens because `useConfigContext` falls back to the global `defaultConfigRef` instead of the custom cache's merged config.

pr_chain.title: Define and centralize configuration merging strategy
pr_chain.description:
The current configuration merging logic is scattered across multiple places and is confusing to follow. It's spread between `useQueryArgs`, `useMutation`, `QueryCache`, and `ReactQueryConfigProvider`, making it hard to reason about precedence and leading to inconsistencies between hooks and direct query cache usage.

    We need to define a formal, explicit merging strategy and centralize it in the core config module. This will make the behavior predictable and easier to maintain.

    The desired merging order should be:

    **When using hooks** (e.g., `useQuery`, `useMutation`, `useInfiniteQuery`, `usePaginatedQuery`):
    1. Built-in defaults (`DEFAULT_CONFIG`).
    2. Defaults from the query cache that will be used (from context or explicitly specified).
    3. Combined defaults from any `ReactQueryConfigProvider`s in the tree (innermost provider takes precedence).
    4. The query/mutation config object passed to the hook.

    **When using a query cache directly** (e.g., `queryCache.buildQuery`, `queryCache.prefetchQuery`):
    1. Built-in defaults (`DEFAULT_CONFIG`).
    2. Defaults from the query cache.
    3. The query config object passed to the query cache method.

    **Goals:**
    - A single, clear implementation of the merge logic in `src/core/config.ts`.
    - Hooks and direct query cache usage should follow the same underlying strategy (with the hooks layer adding the context-provider step).
    - Eliminate the mutable `defaultConfigRef` and any side-effects that mutate it from `ReactQueryConfigProvider`. Providers should be pure context providers.
    - Ensure type safety is maintained throughout.
    - Make sure the behavior is backwards-compatible for existing users.

## Environment Setup
Please refer to the `package.json` at the repository root to find the scripts for building, linting, and running the test suite. The `jest.config.js` file contains the Jest configuration. Also check `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general contribution guidelines. The `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.types.json` files define the TypeScript compiler options.

## Implementation Plan
1.  **Create central merge utilities in `src/core/config.ts`:**
        - Add a `mergeReactQueryConfigs(a, b)` function that deep-merges the `shared`, `queries`, and `mutations` sections of two `ReactQueryConfig` objects.
        - Add `getDefaultedQueryConfig(queryCacheConfig, contextConfig, config, configOverrides)` and `getDefaultedMutationConfig(...)` functions. These functions should implement the merging order described above, taking optional `queryCacheConfig`, `contextConfig`, and the user-provided `config` and `configOverrides` (which should always win). They should return `QueryConfig` and `MutationConfig` respectively.
        - Remove the `defaultConfigRef` export.
    2.  **Refactor `QueryCache` (`src/core/queryCache.ts`):**
        - Remove the private `configRef` property and all logic that merges the `DEFAULT_CONFIG` with the cache's `defaultConfig`.
        - Update `getDefaultConfig()` to simply return `this.config.defaultConfig`.
        - Replace the `getDefaultedConfig` method with a new `getDefaultedQueryConfig` method. This method should call the new `getDefaultedQueryConfig` utility from `config.ts`, passing the cache's own config, no context config, and the user config. It must inject the `queryCache: this` override.
        - Ensure all internal usages (like in `getQueries`, `buildQuery`, `prefetchQuery`) use this new method.
    3.  **Refactor `ReactQueryConfigProvider` (`src/react/ReactQueryConfigProvider.tsx`):**
        - Remove all logic that reads or mutates `defaultConfigRef`.
        - Rename `useConfigContext` to `useContextConfig` and make it simply return the React context value.
        - The provider component should simply merge the incoming `config` with the `parentConfig` from the context using `mergeReactQueryConfigs` and provide the result to the context.
    4.  **Create new hook config-defaulting hooks:**
        - Create `src/react/useDefaultedQueryConfig.tsx` and `src/react/useDefaultedMutationConfig.tsx`.
        - These hooks should call `useQueryCache` (from `ReactQueryCacheProvider`) and the new `useContextConfig`.
        - They should determine the query cache to use (`config?.queryCache || contextQueryCache`).
        - Then call the respective `getDefaulted...Config` utility from `src/core/config.ts`, passing the cache's default config, the context config, the hook's config, and the correct query cache override.
    5.  **Update React hooks to use the new defaulting mechanism:**
        - In `useBaseQuery.ts`, call `useDefaultedQueryConfig` on the provided config before creating the observer.
        - In `useMutation.ts`, call `useDefaultedMutationConfig` on the config and use this defaulted config.
        - In `useInfiniteQuery.ts` and `usePaginatedQuery.ts`, stop using `useQueryArgs` and instead use the pure `getQueryArgs` function from `src/core/utils.ts` (which doesn't perform config merging). They should then optionally modify the config (e.g., add `infinite: true`, `keepPreviousData: true`) and pass it to `useBaseQuery`.
    6.  **Clean up:**
        - Delete `src/react/useQueryArgs.ts`.
        - Update `src/react/index.ts` to export the new hook types and remove references to `ReactQueryProviderConfig` (or alias it to `ReactQueryConfig` if needed for backwards compatibility). Also export the new `useContextConfig` if appropriate.
        - Add a `queryCache?: QueryCache` option to the `MutationConfig` type in `src/core/types.ts` if it's not already there.

We need to clean up the logic in QueryCache so it doesn't have React-specific concerns like preventing setState during render. That guard should live in the useIsFetching hook instead, and the cache should just notify listeners directly. Also, useIsFetching should have a safe state setter that schedules updates in microtasks to avoid setting state on unmounted components or during another component's render phase. pr_chain.title: Fix QueryObserver to only subscribe to queries when started
pr_chain.description:
When a QueryObserver is created, it currently subscribes to a query immediately in its constructor via `updateQuery()`, even before the observer is "started" by calling `subscribe()`. This causes a bug where, in React Strict Mode, components using `useQuery` with `refetchOnMount: false` fail to fetch data correctly because the observer subscribes to the query before it should.

    The fix is to ensure that observers only subscribe to queries when they are explicitly started. This means:
    1. Remove the subscription logic from the constructor path.
    2. Move the subscription to the `subscribe()` method.
    3. Only (re)subscribe when switching to a new query if the observer is already started.

pr_chain.title: Ensure paused and cancelled queries resolve or reject correctly
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to improve the lifecycle management of query promises in the cache. Currently, when a query's fetch is paused (e.g., due to a window focus change) or cancelled, the existing promises associated with that fetch may not settle (resolve/reject) as expected, leaving consumers hanging. We need to ensure that:

    - When a fetch is paused (e.g., during retries when the window is unfocused) and then resumed (e.g., when the window regains focus), all existing promises for that fetch resolve correctly with the final data.
    - When a fetch is cancelled, all existing promises reject with a dedicated `CancelledError` so consumers can distinguish a cancellation from a regular error.
    - Queries are still cached when the underlying request transport (e.g., `fetch`) does not support cancellation.
    - The `CancelledError` is set as the query's `error` state, and a helper function `isCancelledError` is exported so users can check if an error is due to cancellation.

    This requires refactoring the internal promise and cancellation management in the core query module to support explicit `continue()` and `cancel()` flows, and to properly handle transports that don't offer a native cancel method. The `setFocusHandler` should be updated to call the new `continue()` method on all cached queries when the window regains focus, rather than deleting the promise and relying on refetching.

## Environment Setup
To understand how to install dependencies and run the test suite, please refer to the repository configuration files: `package.json`, `jest.config.js`, and `tsconfig.json`. The root `package.json` contains the project's scripts and dependencies. The `jest.config.js` file specifies the test runner configuration.

## Implementation Plan
1. Refactor the `Query` class in `src/core/query.ts` to replace the current promise/cancellation flags with a more explicit state machine. Introduce private methods like `continue()` and `cancel()` that can trigger the resolution or rejection of the currently pending `promise`, and store callbacks (`continueFetch`, `cancelFetch`) to control the underlying fetch operation.
    2. Create a `CancelledError` class and `isCancelledError` helper function in `src/core/utils.ts`. Add a guard function `isCancelable` to check if a query function's result has a native `cancel` method.
    3. Modify the `fetch` method in `src/core/query.ts` to handle the case where the transport layer is not cancelable. When a fetch is cancelled, ensure the promise is rejected with `CancelledError` and the query state is updated accordingly.
    4. Update `setFocusHandler` in `src/core/setFocusHandler.ts` to call the new `continue()` method on all cached queries when the window regains focus, instead of manually deleting the `promise`. This ensures paused queries resume and their pending promises are resolved.
    5. Export the new `CancelledError` and `isCancelledError` from the core public API in `src/core/index.ts`. Add comprehensive tests in `src/core/tests/queryCache.test.tsx` and other relevant test files to cover the new resolution, rejection, and caching behavior for paused and cancelled queries.

pr_chain.title: Refactor query timeout scheduling to use explicit activation method
pr_chain.description:
Refactor the internal timeout scheduling mechanism in the query core. Currently, timeouts for stale data and garbage collection are scheduled automatically in the `Query` constructor when data exists. This needs to change so that timeouts are only scheduled when explicitly activated by the consumer.

    Implement a new `activateTimeouts()` method on the `Query` class that enables and schedules both the stale timeout and garbage collection timeout. This method should be called by all internal consumers (query cache and query observer) after creating or updating a query, rather than having timeouts scheduled automatically in the constructor.

    Make the scheduling methods resilient to being called at any time. Replace `scheduleStaleTimeout` and `scheduleCacheTimeout` with `rescheduleStaleTimeout` and `rescheduleGarbageCollection` respectively, ensuring they correctly handle various query states (e.g., no data, not stale, observers present) without relying on being called only at specific lifecycle moments.

    Change the stale timeout calculation to be based on `updatedAt` timestamp rather than being scheduled from the moment of creation, so that the residual time until stale is calculated correctly for queries that may have been inactive or have existing data. For prefetching scenarios, delay activating timeouts until the prefetch operation completes to avoid premature garbage collection of empty queries.

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` for dependency management and script definitions. Review `jest.config.js` for test configuration. The test file for this change is located at `src/react/tests/useQuery.test.tsx`. Refer to `tsconfig.json` for TypeScript compilation settings.

## Implementation Plan
- Add `enableTimeouts` private boolean field to `Query` class, defaulting to `false`, and remove automatic timeout scheduling from the constructor.
    - Implement `activateTimeouts()` method that sets `enableTimeouts` to `true` and calls both `rescheduleStaleTimeout()` and `rescheduleGarbageCollection()`.
    - Rename `scheduleStaleTimeout` to `rescheduleStaleTimeout` and modify it to check `enableTimeouts`, skip if query is already stale, status is not Success, or `staleTime` is Infinity. Calculate timeout based on `updatedAt` timestamp and elapsed time.
    - Rename `scheduleCacheTimeout` to `rescheduleGarbageCollection` and modify it to check `enableTimeouts`, skip if `cacheTime` is Infinity or if there are active observers.
    - Update all internal callers (query cache's `prefetchQuery` and `setQueryData`, query observer's `updateQuery`) to call `query.activateTimeouts()` after building or obtaining a query. For prefetching, call `activateTimeouts()` in a `finally` block after the fetch operation completes.
    - Update the test in `useQuery.test.tsx` to make the prefetch query function async with a delay, and add `staleTime` to the `useQuery` call in the test to properly verify the non-refetch behavior.

pr_chain.title: Expand caching docs to explain cacheTime behavior on remount
pr_chain.description:
The Caching guide in the documentation walks through a detailed example using `useQuery('todos', fetchTodos)` with the default `cacheTime` of 5 minutes and `staleTime` of 0. The current walkthrough covers mounting, unmounting, and garbage collection, but it is missing an important intermediate scenario: what happens when a new instance of the same query mounts *before* the `cacheTime` timeout expires. This is a common use case — for example, a user navigates away from a page and back within a few minutes — and the current docs don't explain that the cached value is returned immediately while a background refetch happens. This is a key distinction between `cacheTime` and `staleTime` that confused at least one new user, and the goal is to add two bullet points to the walkthrough to make this behavior explicit. The task is purely a documentation update to `docs/src/pages/docs/guides/caching.md`; no source code changes are needed.

## Environment Setup
Check `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general contribution guidelines and how to set up the repo. The documentation site lives under `docs/` and has its own `package.json` and `yarn.lock` for installing dependencies (e.g., Next.js). For running the docs locally or validating the markdown, look at the scripts defined in `docs/package.json`. The root `package.json` also contains scripts for the whole project (linting, testing, etc.) — but since this is docs-only, the docs site setup is most relevant.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `docs/src/pages/docs/guides/caching.md` in your editor.
    2. Locate the "A Detailed Caching Example" section, specifically the bullet list that walks through the lifecycle of `useQuery('todos', fetchTodos)`.
    3. Find the bullet point that says: "Since there are no more active instances to this query, a cache timeout is set using `cacheTime` to delete and garbage collect the query (defaults to **5 minutes**)."
    4. Immediately after that bullet point, insert two new bullet points:
       - First, describe the scenario where a new instance of the query mounts *before* the cache timeout completes. Explain that the query immediately returns the cached value while `fetchTodos` runs in the background to refresh it.
       - Second, note that this new instance eventually unmounts again (i.e., "The final instance of `useQuery('todos', fetchTodos)` unmounts.").
    5. Keep the existing final bullets about "No more instances appear within 5 minutes" and garbage collection unchanged.
    6. Review the surrounding text to ensure the new bullets flow naturally and don't disrupt the existing narrative.
    7. Commit changes with a clear message describing the documentation clarification.

pr_chain.title: Make staleness determination local to query observers instead of global query state
pr_chain.description:
Currently, staleness is tracked as a global property on each query (`state.isStale`). This means that all consumers of a query share the same staleness status and stale time. This creates problems when different components or hooks want to use different stale times for the same query — the last one to update the query config wins, and all observers see the same stale state.

    The goal is to change staleness determination so that it is computed locally per-observer (e.g. per `useQuery` hook call), based on each observer's own `staleTime` config. The query itself should no longer store a global `isStale` boolean or schedule stale timers — instead, each observer should calculate whether the data is stale for its own config, and schedule its own timer to update when the data becomes stale.

    This also simplifies the hydration logic: there's no need to schedule stale timeouts at the query level during dehydration/hydration, since staleness will be recomputed by observers when they mount.

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` for dependency management and available scripts. The `jest.config.js` file configures the test runner. The `CONTRIBUTING.md` may also have relevant guidance.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Remove global stale tracking from `Query`**: 
       - Remove `isStale` from the `QueryState` interface in `src/core/query.ts`.
       - Remove the `MarkStale` action type and handler from the query reducer.
       - Remove `staleTimeout`, `enableStaleTimeout`, and related methods (`activateStaleTimeout`, `rescheduleStaleTimeout`, `clearStaleTimeout`, `invalidate`).
       - Remove `isStale` from the `SuccessAction` interface and from the `setData` method — stop passing an `isStale` flag into dispatches.
       - Adjust `onWindowFocus` and `onOnline` to check staleness differently — these should ask observers if they consider the data stale, or simply let observers trigger refetches. Since observers manage staleness, the query should not gate refetching on `state.isStale`.

    2. **Add an `isStaleByTime` method to `Query`**: 
       - Add a public method `isStaleByTime(staleTime: number): boolean` to `Query` that computes staleness based on the query's `state.updatedAt`, the given `staleTime`, and whether there is initial data. This replaces the global `isStale` checks.

    3. **Update `QueryCache` to use local staleness**:
       - In `prefetchQuery`, replace the check `query.state.isStale` with `query.isStaleByTime(config.staleTime)`.
       - Remove the `query.activateTimeouts()` call from the `finally` block — garbage collection timer should be scheduled in the `Query` constructor instead.
       - Remove `activateTimeouts()` calls from `setQueryData` and `buildQuery`-related paths; when no observer exists, no stale timer is needed.
       - In `invalidateQueries`, when a query has no observers and `refetchInactive` is false, don't call `query.invalidate()` — just return `undefined` (there's no global stale state to update).

    4. **Move staleness scheduling to `QueryObserver`**:
       - In `src/core/queryObserver.ts`, add a `staleTimeoutId` field.
       - Add a private `updateIsStale()` method that computes staleness via `currentQuery.isStaleByTime(this.config.staleTime)` and, if it differs from `currentResult.isStale`, re-creates the result and notifies the listener.
       - Add a private `updateStaleTimeout()` method that clears any existing stale timeout, then schedules a new one based on `staleTime` and `updatedAt` (similar to the old rescheduling logic but on the observer).
       - Rename `updateRefetchInterval` usage to a generic `updateTimers` that calls both `updateStaleTimeout` and `updateRefetchInterval`. Call `updateTimers` in `subscribe` and when the query changes in `updateConfig`.
       - In `updateConfig`, if `enabled` or `staleTime` changed, also call `updateStaleTimeout()`.
       - In `unsubscribe`, clear the stale timeout along with the refetch interval.
       - In `optionalFetch`, change the stale check from `currentResult.isStale` to a computed value: `this.currentQuery.isStaleByTime(this.config.staleTime)`.
       - Add a public `isStale()` method that returns the observer's computed staleness.

    5. **Update hydration**: 
       - In `src/hydration/hydration.ts`, remove the dehydration of `staleTime` (since it's no longer a query-level concern). Remove the `activateGarbageCollectionTimeout` call after hydrate (timers will be scheduled on demand).
       - Update the `DehydratedQueryConfig` interface to remove the `staleTime` field.

    6. **Update documentation**: 
       - In `docs/src/pages/docs/comparison.md`, add a row for "Stale While Revalidate" showing React Query's support as "Server-Side + Client-Side".

    7. **Update tests**: 
       - Remove tests in `src/core/tests/queryCache.test.tsx` that check for stale timeouts on the query (they no longer apply).
       - Replace old hydration staleness tests in `src/hydration/tests/hydration.test.tsx` and `src/hydration/tests/react.test.tsx` with new ones that verify hydration works without scheduling timers, and that observers compute staleness based on their own config.
       - Add a test to `src/react/tests/useQuery.test.tsx` verifying that two components using the same query can have different stale times and each compute stale independently.
       - Add a test for `prefetchQuery` to verify it only fetches if data is older than the provided stale time.

pr_chain.title: Ensure query configuration only updates on query execution
pr_chain.description:
The current query configuration is updated based on the order in which hooks are rendered. This can result in unexpected behavior when multiple hooks for the same query key with different configurations are rendered. For example, if two `useQuery` hooks are rendered with the same key but different query functions, the second hook's configuration overwrites the first hook's configuration on render, even though the first hook should remain active.

    Fix this so that a query's configuration is only changed when it is actually executed (i.e., via a fetch, refetch, or fetchMore call), not on every render. The most recently executed configuration should be the one used for the query.

    Additionally, handle these related details:
    - Ensure the query's `cacheTime` is tracked independently and never decreases below the highest value it has seen (so garbage collection isn't prematurely triggered).
    - Refactor the `QueryCache` to maintain an internal array of queries for more efficient iteration, and expose it via `getQueries()`.
    - Update the `Query` lifecycle so that clearing a query properly removes it from the cache and notifies listeners.
    - Update the hydration logic to use the new `cacheTime` property and query cache iteration method.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's `package.json` for dependency scripts and test commands. The `jest.config.js` file at the root contains Jest configuration. Core library code is under `src/core/`, React-specific code under `src/react/`, and tests are colocated in `src/core/tests/` and `src/react/tests/`.

## Implementation Plan
- In `src/core/query.ts`, add a public `cacheTime` property to the `Query` class. Initialize it in the constructor from the config. Update `updateConfig` to be private and to update `cacheTime` to the maximum of its current value and the new config's `cacheTime`. Update `scheduleGc` to use `this.cacheTime` instead of `this.config.cacheTime`. Modify `refetch` and `fetch` to accept an optional `config` parameter that is used for the execution instead of `this.config`. Split `clear()` into `clear()` (which removes the query from the cache) and `destroy()` (which handles internal cleanup). Make `updateConfig` private.
    - In `src/core/queryCache.ts`, add a private `queriesArray` property to `QueryCache` and maintain it alongside the existing `queries` hash map. Update `notifyGlobalListeners`, `clear`, `getQueries`, and `removeQueries` to use `queriesArray`. Make `getQueries`'s `predicate` parameter optional. Add a `removeQuery` method that destroys the query, removes it from both the hash map and the array, and notifies global listeners. Ensure `clear` uses `removeQueries`.
    - In `src/core/queryObserver.ts`, store a reference to the `QueryCache` in the observer's constructor. Update `refetch`, `fetchMore`, and `fetch` to pass the observer's config directly to the query's corresponding method instead of calling `updateConfig`. In `updateQuery`, use the stored `queryCache` instance instead of the config's.
    - In `src/hydration/hydration.ts`, update `dehydrateQuery` to use `query.cacheTime` instead of `query.config.cacheTime`. Update `dehydrate` to iterate over `queryCache.getQueries()` instead of `Object.values(queryCache.queries)`.
    - Update the affected tests in `src/core/tests/queryCache.test.tsx`, `src/react/tests/ssr.test.tsx`, and `src/react/tests/useQuery.test.tsx` to reflect the new behavior. Add a test verifying that a query uses the longest cache time it has seen and a test that query configuration is not overridden on render.

pr_chain.title: Add timeout handling to API address fetches and refresh data
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to improve the reliability of the `getAddressesapi` function in `_worker.js` by adding a timeout mechanism to prevent the Cloudflare Worker from hanging when upstream API calls are slow or unresponsive. Currently, the function uses `Promise.allSettled` to fetch addresses from multiple APIs, but there is no timeout — if one of these APIs never responds, the entire request hangs. We need to add a timeout using `AbortController` so that all fetch requests are aborted after a short period (e.g., 2 seconds). The function should still collect all successful responses that come in before the timeout and gracefully handle the abort as a non-fatal error.

    Additionally, refresh the sample data in `addressesapi.txt` with a fresh set of working addresses, and make minor polish to the README (clean up link labels and add credit to new sources).

## Environment Setup
Check the `README.md` for project context and available variables. There is no package.json or Makefile in this repository — the project is a single Cloudflare Worker script. Installation and testing instructions are not provided; the primary artifact is the `_worker.js` file itself.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `_worker.js`, locate the `getAddressesapi` function (currently around line 90).
    2. Inside the function, before the `try` block, create an `AbortController` instance and a `setTimeout` that calls `controller.abort()` after 2 seconds.
    3. Pass `signal: controller.signal` as part of the fetch options in the `api.map` call.
    4. Keep the existing `Promise.allSettled` pattern — it already handles rejected/aborted promises gracefully by returning `{ status: 'rejected' }`.
    5. In the `finally` block (which you should add), call `clearTimeout` with the timeout variable to clean up.
    6. Remove the large commented-out block within `getAddressesapi` for code cleanliness.
    7. Update `addressesapi.txt` with a refreshed list of working address/port combinations, keeping the same format (`ip:port#Region`).
    8. In `README.md`, update the link label `[[实现原理 视频讲解]]` to `[[实现原理]]` (removing "视频讲解") and add the additional credit sources `ACL4SSR` and `肥羊` to the "感谢" section.

pr_chain.title: Fix subscription routing for cf-workers-sub user agents
pr_chain.description:
Update the Cloudflare Worker to prevent requests coming from `cf-workers-sub` user agents from being routed to Clash or Sing-box subconverter services. Currently, the routing logic checks for Clash and Sing-box user agents or format parameters, but does not exclude the `cf-workers-sub` user agent. This causes WorkerVless2sub instances that are chained together (one Workers subscription being used by another) to have their requests incorrectly forwarded to external subconverter services, breaking the chained subscription flow. Additionally, refresh the IP address list in `addressesapi.txt` to use newly discovered Cloudflare worker IP addresses to maintain service reliability. The change should ensure that when a request comes from a `cf-workers-sub` user agent, it is not matched by the Clash or Sing-box routes, and instead falls through to the default VLESS subscription output. ## Environment Setup Examine `README.md` for project setup and usage instructions. Check `_worker.js` for the Cloudflare Worker logic and `addressesapi.txt` for the IP address list format. The project has no dependency manifests (no package.json, pyproject.toml, or similar), so testing likely requires deploying the Worker to Cloudflare Workers or running it in a local Workers emulator as described in the README. ## Implementation Plan
  • Modify the Clash routing condition in the request handler in `_worker.js` to append `&& !userAgent.includes('cf-workers-sub')` to the existing condition, ensuring cf-workers-sub requests do not trigger subconverter forwarding.
  • Apply the same exclusion in the Sing-box routing condition, adding `&& !userAgent.includes('cf-workers-sub')` to prevent subconverter forwarding for this user agent there as well.
  • Review the surrounding code to confirm that cf-workers-sub requests now fall through to the default VLESS subscription response path.
  • Update the `addressesapi.txt` file with the provided new list of Cloudflare worker IP addresses, ensuring each line follows the `:#` format.
  • Test the Worker with user agents containing 'clash' or 'sing-box' combined with 'cf-workers-sub' to verify they receive the default subscription output rather than a subconverter response.

pr_chain.title: Replace racy Arc strong-count based cleanups with cancellation tokens
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to remove cleanup logic that relies on `Arc::strong_count` checks inside `Drop` implementations. The Rust documentation warns that the strong count can change at any time (including between calling the method and acting on the result), which makes this pattern unreliable. Two threads can easily both observe a count of 2 when they expect 1, causing cleanup to be skipped. This affects several background task wrapper types and the `Tesseract` key store.

    For the task wrapper types, the current pattern stores an `Arc<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` and aborts the task in `Drop` when the strong count is 1. We need to replace this with a cancellation token approach: store a `DropGuard` from `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` (wrapped in `Arc`), create the token alongside the task, and race the cancelled signal against the task's own completion using `tokio::select!`.

    For `Tesseract`, the current `Drop` impl checks the strong count of `enc_pass` to decide whether to call `lock()`. Remove this `Drop` impl entirely. Also consolidate the many `Arc` fields into a single `Arc<TesseractInner>` struct containing all of them, allowing `Clone` to be derived instead of hand-written.

    As an additional cleanup, rename the `start` methods on the background task types to `run`, since these methods are the task code itself rather than merely "starting" the task.

    Affected files:
    - `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/store/document/cache.rs`
    - `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/store/document/conversation.rs`
    - `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/store/document/root.rs`
    - `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/store/event_subscription.rs`
    - `tools/shuttle/src/store/identity.rs`
    - `tools/shuttle/src/store/root.rs`
    - `warp/src/tesseract/mod.rs`

## Environment Setup
The repository is a Cargo workspace. Check the root `Cargo.toml` for workspace members and dependency declarations (notably `tokio-util` must be available with the `sync` feature). Look at `.github/workflows/cargo-test.yml` for CI configuration. Individual crate manifests (`extensions/warp-ipfs/Cargo.toml`, `tools/shuttle/Cargo.toml`, `warp/Cargo.toml`) may list their own dev-dependencies and features.

## Implementation Plan
1. In each of the affected files, add imports for `tokio::select` and `tokio_util::sync::{CancellationToken, DropGuard}`. Verify `tokio-util` is a dependency in the relevant `Cargo.toml` files; add it if missing.
    2. In `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/store/document/cache.rs`, `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/store/document/conversation.rs`, `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/store/document/root.rs`, `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/store/event_subscription.rs`, `tools/shuttle/src/store/identity.rs`, and `tools/shuttle/src/store/root.rs`:
       - Replace the `task: Arc<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` field with `_task_cancellation: Arc<DropGuard>`.
       - Remove the manual `Drop` implementations that check `Arc::strong_count`.
       - In each `new` constructor, create a `CancellationToken`, derive a `DropGuard` from it via `token.clone().drop_guard()`, and spawn the task with a `tokio::select!` that races `token.cancelled()` against `task.run()`.
       - Store the `DropGuard` wrapped in `Arc`.
       - Rename the `start` method on the task struct to `run`.
    3. In `warp/src/tesseract/mod.rs`:
       - Introduce a private struct `TesseractInner` that contains all the fields currently on `Tesseract` (the Arcs, atomics, channels, and the broadcast receiver).
       - Change `Tesseract` to have a single field `inner: Arc<TesseractInner>`.
       - Update `Default`, `Debug`, and `PartialEq` implementations to access fields via `self.inner`.
       - Add `Clone` to the `derive` list on `Tesseract` and remove the manual `Clone` impl.
       - Remove the `Drop` impl for `Tesseract` entirely.
       - Update all method bodies to access fields through `self.inner` (e.g., `self.inner.internal`, `self.inner.event_tx`).
    4. Search the codebase for any other references to the removed `task` fields or `start` methods and update accordingly.
    5. Run `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` (if available in the repo's CI config) to ensure code style compliance.

pr_chain.title: Fix racy tesseract auto-lock test and event broadcast behavior
pr_chain.description:
The `tesseract` module's test for the "last handle dropped auto-locks" behavior is incomplete — it only drops the duplicate handles and never verifies that the final drop of the original `Tesseract` actually emits a `Locked` event. The test currently has a comment noting that we "wouldn't be able to check" this, but we should be able to verify it properly.

    Additionally, there's a subtle correctness issue in the event broadcast setup: the default channel buffer is quite large (1024), which means events can be queued indefinitely if no receiver is actively draining them. To make event delivery more predictable and to support the test we want to write, we should reduce the buffer to a minimal size and enable overflow behavior so that stale events are dropped rather than accumulated.

    Finally, the `lock()` and `unlock()` methods broadcast events on every call regardless of whether anyone is listening. The implementation plan should consider whether we want to guard these broadcasts (e.g., only broadcast when there are active receivers) — but do **not** add receiver-count checks, as those are inherently racy in a multi-threaded environment (the count can change between checking it and acting on it). The `try_broadcast` failure mode is acceptable and safe to ignore.

    The goal is to:
    - Make the existing `test_with_256bit_passphase` (or a similar test) actually verify that the final drop of the last `Tesseract` handle triggers a `Locked` event.
    - Adjust the event channel configuration so this test — and real-world usage — behaves deterministically without relying on a large buffer.

## Environment Setup
Check `warp/Cargo.toml` for workspace dependency configuration and the `warp` crate's dependencies. The test code lives in `warp/src/tesseract/mod.rs` under `#[cfg(test)] mod test`. Look at `.github/workflows/cargo-test.yml` to understand how CI runs tests, and refer to the root `Cargo.toml` for workspace-level settings. The `c/Makefile` may also be relevant if C bindings are involved, but the core change is pure Rust.

## Implementation Plan
- Reduce the default broadcast channel buffer size from 1024 to 1 in `Tesseract::default()`.
    - Call `set_overflow(true)` on the sender so that when the buffer is full, new broadcasts drop old messages rather than fail silently or block.
    - In the test, subscribe to the tesseract's event stream **before** dropping the last strong reference.
    - Drop the final `Tesseract` handle, then use `now_or_never()` on the stream's next item to synchronously assert that a `Locked` event was received.
    - Clean up any unused imports or dead code introduced in the test module (e.g., ensure `FutureExt` is imported and used appropriately).
    - Run the existing test suite for the `warp` crate to confirm the new assertion is stable and non-flaky.

pr_chain.title: Add Directory::get_last_directory_from_path and refine path traversal logic
pr_chain.description:
We need a new method on `Directory` that, given a valid path string, returns the last directory in that path. This is useful when callers need to know which directory contains a given item or where a path terminates, without having to manually walk the tree.

    The method should:
    - Accept an absolute-style path string (e.g. `"/Sub Directory 1/Sub Directory 2/"`).
    - Resolve the path from the current `Directory` root, traversing any nested directories.
    - Return the deepest directory that is successfully resolved. If the final path segment is a file, the method should still return the directory that contains it.
    - Return an error (`Error::InvalidPath`) if the path is empty or malformed, and `Error::DirectoryNotFound` if the first path segment does not match a directory at the current level.
    - Handle trailing slashes gracefully (i.e., `/Sub Directory 1/` should resolve to `Sub Directory 1`).

    While adding this, also tidy up the existing `get_item_by_path` logic — the current implementation conditionally extracts a directory and then recurses. This can be made slightly more direct by matching on the item type explicitly, which reduces nesting and makes the control flow clearer.

    Please ensure the new method is documented with a doc example and that it behaves consistently with `get_item_by_path` for the same inputs.

## Environment Setup
The repository is a Rust workspace. Check the following for build/test configuration:
    - Root `Cargo.toml` — workspace member list and dependency declarations.
    - `warp/Cargo.toml` — the primary crate containing the directory module.
    - `.github/workflows/cargo-test.yml` — CI workflow that likely shows how tests are run.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `warp/src/constellation/directory.rs`.
    2. Add a new public method `get_last_directory_from_path(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Directory, Error>` to the `Directory` impl block.
    3. Implement the method:
       - Split the path on `/`, filter out empty segments, and collect into a `Vec<&str>`.
       - If the vector is empty, return `Error::InvalidPath`.
       - Pop the first segment and call `self.get_item(name)`.
       - Match on the returned `Item`:
         - If it's `Item::Directory(dir)`, then:
           - If there are remaining path segments, recursively call `dir.get_last_directory_from_path(...)` on the joined remainder, falling back to `dir` if the recursion fails.
           - If no remaining segments, return `Ok(dir)`.
         - If it's anything else, return `Err(Error::DirectoryNotFound)`.
    4. Add a Rustdoc comment with an example demonstrating the method's behaviour (including a case where the last segment is a file, and the containing directory is returned).
    5. Refactor `get_item_by_path`: replace the nested `if`/`else` block with a `match` on the resolved `Item`, separating the recursion for directories from the fall-through return for non-directories.
    6. Run existing tests for the module to verify no regressions and that the new doc tests pass.

pr_chain.title: Refactor FileStore operations to run on a dedicated background task
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to move the FileStore's core logic (put_buffer, get_buffer, sync_ref, and related operations) off the calling thread and onto a dedicated background task. This will prevent large file operations from blocking the main control flow.

    Currently, operations like `put_buffer` perform hashing and other expensive work synchronously before returning. We need to restructure the code so that:
    1. The `FileStore` holds a command channel to a spawned background task.
    2. File operations send their work as futures through a oneshot channel to the background task.
    3. The background task processes the work and sends results back through the oneshot.

    Important: Remove the hashing logic from `put_buffer` (and related operations) entirely — it significantly slows down large file processing. Hashing will be reintroduced later as a concurrent operation, so just remove it for now.

    Please also ensure that thumbnail generation errors are logged rather than silently ignored, and add a test case verifying that renaming files within a directory works correctly.

## Environment Setup

The tests themselves live in `extensions/warp-ipfs/tests/files.rs` with shared helpers in `extensions/warp-ipfs/tests/common.rs`.

## Implementation Plan
- Introduce a `FileTaskCommand` enum that represents the different operations (put_buffer, get_buffer, sync_ref, etc.) and update the `FileStore` struct to hold an mpsc sender and a drop guard for cancellation.
    - Create a `FileTask` struct that owns the actual IPFS node, index, thumbnail store, and other shared state. Spawn this task in `FileStore::new` and have it listen for commands on the mpsc receiver.
    - Refactor `put_buffer`, `get_buffer`, `sync_ref`, and other public methods to create a oneshot channel, send the requested operation to the background task via the mpsc channel, then await the oneshot response.
    - Remove the hashing logic from file operations (both the hashing call itself and any fields/comments referencing it). The `modified` field can be removed if unused.
    - Update the test suite: add a test for renaming files within a directory, and ensure all existing file-related tests still pass with the new architecture.

pr_chain.title: Remove unreachable panic on closed command channel in phonebook
pr_chain.description:
In `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/behaviour/phonebook.rs`, the `poll` method of the `NetworkBehaviour` implementation contains a `Match` expression that processes incoming commands from an mpsc channel. Currently, when the channel returns `Poll::Ready(None)` (indicating the channel has closed/dropped), the code uses `unreachable!("Channels are owned")` which will cause a panic if triggered. While a closed channel may indicate an unusual application state, panicking is undesirable when the application could instead gracefully break out of the loop and continue operation.

    Your task is to replace the `unreachable!` macro with a graceful break from the polling loop when the channel is closed. This ensures the application handles unexpected channel closure without crashing, while still functioning correctly when the command channel is active.

    Additionally, update the adjacent comment on the peer disconnection backoff logic (`//In case peer disconnects due to keep-alive, we should wait before emitting an event for the client to reestablish connection`) to be more concise and accurately describe the behavior without referencing specific failure scenarios.

## Environment Setup
Check the `Cargo.toml` files in the repository root and in `extensions/warp-ipfs/Cargo.toml` for dependency configuration. The `.github/workflows/cargo-test.yml` file contains the CI test workflow, and you should review the `Cargo.toml` files to determine the test setup for the workspace.

## Implementation Plan
- Open `extensions/warp-ipfs/src/behaviour/phonebook.rs` and locate the `poll` method in the `NetworkBehaviour` implementation.
    - Find the `Match` expression that processes the `self.command.poll_next_unpin(cx)` result.
    - Replace the `Poll::Ready(None) => unreachable!("Channels are owned")` arm with `Poll::Ready(None) | Poll::Pending => break`, merging it with the existing `Poll::Pending` arm to break out of the loop gracefully on channel closure.
    - Update the comment associated with the backoff delay insertion to be more concise, e.g., "Delay emitting event in case of reconnection".
    - Run the relevant tests for the `warp-ipfs` extension to verify the change compiles and existing functionality remains intact.

As the calendar year has changed from 2022 to 2023, several unit tests and integration test fixture files are now asserting expected dates (2022) that no longer match what the parser actually produces (2023). 2. The affected integration test fixture files under `server/integration_tests/test_data/` so the expected `chart_config.json` outputs reflect the 2023 detected year.

Note: The fixture updates are not purely mechanical year substitutions — because data availability changes year over year, some expected chart blocks may be added, removed, or changed (e.g., a tile type may switch to `PLACE_OVERVIEW` when only a single data point is available). pr_chain.title: Add download mode for default FT model and embeddings in custom DC build
pr_chain.description:
Implement a new download mode in the custom DC embeddings build script that downloads the default Fine-Tuned (FT) model and base DC embeddings from GCS without building custom embeddings. This mode should be used during Docker image building so that the NL server startup time is significantly reduced from minutes to seconds, as the model and embeddings are already available locally when the server starts. Additionally, skip loading place summaries for custom DCs to avoid GCP authentication failures, and add a check in the shared GCS utility to avoid re-downloading files that already exist locally.

## Environment Setup

## Implementation Plan
1. In `tools/nl/embeddings/build_custom_dc_embeddings.py`, add a `--mode` flag with values `build` (default) and `download`. Make the existing `sv_sentences_csv_path` and `output_dir` flags optional when mode is download.
    2. Create a `download()` function that: gets the default FT model version from `utils.get_default_ft_model_version()`, downloads the model using `utils.get_or_download_model_from_gcs()`, gets the default embeddings filename from `utils.get_default_ft_embeddings_file_name()`, and downloads the embeddings file using a new `utils.get_or_download_file_from_gcs()` function.
    3. In `tools/nl/embeddings/utils.py`, refactor the `_get_default_ft_model_version()` function to extract the embeddings file name first, then parse the model version from it. Add a new `get_default_ft_embeddings_file_name()` function that returns the full embeddings filename from the YAML config.
    4. Add `get_or_download_file_from_gcs()` and `_download_file_from_gcs()` functions in `tools/nl/embeddings/utils.py` that check if a file already exists in the temp directory before downloading from GCS.
    5. In `shared/lib/gcs.py`, add a `get_or_download_file()` function that returns the local path if the file already exists, otherwise downloads it. Refactor the existing `download_file()` to use a shared `_get_local_path()` helper.
    6. In `nl_server/gcs.py`, update `download_embeddings()` to use the new `get_or_download_file()` from the shared library.

pr_chain.title: Enable date range filtering for ranked timeline collections
pr_chain.description:
Extend the Natural Language (NL) exploration system to support date range queries (e.g., "in the last 5 years", "after 2013", "over the last 10 years") when generating ranked timeline collections. Currently, ranked timeline collections ignore the date range specified in a query, leading to charts showing the entire time series instead of only the requested period.

    The system already handles date ranges for other chart types. The goal is to make ranked timeline collections (a set of line charts ranking places or variables by growth over time) respect the user's requested date range.

    Additionally, fix a related facet selection bug. The current implementation stores a single facet ID per statistical variable (SV). This is incorrect when multiple places are involved, as different places may have data in different facets. Change the data structure to store a map of SV -> place -> facet metadata. When building a line chart with multiple places, select the facet that has data for the most places.

    Implement this change without breaking existing functionality for single-date queries or queries with no date specified.

## Environment Setup
- `server/requirements.txt`: Python dependencies for the NL server.
    - `pytest.ini`: Configuration for running Python tests.
    - `server/tests/`: Contains unit tests, including `server/tests/lib/nl/rank_utils_test.py`.
    - `server/integration_tests/`: Contains end-to-end tests, including `server/integration_tests/explore_test.py`.
    - `run_test.sh`: Script to run the test suite.

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify `server/lib/nl/common/utils.py` to change the `sv_existence_for_places_check_single_point` function's return type. Update `existing_svs` to be `Dict[str, Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]]` (SV -> place -> facet metadata), populating it for each place individually.
    2. Update `ChartVars` in `server/lib/nl/fulfillment/types.py` to change the type hint for `sv_exist_facet` to `Dict[str, Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]]`.
    3. Add a new utility function `get_facet_id` in `server/lib/nl/fulfillment/utils.py` that takes an SV, date, the `sv_exist_facet` map, and a list of places. It should select and return the facet ID that has data for the most places. Update `is_coplottable` to accept a list of places and use the new nested structure.
    4. Update `server/lib/nl/common/rank_utils.py` functions `rank_places_by_series_growth` and `rank_svs_by_series_growth` to accept a `date_range` parameter and the `sv_exist_facet` map. When a `date_range` is present, fetch data with `all_facets=True` and filter the series to only use the facet returned by `get_facet_id` before computing growth.
    5. Update the timeline config builder in `server/lib/nl/config_builder/timeline.py` and `builder.py` to pass the `date_range` to the `ranked_timeline_collection_block` function and set the line tile spec's start and end dates. Update all timeline block builders to use the new `get_facet_id` helper when constructing facet IDs.
    6. Update the callers `time_delta_across_places.py` and `time_delta_across_vars.py` to pass the `date_range` and `sv_exist_facet` from the state and chart vars to the ranking functions. Update `correlation.py` to pass places to `is_coplottable`.

pr_chain.title: Enable chart fulfillment with only multi-SV candidates detected
pr_chain.description:
When the NL query handling detects only multi-statistical-variable (multi-SV) candidates and no individual SVs pass the detection threshold, the system currently aborts fulfillment and returns an empty result. This creates a poor user experience for queries like "Does obesity correlate with lack of sleep in US counties" in strict mode, which otherwise produce results in regular mode.

    The goal is to allow the chart fulfillment pipeline to proceed using multi-SV candidates (e.g., scatter chart comparisons) even when no single SVs are detected. Success should be determined by the presence of any chart variables (including multi-SV candidates) rather than requiring at least one individual SV.

    Please also ensure that:
    - Error handling and fallback behavior correctly distinguish between cases where no SVs at all were detected and cases where only multi-SV candidates were found.
    - Any logging or counters are updated to reflect the new success criteria.
    - Integration test coverage is added for the scenario where only multi-SV candidates are detected.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository's `pytest.ini` for test configuration, `server/requirements.txt` for Python dependencies, and the `CONTRIBUTING.md` for overall development workflow guidance. Also review `server/integration_tests/explore_test.py` to understand how integration tests are structured.

## Implementation Plan
- Modify the early-return condition in `server/lib/nl/fulfillment/base.py`'s `populate_charts` function to check for the presence of `state.chart_vars_map` instead of `state.uttr.svs`. This allows the fulfillment to proceed when multi-SV candidates are present.
    - Update the error handling and fallback logic after a failed fulfillment attempt to reference `state.chart_vars_map` instead of `state.uttr.svs` where appropriate, ensuring proper `sv_source` assignment for "UNRECOGNIZED" vs "UNFULFILLED" cases.
    - Remove or update the logging statement in `_add_charts_with_existence_check` that prints `state.uttr.svs`, since `svs` may not be the primary source of data anymore.
    - Add a new integration test case in `server/integration_tests/explore_test.py` (e.g., `test_e2e_strict_multi_sv`) that queries a phrase like "Does obesity correlate with lack of sleep in US counties" in strict mode, and generate the corresponding golden chart config file under `server/integration_tests/test_data/`.
    - Update any existing golden test data files (e.g., `explore_strict_multi_var/chart_config.json`, `fulfillment_api_sdg_specialvars/chart_config.json`) that may be affected by the change in success criteria.

pr_chain.title: Fix chartUrl root and add apikey for API proxy requests
pr_chain.description:
When the nodejs server is behind an API proxy (such as Apigee), the `chartUrl` returned in query results uses the internal protocol and host of the server, not the protocol and host that the user originally requested. We need to:

    1. Update the Apigee configuration to forward the original host in a request header.
    2. Update the nodejs server to read the protocol and host from forwarded headers (if available) when constructing the `urlRoot` for chart URLs.
    3. Also read and include the `apikey` query parameter in the generated chart URLs.

    The goal is to ensure chart URLs returned by the `/nodejs/query` endpoint point to the correct external protocol/host and include the user's API key when applicable.

## Environment Setup
- Check `static/package.json` for the TypeScript/Node.js project scripts and dependencies.
    - Check `static/jest.config.js` for test configuration.
    - Check `static/tsconfig.json` for TypeScript compilation settings.
    - Deployment configuration for Apigee is under `deploy/apigee/bard/apiproxy/`.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Apigee proxy update**:
       - Create a new policy file `deploy/apigee/bard/apiproxy/policies/forward-host.xml` that sets the `x-forwarded-host` header to the value of the original `request.header.host`.
       - In `deploy/apigee/bard/apiproxy/website.xml`, add a reference to the new `forward-host` policy in the `<Policies>` section.
       - In `deploy/apigee/bard/apiproxy/targets/default.xml`, add a step in the PreFlow Request to execute the `forward-host` policy.

    2. **Nodejs server updates**:
       - In `static/nodejs_server/constants.ts`, add `API_KEY: "apikey"` to the `CHART_URL_PARAMS` object.
       - In `static/nodejs_server/utils.ts`, update `getChartUrl()` to accept an optional `apikey` parameter and include it in the `paramMapping` object.
       - In `static/src/server.ts`, in the `/nodejs/query` route handler:
         - Read the protocol from `req.headers["x-forwarded-proto"]` if present, otherwise fall back to `req.protocol`.
         - Read the host from `req.headers["x-forwarded-host"]` if present, otherwise fall back to `req.headers.host`.
         - Read the `apikey` from `req.query.apikey` (default to empty string).
         - Construct `urlRoot` using the resolved protocol and host.
         - Pass `apikey` to `getBlockTileResults` and `getDisasterBlockTileResults`.

    3. **Propagate `apikey` through tile functions**:
       - Update `getBlockTileResults` and `getDisasterBlockTileResults` in `static/src/server.ts` to accept and pass an `apikey` parameter.
       - In `static/nodejs_server/bar_tile.ts`, `line_tile.ts`, `map_tile.ts`, `scatter_tile.ts`, `disaster_map_tile.ts`, and `ranking_tile.ts`, add an optional `apikey` parameter to the respective `get*TileResult` functions.
       - In `ranking_tile.ts`, also update `getRankingUnitResult` to accept and pass `apikey`.
       - In all these tile functions, pass `apikey` to `getChartUrl()` calls.

    4. **Verify**:
       - Ensure no TypeScript compilation errors.
       - Ensure the existing tests still pass.
       - Review the behavior when forwarded headers are not present (fallback to direct protocol/host).

pr_chain.title: Distinguish exclusive vs inclusive date prepositions in NL date ranges.
pr_chain.description:
We need to update the natural language (NL) date detection logic to correctly handle the difference between exclusive and inclusive date prepositions when determining date ranges. Specifically:

    1. Prepositions like "before 2020" and "after 2020" should be **exclusive**, meaning the specified date itself is NOT included in the range. For example:
       - "before 2020" with year precision should generate a range ending in 2019 (not 2020).
       - "after 2013" should generate a range starting in 2014 (not 2013).

    2. Prepositions like "until 2020" and "since 2020" should remain **inclusive**, including the specified date in the range.

    3. When determining if a date is a single date (vs. a date range), the logic should look only at the preposition, not at the year span. For example, "in 2020" or "on 2020" are single dates, but "before 2020" is a range.

    4. For phrases like "over the last X year(s)" (e.g., "in the last 5 years"), the date range should include the current year. For example, if the current year is 2024, "in the last 5 years" should span from 2019 to 2024 (inclusive of the current year/date).

    The goal is make date detection more semantically accurate so downstream chart generation reflects the user's intended time period.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repo files for environment setup instructions:
    - `server/requirements.txt` (Python dependencies for the server code)
    - `pytest.ini` (pytest configuration)
    - `run_test.sh` (likely a script for running tests)
    - `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/developer_guide.md` may also contain relevant workflow information.
    - The primary code changes are in Python (server-side), so focus on Python dependency and test setup.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Update `server/lib/nl/detection/date.py`**:
       - Add a new constant, e.g., `_EXCLUSIVE_DATE_PREPS = ['before', 'after']`, to identify prepositions that exclude the base date.
       - Modify `_is_single_date()`: Instead of using `year_span` to determine if a date is single, just check if `date.prep` is in `_SINGLE_DATE_PREPS`. Remove the `year_span == 1` and `year_span == 0` conditions.
       - Add a constant `_LAST_YEARS_PREP = 'last_years'` and use it as the prep for dates parsed from `LAST_YEARS` and `LAST_YEAR` patterns in `parse_date()`. When creating these `Date` objects, use the current year (`datetime.date.today().year`) as the base year, and keep `year_span` as parsed.
       - Update `_SINGLE_DATE_PREPS` to include `'year'` (since "year XXXX" is a single date).
       - Update `_END_DATE_PREPS` to include `_LAST_YEARS_PREP`.
       - Refactor `_get_month_string()` to take an integer `month` argument instead of a `Date` object.
       - Implement a new helper function `_get_base_year_month()` that adjusts the base year/month based on the preposition:
         - For `'before'` with a month: if the month is January (1), the end date should be December of the previous year (i.e., `year-1`, month 12); otherwise, it should be the previous month of the same year (i.e., `year`, month-1).
         - For `'after'` with a month: if the month is December (12), the start date should be January of the next year (i.e., `year+1`, month 1); otherwise, it should be the next month (i.e., `year`, month+1).
         - For year-only precision with `'before'` or `'after'`, the base date should be the year itself, and the range logic will handle the exclusion (see below).
       - Rewrite `get_date_range_strings()` to:
         - Handle the case where the date is a single date (prep in `_SINGLE_DATE_PREPS`) by returning `('', '')`.
         - For `'before'` and `'after'` (exclusive preps), adjust the start/end date:
           - For `'before'`: if `year_span == 0`, the end date is `year-1` (with month adjustment). If `year_span > 0` (from "last X years"), the end date is the base year (which is the current year), and the start date is `base_year - (year_span - 1)`.
           - For `'after'`: if `year_span == 0`, the start date is `year+1` (with month adjustment). If `year_span > 0`, this case should not occur (as "after" is not used for last years).
         - For `'until'` and `'since'` (inclusive preps), keep the base date as the boundary (no adjustment).
         - For `'from'` and `'by'`, treat them as inclusive (as before).
         - For `_LAST_YEARS_PREP`, the base date is the current year/month. The end date is the base date, and the start date is `base_year - (year_span - 1)` (with month preservation).
         - Use the `dateutil.relativedelta` module to help with month/year arithmetic (import it).

    2. **Update test files**:
       - Modify `server/tests/lib/nl/date_parser_test.py`:
         - Update expected values in `test_main` for "last years" dates to use the new `_LAST_YEARS_PREP` and current year.
         - Update the test cases in `test_main` for `get_date_range_strings` to reflect the new exclusive/inclusive behavior. Add new test cases for `'before'`, `'after'`, `'until'`, `'since'`, and `'last_years'` with various year/month precision and `year_span` values.
       - Modify `server/tests/lib/nl/utils_test.py`:
         - Add test cases for `_facet_contains_date` that differentiate `'before'` vs `'until'` and `'after'` vs `'since'` to ensure the inclusive/exclusive behavior is respected.

    3. **Update integration test data**:
       - If needed, update the expected chart configs in `server/integration_tests/test_data/` to reflect the corrected date ranges. For example, for `femalepopulationinnewyorkbefore2020`, the `endDate` should change from "2020" to "2019". For `populationincaliforniaafter2013`, the `startDate` should change from "2013" to "2014". For `lifeexpectancyinusstatesinthelast5years`, the `endDate` should become the current year (e.g., "2024").
       - Note: The `demo_feb2023` test data changes appear to be unrelated (stat var changes), so they might be a separate concern. Focus only on date-range-related changes.

pr_chain.title: Improve chart image quality and add SVG output option for Bard
pr_chain.description:
We need to enhance the chart images generated by the Node.js server for consumption by Bard. Currently, the PNG images returned lack sufficient resolution for high-quality display in various contexts. Additionally, as an experiment, we want the ability to return charts as SVG to evaluate whether SVG is a better format for Bard's consumption.

    Specifically:
    - Increase the resolution of the returned PNG chart images to preserve quality regardless of the rendered size.
    - Add an option to the `/nodejs/chart` endpoint that allows requesting the chart as an SVG instead of a PNG.
    - When returning SVG, ensure the SVG uses a viewBox instead of fixed pixel dimensions so consumers can scale it without losing quality or clipping content.
    - Preserve text attributes (like `dominant-baseline`) when the chart's text wrapping logic creates multiple tspans — currently this attribute is lost when text is wrapped, causing rendering issues in some SVG viewers.

## Environment Setup
Check the root `package.json` for dependency installation instructions, `static/package.json` for frontend build setup, and `static/jest.config.js` plus `pytest.ini` for test configuration. The Node.js server entry point is `static/src/server.ts`, and relevant chart utilities are in `static/nodejs_server/utils.ts` and `static/nodejs_server/constants.ts`. Refer to `docs/developer_guide.md` for overall development setup guidance.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `static/src/server.ts`, add a constant for the target PNG width (e.g., 1600 pixels) and apply it when converting the chart SVG to PNG using the `sharp` library.
    2. Add a new URL parameter (e.g., `svg`) to `static/nodejs_server/constants.ts` and read it in the `/nodejs/chart` handler. When the parameter is set to a truthy value, set the response content type to `image/svg+xml` and return the raw chart SVG markup; otherwise, keep returning the PNG.
    3. In `static/nodejs_server/utils.ts`, change `getProcessedSvg` to set a `viewBox` attribute with the chart dimensions instead of fixed `width`/`height` pixel attributes. Add `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"` to maintain aspect ratio.
    4. In `static/js/chart/base.ts`, update the `wrap` function to capture the `dominant-baseline` attribute from the original text element and propagate it to each generated `tspan` element, so multi-line wrapped text preserves vertical alignment properties.
    5. Verify all existing tests pass and run the Node.js server locally to confirm that both PNG and SVG responses work correctly, with SVG output rendering properly in various viewers.
